gearNotes.heading: Equipment
gearNotes.text:
This is the recommended equipment for barraging or bursting abyssal demons in the Catacombs of Kourend.

Abyssal demons in the Catacombs are excellent experience due to the AoE effect of ancients; The chambers contain plenty of spawns that can be grouped together for barraging or bursting, making them highly suited for multitarget strategies. This means they're some of the highest slayer experience in the game, and therefore the bracelet of slaughter is preferable over a tormented bracelet or confliction gauntlet as it will increase task length. This is especially true for player looking to train their slayer and magic levels.

Because abyssal demons have low magic defence, magic damage and prayer bonus should be prioritised over magic accuracy. Magic attack bonuses are far less important than damage multipliers.

Items that increase magic damage are especially valuable when bursting or barraging abyssal demons. Kodai wand provides +15% magic damage bonus as well as infinite water runes and a chance to save runes, making it the most effective weapon used here.

The Elidinis' ward (f) is the best off-hand, offering a +5% Magic damage bonus, significantly increasing damage output. The occult necklace also provides +5% Magic damage and is a staple choice, while the tormented bracelet offers further magic damage, though this should be swapped for a bracelet of slaughter to extend the task. Other useful pieces include the Virtus robes which are optimal for casting ancient magicks. Another strong choice for gear is the ancestral robes, imbued god capes and magus ring, all of which contribute to significantly higher kill speed and experience rates.

As it's a slayer task, the slayer helmet (i) should be used.

Dinh's bulwark’s special attack, especially when paired with the Lightbearer, is one way the player can gain aggression. Alternatively, fast weapons such as darts, knives, shortbows, or a toxic blowpipe can be used. Ideally, the player will use goading potion as this is ideal for drawing aggression.

The added weight from Dinh's may require the use of stamina potions or an explorer's ring to maintain run energy.

Reading a teleport anchoring scroll is highly recommended to prevent demons from teleporting the player.

A common method to kill abyssal demons here is to tag all the demons in one chamber, lure them into the corridor, freeze them, then repeat the process with the other chamber to combine all nine into a single stack. After this, use barrage spells like smoke barrage, ice barrage, or your best available AoE spell. Ice spells can be used effectively with a teleport anchoring scroll. After stacking demons in the corridor, players can stand to the east or west of the pile and continuously target one on the original tile. This prevents them from teleporting outside of the spell’s radius.

An extended antifire potion is recommended, as the quickest route to the abyssal demons passes through aggressive iron dragons that deal heavy damage with fire breath. Players can also take a slightly longer but safer path through the bloodveld, nechryael, and greater demon chambers, if they did not bring an antifire potion.

A herb sack may be useful, as abyssal demons drop a steady supply of herbs.

Catacombs ranged = With the venator bow, ranging abyssal demons becomes a viable alternative to barraging them. While it is less efficient, it also requires much less effort as the bow will often tag new abyssal demons without the player's input.

With 90 Magic and completion of A Kingdom Divided (and Dragon Slayer II for Ironman wrath rune access), they can provide strong Prayer training. Using Master Reanimation on ensouled heads and Demonic Offering on ashes yields ~307 Prayer experience per kill, over double their Slayer experience, without leaving the area.

Abyssal demons can be killed in the Wilderness slayer cave. This area is multicombat and allows use of a dwarf multicannon, but as with all Wilderness activities, players should avoid risking items they aren't willing to lose.It can, however, greatly speed up the task and provide a consistent supply of aggression. The cannon will not be lost if you die while it is placed on the ground. A one-click teleport (such as a royal seed pod) is strongly recommended in case of player killers.

The accursed sceptre (a) is notable here, as it provides a 50% boost to both Magic accuracy and damage against any NPC in the Wilderness, making it a powerful option. This effect stacks with the slayer helmet (i). Players should 3-item, or 4-item if using Protect Item, keeping only their sceptre and a few key magic strength pieces as their core items that are kept on death. The rest of the setup can consist of inexpensive equipment, such as monk's robes, bracelet of slaughter, and free items like the completed book of darkness.

Blighted supplies are recommended for food and prayer restoration as well as blighted ice sacks. This is because they are inexpensive and top tier, but can only be used in the wilderness.

Because abyssal demons have low magic defence, magic damage and prayer bonus should be prioritised over magic accuracy. Magic attack bonuses are far less important than damage multipliers and prayer.

It is strongly recommended to use goading potions or a cannon to gain aggression instead of a Dinh's bulwark or ranged weapons, as autocast settings are cleared when changing weapons inside the Wilderness.

Core items:

• Accursed sceptre (a)
• Occult necklace
• Slayer helmet (i)
• Optional: Saturated heart/Imbued heart if it gets the player to 94 magic. Or alternatively, Dinh's bulwark to escape PKers (recommended, as this also can be used as a special attack weapon to gain further aggression).

It is advised to stand as far south as possible within the section of the cave, since much of the northern area lies above level 30 Wilderness where teleports cannot be used.

Other items:

• Cheap prayer equipment
• Saradomin brews
• Stamina potion
• Summer pies; if 72 agility, to use the shortcuts in the cave.

Tips:

• The Wilderness player alarm plugin on RuneLite can alert the player when an enemy is nearby, enabling a quick response due to forced awareness. This can greatly reduce the chance of getting teleblocked before teleporting.

Meleeing abyssal demons offers good experience and easily allows the player access to the Arceuus spellbook for offering spells, thralls, and death charge. If in the Slayer tower bonus experience will also be awarded, scaling with completion of the Morytania Diary.

Use of demonbane weaponry like Arclight or Emberlight is strongly recommended for highest damage output.

tactics.heading: Overview
tactics.text:
At level 85 Slayer and Combat level, the player may be assigned Abyssal demons by mid and high levelled Slayer Masters and Krystilia. They can be found in the Abyssal Area, the Catacombs of Kourend, the Wilderness Slayer Cave, and in the Slayer Tower, where they are found on the third floor and in the task-only basement.

Abyssal demons use a fairly accurate melee stab attack, but with a relatively low max hit of 8. With Bigger and badder unlocked, the Greater abyssal demon has a chance to spawn as a Superior slayer monster. The greater abyssal demon is much more powerful and accurate with a max hit of 27. Protect from Melee will neutralise all damage taken from either variation.

Players on abyssal demon tasks may also opt to kill the Abyssal Sire boss instead, which can be very profitable as compensation for significantly lower experience rates compared to Abyssal demons.

Abyssal demons have a unique mechanic in which they frequently teleport around the area they're being attacked in. They also have a high chance to teleport the player up to 20 tiles away. It is highly recommended to acquire and read a Teleport anchoring scroll before fighting Abyssal demons for the first time, as this will eliminate the chance for the player to be teleported. If the player doesn't have access to the anchoring scroll, it is recommended to enable Auto Retaliate to continue attacking after being teleported. The greater abyssal demon also teleports around the player, and afterward will always land a successful hit if its attack is not prayed against. By having only two open sides through backing yourself into a corner, you can maximize multi-target ice spells since they will no longer be able to teleport behind you. This is best combined with either goading potions in the Catacombs of Kourend or a dwarf multicannon in the Wilderness Slayer Cave.

Abyssal demons are Demons, meaning they are subject to the various accuracy and damage bonuses of Demonbane Weaponry including Arclight, Emberlight, the Scorching bow, and Demonbane spells, although generally, these are not used in favour of damage dealt through area of effect damage.

Because they potentially offer high rates of Slayer experience, players should extend Abyssal demons as soon as possible.

The drop table for Abyssal demons is generally unremarkable with a few exceptions. They drop the Abyssal whip at a 1/512 rate, and therefore will drop an average of one whip every other extended task. They are also one of the only sources of the Abyssal dagger, but this is an extremely rare drop. Ensouled abyssal heads will appear several times in a task, making a Soul bearer useful. The Herb sack will also allow the player to profit further, and an Explorer's ring 4 may be used for the few alchable items among their drops. Abyssal demons in the Catacombs of Kourend also have access to that location's drop table which includes pieces of the Dark totem. Greater abyssal demons in the Catacombs will always drop a piece of the Dark totem.

tactics.heading: Strategy
tactics.text:
The Wilderness Slayer Cave is the only location in which a Cannon can be used against Abyssal demons, although as part of the Wilderness, it is also a Player killing hotspot. The Wilderness Slayer Cave also allows taking advantage of cheaper Blighted supplies and the passive effects of the Accursed sceptre (a) and other weapons charged with Revenant ether.

With their 1x1 size, Abyssal demons are ideal for use with area of effect weapons including the Venator bow and Ancient Magicks. The Catacombs and Wilderness Slayer Cave are the only two Multicombat areas with Abyssal demons. As Abyssal demons are not aggressive, a method to cause them to attack the player, such as Dinh's bulwark or a Goading potion, is recommended.

Because of the teleportation mechanic, Smoke Barrage or Smoke Burst are favoured over their Ice equivalents. After teleporting away, frozen abyssal demons will not move back toward the player until they're unfrozen. Blood spells are significantly more expensive than Smoke and are not recommended.

Killing Abyssal demons outside multicombat areas, usually done only on a Konar task, will result in a slower task requiring more attention. If required to kill Abyssal demons in a single combat zone, it's recommended to use an Expeditious bracelet with a melee setup.

If the player is comfortable with the risk, Abyssal demons in the Wilderness Slayer Cave will provide some of the best rates of Slayer experience in the game. Abyssal demons in the Catacombs are still an outstanding source of experience.

By having only two open sides through backing yourself into a corner, you can maximize multi-target ice spells since they will no longer be able to teleport behind you. This is best combined with either goading potions in the Catacombs of Kourend or a dwarf multicannon in the Wilderness Slayer Cave.

gearNotes.heading: Phase 1
gearNotes.text:
Note: This is only if the player is using melee for phase 2 and 3. The melee gear will be whatever you're using later in the fight. For phase 2 and 3, a melee weapon will be needed (if one handed, a shield slot item too).

The player brings a Scorching bow and arrows with full Melee gear in order to take out the respiratory system with the bow. This is because even with full melee gear, the bow is fairly accurate and usually oneshots the respiratory systems. The scorching bow allows the player to quickly dispose of the respiratory system without needing a full gear switch, making it possible to quickly move on to phase 2 so the player can melee the boss. At that stage, the weapon and shield slot can be switched out.

Unless using a Tumeken's shadow, Magic is only used to kill the respiratory systems. Their magic defence is so low they can be hit when wearing full melee gear.

Unless ranging the boss, Ranged is only used to kill the respiratory systems. Their defence is very low so high accuracy is unnecessary. The Scorching bow will one-shot the systems, even with bronze arrows. You do not need any switches other than the bow.

Melee is only viable for killing the respiratory systems if using a Noxious halberd, but is worse than both ranged and magic due to the extra distance the player must run.

gearNotes.heading: Phase 2 and Phase 3
gearNotes.text:
The optimal strategy is to use Emberlight or Osmumten's fang, along with a Lightbearer. The high accuracy of these weapons makes reducing the Sire's defence unnecessary, so all special attack energy is saved for damage in Phase 3.

If the player can reduce the Sire's defence with an Elder maul or Dragon warhammer special attack, weapons such as the Scythe of Vitur become considerably more effective. However, this approach is typically slower than using a highly accurate weapon and damaging special attacks.

With lower defence levels, players should consider prioritising ranged defence over melee strength to avoid being overwhelmed with damage from the spawns.

Magic is a viable method for killing the Abyssal Sire if using a Tumeken’s shadow as the primary weapon. With the best possible gear, Tumeken's shadow can offer excellent damage output against the Abyssal Sire, comparable to the best possible gear with melee. Important to keep in mind is the overall lower defence of a magic setup, so you should be careful with keeping your health up. The method is low effort as it reduces the amount of swaps; allowing you to bring more supplies.

The Eldritch Nightmare staff and Accursed sceptre can be used interchangeably. It is recommended to use the Accursed sceptre for faster kills as it reduces the boss's magic and defence levels regardless of hit. Remember to bring an imbued heart/saturated heart if possible.

Ranged generally performs worse than melee, and the reduced defence will shorten trips.

However, ranged can be used to deal additional damage before the start of Phase 2. Once all four respiratory systems are defeated, there is a brief window to attack the boss, despite it being out of melee range initially. Once the Abyssal Sire raises its arms, it becomes vulnerable to damage, including ranged attacks. During this window players can shoot the boss three times with the Scorching bow before it comes within melee range. Doing this can reduce its health by a good amount (up to 50% of your Scorching bow's max hit, multiplied by 3) before Phase 2 properly begins, making it a good strategy for players who want to optimize their kills.
Thus, it can be a good idea to bring a few ranged switches, to ensure the player doesn't hit any zeroes while killing the respiratory systems, and to also help with the few bonus hits the Phase 1 to Phase 2 transition provides.

gearNotes.heading: Melee and ranged
gearNotes.text:
• Lunar/Dramen staff (if Elite Lumbridge & Draynor Diary not completed)
• 1 super combat potion (if going for long trips; otherwise, use the divine variant)
• Bracelet of slaughter
• Scorching bow
• Special attack weapon of your choice
• A staff to autocast Ancient Magicks (for long trips); Blood ancient sceptre provides the best effects, allowing the player to overheal up to 108 hitpoints at level 99.
• A quick-teleport for fast banking
• Teleport to house (tablet) or Construction cape for pool and fairy ring back. A Desert amulet 4 and a Quest point cape can also be used.

tactics.heading: Overview
tactics.text:
The Abyssal Sire is a level 350 Slayer boss that can only be killed when assigned Abyssal demons or the Sire itself with the required Slayer level of 85.

It is mainly killed for its unsired drops, which can be used at the Font of Consumption to obtain valuable rewards such as the abyssal dagger, parts of the abyssal bludgeon, or the abyssal orphan pet.

Note that while the Sire is a boss residing in a multicombat area, it can only be fought by one player at any given time. If the attacker does not fight the Sire in ~20 seconds from their last attack, another player may attack it.

tactics.heading: Requirements
tactics.text:
• 85 Slayer with an Abyssal demon slayer task
• Access to Fairy rings or partial completion of the Enter the Abyss miniquest to access the Abyssal Nexus

tactics.heading: Recommendations
tactics.text:
• High combat stats. Although not required, see the skill levels below for an indication of the advised stats:
• 90 Attack or higher
• 90 Strength or higher
• 90 Defence or higher
• 90 Ranged or higher
• 90 Hitpoints or higher
• 92 Magic or higher
• 70+ Prayer for Piety

tactics.heading: Transportation
tactics.text:
The Sire is located in the Abyssal Nexus, which can be easily accessed by fairy ring code DIP. Players without partial completion of Fairytale II - Cure a Queen will instead have to enter the Abyss via the Mage of Zamorak and go through the one-way passage on the south side. This requires running briefly through the Wilderness, Skulling, and will drain all of your prayer points so it is not recommended.

There are four Sires in each world, in the north-east, north-west, south-east and south-western areas of the Nexus. There are four eyes near the Font of Consumption; interacting with them will tell you if there is another player in that chamber.

tactics.heading: Respiratory systems, tentacles, and stunning
tactics.text:
During Phase 1 the player will need to kill all four respiratory systems. They are protected by six immobile tentacles which, when active, prevent almost all damage to the respiratory systems and attack nearby players for up to 30 damage (reduced slightly by Protect from Melee). Players will always hit at least 50% of their weapon's maximum hit on the respiratory systems, meaning all four can be taken down in 2 attacks each with a non-demonbane weapon that has a max hit of at least 50, assuming the player does not miss either attack. Demonbane weapons (other than holy water) will always destroy the respiratory systems in one hit regardless of the player's stats.

The Sire and its tentacles can be stunned for 30 seconds by one of the following methods, leaving the respiratory systems open to attack:
• Deal 75 damage to the Sire with ranged/magic
• Cast a Shadow spell on the Sire (effect applies even if it splashes):
  • Shadow Rush: 25% chance to stun
  • Shadow Burst: 50% chance to stun
  • Shadow Blitz: 75% chance to stun
  • Shadow Barrage: 100% chance to stun
The tentacles are inactive during Phase 2 but become active again in Phase 3.

The fastest way to handle Phase 1 is to attack the Sire with any ranged or magic weapon/spell that is not a shadow spell to wake it up, then manually cast Shadow Barrage on the Sire to stun it for 27 seconds. This allows you to begin attacking the 4 respiratory vents around the edge of the room instantly. While it is possible to initiate the fight by casting Shadow Barrage on an inactive Sire, the stun will not be applied for 10 game ticks after being cast (due to the Sire having to perform its waking up animation before the stun applies), meaning a player who does this may be attacked by the tentacles if they move in to kill the respiratory systems too fast.

tactics.heading: Standard attacks
tactics.text: During phase 2, the Sire uses three types of melee attacks; a swipe from its right arm, a flick from its right tendril, or a flick from both tendrils. These can hit moderately high, with the exception of the double flick attack, which can deal up to 66 damage. Using Protect from Melee will reduce the damage from these attacks to 6, 6 and 26 respectively.

tactics.heading: Miasma Pools
tactics.text:
In all phases of the fight (though it won't be used in Phase 1 if stunning correctly), the Sire can summon a pool of miasma under the player's position. The pool causes damage in a 3x3 area, dealing 10-30 poison damage per tick if on the central tile or 2-8 per tick on the outer tiles. This damage cannot be mitigated by any type of poison protection, and can also poison the player starting at 8 damage. There is enough time upon seeing the pool appear to avoid all damage by running 2 tiles away.

In Phases 1 and 2 the attack is indicated by the Sire clenching both its claws towards its stomach, along with a dark-green spiral energy appearing above it. There is no animation for the attack in Phase 3.

After the Sire explodes in Phase 3, it uses this attack a minimum of three more times then stops if all 15 minions are alive.

tactics.heading: Minions
tactics.text:
In all phases of the fight the Sire can create spawns. They randomly attack with ranged for up to 9 damage and melee for up to 4. They have 15 hitpoints and low accuracy.

The spawns in phase 1 and 2 are indicated with the spawn being thrown out of the Sire's mouth, after which they will land in a random tile in front of/around it (phase 1/2) before attacking the player.

If the spawn is not killed within 15 seconds, it will mature into a scion, which has 60 hitpoints and has higher accuracy. Spawns and scions attack randomly with ranged for up to 16 damage and melee for up to 10. They will close the gap for melee, but will not use ranged unless they decide to change styles. Because the ranged attacks are much more damaging and accurate than their melee attacks, it is highly recommended to keep Protect from Missiles on at all times, as numerous minions using ranged can quickly kill a player in seconds regardless of their defence bonuses. If they are unable to attack the player for ~35 or so seconds (including the morph into a scion), they will automatically die off in a manner similar to Zulrah's snakelings.

Demonbane attacks will always land as successful hits against them regardless of the player's bonuses, but will not guarantee a max hit.

When the Sire is killed, all scions and spawns will die alongside it.

tactics.heading: Forced Teleport and Explosion
tactics.text:
During Phase 2, if the player attempts to safespot the Sire, it will forcibly teleport them next to it before discharging a blast of energy from the portal in its stomach, dealing up to 60 damage if the player doesn't run away in time.

During Phase 3, when the Sire goes under 140 health, it will teleport the player next to itself and trigger a highly damaging explosion; the damage can be avoided by running directly away from the Sire as soon as the player is teleported.

tactics.heading: Strategy
tactics.text: Note: Make sure that Auto Retaliate is off when killing the Sire.

tactics.heading: Phase 1
tactics.text:
The Sire wakes up and begins the fight when attacked. If not stunned, it will summon miasma pools under the player and create spawns. The six tentacles will also awaken. These tentacles are static, but attack with typeless crush that can deal up to 30 damage, slightly reduced with Protect from Melee.

If the Sire is attacked by a player but that player stops attacking it for some reason, the Sire can be attacked by another player after ~20 or so seconds pass.

The player needs to kill all four respiratory systems to progress. However, with the Sire awake, the tentacles will protect the respiratory systems from attacks, and any attacks dealt to them while the boss is awake will be reduced to 0-3 damage regardless of the experience drop given.

In order to remove the protection provided by the tentacles, the Sire must be disoriented. This can be done in one of two ways; dealing 75 damage with ranged or magic (as the boss is not accessible with melee), or using a shadow spell against it. Shadow spells, if they successfully disorient the Sire, will do so for 30 seconds. The chance of this occurring is dependent on the tier of shadow spell; Shadow Rush has a 25% chance, Shadow Burst 50%, Shadow Blitz 75% and Shadow Barrage guarantees it. While casting a shadow spell on an inactive Sire will both wake it up and potentially stun it, the stun from this spell will not be applied for 10 game ticks after being cast. A shadow spell cast on an awoken Sire will be applied instantly.

When stunned, the respiratory systems should be killed with ranged or magic, depending on what the player prefers. Upon a successful hit, demonbane weapons and spells (other than holy water) will destroy them instantly regardless of the player's bonuses. It is highly recommended players bring a scorching bow and bronze arrows, since these are cheap and readily available, and the bow has high accuracy even when not bringing ranged armour switches.

If a non-demonbane weapon is used, the player will deal anywhere from 50%-100% of their maximum hit as damage. Bringing a weapon that has a max hit of 50 or higher will be sufficient enough to destroy the respiratory systems in two hits.

Within 30 seconds, the player will be easily able to destroy all of the respiratory systems in one cycle with demonbane. Without demonbane, it is possible to do so if they can be two hit; three hits will likely require a second stun. Despite the 30 second stun timer, it is actually 27 seconds, as the tentacles will awaken at this mark and immediately protect the systems.

Overall, the optimal strategy for this phase is as follows:
• Switch to your ranged or mage gear and attack the Sire with any ranged or magic weapon/spell that is not a shadow spell to wake it up.
• Cast Shadow Barrage on the Sire to stun it.
• Begin killing respiratory systems. Focus on killing the systems on either the east or west side, re-stun the Sire with Shadow Barrage if needed, then finish off the remaining systems.

Any damage dealt to the Sire during this phase will only count for the purposes of disorientation; if the Sire has taken any damage, it will be restored back to full health until the end of the phase.

After the last respiratory system is killed, head back to the centre and attack the Sire as soon as it steps out into the main arena (or in transit if range/mage). While damage is reduced by 50%, the amount of time the Sire takes to begin the next phase is usually significant enough to deal some damage. If the Sire somehow reaches 0 health before the next phase starts, it will begin the next phase with 40% of its health.

tactics.heading: Phase 2
tactics.text:
Stay on Row 1 during this phase, as attacking it from outside melee distance will cause the Sire to teleport you to itself and discharge a damaging blast of energy.

At this point, if the Sire is not in combat for ~1 minute, it will despawn, resetting the fight.

The Sire will use melee attacks that can hit up to 26 through prayer. Watch for miasma pools underneath the player; when they appear run to the other marked tile on Row 1. Ignore spawns unless killing the Sire at low levels with low DPS (in which case long kill times may make removing minions desirable). If reducing the Sire's defence, use one special attack now, otherwise save all special attack energy for phase 3.

Once the Sire is damaged below 50% of its health (212 health or less) it will start walking south. Run to Row 2 and activate Protect from Missiles. Advanced techniques can be used to pull the Sire south while attacking it, reducing the amount of time spent waiting for the Sire.

If the Sire reaches 0 health before the next phase starts, it will begin the next phase with 20% of its health.

tactics.heading: Stage I
tactics.text:
The Sire will latch onto the floor and summon four spawns to assist it in battle. This will occur before the pools appear. It will no longer attack with melee, but instead launch miasma pools as its "attacks". The tentacles will reawaken, limiting the amount of space allowed to attack the boss.

Once the Sire is damaged below 35% of its health (around 143 or so health), it will teleport the player, beginning the final stage. In the event of multi-hit weapons triggering the transition (e.g scythe of Vitur dealing 66 damage (over 3 hits such as a 44-21-3)) against a Sire with 150 health, the first hit would trigger the transition, while the remaining two hits will apply once the second stage starts.

tactics.heading: Stage II
tactics.text:
The Sire teleports the player to the western tile of Row 2. Two ticks later it explodes, dealing up to 96 damage if the player is within the blast radius. This damage can be recoiled with Vengeance, but this requires either a spellbook switch beforehand via Magic cape, Spellbook Swap, or a second player to assist with Vengeance Other and Heal Other. As soon as the teleport occurs, spam-click on Row 3 to avoid the attack. Then return to melee distance to finish the fight.

After the explosion the Sire creates a huge number of spawns, after which the remainder will spawn either underneath or around the boss. It will use its miasma pool attack a minimum of three more times, then stop as long as 15 minions are left alive. This means you should not kill any minions, but should run back and forth on Row 2 while attacking until it has made three miasma pools, after which it is safe to stop moving. Use any remaining specs and watch your health, as the scions can do a lot of damage. If the player's health drops below 40, they should run away for a brief respite.

It is possible to safespot the minions and heal off them with Blood Burst/Blood Barrage; their low magic defence should ensure all spells hit. This is primarily done for players with lower stats or are doing prolonged trips at the boss, as it is uncommon for a player with good gear to take unusually higher damage or take longer.

When the Sire is killed, all minions will die alongside it. If they were tagged by the player, this will activate Death Charge, maintaining special attack energy at all times but can make trips slower due to the lack of ancients for the first phase.

Attacks made by minions before the Sire dies (including those that spawn on the same tick as its death) will roll as normal, meaning a player can potentially die after the Sire does; although somewhat unlikely, it is possible and players with lower combat stats should be aware of this.

options.text: Seeking dragon arrow / Diamond dragon bolts (e) / Moonlight antler bolts
Seeking amethyst arrow / Diamond bolts (e) / Sunlight antler bolts
Dragon arrow / Runite bolts / Amethyst broad bolts
Seeking rune arrow / Broad bolts / Adamant bolts
Zaryte crossbow > Armadyl crossbow > Dragon crossbow
Harmonised Nightmare staff / Dragon hunter wand / Eye of Ayak
Mystic smoke staff > Twinflame staff / Ahrim's staff
Ancient wyvern shield / Tome of Earth

gearNotes.heading: Equipment
gearNotes.text: With base 90 Melee stats and a Ghrazi rapier, dragon hunter lance, or an Osmumten's fang using melee against adamant dragons is a reliable option. With worse weapons, magic or ranged may be more effective. Adamant dragons have accurate and strong attacks, so Bandos, Justiciar or Barrows equipment is recommended along with Protect from Magic and Piety in tandem to reduce damage taken. Also, Vengeance can be used for dealing with their Blood Forfeit Ranged attacks. A dwarf multicannon may also be used here with significant accuracy.

gearNotes.heading: Inventory
gearNotes.text:
• Digsite pendant or a mounted one in POH with house tabs
• Special attack weapon choice
• 1 divine super combat potion, super combat potion or super set
• 1 extended antifire, or extended super antifire if using a shield without dragonfire protection
• 3-4 prayer potions
• 1-2 antidote++, antidote+, superantipoison or antipoison if not using a serpentine helm
• Rune pouch with runes to cast Vengeance or High Level Alchemy (set warning value to 162,000) (optional)
• One-click teleport (optional)
• Food (sharks / manta rays / anglerfish / karambwan)
• Bracelet of slaughter (optional, if on task)
• Dwarf multicannon
• steel cannonball (optional, about 400 used per hour)

With level 90 Ranged and a dragon hunter crossbow (DHCB), adamant dragons can easily be killed due to the crossbow's passive effect, as well as circumventing their melee attack. A Twisted Bow provides comparable damage to a DHCB if not slightly more depending on luck. Armadyl or Karil's equipment is recommended along with Protect from Missiles and Rigour or Eagle Eye in tandem. Also, Vengeance could be used for dealing with their Blood Forfeit Ranged attacks. A dwarf multicannon may be used here with significant accuracy.

gearNotes.heading: Inventory
gearNotes.text:
• Digsite pendant or a mounted one in POH with house tabs
• 1 divine ranging potion or ranging potion
• 1 extended antifire, or extended super antifire if using a shield without dragonfire protection
• 3-4 prayer potions
• 1-2 antidote++, antidote+, superantipoison or antipoison if not using a serpentine helm

• Food (sharks / manta rays / anglerfish / karambwan)
• Bracelet of slaughter (optional, if on task)
• dwarf multicannon (optional)
• steel cannonball (optional, about 400 cannonballs used per hour)

Tumeken's shadow's high accuracy and damage from its passive effect makes it one of the fastest options for killing adamant dragons, provided the player has enough damage-boosting magic equipment such as an occult necklace and ancestral robes. If not on a slayer task, this makes it even faster than using dragonbane weaponry.

gearNotes.heading: Inventory
gearNotes.text:
To maximize inventory space for food to increase trip length, you should pre-pot a dose of antidote++ and an anglerfish, and use a max cape, Construction cape, or house tabs to teleport to your POH to use your mounted digsite pendant. When fighting, stay out of melee distance and use Protect from Missiles and (optional) Augury. If not using Augury, fewer prayer potions are needed.

• Saturated heart

While not as effective as using Tumeken's shadow, due to adamant dragons' elemental weakness and relatively low Magic defence, Earth spells can be a viable alternative, especially when used with a dragon hunter wand and/or while on a slayer task.

tactics.heading: Overview
tactics.text: After completion of Dragon Slayer II, adamant dragons can be found and fought in the Lithkren Vault. As the second strongest metal dragons, caution should be exercised at all times.

tactics.heading: Attacks
tactics.text:
Similar to their mithril and rune counterparts, adamant dragons use standard dragonfire and attack from all sides of the combat triangle. They also have two unique special attacks:

• Poison projectile: A green, slow-moving projectile that lands on the player's position and splits into two more projectiles on impact, each targeting a tile adjacent to the initial landing tile. Each projectile deals 14-25 poison damage in a 3x3 area around the targeted tile. This can be reduced to 4-8 damage by being under the effect of any poison protection. Alternatively, players may avoid this attack entirely by moving at least three squares away from their original position when the attack was launched.

• Blood Forfeit: A ranged attack that hits through Protect from Missiles and, mimicking the Blood Forfeit effect from enchanted ruby bolts, sacrifices 10% of the dragon's current hitpoints to deal damage equal to 20% of the player's current hitpoints. It is recommended to keep the player's hitpoints around 40-50 to minimise the damage taken from this attack.

tactics.heading: Transportation
tactics.text: The fastest way to get to adamant dragons is by using a digsite pendant to teleport Lithkren Vault directly. Alternatively, players can take the boat by Jardric, found to the north-west of Fossil Island, to Lithkren, and navigate the ruins there to reach the vault.

tactics.text:
• 90+ Attack
• 90+ Strength
• 90+ Defence
• 94+ Magic (optional)
• 90+ Ranged
• 70+ Prayer

gearNotes.heading: Equipment
gearNotes.text:
The Alchemical Hydra has a Defence level of 100. It is weakest to ranged attacks, possessing +45 global ranged resistance.

As it is considered draconic, Dragonbane weapons are effective against it. If using melee, use a dragon hunter lance on stab. The Hydra's stab defence is slightly higher than its ranged but still provides acceptable accuracy due to its lower Defence level. Magic is not recommended due to its Magic level of 260.

Prayer bonus is prioritised over ranged accuracy because of the boss's relatively low defensive stats and the minimal damage taken when dealing with the mechanics correctly. Alternatively, players may use gear that maximizes ranged accuracy if they are confident with prayer flicking, as it greatly reduces the need for prayer potions. With sufficient experience, barely any damage should be taken most kills; the only unavoidable damage players may take is the first hit at the start of kill, and self-inflicted damage from Divine potions or the special attack of Ruby bolts (e).

gearNotes.heading: Inventory
gearNotes.text:
• About 4–20 prayer potions or super restores.
  • More prayer potions allows for longer trips at the cost of not being able to bank hydra bones; however, banking the bones will lower overall kill rates due to time spent running to and from a bank, and is not recommended without Rada's blessing 4.
• About 4-10 food, preferrably Cooked moonlight antelope.
  • As the player becomes more proficient at fighting this boss, they should take very little damage per kill, so excess food can be replaced with more prayer potions if doing long trips.
• Antidote++ if not bringing cooked moonlight antelope.
• Divine ranging potion, ranging potion, or bastion potion (the latter is largely superfluous, as all damage taken in the fight can be mitigated with prayer and good positioning once the player is experienced enough)
• House tablets or rings of dueling to restore stats and bank
• Rada's blessing 4 for fast teleport back, if using a bow of Faerdhinen or toxic blowpipe.
• Zaryte crossbow with ruby dragon bolts (e) is best used for its special attack during the flame phase to maximise the chance of skipping its flame wall attack. Particularly powerful when combined with the Lightbearer.
• Toxic blowpipe for healing special attack if using a twisted bow or bow of Faerdhinen
• Divine rune pouch with runes for High Level Alchemy and Teleport to house (or two open slots for rune drops if using tabs/ring of dueling)
• (Optional) Bracelet of slaughter to extend the task
• (Optional) Bonecrusher or bonecrusher necklace to auto-bury hydra bones. Bonecrusher necklace can also be equipped during boss death animation to restore an extra 8 prayer points per kill.
• (Optional) Noxious halberd can be used to cure poison as necessary at the cost of 50% special attack energy.

• Strength bonus is preferred over prayer bonus for melee.
• Melee setups often provide similar damage output to range setups, especially when a good special attack weapon is available, and typically have lower to no upkeep cost for weapons and armour.
• When meleeing Hydra, effectively luring it over the vents without missing attacks can be more complex than using a range setup.
• Despite having low defence, the Hydra has enough health that a small improvement in DPS from defence reduction adds up greatly over the course of the fight.
• On average, unless the ultor ring adds a max hit of 5 to a dragon hunter lance, lightbearer and a strong spec weapon will result in faster kill times.
• Damaging special attacks should be used during the flame phase to maximise the chance of phasing him before the flame wall attacks, except for when using burning claws, as this phase specifically is immune to burn damage.
• Learning to skip the flame phase will significantly speed up kill times and reduce the chance to take damage during the phase.

gearNotes.text:

• Fill your inventory with the rest high healing food, such as manta rays or cooked moonlight antelope. The latter negates the need for bringing antipoison, as it will cure poison after being eaten, and its healing delay should not be an issue for skilled players. As you gain more experience, less or no food is necessary.

• (Optional) Bracelet of slaughter to extend the task
• (Optional) Noxious halberd can be used to cure poison as necessary at the cost of 50% special attack energy.

gearNotes.text:

If less experienced with the boss, bring a few pieces of high healing food such as manta ray or cooked moonlight antelope. As you gain more experience, less or no food is necessary, especially if bringing saradomin godsword or amulet of blood fury.
• Holy wrench or prayer cape/max cape to increase prayer restored from potions.

tactics.heading: Overview
tactics.text:
The Alchemical Hydra is a level 95 Slayer boss encountered in the Karuulm Slayer Dungeon. In order to fight it, players must be assigned a Hydra task.

To reach the boss, players must run north past the Tasakaal, then east past the Hydras. They will then reach the entrance to the lair by Orrvor quo Maten. Alternatively, players with level 88 Agility can reach it safely by using the mysterious pipe just behind Kaal-Ket-Jor.

tactics.heading: Fight overview
tactics.text:
The fight is instanced; if players die while fighting the Hydra, then they may reclaim their items from Orrvor quo Maten outside for 100,000 coins each time. Dying elsewhere with items still held by him will result in them being lost forever.

While the Hydra is in the room, players cannot leave through the doors, as they are jammed when this occurs. Teleports will still work, however. The Hydra has a respawn time of 20 seconds.

The Hydra has four phases, each one beginning upon each 25% health threshold (~275 health). A head will fall off each time this occurs, as the Hydra roars and changes colour. At the start of each phase, the Hydra will perform three auto-attacks before performing a special attack.

The Hydra attacks with both Magic and Ranged. The Hydra will begin the fight with either combat style. For the first three phases, after every three basic attacks, the Hydra will sway its heads backwards as an indicator that it is changing combat styles.

During the first three phases, the Hydra reduces incoming damage by 75% until it is lured over and sprayed by the appropriate chemical vent. The Hydra will when hit by the correct vent. If Hydra is sprayed by an incorrect vent, the damage of its attacks increase, although protection prayers continue to block all damage regardless.

In the final phase, the Hydra attacks alternately with Magic and Ranged, choosing to start with the opposite of what it attacked with last. On the fourth attack, the Hydra instead throws poison splatters as in the first phase.

tactics.heading: Poison
tactics.text:
In this phase, the Hydra starts with a green carapace, and should be lured to the red chemical pool. After the first kill, the player should stand right next to the red chemical vat (to the east) so that the Hydra is automatically lured to the red chemical pool as soon as it spawns.

After the first three attacks, the Hydra will launch damaging poison blobs on and around the player's location which form poison pools on the ground, damaging the player in several ways:
• The blobs have a 3x3 splatter effect dealing up to 7 damage as thrown
• Standing on the poison pools will deal up to 12 poison damage per tick
• If damaged by the targetted blob, the player is poisoned for 6 damage, and otherwise poisoned for 4 damage

The best way to avoid this attack is by running north on the Hydra's fourth attack.

Once the Hydra reaches 75% of its health, the bottom-right head falls off and it changes its carapace to blue.

tactics.heading: Lightning
tactics.text:
Now with a blue carapace, the Hydra should be lured to the green chemical pool.

Throughout the phase, the Hydra will launch an electric ball in the centre of the room, which spawns four lightning currents in the four corners of the chamber, converging on the player's location. Getting hit by them will bind the player and deal up to 22 damage.

The easiest way to avoid their damage is by running west along the northern wall as the lightning approaches. It is also possible to trap the lightning by standing in the north-west corner, moving one tile diagonally south-east when the lightning is two tiles away from you, and instantly moving one tile north. This does not despawn the lightning, so if the player were to move off of the tile, the lightning will start following them again.

Once the Hydra reaches 50% of its health, the bottom-left head falls off and it changes its carapace to red.

Note: If the Hydra transitions to the next phase while there is lightning on the field, they will dissipate immediately.

tactics.heading: Flame
tactics.text:
Now with a red carapace, the Hydra should be lured to the blue chemical pool.

Throughout the phase, the Hydra will occasionally walk to the centre of the chamber and face the direction the player is at. Once it reaches the centre, it will inflict a stun on the player, but they can still attack it. If the player is underneath the Hydra, then it forces them out into a random direction. Upon reaching the centre, it breathes 5x5 layer of fire to the player's sides based on their location before staring down the middle and launching a tracking fire.

This tracking fire follows the player's movement, and travels significantly faster the further the player is (or if they start running). Turning off run and walking in a line as the fire trails is the best course of action. Getting hit by any of the fires will result in the player taking up to 25 damage, followed by a subsequent burn of 5 damage for 5 hits. The Hydra will not attack for roughly seven ticks after the tracking fire is launched.

Similarly to the lightning trap in the previous phase, the flames can be trapped in by standing on a specific tile adjacent to the green vents, seen in the demonstration to the right. This is mostly for melee players, since range can still attack over the fires without being dragged into one.

Once the Hydra reaches 25% of its health, the middle head falls off and it changes its carapace to grey.

Note: If the Hydra transitions to the next phase while performing this attack, it ends abruptly. This also includes the tracking fire, but any fires started before the phase transition will still persist as usual. For the duration of the side fires, the Hydra also becomes a solid NPC, meaning that it is not possible to walk under it.

tactics.heading: Enraged
tactics.text:
Now with a grey carapace, the Hydra no longer needs to be lured to any chemical pools for this phase, as its damage reduction ability does not reset. During this phase, the Hydra's attack speed will increase to every four ticks, and its enrage stack will increase to max, allowing it to deal up to 55 damage per hit.

The Hydra starts off this phase with the combat style opposite of what it used in the previous phase; if it attacked with magic, then it will start the phase with ranged. If the Hydra attacked with magic and changes to ranged as it transitions phases, it will still start with ranged attacks. These attacks will alternate after every single hit; e.g one magic attack is followed by a ranged attack and repeats. Continue to switch prayers with each basic attack for the remainder of the fight. The player can safely switch to the next prayer as soon as the Hydra starts its attack animation for the current attack.

After the first three auto-attacks, the Hydra will use the poison attack from phase 1, and will continue to use it after every nine subsequent auto-attacks. Unlike the first phase, there is a possibility of one poison blob being launched rather than five. This is mostly guaranteed if any fires from the previous phase are present.

If the Hydra is killed while queuing up an auto-attack, it will still be launched but deal no damage. Poison blobs will still deal damage and need to be avoided as these will fade as normal.

Players may choose to bring a bracelet of slaughter to extend their slayer tasks, and sometimes bring it as a switch so that gloves with offensive stats can be worn for the majority of the kill. If going with this option, remember to switch to the bracelet sometime during this final phase. It can be convenient to switch to the bracelet while dodging the poison special, as prayer does not have to be changed during this attack, though optimally the offensive gloves should be worn as long as possible.

gearNotes.heading: Equipment
gearNotes.text:
The boss has -2 flat armour and is weak to crush, so it is recommended to use a crush weapon that deals damage with multiple hitsplats such as the scythe of Vitur, dual macuahuitl, or glacial temotli. However, Torag's hammers are not recommended, as their slower attack speed means that they perform worse than a dragon mace and dragon defender, assuming all other gear is equivalent.

Given the relatively low defence of the boss, strength bonus should be prioritised.

Although the boss has a 30% elemental weakness to fire, it is better to take melee as the unstable ice can only take damage from melee sources. This means taking thralls is recommended.

tactics.heading: Overview
tactics.text: After completion of The Heart of Darkness, players can fight Amoxliatl as a regular boss encounter within the Ruins of Tapoyauik, albeit slightly stronger than when fought during the quest.

tactics.heading: Recommendations
tactics.text:
• Level 60 Attack or higher
• Level 60 Strength or higher
• Level 60 Defence or higher
• Level 60 Hitpoints or higher
• Level 37 Prayer for Protect from Magic
• Level 85 Hunter or higher if wishing to barehand moonlight moths for Prayer restoration (75 with an equipped butterfly net)

tactics.heading: Transportation
tactics.text:
The two easiest ways to reach the Ruins of Tapoyauik include:
• Pendant of Ates - Teleport to the Twilight Temple statue outside the Tower of Ascension after activating it.
• Quetzal Transport System - Travel to the Salvager Overlook and head south-east towards the Twilight Temple (after building landing site) or travel to Quetzacalli Gorge and pass the large gate.

By returning to the chamber with the statues and murals within Tapoyauik, players can use the lift platform in the centre (which appears after completion of the quest) to ascend to the Tower of Ascension. This unlocks a permanent shortcut which allows quick access to Amoxliatl.

tactics.heading: Fight overview
tactics.text:
Amoxliatl uses three different attacks. Her standard magic attack summons ice spikes on the player's current tile and around the arena. Protect from Magic will protect against the initial attack, but the ice spikes additionally deal typeless damage. Finally, an icy pool will be left on the tile where the player was originally standing on that will deal 6-10 damage per tick.

After every 2-4 standard attacks, Amoxliatl will use one of two special attacks. Her initial choice is random, but she will alternate between the two afterwards. The only exception is if the player is standing in the 3-tile wide pathway leading up to her main platform when she chooses her next special attack. If so, Amoxilatl will not have space to use Unstable Ice and will exclusively use Icicle Crash.
• Unstable Ice - 1-4 blocks of unstable ice are launched near the player, indicated by the game message . If not destroyed within 15 ticks (9 seconds), all remaining ice blocks will shatter, causing icy pools to form within 3x3 of where they were, and healing the boss (16-25) for each block shattered. The unstable ice blocks can only be destroyed with melee, and melee attacks against them will result in a max hit with an attack speed of 1. After destroying an ice block, the player may eat a piece of food without incurring the normal attack delay, should they need to heal.
  • It is possible to hit Amoxliatl and unstable ice with the same swing of a Scythe of Vitur, capitalising on the increased attack speed to do extra damage to the boss while also not incurring additional delay for the first regular attack after the final ice block is destroyed.
• Icicle Crash: Amoxliatl will first disable all the player's active prayers before launching an icicle attack directly toward the player, dealing up to 34 damage (which can be negated by reactivating Protect from Magic). This attack is indicated by the game message

A good tip for the fight is to run to any two tiles from wherever they are standing after Amoxliatl begins her standard attack to drag her forward, then attack her again to stand on a new non-icy tile. Players comfortable dodging ice spikes in confined spaces may also choose to drag Amoxilatl to the pathway leading to her main platform so she can only use her Icicle Crash special attack: this may speed up kills slightly by reducing the time spent destroying Unstable Ice blocks.

After the fight, players can leave the boss room and refill their prayer points by catching moonlight moths just outside, with the required hunter level. Doing so can reduce supplies used and frequency of banking by taking the place of prayer-restoring items such as prayer potions.

gearNotes.heading: Equipment
gearNotes.text:
This is the recommended equipment when using the slash special effect to lower the Aquanite's stab Defence.

The Saradomin godsword or Dragon claws special attack can be used to sever the Aquanite's lure.
The Voidwaker's special attack does not sever the lure due to being a Magic-based attack, but it still deals high damage. The Voidwaker can still sever the lure with its regular slash attack, saving an inventory slot by not requiring a second slash weapon.

An Abyssal whip or Scimitar is recommended when you do not have enough special attack energy to use the Saradomin godsword or Dragon claws.

Seed box may be useful, as Aquanites drop a variety of seeds.
Rune pouch or Divine rune pouch is recommended, along with the required Runes to cast High Level Alchemy.

tactics.heading: Overview
tactics.text: Aquanites are monsters found exclusively in Ynysdail Cavern, unlocked via the Sailing skill.

tactics.heading: Requirements
tactics.text:
• Level 78 Slayer and Level 73 Sailing
• Boat requirements Adamant keel or better.

tactics.heading: Recommended skills
tactics.text:
• When killing Aquanites with Ranged, the following skill levels are recommended:
  • 80+ Ranged
  • 63 Prayer for Deadeye or 74 for Rigour

• When killing Aquanites with Melee, the following skill levels are recommended:
  • 80+ Attack
  • 80+ Strength
  • 70 Prayer for Piety

tactics.heading: First-time access
tactics.text:
The first time traveling to Ynysdail, you must sail there manually. This requires:
• 73 Sailing
• Your boat must be equipped with an Adamant keel or better

tactics.heading: Rowboat
tactics.text:
With 70 Construction, players can build a rowboat on Ynysdail.
This requires the following materials:

After building the rowboat, players can travel freely between Ynysdail and Gwenith.

tactics.heading: Strategy
tactics.text:
Aquanites can be killed normally; however, to receive them as a Slayer task, players must first unlock them for 80 Slayer reward points. They may be assigned by Nieve, Duradel, and Mortimer. Aquanites are found in a single-way combat area, and a Dwarf multicannon cannot be used as the ground is too damp to place one.

Aquanites attack with Magic and have high accuracy, so using Protect from Magic is highly recommended.

When killing Aquanites with melee, slash attacks have a special effect: if an Aquanite is hit with a slash attack, its lure will be severed and its stab Defence will be reduced by 50 (from 60 to 10). This significantly improves the accuracy of subsequent stab attacks and is especially useful for players with lower Attack levels.

Because dealing damage is not required to sever the lure, a fast 4-tick slash weapon such as a Scimitar or Abyssal whip is recommended. The Saradomin godsword Special attack provides an efficient option to sever the lure while also restoring Prayer points.

tactics.heading: Overview
tactics.text:
Aquanites are Slayer monsters found in the Ynysdail Cavern beneath Ynysdail. They require level 78 Slayer to fight, and accessing Ynysdail itself requires 73 Sailing and a boat equipped with an adamant keel or better.

Aquanites can be killed normally and Mortimer can assign them as a Slayer task by default; however, to receive them as a Slayer task from Nieve or Duradel, players must first unlock them for 80 Slayer reward points. A task extension is also available for 100 points.
Aquanites can drop the unique Aquanite tendon, used to make the Aquanite hopper.

Accessing Ynysdail requires the player to enter the crystalline maze from the outside, or build the rowboat hotspot on the island. This rowboat, once built, will generate another one north of Gwenith. Using this rowboat requires completion of Song of the Elves. It is recommended to complete the quest to avoid having to set the ship back to a mooring point if a greater teleport focus is not on it.

While on an Aquanite slayer task, there is a 1/200 chance (1/150 with completion of the elite tier of Combat Achievements) for an Elder Aquanite to spawn after killing an Aquanite, provided the player has the Bigger and Badder unlock. Elder Aquanites have a special attack that will deal 50 damage if Protect from Magic has been active for some time, so flicking the prayer on and off between the enemy's attacks is required to avoid taking damage.

Aquanites attack with Magic and have high accuracy, so using Protect from Magic is highly recommended. Alternatively, they can be safespotted with a 9 or 10 tile attack range. They are located in a single-way combat area, and a Dwarf multicannon cannot be used as the ground is too damp to place one.

When hit with a slash attack, an Aquanite’s lure will be severed, reducing its stab Defence by 50 (from 60 to 10). This greatly improves the accuracy of subsequent stab attacks and is especially helpful for players with lower Attack levels. Because dealing damage is not required to sever the lure, a fast 4-tick slash weapon such as a Scimitar or Abyssal whip is recommended. The Saradomin godsword's special attack can also be used if no other special attack weapons are brought along. Alternatively, a weapon that has both attack styles may be used, such as the Ghrazi rapier, while swapping between slash and stab styles.

tactics.heading: Recommended skills

  • 80+ Ranged
  • 63 Prayer for Deadeye or 74 for Rigour

• When killing Aquanites with Melee, the following skill levels are recommended:

  • 80+ Strength
  • 70 Prayer for Piety

70 Construction is needed to construct the rowboat.

The twisted bow with Masori offers DPS better than the abyssal bludgeon and lower tier melee weapons, but is significantly outclassed by the scythe of Vitur.

tactics.heading: Overview
tactics.text:
Araxxor is a level 92 Slayer boss found in the Morytania Spider Cave. In order to fight him, completion of Priest in Peril to access Morytania is required, as well as having been assigned an Araxyte or spider Slayer task.

If the player dies while fighting Araxxor, their grave will be placed outside the entrance to his lair, which follows normal death rules.

tactics.heading: Recommendations
tactics.text:
• High melee combat stats
  • Level 85 Attack or higher
  • Level 85 Strength or higher
  • Level 70 Defence or higher
  • Level 85 Hitpoints or higher
  • Level 70 Prayer or higher for access to Piety
• A way to cure or protect from venom
• Completion of Sins of the Father for access to Darkmeyer

tactics.heading: Transportation
tactics.text:
The quickest methods of reaching the cave entrance are as follows:
• Teleporting directly to the cave via use of a spider cave teleport
• Teleporting to Hallowed Sepulchre using a hallowed crystal shard, then exiting and using the wall shortcut just south-east. Requires completion of Sins of the Father, level 63 Agility, and installing 2 long ropes.
• Teleporting via ectophial or to fairy ring code ALQ, then running south past the small bridge.

tactics.heading: Fight overview
tactics.text:
As with all araxytes, Araxxor's attacks can inflict venom, and as with most spiders, is weak to crush. He has a Defence level of 135, with his lowest defence bonus being crush at +15. His Defence level can be only drained by up to 45 levels, therefore one elder maul special attack will suffice. Alternatively, a dragon warhammer special attack is nearly as effective, draining 40 Defence levels. Though Araxxor has an elemental weakness to fire spells, his high magical defences makes this trait mostly thematic, and the generally lower defences of magic robes will have the player take more damage overall.

Araxxor spawns in the middle of his chamber and attacks with melee; if out of his melee range, he will close the distance and attack with either magic or ranged - whichever of the player's defensive rolls is lower. Araxxor is capable of attacking diagonally, in which case he will use melee. The melee attack can deal up to 38 damage, and using Protect from Melee will significantly reduce the damage up to a max of 5. The ranged attacks can deal up to 34 damage, with Protect from Missiles reduces the damage by ~45%, with a max hit of 18. A successful ranged attack will additionally drain 9% of the player's Defence level. The magic attacks deal up to 21 damage, with Protect from Magic reducing the damage by ~50%. A successful magic attack additionally drains 9% of the player's Prayer. These attacks are calculated upon start and late reactions will not mitigate damage.

As the attack style used is dependent on the player's defence rolls, prayers such as Rigour might change which style the boss uses. Aranea boots can be used to block Araxxor's ranged attack once every 8 ticks (4.8 seconds), but not his magic attacks. Players with high magic defence armour can take advantage of this negation effect by moving out of the melee range every second attack; forcing a ranged attack. The high magic defences are easiest to achieve whilst ranging and using high end ranged gear such as fortified masori.

Around Araxxor's lair, there are nine eggs; three each of red, white, and green. The first egg hatches after three standard attacks from Araxxor, hatching clockwise starting from the south-easternmost egg, with subsequent eggs hatching after every six standard attacks.

The eggs will always follow one of three potential patterns, with the last two sets copying that of the first:
• Green > White > Red
• White > Red > Green
• Red > Green > White

Players can opt to destroy the eggs, which have 65 Hitpoints. If an egg has been fully destroyed, Araxxor will simply spawn an araxyte from the next egg in the rotation, skipping over the destroyed egg. Any damage dealt to an egg without destroying it will carry over to the hatched araxyte, however if an egg has taken more damage than the araxyte that would have hatched from it (58 Hitpoints), then the egg will simply despawn, and Araxxor will use another six standard attacks before the next egg in sequence hatches.

Players will always max hit when attacking the hatched araxytes with a noxious halberd, crush weapons, or heavy Ranged weapon (such as a crossbow or ballista) if crush or ranged is their highest accuracy style respectively. Attacking the hatched eggs with anything else - or attacking the unhatched eggs - does not guarantee a max hit, and rolls damage normally. Both the eggs and the araxytes count as on-task monsters for the purposes of benefiting from the slayer helmet's damage bonus, but will not reduce the player's task kill count.

Every six standard attacks, Araxxor will use the same one of three possible special attacks for the remainder of the fight, which can be quickly determined by identifying the south-easternmost egg. All of these attacks leave acid pools, which inflict venom and deal increasingly larger damage (starting from 4) the longer the player stays on them.

It is always best to lure the red araxytes so they explode underneath Araxxor for the extra damage; while optional, it is generally recommended to lure them to white eggs if the player does not wish to directly attack them to avoid wasting time preparing to kill the white araxytes.

If attacking the white araxytes directly, they can be one-hit with a crush weapon while under the effects of vengeance, and also with the same methods as all araxytes, listed below. Alternatively, a noxious halberd will one-hit them which saves a lot more time on average than having to weaken the eggs.

tactics.heading: Enrage phase
tactics.text:
When Araxxor falls below 255 health, he will enter an enrage phase. This is signified with a distinct screeching sound, along with Araxxor coating his two front legs with venom. This will additionally increase his Defence level by 35, Magic by 28 and Ranged by 31; drained stats will carry over to enrage. Alongside the increased stats, Araxxor's attack speed is increased from 6 (3.6 seconds) to 4 (2.4 seconds).

For the remainder of the fight, Araxxor will replace his melee attack with a cleave attack that has an attack range of 2, although he will still try to close the gap. Magic or ranged attacks will be used if the player is more than two tiles away from him. The cleave attack targets a 1x3 area around the player's location, dealing melee damage and leaving acid pools on the ground. If the player is standing underneath or diagonally across from Araxxor, the positioning of the pools will be different. Standing underneath Araxxor as he uses the cleave attack will result in a single poison pool (although the AoE of the cleave is still maintained), while standing diagonally across Araxxor results in pools being left appropriately across him (e.g if attacking while facing south-west the pool will appear both north and east of the player).

The player can dodge the cleave attack by moving outside the targeted area immediately when Araxxor shouts . If the player fails to dodge the cleave attack. they can be hit for up to ~38 damage, with Protect from Melee reducing the damage by ~66%. Aranea boots can be worn to protect the player from the cleave attack up to once every 20 ticks (12 seconds) - as well as from Araxxor's ranged attack - although they will not negate the poison damage from the acid pools left behind.

A way to finish the enrage phase slightly quicker is to bait Araxxor into attacking the tiles he occupies, which results in him damaging himself for 8-12 damage. To perform this method:
• When enrage phase starts, move two tiles into him.
• When Araxxor shouts , click on him to attack. You will move two tiles away to attack.
• For the rest of the kill, repeat the following: when Araxxor's cleave animation shows his front two legs stabbing forward, click to move to a tile without acid, then immediately click him to attack.
• Optionally, stepping 1 tile back immediately after attacking allows the player to walk Araxxor and use a new tile each attack to avoid the acid pool damage - it is recommended to use a 4-tick weapon if doing this.
  • While one acid pool is visually left behind, the attack still has 1x3 AoE.

If players find themselves unable to perform the step-under technique, they can dodge by moving either two tiles to the side or one tile backwards when he shouts . Note that if moving backwards, wait an additional tick before attacking or you will be dragged onto the new acid tiles.

Players who've decided to opt out of killing the acidic araxytes and who feel confident in always avoiding the enrage phase melee attack can instead change their overhead prayer to Protect from Missiles in order to completely negate the araxytes' ranged attacks for the remainder of the fight.

After the fight is finished, Araxxor will not respawn just yet, and players can use this time to recover. When ready, the player must either choose to harvest or destroy the boss's corpse. Harvesting will yield normal rewards, while destroying forfeits all rewards, except elite clue scrolls, for a doubled rate of the pet. The player will not be able to preview loot before destroying the corpse. Unless the player is killing Araxxor with the sole purpose of obtaining the pet, it is generally ill-advised to destroy the corpse as this may result in the loss of an araxyte fang or noxious halberd pieces, which are incredibly valuable and make up the majority of the boss's profit. Araxxor will respawn shortly after either decision is made.

If harvesting the boss, players should be mindful of supply drops, as Araxxor can potentially drop up to six items at once; an araxyte venom sac or a 1-dose super combat potion, one or two 3-dose prayer potions or a 4-dose prayer potion, along with 2-3 sharks or wild pies. If the player's inventory is full due to having no space after looting, excess rewards will be dropped to the floor. These last for three hours like player-dropped items do.

gearNotes.heading: Setups
gearNotes.text:
Note: As Artio is in the Wilderness in an area that is active with PKers, ensure valuables are kept protected, and check items screens for kept on death equipment—you may lose untradeables here if trouver parchment is not used on them. The best way is to not take anything into the Wilderness you are not willing to lose. The PK skull prevention option is highly recommended for added security.

Artio can deal incredibly high melee damage through prayer, so melee combat is not advised. She is not immune to magic damage, so binding her in place is strongly recommended. Ice spells, such as Ice Barrage or Ice Blitz, are commonly used. They are also guaranteed to hit Artio while she is not frozen, if the player has 0 or higher magic accuracy bonus. Players can use either ranged or magic after freezing the boss. One method involves using Protect from Melee and healing with Bloodbark armour and Blood Barrage. Players with high Magic and Defence levels will find they are able to heal more with Blood Barrage than Artio can damage them with melee, making this a very low-effort method, only requiring occasional eating and prayer restoration.
Webweaver is the strongest weapon against Artio. Ideally you want to maximize range damage, while keeping your magic attack bonus at 0 or higher to allow for guaranteed freezes on Artio. Gear like bloodbark boots, barrows gloves, imbued god capes, god books and ring of shadows are good to keep your magic bonus high enough, without sacrificing much range dps or incurring high risk. Defence bonus -- particularly magic defence -- is also beneficial for tanking PKers.

gearNotes.heading: Equipment
gearNotes.text: Note: Ensure items are protected. Do not take anything into the Wilderness you are not willing to lose. The PK skull prevention option is highly recommended for added security.

gearNotes.heading: Inventory
gearNotes.text:
If the player is 93 or higher hitpoints, blighted anglerfish are superior, cheaper, and have higher utility than the alternative manta rays. Therefore they should be used for higher levelled players. The player can also switch out a protected item for Dinh's bulwark if looking for added survivability.

• Looting bag
• Stamina potion (for running)
• Divine ranging potion
• Anti-venom+ in case of venom from PKers
• Some blighted super restores
• Some blighted ancient ice sacks or blighted entangle sacks to freeze Artio.
• A royal seed pod to teleport at level 30 Wilderness (if you choose not to wear amulet of glory)
• Rest of inventory spaces to be filled with food (you may want to leave 2-3 slots empty for picking up items)

Artio is significantly vulnerable to Magic. However, compared to Ranged, a Magic setup typically results in lesser defences which leaves the player more vulnerable to PKers.

It can be difficult to survive PKers if using magic equipment. Therefore, swapping out a protected item for Dinh's bulwark can aid in survivability; the player can simply switch to Dinh's if under attack. Bringing black d'hide to switch to is also wise. Players using Tumeken's shadow can get away with wearing defensive ranged items like fortified masori or Armadyl, if they have a high magic accuracy bonus (+100, or higher).

tactics.heading: Overview
tactics.text:
Artio is a level 320 bear that can be found inside Hunter's End. She is killed for the valuable Voidwaker hilt, though she can also drop the claws of Callisto, tyrannical ring, Callisto cub, the dragon 2h sword and dragon pickaxe. The hard Wilderness diary is required to fight Artio.

Warning: Artio resides in a singles-plus area and in mid-level Wilderness. You may be attacked at any time during the kill. Do not bring any items that you are not willing to lose.

tactics.heading: Suggested skills
tactics.text:
• 90 Combat (95+ recommended)
• 60 Hitpoints (90+ recommended)
• 70 Defence (for Rigour/Augury)
• 44 Prayer (77+ recommended for Augury)
• 75 Ranged (90+ recommended)
• 92 Magic (94+ recommended for Ice Barrage)

tactics.heading: Transportation
tactics.text:
• Teleport to Ferox Enclave with a ring of dueling and run north.
• Teleport to Carrallanger with 84 magic or a teletab and run west.
• Teleport to Corporeal Beast with a games necklace and run west. (BEWARE: The area directly outside the Corporeal beast cave is multicombat)

tactics.heading: Attacks
tactics.text:
• Melee: Artio swipes at the player. This has AoE capabilities and can be used diagonally across a target. This deals up to 35 damage, with a minimum of 15; using Protect from Melee reduces the damage by ~50%.
• Ranged: Artio launches crescent-shaped projectiles at everyone in the den dealing up to 17 damage if she cannot attack with melee.
• Knockback: Artio will launch a white orb-like projectile at a targeted player, which will send them flying backwards and inflict damage if Protect from Magic is not activated when the attack visually hits the player.
  • The knockback attack is a single-target attack with splash AOE. This means that it will only target one player, but the spell will affect all players within a 3x3 square of the targeted player when it hits.
  • The damage the player will take from this attack when it hits them off prayer depends on how far the player can be knocked back before they hit the walls of the arena. The attack will attempt to knock the player back 3 tiles. If the player can be knocked back the full 3 tiles without hitting a wall, they will take 5 damage. This scales up by 15 damage for each tile of knockback that cannot be completed, so the player will take 20 damage if they were 2 tiles away from the wall they were pushed into, and 35 damage if they were 1 tile away. If the player is directly next to the wall that the attack pushes them into, they will take 50 damage.
  • If the player is knocked back into a trap, this attack will deal 5 damage (along with the damage from the trap).
• Bear Traps: At 66% health, Artio will deploy red, ghostly-like bear traps around the arena. Getting caught in a trap will deal up to 15 damage and briefly bind the player. The traps will be redeployed again at ~33% health and appear afterwards with every attack she makes.

tactics.heading: Strategy
tactics.text:
Artio will spawn to the south of the den, right in front of the exit. If you wish to avoid player killers, it is recommended to place a secondary account waiting outside the entrance to scout potential threats. All players who enter the den will spawn to the north, similar to Callisto's lair.

Artio uses highly damaging melee attacks and is weakest to magic and ranged attacks. Ice spells will land often even with minimal magic gear, binding her temporarily. If she cannot attack with melee, she will begin using a much weaker ranged attack until she can reach her target. Artio will occasionally launch a white orb at her target, which should be protected against by switching on Protect from Magic or risk taking up to 50 damage from the attack.

Upon reaching 66% and 33% of her health, Artio will roar, launching bear traps all across the arena. Stepping on one will deal up to 15 damage and bind the player for a few seconds. The traps will linger around for a short duration before expiring, but will immediately be replaced with a fresh set of traps. While roaring, she will also glow red, breaking free of binds in the process and requiring a player to refreeze her.
