• 3-5 Blighted super restores
• Looting bag (optional)
• Summer pies or curry as food so your items do not get unequipped
  • Alternatively, Armadyl brews can be used in place of both food and the ranging potion, as they are cheap, heal more than any hard food per inventory slot, and boost your Ranged level. They also do not cause any attack delay.
  • However, keep in mind that you may wish to bring more blighted super restores, as the brews drain your Defence and Magic levels. You must also remember to toggle off automatically smashing vials as so to not leave empty spaces in the inventory.
• Anti-venom or Antidote++ to remove venom from pkers
• Optionally, you can bring a Ring of wealth (i) switch for a doubled chance at a Clue scroll (elite).

Only bring the 3 or 4 valuable items from this setup into the wilderness unless you are experienced enough to easily escape. The risk of getting killed by pkers is high and there is always the possibility of getting smited. Activate Protect from Magic and Protect Item if high risk, or just use the safespot. Don't linger in the same world for too long as there's a high chance to encounter player killers.

gearNotes.heading: Inventory
gearNotes.text:
• Special attack weapon like Voidwaker
• 1 Divine super combat potion or Super set
• 2-3 Blighted super restores
• Looting bag (optional)
• Anti-venom or Antidote++ to remove venom from pkers
• Summer pies or curry as food so your items do not get unequipped

tactics.heading: Overview
tactics.text: Fighting the Chaos Elemental is a matter of countering its unequip attack by keeping your inventory full and avoiding player killers. As it attacks with random damage types, you will always be taking damage unless you are flinching or using the safe spot. Therefore, it is critical to maximise the amount of healing you bring while minimising your risk. Dragonhide armour is effective. Always check your Items Kept on Death before fighting this boss, and never bring anything you are not willing to lose.

tactics.heading: Transportation
tactics.text:
• If you have completed the hard Wilderness Diary, you can redirect a Wilderness Obelisk from your house or outside the Ferox Enclave to Level 50 and run west. This is generally the best option, as it does not require any items and is the shortest.
• Teleporting to the Fountain of Rune via wilderness sword 4; requires completion of the elite Wilderness Diary.
• Using an Annakarl Teleport or tablet (requires completion of Desert Treasure I), then running north-west to a gate in the fence, and north-east from there.
• From Edgeville bank: bring a knife or slash weapon, run south and pull the lever, run north, cut the web, then run east past the Resource Area and Scorpion Pit.
• From Mage Arena bank: bring a knife or slash weapon, pull the lever and cut the two webs, then continue east.

tactics.heading: Attacks
tactics.text:
The Chaos Elemental's primary attack, Discord, is a projectile attack that resembles series of three different colours fired at the target. This attack can deal either Magic, Ranged, or Melee damage — it is impossible to distinguish what damage is dealt. The projectiles hit into the 20s, but it is still suggested that players utilise Protect from Magic to reduce the chance of being hit, as the projectile deals magic damage most frequently.

It also has two special attacks. The first one, Confusion, teleports players a short space or several spaces away from it. The second attack, Madness, unequips up to four items that players are wielding, forcing them to take time to re-equip their armour and weapons before continuing the battle. Like most monsters, its attacks will continue to follow the player until impact and can travel through walls. The weapon of the player is always prioritised, so when this attack is successful, the player will always have to re-equip their weapon.

tactics.heading: Countering Madness
tactics.text:
Bringing food that leaves an item behind, such as Guthix rest, curry, and summer pies, will force the Chaos Elemental to never use its Madness attack, as it cannot unequip the player's items if there is no room in the inventory to do so. Players who have completed Alfred Grimhand's Barcrawl should also disable vial smashing via the barbarian guard or through the game settings as well, so that finishing a potion will leave the vial behind.

This does, however, give the Chaos Elemental a chance to use its Discord and Confusion attacks in turn, so you could leave just a single empty spot in your inventory for the Chaos Elemental to unequip one of your items instead of up to four. With enough practice this can save some supplies in the long run, since its Madness attack does not deal any damage and replaces the potentially high-hitting Discord attack.

Another strategy to prevent this attack from being launched is to bring a sack (or basket) of potatoes, cabbages, onions, etc. Whenever you need to eat, simply empty the sack or basket after each bite. With practice this can be done quite quickly without interrupting your attacks. Additionally, if you leave an open inventory slot and wait for its Madness attack to be launched, you can empty the sack before the attack lands to fill the empty inventory slot and negate the effect, guaranteeing a zero damage attack.

tactics.heading: Solo Flinching Method
tactics.text:
The safest method for soloing the Chaos Elemental is flinching it with melee. After attracting its attention, the player should run behind a tree to prevent it from attacking. Once its Hitpoints bar disappears, the player can attack it once before immediately returning behind the tree. This process can be repeated until the Chaos Elemental is defeated.

Any melee weapon can be used, although weapons with high offensive bonuses are preferable because attack speed does not affect flinching. A full set of Verac's equipment provides fast kills, but one piece may be lost if the player is smited by player killers.

A lower-risk setup can use up to three valuable items, such as a godsword, a dragon warhammer with a defender, or Dharok's greataxe. Any remaining protected item slots can be used for equipment that increases offensive bonuses. Cheap prayer-boosting equipment, such as monk's robes, can be worn while using offensive prayers and Preserve.

Players not using the flinching method can instead wear a Karil's leathertop, Verac's helm, and Verac's plateskirt, alongside a crystal shield or dragonfire shield. A rune crossbow or Armadyl crossbow with diamond bolts (e) can be used to attack from a distance. This setup is effective even below 100 combat, but risks several valuable items. Due to the likelihood of encountering player killers, lower-cost alternatives are recommended.

tactics.heading: Solo Safe Spot Method
tactics.text:
You can also set up a safe spot where you can freely attack the Chaos Elemental without it being able to attack you back. To use this method efficiently, you will need to mark a column of tiles running north to south, near the Wilderness Resource Area.

The northernmost tile to mark lines up with the north-easternmost Yew tree (left image). Staying on this line, run all the way south to the Wilderness fence and mark this southernmost tile (right image). This tile line is the farthest west the Chaos Elemental can attack.

Now, with the Chaos Elemental near its spawn by the Rogue’s Castle, aggro it and then run straight south to the Wilderness fence. (There is a 2x2 tree near its spawn you can hide behind to avoid a few hits as you lure it south). With the Chaos Elemental still trying to attack you, run west along the Wilderness fence—staying as close to the fence as possible—until you reach your marked tile. Wait here until the Chaos Elemental catches up to you. As soon as you see the Elemental, run directly north. Once you get to your two northernmost tiles, stop and wait for the Chaos Elemental to catch up to you again. When you can see the Chaos Elemental, run directly towards it. You can do this by attacking it. As you get close to melee range, step one tile to the west and attack the Chaos Elemental from its western side. If you have done this correctly, the Chaos Elemental will be floating on your tile line (which, again, is as far as it can roam or attack) and the player will be one tile west of that line. At this point, you can freely attack the Chaos Elemental and it will never attack you back as long as you do not cross back over the tile line.

It is important to note that the red teleportation attack when running from the southern to northern tiles can teleport you west of the attackable line. If this happens and you're not able to re-aggro the Chaos Elemental before it starts resetting, you may have to wait for the Chaos Elemental to return to the spawn area and restart the lure entirely.

This method can be very useful for lower-levelled or lower-geared accounts (such as irons). It can take some practice and trial and error to set up, but once the lure is complete you can finish the kill almost entirely AFK and much faster than flinching every hit with a tree.

You should plan to bring food with you, as you will be attacked by the Chaos Elemental on average 10 times during the setup. Even low healing food, such as Tuna, may be sufficient.

If you have access to stamina potions or energy potions, they can be useful if you have to restart your lure, as this method does require a lot of run energy.

tactics.heading: Team
tactics.text: Players fighting with Melee should take armour with high Ranged and Melee Defence, such as Dragon or Barrows equipment, and use Protect from Magic. As there's a strong chance to encounter player killers, it would be better to stick to lower-cost gear to alleviate the risk.

tactics.heading: Suggested skills
tactics.text:
• 80+ Attack
• 80+ Strength
• 70+ Defence
• 75+ Ranged
• 37+ Prayer (70 Recommended)

tactics.heading: Avoiding and escaping player killers
tactics.text:
Due to the Chaos Elemental's location in multi-combat deep Wilderness, you will likely encounter player killers in both teams and as individuals. The nearby Rogues' Castle is useful for attackers to hop worlds (sometimes using low-level scouts) and spot potential victims, as the projectiles are visible beyond normal viewing range. It may be effective to switch worlds between kills to potentially avoid PKers, although Chaos Elemental's short respawn time of 8.4s leaves little room for switching worlds.

If you are spotted and/or attacked, quickly select and pursue an escape option:

• A Wilderness Obelisk (Level 50) lies on the south-east side of the Rogues' Castle. By default the obelisks' destination is random, but it is likely you will be teleported to relative safety such as single-way combat or a lower Wilderness level. Completing the hard Wilderness Diary allows you to select a destination (the level 13 obelisk being the safest, as it is close to the Ferox Enclave). Warning: You cannot use obelisks while under the effect of Tele Block.
• The Rogues' Castle has many doorways and staircases that can be used to confuse and shake loose of an attacker. Moving unpredictably and closing doors behind you can buy you time to log out. This is less effective when being chased by a team.
• The Resource Area to the west requires 7500 coins to enter, or less depending on completion of the Wilderness Diary (6000 coins for medium, 3750 coins for hard, or 0 coins for elite). If your attacker(s) did not bring coins and lacks the elite diary perk, you can escape them here.
• The Magic axe hut to the north-west requires a Lockpick and 23 Thieving to enter. Although there are aggressive magic axes contained within which prevent you from logging out, it is in single-way combat. It is very likely that either you or your attacker will be attacked by an axe, which may allow you to X-log. There are also two entrances/exits, which can help you create space.
• The Deserted Keep to the west has a teleport lever which can take you to Ardougne (or Edgeville, if the easy Wilderness Diary is completed). A web blocks the entrance, so bring a knife or slash weapon to open it. Warning: You cannot use the lever while under the effect of Tele Block.

If it isn't likely that you will survive, prioritise keeping your prayer points so that you can keep Protect Item active. If you run out of prayer restoration, it may be advisable to accept your fate rather than continue eating food, as taking damage allows your attackers to potentially smite you for your fourth valuable item. Consider bringing a Falador shield for a last-resort prayer restoration option, as it is free to reobtain. The Demonic Ruins to the south also passively restore 1 prayer point every 3 seconds, which may provide a slim chance of reactivating Protect Item.

options.text: Ava's accumulator (Or Dizana's quiver / Ava's assembler
Dragon arrow / Amethyst arrow / Rune arrow
Black d'hide chaps (Masori chaps if comfortable with the risk)

gearNotes.heading: Equipment
gearNotes.text:
Activate Protect from Magic, and be prepared to use Protect Item if 4-iteming. Similar to the chaos elemental, he can unequip your items.

Note: Ensure you are not risking more than you are willing to lose.

It is recommended to use inventory blocking food as he cannot disarm you if there are no slots in your inventory for your weapons. Examples of this are Pies, Curry, and Stew. Another option since the release of Sailing are Armadyl brews, which can heal up to 44 in a single inventory slot, keep your ranged boost up, leave a vial behind and works well with blighted super restores.

If you are using potions, it is advised to make sure that vial smashing is turned off. This option can be turned off in the settings menu under the gameplay section. Blighted super restore can be used, as it's in the Wilderness.

gearNotes.heading: Inventory
gearNotes.text:
• 2 divine ranging potion.
• 4–6 blighted super restores.
• Looting bag (recommended).
• Ghorrock teleport (at least 2 as otherwise you will be left with an empty inventory space after you use the first one, and the boss would unequip your gear), runes for casting, or burning amulet (optional, as you can get to the boss via the Wilderness obelisk to the north).
• An emergency teleport (optional—only works in level 30 or 20 Wilderness or less. See Wilderness teleport restrictions for info).
• Summer pies or Wild pies are the best food to bring here, as they heal 22 per slot and leave the pie dish in the inventory, to counter the disarming ability of the chaos fanatic. Alternatively, Curry heals less (19 Hitpoints) but heals in one bite, whereas the pies are eaten in two bites healing 11 per bite.

tactics.heading: Overview
tactics.text:
The Chaos Fanatic is a relatively simple boss similar to the Crazy archaeologist and the Deranged archaeologist; his special attack has the potential to cause major damage if not avoided.

Due to his high magic level and defensive bonuses, the most effective strategy is to use Ranged while protecting from magic and avoiding his green special attack by moving away from where you are standing.

Players can optionally walk to the altar that lies to the south-west in order to recharge their prayer after each fight, although this is a highly active player killing spot. Player killers can only attack you in between kills while waiting for the boss to respawn, so always be aware of players nearby who may be waiting for you to finish your kill.

In order to escape from player killers, a good option is to make use of the Wilderness obelisk to the north to teleport to level 13 Wilderness (possible to guarantee after completion of the hard Wilderness Diary) which will then allow the player to teleport away using a standard teleport method. Players can also run east into the King Black Dragon Lair (non-Wilderness) and teleport from there.

tactics.heading: Suggested skills
tactics.text:
• 75+ Ranged
• 70+ Defence
• 37+ Prayer
• 96+ Magic (optional for Ghorrock Teleport)

options.text: Ancient wyvern shield / Mage's book / Malediction ward
Seeking dragon arrow / Diamond ascension bolts (e) / Diamond dragon bolts (e) / Moonlight antler bolts / God blessing
Seeking amethyst arrow / Diamond bolts (e) / Sunlight antler bolts
Armadyl crossbow > Dragon hunter crossbow > Dragon crossbow > Rune crossbow
Saradomin d'hide body / Zamorak d'hide body
Pegasian boots or Saradomin d'hide boots / Zamorak d'hide boots
Ring of suffering (ri) / Ring of endurance

gearNotes.heading: Inventory
gearNotes.text:
• Zorya's tome or Eldritch Nightmare staff or Eye of Ayak/accursed sceptre for special attack
• Sanguinesti staff switch for healing (optional with Blood Barrage)
• Saturated heart
• Ecumenical key (optional)
• Saradomin brew and anglerfish for emergency healing
• 16 super restores
• Bones to peaches tablets (optional)
• Stamina potion to restore run energy (optional)
• Explorer's ring 4 for High level alchemy and run energy restoration
• Divine rune pouch with runes for Blood Barrage and Ice Barrage

gearNotes.heading: Inventory
gearNotes.text:
• Toxic blowpipe (to kill minions)
• Serpentine helm (to envenom minions at start of kill) (optional)
• Venator bow (to kill minions while stacked and/or as a Zarosian item, optional)
• Ecumenical key (optional)
• Any required god items, with one Saradomin and one Zamorak item being strongly recommended, and optionally a Zarosian item if banking at the Ancient Prison
• 1-4 Extended stamina potions or stamina potions (optional for higher levelled and geared players, or those using run energy neutral kiting methods)
• 8-16 Saradomin brews or sharks (brews & super restores should be brought in a 3:1 ratio)
• 6-12 Super restores or prayer potions
• 1-4 Divine bastion potions or divine ranging potions
• Explorer's ring 4 for access to High level alchemy regardless of spellbook and run energy restoration
• A divine rune pouch containing law runes, nature runes, dust runes and steam runes will allow the player to cast Trollheim teleport, Teleport to house, High level alchemy and Bones to peaches
• Ghommal's hilt or two Trollheim teleport tablets. Revert one to a Teleport to house (tablet) once you arrive.
• Alternatively, a Book of the Dead with a rune pouch containing fire runes, blood runes, and cosmic runes for resurrection spells.
• Armadyl brews can be used in place of Saradomin brews with a more advanced method involving Menaphite remedies to restore lowered defence levels; defence levels lost are restored by the remedy every 15 seconds.
  • This has the benefit of keeping your Divine ranging boost and also requiring one fewer sipping action when healing via Armadyl brews when done correctly.
    • e.g. Menaphite remedy -> Divine ranging -> 2x Armadyl brew sips per 15 seconds to maintain a decent defence level while also not cancelling the divine status.
  • This comes with a caveat that you must have sufficient equipment with high ranged defence as Bree has a low max hit, but will be very consistent on your lower, unboosted defence.
    • Due to this, Consider bringing Super restores instead of Prayer potions with this method as consecutively drinking Armadyl brews may lower defence too much for the Menaphite remedy to restore defence in a timely manner, negating any health gained.

tactics.heading: Overview
tactics.text:
This is a guide to defeating Commander Zilyana, the Saradominist general in the God Wars Dungeon.

While Commander Zilyana has an equal amount of resistance to all attacks, Magic (apart from the Tumeken's shadow) is generally impractical here due to the lack of defence provided by magic armour and unnecessary rune costs.

tactics.heading: Requirements
tactics.text:
• Completion of Death Plateau and the start of Troll Stronghold to the point where you defeat Dad
• Alternatively, Ghommal's hilt can be used to teleport to Trollheim without requiring either quest
• One rope is required to access the God Wars Dungeon for the first time.
• Two (additional) ropes are required to navigate Saradomin's Encampment for the first time.
• Level 70 Agility is required to access Saradomin's Encampment (cannot be boosted).
• Level 37 Prayer to activate Protect from Magic.

tactics.heading: General Strategy
tactics.text:
Similarly to Kree'arra, many players prefer using an ecumenical key to skip kill count. Although Saradominist kill count is considered to be somewhat quick, this is only partially true if the player has 83 Slayer, as Saradominist spiritual warriors and mages are aggressive towards Zamorakian followers. The remaining Saradominist followers are passive and will only attack in self-defence.

Zilyana attacks with both melee and magic. Pray Protect from Magic while killing Zilyana if using ranged or Protect from Missiles if using mage. If done correctly the only damage you should take is from the range or mage minion, respectively. Although her max hit is relatively low, with her melee attacks dealing up to 27 damage and her magic dealing 10-20 damage, she makes up for this with an attack speed of 2 (1.2 seconds). Combined with her tremendous accuracy, this makes fighting her in melee range extremely dangerous, as the precise attacks and rapid attack speed will cause a swift death for her target. Like Graardor and K'ril however, Zilyana can only attack when in melee distance of a player.

Zilyana has three bodyguards; Bree, Growler and Starlight, who use ranged, magic and melee with maximum hits of 16, 16 and 15 damage respectively. Her bodyguards are significantly weaker compared to the other generals', but they still should not be underestimated.

The kiting method should be used when fighting Zilyana, as her chamber is quite large. This means that damage will only be incurred from the bodyguard that the player is not protecting against, as Starlight and Zilyana will not be able to reach the player unless they stop moving. The most common method involves running around the chamber, though there are advanced methods that reduce or even negate the need for stamina potions, even with low Agility levels.

tactics.heading: Ranging
tactics.text: For players ranging Zilyana, the most common methods are to either use a crossbow with enchanted diamond bolts, full crystal armour with a Bow of Faerdhinen, or a twisted bow. A toxic blowpipe and a serpentine helm switch, while optional, are helpful in envenoming the bodyguards, as it will guarantee that they will be envenomed upon hit. This will help whittle down their health while Zilyana is being killed, especially if not using a twisted bow.

tactics.heading: Bow of Faerdhinen No Stamina
tactics.text:
This advanced ranged setup allows players to kill Commander Zilyana without using stamina potions. This method requires following a specific pattern in order to attack Zilyana up to 12 times without getting attacked in the process, while also conserving energy. The player should always pray protect from magic while killing Zilyana.

For every kill except the first kill:
• Start on blue tile labelled 1 and attack twice.
• Run to tile 2 and attack once
• Click on yellow tile (your character will automatically walk this tile) before running to tile 3 and attacking once
• Click on the next yellow, then run to tile 4 and attack again. On the last tile (12), attack and run to tile 2 and restart the process
• Turn off run once Zilyana is dead

Attack on every red tile, while walking all the yellow tiles. This allows your character to conserve and restore energy while also allowing you to stay out of range of Commander Zilyana.

Assuming the player has about 80 Agility, around 10-12 run energy is used per lap.

The bodyguards Bree, Starlight and Growler all have a chance to drop summer pies which can be used to restore 10% run energy per bite (total 20%).

For the first kill
• Start on green tile 1, attack once and run to the green tile 2
• Run to red tile 4 and carry on like you would for all normal kills.

tactics.heading: Magic
tactics.text:
Tumeken's shadow, with its passive effect enhancing adequately powerful magic gear, is the strongest weapon for conventional methods of killing Commander Zilyana. Additionally, the combination of Blood barrage to heal off the bodyguards and the special attack of an Eldritch Nightmare staff, especially with the reduced cooldown granted by the Lightbearer, can allow players to remain in Zilyana's lair indefinitely, limited only by runes, weapon charges and run energy.

If players wish to save some costs on runes, bringing a powered staff can help in clearing minions.

However, it should be noted that this strategy requires almost completely maxed mage gear. Even a single downgrade from an Ancestral robe top to an Ahrim's robetop for example will dramatically impact kill times and trip length, due to the multiplicative effect Tumeken's shadow has on the magic stat bonuses of other pieces of equipment. The barrier to entry is therefore extremely high, and for players who do not have the best-in-slot options for two or more gear slots, ranging is likely to be more effective.

tactics.heading: Team
tactics.text:
In a team setting, if Zilyana cannot attack her current target, she will change her aggression to a nearby attacker. This is commonly used by ranging teams to minimise the amount of stamina potions needed, allowing for other supplies to be taken. Team settings also allow for melee, although players will need to be wary of Zilyana shifting aggression when she cannot attack her target.

Instead of attacking Zilyana directly, players (or alternate accounts) can attack Bree and Starlight. If multiple players are in the room, the bodyguards will only attack those who have attacked Zilyana, so this means the only danger for these players is Zilyana's magic attack. If the bodyguards are killed before Zilyana herself is killed, then they are likely to respawn, and so it may be beneficial to limit the damage done to them.

tactics.heading: Suggested skills
tactics.text:
• 100+ Combat
• 70+ Agility (Required)
• 80+ Ranged
• 80+ Defence (90+ Recommended)
• 70+ Hitpoints
• 44+ Prayer (74+ Rigour)

gearNotes.heading: Notes, gear, and inventory
gearNotes.text:
• See the above quick-pool section for a more detailed outline of the strategy.
• Due to the accuracy and damage of Corp's magic attacks, magic defence is highly valued, sometimes at the expense of strength bonus. In addition to costing time, using the pool/statue will heal the boss, so minimising downtime is essential.
• Bring an elder maul or dragon warhammer for their special attack, as well as your maximum crush bonus gear such as Inquisitor's armour, mythical cape and tyrannical ring (i)
• Bring a Voidwaker for its special attack, and an ultor ring or berserker ring (i) swap when using VW specs
• On the Lunar spellbook, bring runes for Spellbook Swap, Vengeance and Thralls
• Bring a divine super combat potion or super combat potion to boost combat stats
• Saturated heart or Imbued heart are used to boost magic defence
• Bring your fastest teleport to a restore pool to restore HP and Spec (Desert amulet 4 > Nardah teleport > Teleport to house (tablet))
• Bring games necklaces to teleport to Corp, and a fast teleport to a bank for in between kills
• With 70+ Prayer level, prayer potions should never be necessary since you're forced to use restore pools frequently

gearNotes.heading: Equipment upgrades and downgrades
gearNotes.text: See the above dolo section for more information. The gear setup is identical for both accounts and focuses for DPS over defence in many slots because the added defence is unnecessary. The food both accounts are carrying is more than enough to see the kill through in this equipment following the outlined strategy, so shedding DPS in these slots only slows kills down.

gearNotes.heading: Equipment upgrades and downgrades
gearNotes.text:
This method focuses on draining only a part of Corporeal Beast's defence and dying in the room to have an extra supply of food. As the majority of the time is used on killing the boss as opposed to draining its stats, this method is slightly faster but requires more high-end gear and is more resource and skill intensive.

Before equipping this setup, use three Elder maul and four to six Emberlight special attacks on the boss, then purposefully die within the room (preferably close to the entrance) with a full inventory of cooked karambwan two or three times; unless picked up and dropped again, these will stay on the floor for a full hour before despawning and serve as extra supplies that will be needed due to the boss's high damage output.

The setup is based on a mix of magic defence and strength gear. For ironmen, including the time to obtain the extra food used, this method may not be faster effective kills if you do not have some of the demonstrated equipment such as Armadyl armour. It also requires more practice to become a consistent method; a large portion of mitigating damage taken, and therefore needing to heal less which takes time away from damaging the boss, is switching between a shield and a magic staff (for their added magic defence) and the spear between attacks, and optionally switching between a magic prayer (e.g. Augury) and Piety. Making mistakes is also more punishing due to the increased risk of dying and effectively resetting the fight.

tactics.heading: Overview
tactics.text: The Corporeal Beast is a high level boss monster in Old School RuneScape.

tactics.heading: Requirements
tactics.text: There are no strict requirements to killing the Corporeal Beast.

tactics.heading: Recommendations
tactics.text:
• High combat stats. Although not required, see the skill levels below for an indication of the advised stats:
  • If using Melee:
    • Level 85 Hitpoints or higher
    • Level 94 Attack or higher
    • Level 94 Strength or higher
    • Level 94 Defence or higher
    • Level 70 Prayer or higher for the Piety prayer
  • If using Ranged:
    • Level 90 Hitpoints or higher
    • Level 90 Ranged or higher
    • Level 74 Prayer or higher for the Rigour prayer

tactics.heading: Transportation
tactics.text: The Corporeal Beast can be found in a cave at level 19-20 Wilderness, which is surrounded by hostile ents and black unicorns. As the area is frequently visited by PKers, entering through the Wilderness is not recommended. Instead, use a games necklace and teleport to the Corporeal Beast. The cave in which the Corporeal Beast resides is not part of the Wilderness.

tactics.heading: Attack styles
tactics.text:
The Corporeal Beast attacks with Melee and Magic. It attacks normally every 4 ticks, but it can occasionally attack 3 ticks after its last. When its targeted player is in melee range, it will use a melee attack 40% of the time, while all magic attacks are used with a 20% chance. When outside of melee range, all magic attacks occur with a 33% chance and the melee attack is unused.

Protect from Melee will block all damage from the melee attack and Protect from Magic will block 1/3 of the damage from the magic attacks. Despite this, it is recommended to always use Protect from Magic due to the magic attacks' higher damage, accuracy and frequency.

• The Melee attack is only used when the player is standing in Melee distance and can hit up to 33.
• The Magic attack has three variations. See the images below on how to identify the different variations.
  • A regular Magic attack that can deal up to 65 damage.
  • A Magic attack that can deal up to 55 damage and has a chance to drain Magic or Prayer by 1 or 2. The stat drain effect only takes place upon a successful hit. The boss is healed by half of the damage dealt, rounded down.
  • A Magic attack targeted at the player's location that splits into six smaller projectiles that land randomly in a 7x7 area. Both projectile themselves have an AoE of 3x3. The main attack can hit up to 40 if landing directly or up to 30 if landing adjacently. Each smaller projectile can hit up to 30 if landing directly, or up to 20 if landing adjacently. All projectiles can be dodged by moving at least 5 tiles away from the original targeted tile.

If the player steps under the Corporeal Beast, it may perform a stomp attack that will always deal 30–51 damage. This attack is on a timer that checks if any players are under the Corporeal Beast every 7 ticks (4.2 seconds). This attack cannot be negated with protection prayers.

tactics.heading: Dark energy core
tactics.text:
The Corporeal Beast can occasionally send out a dark energy core. It has a 1/8 chance of spawning whenever the Corporeal Beast is hit for at least 32 damage, or when it attacks while its hitpoints are under 1,000. Whenever the dark energy core is summoned, the Corporeal Beast's attack timer is reset to 4 ticks.

The dark energy core leeches hitpoints from any players adjacent to it (in a 3x3 area) to heal the Corporeal Beast. It can deal 5–13 damage every 2 ticks (1.2 seconds). The dark energy core will jump to players if none are adjacent.

It can be weakened significantly by poisoning it. Once it has been poisoned, its attacks will be extremely slow. However, there must be at least one player around the dark energy core or else it will start hopping around again and will attack normally. If the dark energy core was stunned but someone moved away from it and it starts hopping around again, it cannot be stunned again. It will keep dealing damage rapidly until it is killed. If the Corporeal Beast dies, the dark energy core will disappear.

The dark energy core will usually follow the player that stands northernmost. If no players are on the northern side, it will focus on the person that stands on the eastern side of the Corporeal Beast. It is usually advisable for the person who tanks or runs the core to stand north or east of the Corporeal Beast. Players that have experience with the Corporeal Beast typically know that there are specific game tiles that cause the core to prioritise and follow a player.

tactics.heading: Damage reduction
tactics.text:
The Corporeal Beast has a 50% damage reduction against any melee and ranged weapon that is not a Corpbane weapon. These weapons must also be on the stab attack style. This damage reduction does not apply to magic, recoil damage (such as Vengeance or rings of recoil), Retribution. The damage reduction applies to the special effect of enchanted ruby bolts, before the cap of 100 damage is calculated.

There is also currently a bug that causes attacks from the dwarf multicannon to be reduced by 50% damage twice.

tactics.heading: Stat regeneration
tactics.text:
By default, the Corporeal Beast regenerates each drained stat once every 20 ticks (12 seconds), regardless of if there are players in the room. If there are no players in the cave, it will heal 75 hitpoints every 7 game ticks (4.2 seconds), and heals an additional 10 hitpoints cumulatively every 7 ticks thereafter. This timer is shared with the Corporeal Beast's stomp attack timer. It will fully heal after three minutes if no one has attacked it.

If there are eight or more players in the room simultaneously, it will regenerate an additional 5 Hitpoints per player every 7 ticks (4.2 seconds). This also coincides with the stomp attack timer.

tactics.heading: Ironmen room
tactics.text:
Ironmen with a combat level of 90 or higher have a separated Corporeal Beast room. All other accounts use the normal room. This is to reduce griefing.

In addition, other players cannot assist in the encounter in any way: should someone damage or be attacked by the boss after the fight has been started by another player, kill credit will be invalidated for all players. This is to prevent players using other accounts to use stat-draining special attacks to speed up the kill. If someone has started the fight, a brazier in the lobby is lit with a blue flame.

tactics.heading: Dark energy core
tactics.text:
To deal with the dark energy core, a number of strategies can be used:
• Use a crossbow that can fire emerald bolts (e); if the special goes off, it will reduce the speed at which the dark energy core can sap players' hitpoints and prayer points. This requires a person to stay near it though, as failure to do so will result in the core bouncing around and the bolts' effects being removed.
• Move at least two tiles away whenever it jumps towards the player.
• Attack it as soon as it lands and immediately move away from it so it jumps; if it dies while midair, it will not respawn (this can be confirmed by its lack of ashes dropped). A dwarf multicannon can also be used to attack it midair, but this requires more timing as well as steel cannonballs.

tactics.heading: Stat draining
tactics.text:
While weak to stab attacks, the Corporeal Beast has a very high Defence level. A common method to lower its Defence is to use the Elder maul, arclight and Bandos godsword's special attack at the start of the fight.
• The Elder maul's special attack will lower the target's current Defence level by 35% on a hit.
• The Arclight's special attack will lower the opponent's Strength, Attack, and Defence levels by 5%+1 on a successful hit.
• The Bandos godsword's special attack will lower the opponent's combat levels equivalent to the damage hit in the following order: Defence, Strength, Prayer, Attack, Magic, Ranged.

The Elder maul's special attack is very useful in significantly increasing the player's damage output while fighting the Corporeal Beast.

The other special attacks are especially useful to players soloing the Corporeal Beast, as this will increase the player's damage output significantly while almost nullifying the Corporeal Beast's damage output. To achieve this, the special attacks have to be used in the following order:
• 3 successful Elder maul special attacks. Although not required, this step is highly recommended to increase the accuracy of the arclight's special attacks.
• 19 successful Emberlight special attacks. These attacks will completely drain the Corporeal Beast's Strength, Attack and Defence levels.
• A total damage of 200 with the Bandos godsword's special attack. These attacks will completely drain the Corporeal Beast's Magic level to almost completely negate its magical accuracy (although its maximum hit will be unaffected) and drastically reduce its overall damage output.
  • The special attack's stat reduction effect is calculated before the Corporeal Beast's 50% damage reduction, meaning 175 damage is enough to drain its 350 Magic levels. The remaining 25 damage is done to nullify the passive stat regeneration during the process.

It is recommended to bring item switches for gear that boost crush accuracy while using the Elder maul's special attacks, such as the tyrannical ring (i), mythical cape and dwarven helmet.

For teams, it is often recommended to only reduce the Corporeal Beast's Defence level before proceeding to killing it, as it takes more time than it is worth to further reduce its stats in bigger groups.

tactics.heading: Player-owned house
tactics.text:
As most Corporeal Beast strategies heavily rely on using special attacks in quick succession, it is highly recommended to have a restoration pool or better in the player-owned house. Alternatively, players can pray at the Elidinis Statuette in Nardah after completion of Quest Spirits of the Elid quest. Both methods will restore the player's special attack energy.

To return to the Corporeal Beast quickly, it is highly recommended to have a basic jewellery box or better in the player-owned house. Alternatively, bring enough games necklaces in the inventory.

If no special attacks hit, players may typically restore their special attack through a restoration pool (or higher) and teleport back.

tactics.heading: Instance
tactics.text:
Players can pay 200,000 coins coins to host an instance. Players ranked as Captain or above in a clan chat can pay the instance cost for their clan. Once the instance is opened, anyone from the clan chat will be able to enter the instance for no cost. As long as there is one player present in the instance, it will remain open.

Note that ironmen cannot enter this instance.

tactics.heading: Stat draining
tactics.text:
For solo players (or small teams with low stats), killing the Corporeal Beast without massively reducing its stats can prove difficult as they may run out of food before killing it. Therefore, it may be more beneficial to drain its combat stats to zero by using their player-owned house to restore special attacks and teleport back repeatedly. An effective strategy is to:

• hit 3 Elder maul special attacks to lower its Defence to approximately a third, then
• hitting 19 Emberlight special attacks to reduce its melee stats, and then
• deal a total of 200 damage with Bandos godsword special attacks to reduce its Magic to 0.

Following this, the Corporeal Beast can be killed with relative ease and little food required. As a downside, the process is very slow; including the time to reduce its stats, solo players will take approximately 10 to 15 minutes per kill. However, it is the only realistic option for ultimate and hardcore ironmen to kill the boss.

tactics.heading: Quick-pool
tactics.text:
Reset (meaning teleport to a restore pool then tele back) until you land 1 Elder maul or Dragon warhammer spec. Then stop resetting, but continue attempting maul/hammer specs until you've landed 2-3 total or Corp reaches ~1700 HP, at which point use Voidwaker instead. Reset whenever your HP reaches Corp's max hit of 43. This method is significantly higher kills per hour than fully reducing Corp's stats, but is not recommended without high end gear & stats. Osmumten's Fang, Voidwaker and an Elder Maul or Dragon Warhammer are particularly essential.
• Swap to maximum crush attack bonus gear when using Elder maul or DWH specs
• Swap to strength boosting gear when using Voidwaker specs (Amulet of rancour and Ultor ring or Berserker ring (i))
• Food is not needed, and teleporting to a bank during kills to restock on food will slow down kills compared to only teleporting to a restore pool
• Use Spellbook Swap to maintain Vengeance and Thralls constantly
• If you spellbook swap after red clicking Corp upon entering the arena, you can use the spell while running to avoid tick delay
• Mage defence (and to a lesser extent Crush defence) is beneficial

tactics.heading: Death piling
tactics.text:
An alternative strategy is only lowering its Defence and dying in the boss room with an inventory full of food; because of the changes to death mechanics, it will stay on the floor for 60 minutes. This will supply the player with enough food to outlast the boss. This strategy requires more effort and supplies, but it results in faster kills. Gear with a higher emphasis on magic defence is highly recommended, as the Corporeal Beast will be able to deal damage as normal.

Though the beast will regenerate its stats throughout the fight, it usually does not have enough time to regenerate much before it is killed. However, as it regenerates its Magic level, the chance of its attacks becomes more likely, and its maximum hit remains the same regardless of its Magic level. Therefore, using Protect from Magic and gear with high magic defence is beneficial even if its stats are reduced to prevent taking high damage hits.

tactics.heading: Quick-banking
tactics.text: Another option for players with access to Osmumten's Fang is to bring a full inventory of karambwan, attack the boss without draining defence (or with only one or two Elder maul hits), teleport out using a fast bank teleport like the Crafting Cape to refill on food, then teleport back to the Corporeal Beast's lair as quickly as possible. The boss will heal for 100-150 hp in the time you are outside the room, but this is easily overwhelmed by the damage you can do to the boss before running out of food, with most kills requiring 3-4 food refills. Because of the Fang's high accuracy even against a Corporeal Beast with full stats, this strategy gets rapid kills without the effort of de-gearing, dying in the boss room, and re-gearing every kill. You will take large amounts of damage using this method, burning through 60+ karambwan per kill, and you should plan to eat any time your HP drops below 70, but the low tick delay on eating a karambwan without eating another food at the same time means eating does not significantly decrease your DPS. The ring of suffering (ri) and Amulet of Blood Fury are better options than the traditional DPS rings and amulets, to decrease the amount of time spent eating and recoil the boss' attacks. This strategy will not work with weapons other than the Fang.

tactics.heading: Solo with an alt (dolo)
tactics.text:
For players with access to an alt that has 82 attack and reasonably high strength, defence, and magic levels (85+), doloing the Corporeal Beast (fighting it on two accounts at the same time) with Osmumten's fang offers far more kills per hour than other solo methods (~21 with a maxed alt), because it eliminates the need to both drain the boss and leave the room for food. It is recommended to bring an elder maul or dragon warhammer on each account and reset with house pools until at least one spec lands. From there, each account's inventory of food should be enough to simply kill Corp head-on if both are using Osmumten's fang. An inventory of mostly karambwans with only about 4-6 normal food for combo eating is ideal to minimize the high amounts of attack delay that will be incurred. If Corp is targeting one account heavily, one may drop some food on the non-targeted account as a precaution, then pick it up on the targeted account 1 minute later.

It is recommended the player familiarizes themselves with permanently eliminating the dark core using melee before attempting the dolo method, as it is a consistent and quick way to eliminate the core and leaving it alive will greatly complicate the kill when playing on two accounts. The easiest way to permanently kill the dark core in a dolo is to keep your two accounts spaced out as they attack Corp until the dark core spawns. When you see the dark core spawn, stop attacking Corp by equipping each account's elder maul/dragon warhammer. Watch the dark core to see which account it jumps to, and hover your cursor under that account's feet until the option to attack the core appears. Attack it right away and then immediately run away from the core. If the hit is fatal, the core should jump away after you kill it and permanently disappear when it lands. If this fails to kill the core permanently, simply try again. Once the core has been killed, continue to fang Corp on both accounts, eating as necessary, until it dies.

A 3rd account may also be used for backup elder maul/dragon warhammer/Tonalztics of Ralos specs, as well as casting vengeance other, heal other, and energy transfer on the dps accounts (for voidwaker specs). This can result in up to 26 kills per hour.

It is recommended to bring either a crafting cape or amulet of eternal glory on the accounts to facilitate faster banking. Travelling through the house to bank is about 10-11 seconds slower per kill than using one of these alternatives.

• It is recommended to have the supply piles six tiles east of the entrance and lure the boss to the entrance before starting the fight, then moving east of it. The Corporeal Beast moves randomly during the fight, which will drag the player away from the supply piles if it is not trapped between the player and the entrance.

gearNotes.heading: Equipment
gearNotes.text:
The setup focuses on only taking 3 or 4 expensive items as this boss is located in the Wilderness with the possibility of player killers appearing. Although the Crazy Archaeologist wanders between levels 22 and 25 Wilderness, meaning you can teleport out, you can still get teleblocked or killed before you are able to teleport.

With a powered staff, a magic boost such as Magic potion, Forgotten brew, or Saturated or Imbued heart will provide a bigger damage increase than additional magic damage gear.

gearNotes.heading: Inventory
gearNotes.text:

• Runes to cast Iban Blast if using Iban's staff

• A looting bag, be aware you will drop any items within the looting bag should you die, regardless of the value of the items
• A teleport that works up to level 30 Wilderness, such as a royal seed pod, charged amulet of glory, or Slayer ring.

tactics.heading: Overview
tactics.text:
The crazy archaeologist is a relatively simple boss, but a simple mistake can cause some damage to you with his area of effect attack.

The most effective way is to use Magic while Protecting from Missiles and avoiding his area of effect attack. His area of effect attack casts 3 books into the air that slowly land and hit a 3x3 area. This area is centred around where the books land. It is preceded by the crazy archaeologist yelling "Rain of knowledge!".

It is recommended to bring low value gear such as monk robes for Prayer bonus as even with the crazy archaeologist's somewhat high Magic defence, his Magic level is negligible, and thus is weak to Magic and your own Magic accuracy matters little. This is because Magic defence is calculated primarily based on one's Magic level.

While you can melee him, he will start using melee attacks in addition to ranged ones when you are close. This extra damage, along with a shorter reaction time to the "Rain of knowledge!" attack means you will need to resupply more often and have less supplies for player killers.

Alternatively the crazy archaeologist can be killed without taking damage. This can be done by luring him behind the obstacles to the north of the area, attacking him and quickly running back behind the obstacle (flinching).

tactics.heading: Overview
tactics.text:
Custodian stalkers can be assigned as a Slayer task starting at level 54 by Chaeldar, Nieve, and Mortimer, and can be found in the Stalker Den after the completion of the Shadows of Custodia quest. There are multicombat areas where cannons can be placed in the south-western side of the dungeon, and single-combat caverns in the south-eastern and northern parts.

The stalkers all drop broken antlers, which are used to create atlatl dart tips for creating atlatl darts outside of subduing the Moons of Peril. The mature and elder variants are also able to drop the antler guard, a powerful off-hand item boasting offensive stats in all styles, with no defence requirement to wield. These tougher variants require a higher Slayer level to fight however, of level 67 and 76 respectively.

While most damage can be prevented with the use of Protect from Melee, once their Hitpoints get low they will use a special attack that causes a bleed effect; this attack can be blocked with Protect from Magic. When fighting multiple at once, changing prayers can be unwise, so some healing may be necessary. Gear with high magic defence such as dragonhide armour can be beneficial to reduce the amount of damage taken. Bones to Peaches can also allow the player to sustain longer trips with only prayer gear and potions. Stalkers also drop cooked fish, which may be enough to keep up with damage.

Players who wish to do this task are encouraged to get 76 Slayer in order to kill the elder stalkers. In addition to better drops, only the elders can spawn a superior slayer monster, the Ancient Custodian.

gearNotes.heading: Equipment
gearNotes.text:
The Dagannoth Kings can take a long time to reach and can be difficult to setup properly, so it is often more valuable to reduce unnecessary gear switches and bring extra supplies in order to extend trips. Balance damage output between each style, (if killing all 3 Kings), with ranged defence and prayer bonus to reduce unnecessary damage taken from the Spinolyps.

A tribrid setup means a single player using Magic, Ranged and Melee to kill all three Dagannoth Kings. It is only recommended for people who can afford good enough equipment to be able to kill all Kings fast enough.

If the player is not experienced, an alternative to attacking all three kings is to have another person targeting Rex, while the player targets Prime and Supreme. The person targeting Rex may help defeat Prime/Supreme if needed.

Because the run there takes so long, especially without the shortcuts, overall kills per hour are maximized by ensuring you complete a full Slayer task in only 1 trip, or as few trips as possible. It's preferable to sacrifice some DPS in favour of sustainability if you need to do so in order to last the full task. It's often worthwhile minimising gear swaps to bring more supplies (e.g. using Barrows gloves instead of Ferocious gloves + Zaryte vambraces, ignoring Bandos tassets) or favouring sustainability oriented gear (e.g. using Spectral spirit shield instead of a defender, using Guardian boots over Primordials, using SGS + Lightbearer over offensive options)

This setup is used to solo Dagannoth Rex. Rex is the easiest out of all the Kings as it can be safespotted, and offers the chance of receiving the berserker ring. Long trips can be achieved using Guthan's armour set, a Saradomin godsword or blood spells on the Spinolyps in between kills.

Magic is highly effective against Rex due to his extremely low magic defence. With a decent Magic level, players can wear full melee armour for the increased ranged defence and still hit Rex consistently.

For midgame players, Rex's 35% weakness to earth spells means that Earth Wave will do more damage than Iban Blast at a Magic level of 75, or upon unlocking it if using an elemental amulet or amulet of earth. It will also outdamage the warped sceptre at most Magic levels. Earth Blast however will always be weaker than Iban Blast.

Players may wish to kill only Dagannoth Prime for its unique drops or the pet. Once inside the north-east corner of the room, Prime can be ranged while remaining out of aggression range of Supreme and Rex. Use of Telekinetic Grab will aid in collecting drops. Maximize ranged strength and accuracy, or bring additional tank gear or switches to heal while waiting for Prime to respawn.

tactics.heading: Overview
tactics.text: Dagannoth Kings are a trio of bosses found in the Waterbirth Island Dungeon, known for their dragon axe, berserker ring, archers ring, warrior ring and seers ring drops. Their bones are also valuable, making them consistently rewarding to kill.

tactics.heading: The Kings
tactics.text:
The Kings reside on the sixth floor (the deepest) in Waterbirth Island Dungeon.

• Dagannoth Prime: The Dagannoth King who uses 3x3 area-of-effect (AoE) magical attacks. Whenever he is attacking, Protect from Magic must be on at all costs as Prime can hit up to 50 damage and easily kill in two hits. Prime is weak to ranged attacks.
• Dagannoth Rex: The Dagannoth King who uses melee attacks. He is extremely easy to deal with, as he can be either bound or lured to the edges of the islet where he can get stuck easily.
• Dagannoth Supreme: The Dagannoth King who uses ranged attacks. Supreme is also easy to deal with, hitting harder than Rex but lower than Prime. Supreme's attacks can hit multiple players if they are facing his direction.
• Spinolyps inhabit the moat surrounding the Dagannoth Kings' island. They are generally weak and have 75 Hitpoints. Their attacks are not very accurate, especially if the player has armour with high ranged defence, but their ranged attacks can inflict poison, and their magic attacks drain one prayer point if they hit. The poison damage starts at 6, so it is worth bringing Antidote++ potions. They can be used to heal with the use of Guthan's set or Saradomin godsword while waiting for the Kings to respawn.

tactics.heading: Suggested skills
tactics.text:
• 70+ Attack
• 70+ Strength
• 75+ Magic
• 70+ Ranged
• 60+ Defence (80+ Recommended)
• 70+ Hitpoints
• 45+ Prayer for Mystic Might, 70+ for Piety
• 85+ agility for shortcuts skipping the tunnels and need for Rune Thrownaxe/Pet Rock (can be boosted from 80 with a Summer Pie)

tactics.heading: Strategy
tactics.text:
As the Kings all attack with different styles, reducing the amount of time spent attacking multiple Kings is essential for staying alive and extending trips. This can be done by killing the Kings in a cycle and utilising the downtime before they respawn to safely kill the other kings, by safespotting, or by attacking a King outside the aggression range of the others. The aggression range for Dagannoth Rex is 5 tiles from their south-western tile. The aggression range for Dagannoth Prime and Dagannoth Supreme is 7 tiles from their south-western tile. As Dagannoth Kings are size 3x3 monsters you can get closer to Dagannoth Kings if you're in the north-eastern side of the room.

Download the tile markers above to show safespots for Rex, along with ladder locations throughout the entire dungeon route.

tactics.heading: Entering the lair
tactics.text:
Upon entering the lair, the player can be targeted by any amount of Kings at the same time, though it is most common to be attacked by both Prime and/or Supreme upon dropping down. Protect from Magic should be activated before entering their lair since Prime is likely to be very accurate and also hits the hardest of the three by far.

For players wishing to safespot Rex or Prime, they should enter and exit the room (leaving via the ladder will nullify some incoming attacks if done quickly enough), until they can safely run along the southern side of the island without being targeted by Supreme or Prime. Once on the eastern wall, players can attack Rex with magic and use either safespot freely.

For players planning on killing all 3 Kings, there are a few common options to start.

• You can sneak to the eastern wall and start the rotation with Rex with magic.
• If Supreme is not aggressive, you can run north and begin attacking Prime with ranged.
• If Prime is not aggressive, you can attempt to kill Supreme quickly with melee. Note that Supreme's spawn location makes it more likely that a second or third king will notice you, so starting with Supreme is typically the most difficult option.

tactics.heading: Handling multicombat
tactics.text:
If multiple Kings begin attacking you, you can attempt to off-tick their attacks and correctly pray against all of them. For a more relaxed approach, you can stick with Protect from Magic while quickly killing Supreme first or safespotting Rex.

With very high defence bonuses (such as with 99 Defence and expensive armour), Rex and Supreme will only have 15-30% accuracy against you. This makes it possible to run in with Protect from Magic and strong melee armour to kill both Supreme and Rex before finally switching to weaker ranged armour to defeat Prime. You will typically take very little damage even if all three kings attack you at once.

tactics.heading: Logging out in the lair
tactics.text:
Entering the lair without drawing aggression from the Kings is the most difficult part of setting up rotations, as well as Rex's safespot. To avoid having to repeat this process after a break, it is possible to logout in the Rex safespot; upon login the player will return to the same position.

Normally the player will receive constant damage from Spinolyps, however if enough of them can be killed or submerged in a short enough time while also not under aggression from any of the Kings, the player can be considered not in combat for the 10 seconds required to logout. This requires a fair amount of damage and is somewhat luck-based, but it can be done consistently.

tactics.heading: Tribrid rotation (3 Kings)
tactics.text:
Depending on gear and stats, the Kings can be killed quickly enough that there is very little overlap where multiple kings are alive and able to reach the player. Rex can easily be safespotted on the north-eastern, south-eastern, or north-western walls. With a long range ranged weapon, Prime can be reached from the northern side while staying out of the aggression ranges of Supreme and Rex. Supreme, however, should be defeated with melee, and is very close to Prime and Rex. Ideally, defeat Supreme after Prime so both aren't attacking the player at once.

A safe example rotation:

• Enter the room without drawing aggression and head counter-clockwise along the southern wall to the east side of the room.
• Attack and safespot Rex with magic along the east wall.
• Rotate counter-clockwise north and begin attacking Prime with ranged along the northern wall.
• Rotate counter-clockwise south and begin attacking Supreme with melee while staying as west as possible to avoid Rex when he spawns.
• Move to the eastern wall and safespot Rex again.

A faster rotation, best done with powerful equipment capable of defeating the Kings quickly.

• Enter the room and attack Supreme with melee, taking care to either avoid Prime or correctly pray against its attacks.
• Attack Rex with magic while dragging him to the north-western safespot, praying against Prime if they have noticed the player.
• Move to the north side and attack Prime with ranged, avoiding being too close to Supreme when he spawns.
• Attack Supreme with melee, avoiding Rex by staying as north/west as possible.
• Attack Rex with magic and use the north-west safespot again.

tactics.heading: Rex only
tactics.text: Once safely on the eastern wall of the lair, Rex can be attacked with a long range magic spell or staff without alerting the other Kings. As Rex approaches the eastern wall, pray Protect from Melee and move north or south until they are stuck on a wall and unable to reach the player. From there, you can attack with magic. Bring equipment with high range defence, as Spinolyps attack with Ranged-based magic and will be the main drain on your supplies. Players can utilise blood spells, Guthan's equipment, Regen bracelet, Hitpoints cape, the Saradomin godsword, or Sanguinesti staff to passively heal off Rex or Spinolyps to greatly extend trips. Players should use caution even while in the safe area. Others may attempt to kill you with Dagannoth Prime's AOE attack.

tactics.heading: Prime only
tactics.text: Prime can be reached in a similar manner to Rex from the eastern wall with ranged attacks. However, he will not approach the player and instead attack from a distance. This means the player needs to wait until it is safe to grab his drops or bring Telekinetic Grab to loot. Players can safely alternate between Rex and Prime if desired.

tactics.heading: Tips and tricks
tactics.text:
• The use of the dwarf multicannon with 1,000–2,000 cannonballs to kill Dagannoth Prime can be helpful to smooth out the rotation when fighting all three Kings. Place the cannon on Prime's spawning area, and only load cannonballs when it spawns; do not keep reloading, as it is less effective on Rex and Supreme and will cause them to attack you immediately upon being struck by a cannonball.
• Attune a portal in your house to Waterbirth. This will make travel time significantly easier and will negate the need of having your house in Rellekka or have redirecting scrolls for it.
• The suggested food is Super restore potions and Saradomin brews, although for simplicity and cost-effectiveness, sharks and a few Saradomin brews/Super restores for emergency will suffice. Bringing Guthan's set and Saradomin godsword can help reduce the use of food.
• If bringing Saradomin brews for food, always try to use a super restore before re-boosting your combat potions. If timed correctly, (with when you would normally reboost with a combat potion), this can greatly increase the amount of healing in your inventory with little to no loss of your damage output.
• Various Ancient Magicks can prove useful: Ice Barrage can be used to freeze Dagannoth Rex and Blood spells can be used in combination with a Trident of the Seas or swamp to heal.
• Antipoisons are important to bring, as the Spinolyps residing in the water around the lair will poison players. This is not the case if the player wears a Serpentine helm throughout the trip. Sanfew serums are also useful, as they function as both an antipoison and a super restore. However, the resistance to poison given to the player lasts half as long as that of an antidote++.
• There is a safe spot if you jump over the root slightly east of the Dagannoth Kings' ladder where you can 'peek' to see if there is someone within the arena. This is also a convenient spot to hop worlds looking for a vacant lair.
• Completion of the elite Fremennik Diary will cause Dagannoth Kings' bones to drop in noted form, substantially increasing trip profitability.
• Bringing an explorer's ring in place of a stamina potion for high alchemy will bring a bit more profit.
• If your melee stats are high enough (80+) and you're on a dagannoth task, consider using a Saradomin godsword or any other godsword as your spec weapon and your melee weapon to kill Supreme with, saving an inventory space.
• Bringing Divine boost potions along with a Menaphite Remedy can significantly increase how long your boosts last while saving an inventory slot over bringing 2 Super Combat and 2 ranging potions
• A shortcut requiring 85 Agility (or 80 Agility with the boost from a Summer pie) will skip the need for a rune throwing axe and pet rock, saving two inventory spaces. It is best to pre-boost prior to arriving at Waterbirth Island to minimise stat decay, especially if the player is not 81 Agility.
• Bringing a Falador Shield 4 helps, as its full prayer recharge twice a day is more than 1 Prayer Potion will restore.
• One sip of an extended stamina potion and the use of the level 85 agility shortcut lets you run all the way to the boss room.

tactics.heading: Overview
tactics.text:
Dark beasts can be killed with Melee, Magic or Ranged. Melee is the most effective against them and should be used in conjunction with high prayer bonus armour, such as Proselyte armour, for Protect from Melee. To maximise profit, players should bring a herb sack and a gem bag so that they can loot all herbs and gems they receive.

Dark beasts are good point-gaining tasks as they are not assigned in large numbers; even the extension doesn't give as much as other monsters, though this is balanced by their large health pool.

Dark beasts are a unique monster in that they are permanently aggressive towards the player no matter how long they stay there for. They will only use Magic as their first attack if they are attacked by the player first, or if they cannot attack the player with Melee. As such, while they can be hit with a dwarf multicannon, it is not recommended to bring one. Not much attention is required for killing them, apart from restoring prayer, though players who have unlocked Superior slayer monsters will need to pay attention for any night beasts that spawn. Unlike their normal brethren, they are not aggressive and will always initiate with a magic attack even if forced to be made aggressive.

Blood Moon, Bandos, and oathplate armour). However, as all of the boss's special attacks will always hit if not dodged, elite void armour with a void melee helm may suffice if death costs are a concern, especially when practicing.

tactics.heading: Overview
tactics.text: After completion of Desert Treasure II - The Fallen Empire, players are able to pluck abyssal potatoes from a growth found within the Scar, which can be fed to Brutus to initiate an encounter with Demonic Brutus, a much harder variant of the boss.

tactics.heading: Fight overview
tactics.text:
Unlike Brutus, Demonic Brutus' basic melee attack can hit through Protect from Melee, with a max hit of 4. He cannot be killed as part of a cow slayer task, and is immune to stat drains and enchanted bolts effects. Additionally, despite his name, Demonic Brutus is not classified as a demon.

Every two to three attacks, Brutus will use one of two special attacks; which one he chooses initially is random, but it will alternate between the two afterward in a predictable cycle.
• Charge - Brutus will spawn orthogonally across the player before charging, followed by three ghosts that repeat the same attack in rapid succession in a clockwise order, starting with the real Brutus.
• Slam - Brutus will disappear and spawn diagonally across the player, stomping the area in front of him, followed by three ghosts that repeat the same attack in rapid succession in a clockwise order, starting with the real Brutus.

Getting hit by any of the bulls will deal 45-56 damage each, resulting in a swift death if two bulls are missed in quick succession without healing. Additionally, if the player is standing too close to an obstacle when Brutus starts a special attack, they will be pushed into open space and will be unable to run for the special attack's duration, which effectively spells instant death.

There are two possible attack rotations, of which there are four possible positions for him to initiate a special attack. This will be performed in a cyclical pattern, as seen in the following demonstrations.

Upon reaching 500 (66.6%) health, Demonic Brutus' special attacks will be performed quicker, giving players little time to react to the attack.

Upon reaching 250 (33.33%) health, the boss's special attacks are performed in counterclockwise pattern instead, which necessitate different tiles to stand on to dodge depending on the attack rotation it chose.

Once Demonic Brutus' health reaches 0, it will exclaim and heal itself for 487 health, beginning phase 2 of the fight. The fight is almost identical to the first phase at 66.6% health (faster special attacks), so players must return to using the tiles for dodging the bulls moving clockwise and return to the counterclockwise tiles once Brutus is at 33.3% health again.

During phase 2, each time Brutus initiates a special attack, four orbs will appear above the player's head with their colour indicating the type of attack to pray against. These projectiles will land on the player whenever each bull attacks, dealing 18-20 damage; the first three projectiles are always magic-melee-ranged, with the fourth being random. These projectiles will also trigger auto-retaliate, so it's recommended to have it turned off so it doesn't cause the player to path into the special attacks.

A simple strategy to avoid the majority of damage while still keeping dodge timing using the above tiles is to keep praying melee and just tank the initial mage orb. Once you step onto the second dodge tile you can then flick the range + random prayer without having to worry about further movement commands. While this does involve you tanking a little damage (18-20), most players die during the fight when they get hit by Brutus and his ghosts while trying to focus on flicking prayers.

gearNotes.heading: Special attack weapons
gearNotes.text:
Experienced players and players with high combat levels may not need any food while fighting gorillas, as the healing effect from the Saradomin godsword's special attack will restore enough Hitpoints, especially with a lightbearer. If you don't have a Saradomin godsword, you can also use toxic blowpipe's special attack to heal.

Multi-hit melee special attack weapons, such as dragon claws, burning claws, and even the dragon dagger, can potentially lose out on damage if used at the wrong time or if the player is in endgame gear. This is because the subsequent hitsplats will be nulled if the gorilla ends up changing prayers in the process, as the prayer switching and landing hits will apply on different ticks. If using these special attacks, it is thus recommended to use them immediately after the gorilla switches away from praying protect from melee. This maximizes the potential damage done and can quickly let the player switch back to ranged, allowing them to sometimes skip having to do the step-back method.

If using the Scorching bow as the primary ranged weapon, its special attack can be useful for the bonus Burn damage and the binding effect, which can be utilised to allow extra leeway when switching prayers from ranged or magic, making the step-back method easier. Care should be taken however, as if the gorilla takes too long to melee attack the player, it may unexpectedly switch to using ranged or magic instead as an "anti-safespot" mechanic.

Please note that any Burn damage is cleared when the Demonic Gorilla changes prayers, which is mainly relevant for Burning claws and the Scorching bow.

gearNotes.heading: Equipment
gearNotes.text:
Melee is a preferred style to use at demonics for its cost, ease of use, and early access to Arclight, one of the strongest weapons to fight Demonics with. If choosing to reduce switches, it is generally recommended to camp melee equipment when available.

Ranged is generally the 2nd style used at demonic gorillas due to its power and accessibility. The Toxic blowpipe is one of the strongest weapons against Demonic gorillas (especially with the on-task accuracy boost from the imbued slayer helm or black mask) and can perform well with minimal switches. A Bow of Faerdhinen or Scorching bow can utilise even less switches and still performs well. The Twisted bow can deal large damage without much lost dps.
