tactics.heading: Overview
tactics.text: Demonic gorillas can be fought in the Crash Site Cavern after the completion of Monkey Madness II. They are popular monsters to kill as they drop valuable zenyte shards, which are used to create some of the best jewellery in the game, as well as components for ballistae. They count as black demons or monkeys for the purposes of a Slayer task.

tactics.heading: Requirements
tactics.text: • Completion of Quest Monkey Madness II to enter the Crash Site Cavern.

tactics.heading: Recommendations
tactics.text:
• High combat stats. Although not required, see the skill levels below for an indication of the advised stats:
  • Level 80 Attack or higher
  • Level 85 Strength or higher
  • Level 80 Defence or higher
  • Level 85 Ranged or higher
  • Level 80 Hitpoints or higher
  • Level 70 Prayer or higher
  • Level 70 Magic or higher (for magic defence)

• Completion of Quest Recipe for Disaster for access to Barrows gloves.
• Completion of Quest Dragon Slayer II for access to the Ava's assembler.
  • Alternatively, completion of Quest Animal Magnetism for access to the Ava's accumulator.
• Completion of Quest Shadow of the Storm for access to the arclight.
• Having access to the imbued version of the Slayer helmet or black mask.

tactics.heading: Transportation
tactics.text:
The entrance to the Crash Site Cavern may be found north-west of the Grand Tree through the opening in the fence. Once through the fence run north-east to enter the cavern.

Note that some parts of the cavern are a multi-combat area, which solo players may wish to avoid.

There are a few ways to get to the Grand Tree.

• Use the royal seed pod's teleport option which takes you to the base of the Grand Tree. This is the fastest travel option.
• Use a Spirit tree to the Gnome stronghold and run north and then north-west to the gap in the fence.
• Use the Gnome glider to Ta Quir Priw which will take you to the top of the Grand Tree. Descend the tree and run north-west to the gap in the fence.

tactics.heading: Mechanics
tactics.text:
Demonic gorillas have a few unique mechanics that players should be aware of before fighting them, making them a difficult foe to inexperienced players.

In order to kill demonic gorillas, it is required to bring at least two combat styles, as they utilise protection prayers in combat. This is generally melee and ranged, due to their cheapness and the gorilla's lower Defence level. Magic may be used, however this is generally a worse option given the higher costs incurred from runes and the gorillas having a higher magic defence roll.

tactics.heading: Attack styles
tactics.text:
Demonic gorillas use all three forms of combat, each one hitting up to 30 damage.

• Magic attack: The gorilla rears up and dangles its forelegs, then emits a green orb from its mouth.
• Melee attack: The gorilla swipes its claws downwards at the player.
• Ranged attack: The gorilla uses its two front claws to grab a small boulder and throw it at the player.
• Boulder toss: The gorilla beats its chest to drop a boulder, which will appear above the player's position at the time it performs this attack. Players will take 33% of their health as damage if they don't move away from it. The boulder has an area of effect of 1x1. This ability is only used when the gorilla is using Ranged or Magic. The gorillas will not use this attack while using melee.

tactics.heading: Attack style switching
tactics.text:
Demonic gorillas start with a random attack style, initiating combat as soon as they are attacked by a player.

They will switch attack styles after three (3) missed hits against the player (i.e., no damage is taken), regardless if the player's protection prayer blocked them or not. The boulder toss does not count towards these missed hits. It is helpful to count each missed hit in order to predict the next attack style switch.

However, the third attack must be prayed correctly against for the gorilla to consistently change its attack style. When the gorilla switches its attack style, it will emit a "bone-chilling scream," auditory cue at the same time as they say over their head.

tactics.heading: Prayer switching (gorilla)
tactics.text:
When a gorilla spawns, it will stand idle for a brief second before pounding its chest, changing its protection prayer. Each gorilla uses all three protection prayers (Protect from Melee, Protect from Magic, and Protect from Missiles), but only one of them is active at any given time. The protection prayer gives them complete immunity towards attacks of that style, and it cannot be bypassed with a dragon scimitar, but it can be bypassed with Verac's set.

The gorilla will switch prayers against another style after having been dealt damage at least four times, alongside a total of 70 damage in the style(s) it is not protecting against. This is in total damage, not damage from one combat style. For example, if a gorilla takes 49 Melee damage but then is hit for 26 damage from Ranged, it will immediately use Protect from Missiles. This is usually only an advantage if the gorilla prays against Magic, since their Magic level and Defence bonuses are too high for Magic to hit them reasonably.

When the gorilla changes protection prayers, the player(s) attacking it will end combat, so it is important to change gear immediately and re-click on the gorilla to resume combat.

Note: While an ancient godsword's blood sacrifice can cause the gorilla to swap to Protect from Magic if it reaches the threshold, attacking on the same tick as the blood sacrifice while also causing a prayer swap will cause it to become nulled.

tactics.heading: Boulder attack
tactics.text: When the gorilla is using Ranged or Magic only, the gorilla will sometimes toss a boulder, which will appear above the player's position when it performed this attack. Players will take 33% of their health as damage if they don't move away at least one tile away from it. The boulder has an area of effect of 1x1, and a shadow can be seen where the boulder will fall. The gorillas will not use this attack while using Melee. This attack does not count toward the three "missed" hits required for the gorilla to change its attack style.

tactics.heading: Predicting their attack styles
tactics.text:
Although the demonic gorillas will switch their attack style to a randomly chosen attack style, there is a good method to predict their next attack style in 83% of the situations:
• If the previous attack style was Melee: They will switch to either Magic or Ranged, there is no way to predict this. However, you can switch your prayer to Magic or Ranged, and guess correctly 50% of the time. Pray your lowest defence between Magic or Range to have a better chance of blocking the damage if guessing wrong.
• If the previous attack style was Magic: They will switch to either Melee or Ranged. To predict this, move away from the gorilla:
  • If the demonic gorilla follows the player, it will attack with Melee next.
  • If the demonic gorilla stays on its tile, it will attack with Ranged next.
• If the previous attack style was Ranged: They will switch to either Magic or Melee. To predict this, move away from the gorilla:
  • If the demonic gorilla follows the player, it will attack with Melee next.
  • If the demonic gorilla stays on its tile, it will attack with Magic next.

If an attack style switch is needed and the gorilla starts off the new attack pattern with a boulder, they will follow up with either Ranged or Magic attacks, so pray accordingly.

tactics.heading: Item switches
tactics.text:
As the player will have a relatively high damage output against the gorillas (especially with higher-end weaponry such as emberlight and the scorching bow), it is recommended not to bring too many switches when killing demonic gorillas. It is very common to bring a few switches, primarily a body, weapon and amulet swap. Gloves, boots and rings are not recommended for swaps, as the demons' low swap thresholds would make these switches difficult to make optimally.

It is highly recommended to use a convenient keybind (a.k.a. F-keys) for the prayer and inventory tabs, as this makes it easier to quickly switch between both interfaces.

If the player is staying for a prolonged period of time, bringing a set of Guthan's can help in restoring health in the event that too much damage is taken, or the Saradomin godsword fails to deal enough damage with its special attack. Demonic Offering can also be used to restore additional prayer points and grant more Prayer experience than an Ash sanctifier or leaving the Malicious ashes on the ground.

tactics.heading: Prayer swapping priority
tactics.text:
Prioritise using Protect from Magic first, followed by Protect from Missiles and/or Protect from Melee. Watch the gorilla's attacks closely, and always count missed hits and/or listen/watch for the scream indicating an attack style switch.

After three missed hits that are not correctly prayed against, the gorilla will a) keep using the same attack style for the next 3 attacks or b) switch to another style. This makes it important to change to the correct protection prayer in spite of occasionally taking zero damage.

Off the correct prayer: If the hit was either a ranged or magic hit the following attack will always be the same as the one just used, or a melee attack. For example, if prayer is switched before getting hit a 0 by the third magic attack, the gorilla will keep using magic for the next 3 hits unless it starts walking towards the player, indicating an incoming melee attack. Watch the gorilla's position to avoid "guessing" the next attack style after missing a prayer switch on the third ranged or magic hit.

tactics.heading: Example fight
tactics.text:
• A player engages a Demonic Gorilla using the Protect from Missiles prayer while using Melee equipment. The player has Protect from Magic active.
• The Demonic Gorilla opens with a Magic attack. The player takes zero (0) damage for three consecutive "missed" hits. Because of these three missed hits, the gorilla screams and switches its attack style to Ranged:
  • Meanwhile, the player deals 70+ Melee damage, causing the gorilla to switch its protection prayer to Protect from Melee.
  • As soon as the player sees and/or hears the attack style switch, they quickly activate Protect from Missiles and swap to their Ranged gear to counter the gorilla's prayer change to Protect from Melee.
• The player takes zero (0) damage for two consecutive hits, dodges a boulder attack, then another zero (0) damage hit with Protect from Missiles active:
  • The missed hits cause the gorilla to scream indicating an attack style switch, and the gorilla starts to move closer, indicating an incoming Melee attack. The player quickly switches to Protect from Melee.
  • Meanwhile, the player deals 30+ Ranged damage while at least one (1) tile away from the Demonic gorilla. The gorilla follows the player because it is using a Melee attack.
• The player continues to fight the gorilla with their Ranged gear while praying Protect from Melee. The player takes zero (0) damage three consecutive times from the gorilla using the Melee attack style:
  • The player then deals an additional 20+ Ranged damage, causing the gorilla to activate Protect from Missiles. The player quickly swaps to their Melee equipment and activates Protect from Magic in preparation for the next attack.
• The gorilla instead attacks with a Ranged attack, causing the player to take damage. The player quickly activates Protect from Missiles while attacking with Melee equipment.
• The player deals 70+ Damage with their Melee gear, causing the gorilla to activate Protect from Melee.
  • The player also receives three "missed" hits of zero (0) damage, causing the gorilla to switch their attack style to Magic (Melee is also a possibility).
  • The player swiftly switches to their Ranged gear and activates Protect from Magic.
• This cycle will continue for the rest of the fight until the Demonic Gorilla is dead: anticipating their attack styles, counting missed hits, choosing the correct protection prayers, avoiding boulder attacks, and gear switching to deal damage. Always try to predict their attack styles as listed above.

tactics.heading: Duo strategy
tactics.text:
Since there is also a multicombat area with demonic gorillas, they can be fought against in a team. An effective method therefore is duo'ing with one player in full Dharok's equipment on 1 Hitpoint, while the other player is tanking the gorilla's attacks, as the player in the Dharok's equipment will have very high damage output.

With this duo strategy, one player starts attacking a demonic gorilla and, after the gorilla starts fighting back, the other will assist in the fighting. For the first player, it is advised to bring standard equipment, while for the other player it is advised to bring full Dharok's equipment for melee attacks, as the player doesn't have to worry about being attacked (if the strategy is done correctly by both players) and this equipment offers high damage output for Melee attacks.

• Make sure that the gorillas are never aggroed towards the player in full Dharok's while they are at 1 Hitpoints.
• The tanking player should bring runes to cast the Boost Potion Share spell on the Lunar spellbook. Make sure both players have accept-aid enabled.
• Don't bring too many item switches, as it will be difficult to keep up with them, since multiple players will deal damage.
• Consider bringing a full Guthan's equipment to infinitely heal Hitpoints on the tanking account.
• Try to time attacking the gorilla simultaneously with both accounts, to prevent attacking the gorilla while it just switched its protection prayer.

options.text: Sanguinesti staff > Trident of the Swamp > Trident of the Seas

gearNotes.heading: Equipment
gearNotes.text:
The recommended gear setup maximises Magic damage bonus for maximum efficiency.

Prioritise Prayer bonus over Magic attack bonus, since the archaeologist's low Magic level makes him very easy to hit despite his high Magic defence.

Lower level players or ironmen seeking runite limbs can use Iban Blast for longer but consistent kills.

gearNotes.heading: Inventory
gearNotes.text:
Recommended inventory:
• 2-3 prayer potions (forgotten brews or moonlight moth mixes can be used to supplement these due to the excess of inventory slots)
• Antipoison (can drink a dose when banking; is needed only to block poison from the spine mushroom on the path to the boss)
• Digsite pendant with Fossil Island teleport option unlocked
• Ring of dueling to resupply at Ferox Enclave
• A few pieces of food (in case you take a hit)
• Runes to cast High Alchemy
• Magic boost if using a powered staff (saturated heart, forgotten brew, etc.)
• Holy wrench
• Axe for chopping swamp vine
• Rake for clearing vines, if not using the rubber cap mushroom or magic mushtree to cross the swamp

tactics.heading: Overview
tactics.text:
The Deranged archaeologist is a boss located on Fossil Island. A simple mistake during the fight can cause instant death due to his special attack.

He attacks with both Ranged and melee but will use only Ranged if the player does not stand in melee distance. Although his Magic defence stat is quite high, his Magic level is very low, which makes him very easy to hit with Magic. The most effective way to kill the archaeologist is to use Magic from several tiles away while using Protect from Missiles and avoiding his special attack. Note that the archaeologist can use melee attacks on tiles immediately diagonal to him.

tactics.heading: Suggested skills
tactics.text:
• 50 Magic for Iban's staff
  • 75 Magic for Fire Wave or powered staves
• 40 Prayer for Protect from Missiles

tactics.heading: Transportation
tactics.text: An axe and rake are required in order to manoeuvre throughout the tar swamp effectively. If you have the Mycelium Transportation System unlocked and the House on the Hill teleport option unlocked on the Digsite pendant, teleport to the House on the Hill and take the Magic Mushtree to the Sticky Swamp. (Otherwise, get to Fossil Island via the Canal barge and run through the Swamp to reach the southernmost area.) Run south and cut the thick vine with your axe, as well as bringing a rake for the smaller vines, to clear a path. Continue south past the spined mushroom. If it attacks you, drink 1 dose of your antipoison. Turn on Protect from Missiles and climb over the decaying trunk to begin the fight.

tactics.heading: Special Attack
tactics.text:
The archaeologist will shout and throw three orange books which explode on impact with the ground, four ticks (2.4 seconds) after he speaks. One book always hits exactly where the player was standing when the books were thrown. This book will burst into two additional books which also explode on impact. It can be easily dodged by reacting to his overhead text, and then click to an opposite diagonal corner of the arena, at least 9 tiles away.

The two other books from the initial attack, as well as the two additional books originating from the central book's impact, will typically hit somewhere in a 5x5 area surrounding the original location of the player. On rare occasions, some of these four books may hit up to a 9x9 area around the player's original location.

The damage from the explosions ignores all defence (including armour bonuses) and protection prayers. Each explosion deals maximum damage (up to 56) on the tile where it impacts, but it will deal reduced damage (up to 18) to all immediately adjacent tiles.

It is impossible for two books to target the same square. This means the maximum possible damage taken from the three initial books is 92: a direct hit for 56 plus twice 18 from the two indirect hits on surrounding tiles. The two subsequent books originating in the central square could then deal an additional 74 damage, again through one direct hit and one indirect hit. Do note that this series of events is highly unlikely, not only requiring all books to land in the most unfortunate locations, but also requiring the player to stand still and the books to all deal their maximum damage.

The attack has a 25-tick (15 second) internal cooldown and has a 1/3rd chance to be used instead of a normal attack. He can use this as his first attack against players initiating a fight. This means that players can relax after each special attack, knowing the Deranged archaelogist won't use it for the next 15 seconds — which with relatively good gear, he will be defeated before getting to use it again.

Note: The attack will deal damage on impact even if the archaeologist dies before the books explode.

tactics.heading: Avoidance Strategy
tactics.text:
A strategy to avoid all damage from the special attack is to run on a straight line out of the 9x9 area centred around your initial position as soon as the text appears over the archaeologist's head.

If the player begins moving on the first tick after the text appears, running in a straight line will take the player 8 tiles away from the centre book's target by the time the books detonate, which avoids all damage. If movement begins one tick later, the player can still take damage, since they will be on the edge of the 9x9 area when the books detonate. In this case it is technically possible to take up to 74 damage (by receiving one direct and one indirect hit), but the odds of this happening are extremely small.

Players who have especially good reflexes can try to predict the books' impact locations and dodge them by running to a safe tile within the 9x9 area, but this is not recommended. Even if successful, the player can be subsequently hit by the secondary books which burst from the centre.

options.text: Sulphur blades / Glacial temotli / Earthbound tecpatl
Any staff that can autocast demonbane spells
Dual macuahuitl or other multi-hit melee weapons

gearNotes.heading: Equipment
gearNotes.text:
Ranged is the recommended attack style for Doom. The twisted bow is the strongest weapon to use, given Doom's Magic level of 275. The demonbane scorching bow is the next best alternative, as its damage only slightly trails behind the twisted bow and is far cheaper. The faster attack speed of the scorching bow is suboptimal: it generates 25% more acid, it's more difficult to attack at every opportunity while avoiding damage, and it misses an attack opportunity at the end of car phase (which does not last a multiple of 4 ticks).

In order to face the deeper delve levels comfortably, players must have both demonbane melee and magic swaps. The cheapest melee demonbane weapon is a Darklight, while the most efficient magic demonbane is Superior Demonbane coupled with a skull sceptre, although the Slayer's staff is much easier to obtain. Inferior Demonbane may be used but this will waste another inventory slot since soul or aether runes are required for Death Charge.

Doom is technically weakest to melee crush attacks, but the fight has many mechanics that make melee inadvisable.

gearNotes.heading: Special attack weapons
gearNotes.text:
The Zaryte crossbow is the most powerful special attack weapon and should be paired with regular ruby bolts (e) for cost efficiency as the dragon variant provides no additional benefit in this scenario. When to use it will vary - at delve levels 1-4, a successful special attack can speed up progress. At delve levels 6 and beyond players may either spec at the start of or during the burrow phase. Most players will prefer reserving the special at the start of burrow phase, as this guarantees the crossbow's special and maximising Death Charge, however on deeper delves an early crossbow spec may result in starting shield phase before setting up rockblock. On the other hand, failing to deal enough damage, especially after delve 8+, may result in shockwaves which are highly detrimental and should be avoided at all costs.

For players without a Zaryte crossbow, their next best option is a crystal halberd, which guarantees a minimum of 46 damage on each melee punish (two bonus hits of 23). The halberd matches the guaranteed damage from a Scythe of Vitur (three bonus hits of 15), has very useful bonus range and is much more available to players. A toxic blowpipe or eldritch nightmare staff can be used to benefit for much deeper delves, since they are guaranteed maximum hits on volatile earth. Bringing extra switches for melee punish is not recommended, as the damage increase is marginal and inventory spots are very valuable.

Rosewood blowpipe special attacks are a viable budget alternative to dragon knife special attacks, as its max hit is only 2 lower and it costs significantly less ( coins and coins per special respectively).

When car phase starts, use a Zaryte crossbow special or dump 3-4 dragon knife special attacks. At deeper delves, using short-ranged weapons can be difficult without a roadblock setup. The goal is to deal enough damage to Doom so the player can skip its dangerous earthen shield phase (or at least kill Doom before it uses shockwaves).

A Lightbearer is highly recommended over other rings as special attacks are important on key phases of the fight. Upgraded Death Charge from Yama is also very strong, as Death Charge procs on both Doom and its larvae. With upgraded Death Charge and a Lightbearer, players can restore 40-50% energy per delve level. Special attack energy does not restore between floors, and a floor completion will reset special attack energy restoration (i.e it will always take 30/15 seconds for the first restore tick on the next floor).

Defence-draining weapons are not recommended. Doom has a defence reduction cap of 60, has guaranteed accuracy on several phases, and resets defence on each floor.

gearNotes.heading: Summary
gearNotes.text:
Best in slot:
• Bring a Zaryte crossbow and noxious halberd.
• On 1-4, immediately crossbow spec. Use halberd for punishes.
• On 5-8+, do not immediately crossbow spec.
• When car phase starts, crossbow spec as your first attack.

Budget:
• Bring a toxic blowpipe and a crystal halberd.
• On all phases, use halberd spec on melee punishes.
• Toxic blowpipe spec can restore the maximum health possible on volatile earth or ranged larvae if deemed necessary.

gearNotes.heading: Masori vs Elite void
gearNotes.text:
The best primary ranged gear sets are Elite Void Knight equipment or fortified masori. Both give a very similar performance, but there are various factors that can influence the gear used.

With a scorching bow, elite void with seeking dragon arrows is recommended. It has about the same DPS as Masori, and has higher damage on the 100% accuracy phases of doom. Elite void is also much cheaper and has very low reclaim costs, which minimises death costs and allows players to upgrade other slots.

With a twisted bow, either masori or elite void may be used. Masori will provide additional accuracy outside of burrow phases, but will trail behind in damage compared to elite void, which shines much better there. Masori also marginally protects the player better from Doom's attacks, since many of Doom's attacks are already highly accurate or outright ignore armour values. Elite void is still better under most circumstances since frequent deaths in masori will greatly deplete the player's death coffer, while elite void has a much lower cost, being four times less with an ornate anguish necklace or halved with a necklace of rupture.

gearNotes.heading: Spellbook choice
gearNotes.text:
If using the Eye of Ayak, players may choose to use the Lunar spellbook for access to Cure Me with Spellbook Swap for Death Charge, though keep in mind the Eye will not disrupt the Doom's shield phase charging and will increase death costs if not protected.

If not using the Eye of Ayak, players should stay on the Arceuus spellbook with runes for Death Charge. Thralls are not recommended, as their attacks cause Doom to spread much more acid.

As discussed, Masori equipment is marginally better with a twisted bow. Elite void ranged is better with a scorching bow, is only marginally worse with a twisted bow, and is much cheaper with much lower reclaim costs.

To deal with larvae, players should bring a one way demonbane (or multi-hit) swap for each combat style. Bring a Darklight, Arclight or Emberlight for melee larva. Bring any staff that can auto-cast demonbane spells, though a cheaper staff like slayer's staff is recommended to reduce death costs. Use Superior Demonbane instead of Dark Demonbane on autocast, as it's harder to brew below its casting requirement. If you're not using Death Charge, you can bring runes for the lower levelled Inferior Demonbane.

It's worth bringing a multi-hit melee weapon for the melee punish attack (discussed above). Devoting inventory slots to marginally improve a melee punish — such as melee strength gear, void melee helm or a super combat potion (neither of which even increases the bonus damage) — is not worthwhile. Halberds can avoid melee range (which requires a quick click off to avoid a melee attack) and give useful positional flexibility around acid.

gearNotes.heading: Inventory setups
gearNotes.text:
• Twisted bow + Zaryte crossbow for special attacks
• Scorching bow, Darklight, and Slayer's staff (e) for ranged, melee, and magic larvae.
• Scythe of Vitur or Noxious halberd for melee punish. If delving at 13+ a halberd is recommended to minimise splatters; otherwise a scythe is more ideal.
• Elite void ranger equipment, only if players do not mind the extra swaps for increased damage in car phases.
• If the player doesn't have Dizana's quiver, an inventory spot would instead be replaced with ammo.
• 1-2 divine ranging potions, 1-3 regular ranging potions or Armadyl brews
• Supplies such as Anglerfish, Saradomin brews, Super restores, and / or Armadyl brews depending on how confident the player is on avoiding damage and how deep they are capable of delving.
• An Extended anti-venom+ or best available anti-venom potion.
• Mokhaiotl waystone for faster return trips, or a pendant of Ates.
• Divine rune pouch with runes for Thralls and Death Charge. Requires an extra inventory slot without Aether runes.

• Necklace of anguish can easily be replaced with Amulet of fury or Amulet of glory to lower death costs. Alternatively, using a Anguish ornament kit makes the item untradeable so it is always kept on death.
• Scorching bow + Crystal halberd for special attacks on the melee punish.
• Darklight, and Slayer's staff (e) for melee and magic larvae.
• Ranged Void Knight equipment.
• Best available blowpipe for better damage during burrowing (car) phase.
• 1-2 divine ranging potions, 1-3 regular ranging potions or Armadyl brews
• Supplies such as Anglerfish, Saradomin brews, Super restores, and / or Armadyl brews depending on how confident the player is on avoiding damage and how deep they are capable of delving.
• An Extended anti-venom+ or best available anti-venom potion.
• Mokhaiotl waystone for faster return trips, or a pendant of Ates.
• Divine rune pouch with runes for Thralls and Death Charge. Requires an extra inventory slot without Aether runes.

tactics.heading: Overview
tactics.text:
After completion of The Final Dawn, players can challenge the Doom of Mokhaiotl, who is found in the Ruins of Mokhaiotl by returning through the northernmost entrance.

Similar to Yama, players who die fighting the Doom are sent back to the lobby area instead of their respawn point, where their graves are also located. Players will have their reclamation fee reduced by 75% until they have 20 total delves, after which the standard death cost will apply.

tactics.heading: Requirements
tactics.text: • Completion of Quest The Final Dawn

tactics.heading: Recommendations
tactics.text:
• Completion of Quest While Guthix Sleeps and a scorching bow
• Completion of Quest A Kingdom Divided for access to Yama; having unlocked double Death Charge via the rite of vile transference is helpful.
• Completion of Diary Hard Western Provinces Diary for access to elite void and the crystal halberd
• 90+ Ranged
• 43 Prayer minimum for access to all three protection prayers.
  • 62 Prayer to unlock and use Deadeye.
  • 74 Prayer and 70 Defence to unlock and use Rigour. Highly recommended.
• 75 Agility for the pit jump shortcut in the ruins.

tactics.heading: Transportation
tactics.text:
• The Mokhaiotl waystone is a single use item that teleports players to the centre of the ruins, just south of the pit jump shortcut.
• The pendant of Ates teleport to Kastori takes players south-east of the lift platform that takes players just south of the entrance to Mokhaiotl.
• The Quetzal Transport System can also be used to travel to near the boss.
  • Tal Teklan - West of the lift to the boss, a bank is available in town.
  • Kastori - South-east of the lift to the boss, no bank available.

West of the lift platform underground, a chest can be opened to obtain two ancient teleporters, which can be used to speed up the run north to the entrance to Mokhaiotl. It is optimal to place the initial teleporter a tile or two north of the lift platform, then placing the destination teleporter adjacent to the door to skip the delay before entering the door after teleporting.

tactics.heading: Fight overview
tactics.text:
As a delve boss, defeating the Doom will cause it to delve deeper into the archive and grow in power. Pursuing it into deeper delve levels increases the difficulty of the fight, up to delve level 8.

The initial delves are similar in difficulty to the Corrupted Gauntlet, in which the boss has highly damaging attacks but is easily mitigated with prayer, though the frequency of prayer swaps will begin to gradually increase, initially capping at delve level 4. The first significant increase starts at delve level 6, where players must carefully position the boss to avoid its slam attacks, then a second minor increase at delve level 7 where the rock attacks are launched extremely fast. The final increase is at level 8, where two boulders are launched instead of one, and can quickly overwhelm inexperienced players, as it may be hectic to dodge both incoming rocks while praying against its projectiles at the same time.

The Doom of Mokhaiotl starts with 525 Hitpoints and 558 combat level. For each delve level it gains 25 Hitpoints and 50 combat levels (except for delve 7, where it retains 650 hitpoints) up to delve level 8. On delve level 9 and onwards, it has 625 Hitpoints. While Doom's stats remain the same across all delves, the max hit of its attacks gradually increases, capping out at delve level 8.

Delve levels beyond 8, referred to as deep delves, retain the same mechanics as delve level 8, but the fight's persistent mechanics (primarily acid blood) can make the fight challenging, especially on very deep delves.

The Doom has a Defence level of 90 and Magic level of 275. It possesses +300 stab and slash defence, +60 crush defence, and +160 magic and overall ranged defence. The boss's defensive stats remain identical across delve levels. Doom has a defence drain cap of 30, meaning that its Defence can only be lowered to a minimum of 60. It is not immune to poison, though any hits that would inflict venom are converted to poison instead.

At the start of each level, the Doom will not appear until the player exits the prompt (either by advancing the prompt, moving, or activating a prayer).

tactics.heading: Mechanics
tactics.text:
The Doom's standard attack consists of a single projectile, with its colour and shape indicating the combat style to pray against:

• blue for magic,
• green for ranged,
• and red for melee (used at delve level 2 and higher)

These attacks calculate damage on impact and (as such) can be protected against after the Doom launches the projectile. An unblocked attack has a max hit of 47, which gradually increases to 65 damage by delve level 8. The travel speed of these projectiles is slow at the first few delve levels, but steadily increases through delve level 6. The Doom’s attack speed also increases through delve level 7, at which point the Doom attacks at a 4 tick speed.

Standing next to the Doom will result in a melee attack (whipping the player with its tongue) that deals up to 40 damage. Protect from Melee reduces the damage of the attack by 50%.

The Doom has a multitude of special attacks and hazards, with various additions, enhancements and combinations as the delve level increases.

tactics.heading: Demonic larvae
tactics.text:
Occasionally, demonic larvae will drop from the ceiling and begin moving towards the Doom. These larvae will always spawn around the player's position.

If a larva reaches the very centre of the Doom, it will heal it and damage the player, as well as gaining one stack of Demonic Charge. This initially starts at 10 health healed and 1 damage dealt. For every stack of this debuff, the healing given and damage dealt from larvae reaching Doom increases by 1; e.g a sixth larvae that reaches Doom will heal it for 16 health and deal 6 damage to the player. Stacks are not reset between delve levels, so it is important to kill the demonic larvae when the opportunity allows.

Players can deal additional damage to the Doom's actual health by prolonging the shield phase. By interrupting the Special Beam with weak demonbane attacks rather than breaking the shield quickly, and killing demonic larvae before they reach the Doom, damage is stored and applied to the Doom's health, up to a maximum of 50 damage. Each larva killed contributes approximately 3 damage, so roughly 15 larvae are needed to reach the cap. This is slow and mainly useful for Mokhaiotl Drift.

Demonic larvae have 2 Hitpoints and can only be one-shot by demonbane weapons, multi-hit weapons, and the Eye of Ayak; any other weapon will only deal 1 damage, requiring two attacks to kill one. They may be attacked on attack cooldown: non-demonbane attacks incur the weapon's attack delay afterwards, whereas demonbane attacks and the Eye of Ayak will not incur any attack delay. Fast non-demonbane weapons (e.g. a blowpipe) may be used to overwrite the original attack cooldown, allowing for faster attacks on the Doom.

When demonic larvae are killed, they will explode and deal up to 21 damage in a 3x3 area; however, if this hits the Doom, it will deal 5-10 damage (or 100 shield damage) instead, and the player will not take any damage from the explosion. Try to avoid killing larvae when they are out of Doom's range.

The demonic larvae will begin to increase in intensity as the delve level increases:
• At delve levels 1-3, they will have a random protection prayer active (or none at delve level 1)
• At delve levels 4+, they will have two protection prayers active, with their colour indicating which combat style to use: blue for magic, green for ranged, and red for melee. Melee demonic larvae will only appear during the shield phase.
• At delve levels 5-7, two larvae will spawn at a time outside of the shield phase.
• At delve levels 8+, a giant demonic ranged/magic larva can spawn outside of the shield phase. These larvae have doubled health (4 instead of 2), have a 4x4 AoE explosion around itself and tripled penalties if allowed to reach the Doom; e.g a missed large larvae, at 0 charge stacks, will heal Doom for 30 hitpoints and deal 3 damage to the player.

Larvae will despawn after ~20 or so seconds have passed after spawning, however this can only occur when the Doom has repositioned itself during the burrowing phase, or if the Doom has been completely surrounded by boulders. They will always be able to reach the Doom otherwise.

tactics.heading: Rock Throw
tactics.text:
The Doom launches a large rock into the air, exploding after 7 ticks into multiple falling rocks that target the area where the player stood, indicated by looming shadows. As the player descends further down, the number of falling rocks and projectiles increases.

When the rock explodes, the player's current tile will be marked for a solid rock, which if not avoided, will push the player to a random valid tile within a 3x3 AoE of it. Getting hit by any rock (including the solid rock) will deal up to 21 damage, so it is important to avoid marked tiles once the rock explodes. Additionally, the player's overhead protection prayers will be disabled, and the rock will also launch one, two or three additional projectiles (refer below) at the same time. These projectiles are always ranged or magic, and can never be melee.

The rock throw attack will increase in intensity as the delve level increases:
• At delve level 1, only one projectile is launched.
• At delve levels 2 and 3, two projectiles are launched, with the second landing one tick after the first.
  • The projectiles will never repeat in a row (i.e. a ranged projectile will always be followed up with a magic projectile and vice versa)
• At delve levels 4+, three projectiles are launched, and often sync up with the Doom's standard attacks, which can result in the player being hit 4 times in 4 ticks.
• At delve level 7, the projectiles will reach the player 2 ticks (1.2s) after the debris lands.
• At delve level 8, two rock throws are performed, which will always be identical.
  • To avoid damage from the attack, the player must pray after the second rock explodes; projectiles from the first rock will not reach the player until this occurs.
  • Additionally, to avoid damage from the shattered debris, players should stand on tiles targeted by the first rock shortly after the second rock explodes; the debris will never overlap, meaning that a tile targeted by the first rock cannot be targeted by the second rock.

tactics.heading: Special Beam Cannon
tactics.text:
The Doom enters a defensive stance and begins to charge up, indicated by a yellow charge bar appearing. If allowed to charge completely, the Doom will unleash the Special Beam Cannon, dealing 60 damage. This increases to 80 at delves level 4-5, and deals 99 damage at delve level 6+. This makes it the highest priority attack to deal with, as the Doom will also charge faster at higher delve levels.

There are three distinct occasions in which the charge bar appears, and the player must attack the Doom to interrupt/reset the charge bar. Attacks whilst charging are 100% accurate and will always result in a successful hit.
• Melee Charge - on all delve levels, the Doom will pray against ranged and magic () and begin charging. This is always accompanied by the Rock Throw attack. Only a melee attack will interrupt the charge.
• Shield Charge - at delve levels 3+, the Doom will begin using a demonic shield with 500 shield health and begin charging constantly. Only demonbane (excluding holy water) will reset the charge.
• Burrow Charge - At delve levels 5+, the Doom's burrowed form (commonly referred to as "car phase") will always be charging constantly. Any attack will reset the charge.

tactics.heading: Melee punish
tactics.text:
Whenever the Doom begins a melee charge, only a melee attack will interrupt the charge (this interruption can be done whilst on attack cooldown and this attack overwrites the original attack cooldown), which will also deal bonus damage that deals damage, where is the player's visible Strength bonus. As such, offensive prayers and set bonuses (such as Void Knight equipment) will not increase the bonus damage. When using multi-hit weapons such as the dual macuahuitl or the crystal halberd's special attack, the bonus damage duplicates itself once per hitsplat.

Melee charges are only performed in tandem with rock throw attacks, but is not always guaranteed. This will never occur in the rock throws that are used right before shockwaves during the volatile earth mechanic.

The Doom's next attack is additionally delayed by several ticks if melee punished; this starts with a 8 tick delay at delves 1 and 2, 7 ticks at delves 3-6, and 6 ticks at delves 7+. Using any weapon with an attack speed of 5 or lower, such a scythe of Vitur or noxious halberd, will always allow for the player to get a hit in with their ranged weapon before the Doom resumes its attack rotation regardless of delve level.

At delve 8+, players will only be able to get a hit in on Doom after melee punish by using a 4-tick or faster weapon, as any weapon 5 ticks or more will be too slow, in which the projectiles from the second rock would have to be protected against.

Additionally, if the Doom is defeated by a melee punish during delves 1-8, projectiles resembling holy water will be launched around it, restoring 28 Hitpoints, 14 prayer points, and 25% special attack energy, as well as clearing up acid blood in a 3x3 area around the projectile's landing tile.

tactics.heading: Shockwave
tactics.text:
Generally performed around a minute into the fight or (from delve 5 onwards) directly after a burrow phase. This attack is indicated by multitudes of volatile earth spawning in the area. 20 ticks (12s) after they appear, the Doom will initiate its shockwave attack, dealing 30-42 damage per shockwave. This equates to three attacks from the Doom before this occurs. The second or third attack is guaranteed to be a Rock Throw, and in unfortunate circumstances players may get two instances of Rock Throw before shockwaves. If a standard attack is used as the last attack, it will be partially cut off by the shockwave animation.

To protect against the shockwave, the player must attack two volatile earth (may be attacked on attack cooldown: Non-demonbane attacks incur the weapon's attack delay afterwards, whereas demonbane attacks and the Eye of Ayak will not incur any attack delay) to generate an earthen shield, then stand within it for protection. Please note that the player's hit delay, i.e projectile travel, plays a role in when the earthen shield will spawn. The volatile earth will only begin spawning the shield once the player's projectile has landed. So it is important to be relatively aware of how far away one is when attacking the second orb in order to time the spawning of the shield properly.

Notably, a player will deal their maximum hit to a volatile earth (despite having 1 Hitpoint), meaning health or prayer restoring special attacks such as the toxic blowpipe and eldritch Nightmare staff can be used to effectively restore off them.

The first volatile earth destroyed determines the destination of the shield, while the second determines its spawn point. Additionally, the shield will move at walking speed (half at delve level 1) prioritising diagonal movement before moving straight towards its destination. The centre tile of the shield will also remove acid blood if present in its path.

The earthen shield will dissipate upon reaching its destination or when the Doom's shockwaves end, whichever happens first. Due to the threat of Rock Throw, players must time the spawning of the earthen shield accordingly to avoid as much damage as possible. If it is used as the second to last attack, players can stall the shield slightly. If it is the final attack before shockwaves, it is important to trigger the shield immediately as to focus on prayers, since it is very likely to get killed in two unprotected hits compared to two shockwaves. Utilising ctrl+click can help force the player into walking alongside the shield while praying against the projectiles at the same time.

The shockwave attack will increase in intensity as the delve level increases:
• At delve levels 1 and 2, there will be only one shockwave.
• At delve levels 3 and 4, there will be two shockwaves, occurring two ticks in between.
• At delve levels 5 and 6, there will be three shockwaves.
• At delve level 7, there will be four shockwaves.
• At delve levels 8+, there will be five shockwaves.

With top-end gear, the player may occasionally defeat the Doom right as the volatile earth spawn in. In these cases, it is recommended to quickly destroy a pair to create a path that would clear the most acid blood before descending further, as they will only remain for a short duration before all of them despawn upon the Doom's defeat.

It is also possible to create an earthen shield by killing the boss a few ticks before attacking the second volatile earth at a distance. This can be approximated by checking if the boss is at low health and estimating whether the subsequent hit will kill the boss based on the XP drop. Because the boss is dead and no further shockwaves can occur, the shield lasts until it reaches its destination.

tactics.heading: Acid blood
tactics.text:
Starting at delve level 3, the Doom will spray acid blood in a randomly chosen cardinal direction up to five tiles away from it (and also under itself) when it takes any source of damage, such as larvae explosions and melee punishes. Acid will not generate when hit during the shield and burrow phases, although it will spray acid if a hit lands just as the final burrow slam concludes. Stepping on acid blood will deal up to 7 venom damage and envenom the player if they are not immune to venom. The splattered tiles are random and they may overlap on each other.

2-3 tiles are splattered per hit at delve level 3-7. At delve 6+, the range of splatters increases, while at delve 8+, four tiles are splattered per hit. The targetted tiles are random (in the chosen direction), though Doom can target already splattered tiles.

Splattered tiles are carried over between delve levels, though delve level 6 resets the area and clears the acid. The only other ways to clear acid blood are to use the earthen shield's central tile or (before delve level 9) to defeat Doom with a melee punish.

Doom will spray acid from thralls and each hit of multi-hit weapons (such as a crystal halberd or scythe of Vitur). Thralls in particular create a lot of acid for their damage output, and are not recommended at higher delve levels.

tactics.heading: Demonic shield
tactics.text:
Starting at delve level 3, the Doom will start initiating a shield phase with 500 shield health and begin charging constantly for its Special Beam Cannon upon reaching 75% or lower health, along with having made a minimum of two attacks of any type.

As the Doom does not change appearances, there are a number of ways to determine whether it has started this:
• If the in-game setting "Show boss health overlay" has been enabled, the health bar will change from green to blue.
• When the Doom's name is changed to "Doom of Mokhaiotl (Shielded)"
• The appearance of a blue health bar or a purple game message stating
• Use of a RuneLite plugin
• The player will stop attacking Doom after the transition.

If an attack was launched during the transition from actual health to the shield phase, it will deal actual damage to the Doom if it lands before the shield is set up. If the shield is set up and the attack lands shortly afterwards, it will damage the shield and interrupt charge.

The Doom's shield can only be harmed with demonbane weapons (excluding holy water), which have 100% accuracy and will also reset the charge bar; as such, the Doom must be attacked every now and then to interrupt the charge. Letting the boss fully charge will result in the shield phase instantly ending; this is a popular speedrunning technique, albeit a risky one. Additionally, demonic larvae will continuously spawn from one direction and move towards the Doom, usually from the south-west, west, north-west or north, rather than strictly around the player. If these are not available due to a wall blocking their path, they will spawn in other directions. During the shield phase, exploding larvae will deal 100 shield damage to speed things up considerably, especially at higher delve levels when the rate of spawning larvae increase.

Be sure to stay out of melee distance from the Doom before the shield phase ends before delve level 5, as Doom will immediately resume attacking, which can often result in a melee attack without any animation.

At delve levels 5+, Doom will always initiate the shield phase after two attacks from the last shockwave in sequence.

tactics.heading: Burrowing (car phase)
tactics.text:
Popularly known as the "car phase". Starting at delve level 5, after the shield phase ends, the Doom will enter a burrowed form and cause numerous rocks to fall from above. During this transition, there is a short grace period in which players are immune to all incoming damage incurred from Doom and its related assets; exploding larvae, acid blood and the beam cannon.

Once burrowed, the Doom checks which of the 8 compass directions the player is located in relative to its centre, then spawns a yellow eye four tiles past the player in that direction. After a short duration, the Doom will zoom straight towards the eye, destroying any rocks and trampling players in the way, before doing so a second time. If the player is hit by Doom at the end destination, then they will additionally be shoved out of the way.

During the car phase, the Doom will be charging constantly for its Special Beam Cannon, making it an opportune time to use a Zaryte crossbow, dragon knife or rosewood blowpipe special attack as all attacks made whilst charging are 100% accurate. Any attack will reset the charge.

The car phase will increase in intensity as the delve level increases:
• At delve level 5, the Doom will zoom twice, and trample damage dealt is at 10. It also moves at its slowest, at ~4 tiles per tick.
• At delve level 6, the Doom will zoom, launch 1-3 standard attacks depending on distance travelled, then initiate a Car Slam attack. It will do this three times. Trample damage is also increased to 20.
  • Instead of an earthen shield, the rocks that fall when it begins burrowing serve as protection from its slams.
• At delve level 7, trample damage is increased to 30.
• At delve level 8+, fewer falling rocks are provided when the car phase is initiated. The Doom's speed is significantly increased, reaching its destination within 1 or 2 ticks. Trample damage is also increased to 40.

tactics.heading: Rockblock
tactics.text:
At delve levels 6 and above, the Doom will utilise Car Slams, destroying every rock within 15 tiles from its centre tile, excluding rocks that were protected by another rock. As such, players must be mindful about where they lure the Doom, lest they have it destroy a set of rocks that the player intended to use in a subsequent Car Slam. This is especially important at delve levels 8+ when fewer rocks will fall when it burrows.

With some planning, players may use rocks that are placed from Rock Throw attacks to their advantage by standing on specific tiles as the rock explodes, then luring the Doom towards it so that its centre tile is right where a rock is. When the Doom performs a Car Slam, that rock will fully block it and result in no rocks (besides itself) crumbling for that Car Slam. This is known as "Rockblock".

There are multiple ways to execute Rockblock. With the tile markers provided, players should stand on the green tile in the north or east side and wait until the Doom uses a Rock Throw. When the rock begins to dip down (one tick before it explodes), running towards the white/pink tiles will always place the rock at tile the player stood on and put them outside of the 9x9 debris field. This makes it useful to avoid the looming shadows from a rock throw, and at delve levels 8+ allows the player to commit more focus on praying and dodging the second rock throw.

When the Doom uses another Rock Throw, place the rock around the purple tile labeled "3" if possible; otherwise, the white/pink tiles will suffice. Players may damage the boss too quickly for it to use a second Rock Throw in delve levels 6 or 7, in which case players may have to hold back on proccing shield phase until it does or hope that the start of the car phase will put falling rocks in a favourable position.

Once the car phase starts, keep attacking the Doom whilst doing the following:
• Stand by the gold tile labeled "1" until the Doom's eye appears over it.
• Move to the cyan tile labeled "2" until the Doom's eye appears again, using the rocks placed around the aforementioned area to protect against the second slam. Doing these first two steps correctly should preserve a sufficient amount of rocks in the south-western area.
• Stand around the purple tile labeled "3". If the player is able, standing beyond the row of three purple tiles labeled "3t" will cause the Doom to move for one extra tick, which can sometimes be enough to squeeze in one more attack.

tactics.heading: Double Rockblock
tactics.text:
At delve levels 8+, players can improve upon Rockblock and perform a Double Rockblock instead. While possible at delve levels 6 and 7, this can take some time as it is reliant on waiting for the Doom to perform two Rock Throws instead of one. Players can still perform a Double Rockblock at those delve levels for practicing or if the fight lasts long enough pre-shield for the Doom to perform two Rock Throws.

Similar to regular Rockblock, when the rock begins to dip down (one tick before it explodes), move out of the way for the first rock to be set. In the demonstration provided, moving to the next green tile will then place the second rock in position and complete the setup for Double Rockblock. Players should stand somewhere north of the Doom so that additional Rock Throws can be used for protection against the third Car Slam.

With this setup, any tiles between the two gold tiles will have the Doom place its eye on the tile where the first rock is. For the second rock, players must be standing on the centre-west tile of the Doom on the 5th tick after the first Car Slam for it to place its eye on the tile where the second rock is. Otherwise, it will place its eye one tile north of the second rock and only offer protection south of the Doom.

Performing the Double Rockblock correctly will result in only two rocks being destroyed by the Doom for the first two Car Slams, and allowing much greater flexibility in dealing with the car phase.

tactics.heading: Attack rotations
tactics.text:
During delve levels 1-4, the Doom uses standard attacks, charges with protection prayers, Rock Throw, and Shockwave attack in its rotation. Shockwave attacks during these delve levels generally begin roughly one minute into the fight.

During delves 5 and higher, the attack rotation is slightly changed due to the addition of the car phase:
• Standard delve level 1-4 attack rotation
• Shield phase (upon reaching 75% health)
• Car phase (two zooms)
• Volatile earth spawn
• 3 standard attacks
• Shockwave
• 2 attacks, of which one will always be a Rock Throw
• Loop back to shield phase

After delve level 6, the attack rotation would always be as follows:
• Standard delve level 1-4 attack rotation
• Shield phase (upon reaching 75% health)
• Car phase (Zoom then Car slam, does this 3 times)
• Volatile earth spawn
• 4 attacks, of which one will always be a Rock Throw
• Shockwave
• 2 attacks, of which one will always be a Rock Throw
• Loop back to shield phase

tactics.heading: Plugins
tactics.text: All of the following plugins are available on both officially approved third-party Game clients. On RuneLite they must be installed separately from the Plugin Hub, accessed from the Configuration button (wrench icon on sidebar), then clicking the Plugin Hub button (right-most plug icon). On HDOS these plugins come preinstalled.

tactics.text:

  • Select the "Tile Highlight" tickbox to enable NPC highlighting and choose the colour and highlight settings preferred.

tactics.heading: Radius Markers
tactics.text:
Radius Markers (found in the sidebar after installation) can be used to outline specific attack ranges from the Doom, to enable safe drag attacks with a halberd. Copy the below import and then click the import icon, which will add a 4-width floor outline around Doom, and meleeing Doom with a halberd while on the inner edge of the line will always safely not drag you into melee distance. Additionally, this marker will change from blue to green when the Doom initiates their shield phase, so that you do not mistakenly attack with a halberd and cause a long attack delay.

tactics.heading: Overview
tactics.text:
Drakes are high level Slayer monsters found in the Karuulm Slayer Dungeon. They can drop their claws and teeth, which are used to upgrade the boots of stone and holy sandals into boots of brimstone and devout boots, respectively. These items are five times more common when killed on a Slayer task.

Drakes use both ranged and ranged melee, so melee armour is recommended against their attacks. Additionally, they will launch a fireball at the player's position, which deals 6-8 damage per hit for four hits if dragonfire protection is not used. It functions the same as chromatic dragonfire, although it can also be avoided by stepping away from the target tile.

Prior to completion of the elite Kourend & Kebos diary, boots of stone, boots of brimstone or granite boots must be worn within the dungeon to avoid taking constant damage.

Drakes are considered draconic and as such dragonbane weapons are very effective. They take 50% more damage from water spells.

A superior version of the drake, the guardian drake, can occasionally appear if superiors are enabled. Guardian drakes additionally have a special attack that will deal heavy damage and stun the player if they do not move out of melee distance in time, so flinching or using ranged weapons are recommended when killing them.

Most players tend to block drakes despite them being cannonable; they have a very high weight, somewhat lackluster drops and high stats for their level, in addition to their two flat armour value. It is recommended to kill drakes in the task-only area, as while both rooms are still large, the task-only area is smaller for a cannon to make the most out of.

tactics.heading: Requirements
tactics.text:
• Level 84 Slayer to deal damage or receive a task.
• Access to Mount Karuulm.

tactics.heading: Recommendations
tactics.text:
• High combat stats. Although not required, see the skill levels below for an indication of the advised stats:
  • If using Melee:
    • 80+ Attack
    • 80+ Strength
    • 80+ Defence
    • 80+ Hitpoints
    • 70+ Prayer for the Piety prayer
  • If using Ranged:
    • 75 Ranged or higher
    • 62+, 74+ Prayer for either Deadeye or Rigour
  • If using Magic:
    • 85+ Magic
    • 63+, 77+ Prayer for either Mystic Vigour or Augury
• 29+, 62+ agility for shortcuts at the volcano, if not using Rada's blessing 3 or higher for transportation

tactics.heading: Transportation
tactics.text:
• Mount Karuulm teleport from Rada's blessing 3 or Rada's blessing 4.
• Using the fairy ring (code cir) and travelling up the volcano
• Casting Battlefront Teleport or using its magic tablet variant, and running north-west
• The skills necklace and Farming cape provide teleports to the nearby Farming Guild just south-west.

tactics.heading: Mechanics
tactics.text:
Drakes' normal ranged attacks can be fully blocked by protect from missiles.

Drakes do not require a fire protection shield or potion to be slain, unlike most other dragons. However, after seven auto-attacks, drakes will launch a volcanic breath towards the player's current position, which deals 6-8 damage for four hits if the player is struck by the projectile.

• The levels of dragonfire protection apply to this special attack.
• Having a form of dragonfire protection will reduce this to 3-4 damage.
• Wielding a dragonfire shield, dragonfire ward, or anti-dragon shield alongside drinking an antifire will negate the damage.
• Using a Super antifire potion or its extended version will negate the damage, allowing you to wear a defender or use a blowpipe.

Alternatively, moving one tile elsewhere when the projectile is launched allows complete avoidance.

Together, a player can take no damage when using protect from missiles and dragonfire protection, if attacking from at least 1 tile away.
