gearNotes.heading: Equipment
gearNotes.text:
Duke Sucellus is weak to slash, so slashing weapons are preferred for the fight.

The scythe of Vitur will hit three times due to Sucellus' large size, but is costly to use. An Emberlight, if available, should be used for cost-conscious players as it performs slightly worse but with no upkeep, while being a 4-tick weapon which can allow for additional hits at some points in the fight. The soulreaper axe is another alternative as a five-tick weapon, however it will lose soul stacks every few kills, when the player must restock on poisons.

The effectiveness of different special attack weapons can vary depending on the rest of the gear, particularly whether you are using Oathplate armour. Without it, players should use a Bandos godsword to help lower Sucellus' Defence, as he has a very high Defence level. It is not recommended to use an elder maul or dragon warhammer because it is much more likely to miss due to Sucellus' high crush Defence. Emberlight's special attack is also not recommended due to it rolling against Sucellus' high stab defence. Alternatively, Voidwaker can be used to deal guaranteed damage. With Oathplate armour providing significant slash accuracy, dragon/burning claws become more effective as they deal more damage, and reducing defence or dealing guaranteed damage is less important.

gearNotes.heading: Inventory recommendations
gearNotes.text:
• A stamina potion if you have a lower Herblore or Agility level.
• 4-7 prayer potions or super restores if using amulet of blood fury depending on trip length. A Prayer regeneration potion is recommended if you are capable of surviving for long trips.
  • Consider bringing Saradomin brews alongside super restores for longer trips, as well as an extra super combat potion.
• Ring of shadows for teleporting back.
  • Use icy basalt if you have not received the frozen tablet. Alternatively, teleport to Weiss using a player-owned house portal nexus.
• Food in remaining inventory space, ideally high healing such as marlin, anglerfish, summer pies or karambwans.
• The book of the Dead and a divine rune pouch to cast Death charge and Resurrection spells for Thralls. The rune pouch should contain Blood, fire, aether (Or Cosmic and Soul runes separately), and Death runes. Thralls add extra damage and Death charge allows more usage of special attacks.
  • Vile Vigour can optionally be brought to use prayer points to restore run energy if needed, for players with lower Herblore who cannot prepare as many poisons at a time. This can be done by swapping out the fire runes for smoke runes.
• The best pickaxe you can use, as this increases the rate you get salt.
  • You can also 3-tick mine the salt if you collect the mushrooms first, which makes all pickaxes equal; in this case you can simply take the iron pickaxe from the wall.
• A house tab or other teleport configured to be one click, for emergency escapes or leaving.
• Upon entering the arena, drop 3-4 supplies to make room for mushrooms, salt, and a pestle and mortar.

tactics.heading: Overview
tactics.text:
After the completion of Desert Treasure II - The Fallen Empire, players can fight a stronger variant of Duke Sucellus. An even stronger awakened variant can be fought by entering the asylum gates with an awakener's orb in the player's inventory and selecting "Yes" when prompted.

If the player dies while fighting Duke Sucellus, their grave will appear by the asylum gates. Players will have their reclamation fee reduced by 75% until they have five kills, after which the standard death cost will apply.

tactics.heading: Requirements
tactics.text: • Completion of Quest Desert Treasure II - The Fallen Empire

tactics.heading: Suggested skills
tactics.text:
• 75+ Attack
• 75+ Strength
• 70+ Defence
• 80+ Hitpoints
• 70+ Agility
• 70+ Mining
• 76+ Magic for Resurrection spells

tactics.heading: Transportation
tactics.text:
The quickest methods of reaching Ghorrock Prison, where Duke Sucellus resides, are:
• Using the ring of shadows to teleport to the Ghorrock Dungeon. This requires having used the frozen tablet on it, which is an untradeable 1/25 drop from Duke Sucellus.
• Using an icy basalt (or Weiss Portal), squeezing through the broken fence to the east, then entering the Salt Mine and continuing through it to the dungeon entrance.

Weiss can also be reached by using Larry's boat (on the coast between Rellekka and the DKS fairy ring) and climbing through the cave entrance.

Once in the Ghorrock Dungeon, head north-east to the heavy door to enter Ghorrock Prison, where players will reach the asylum entrance directly instead of traversing through the entire prison as they did during the quest.

tactics.heading: Brewing poison
tactics.text:
Upon entering the prison, Duke Sucellus is initially asleep and must be weakened with arder-musca poisons, made from resources found within the asylum - arder powder, musca powder, and salax salt. Making this poison requires six portions of each, and two poisons are required to wake the Duke up, so twelve of each will be needed in total. To the left and right of the asylum upon entering it, there is a pestle and mortar and iron pickaxe on the walls that players can take. Note: Escaping/leaving the instance will automatically remove all arder-musca poisons, arder powder, musca powder, and salax salt from your inventory.

The salt piles are found in the centre of the asylum, surrounded by gas vents; three of these will release gas in a 3x3 AoE from the vent, draining 4 prayer points and dealing up to 12 damage that can be reduced with a slayer helmet or gas mask. Once a vent stops emitting gas, the next one will be one vent to the east, looping back to the opposite side if already on the eastern-most vent. Players are also recommended to bring the best pickaxe available, as this increases the rate of mining them. Having 80+ Mining also ensures that only two harvests need to be made.

Meanwhile, the mushrooms are found at the end of the opposing sides of the asylum, past the extremities. Up there, ice falls will randomly strike on a tile, freezing the player for 2 ticks (1.2 seconds) and dealing up to 18 damage. These occur specifically in the area right before the second staircase on both sides, and are indicated by a shadow looming over the tile they will strike on.

In addition, the extremities will periodically wake in succession and unleash their gaze in a cone radius; they will start from the middle, south, and then north in that order on both sides. Getting caught by their gaze will freeze the player for 5 ticks (3 seconds), drain 1/4th of their prayer points, and deal up to 70 damage. Players can ignore the extremities entirely by starting from one tile south of the southern extremity and running straight to the mushrooms, only having to watch out for ice falls. To do the same in reverse, start running from one tile north of the northern extremity.

In both of these corridors, there are only two safe spots in the actual area; the tile used to grab the mushrooms from, and the tile east from it for the arder mushrooms and the tile west for the musca mushrooms. These two tiles will never be targeted by ice falls and are safe from the nearby extremity.

Grinding arder and musca mushroom yields varying amounts of powder; at level 70 Herblore, each mushroom provides five powder, so three mushrooms of each type are needed. At 80+ Herblore, players will only need to grind two of each mushroom.

After acquiring twelve salax salt, arder powder, and musca powder, place them in both Fermentation Vats and let it ferment for several seconds before collecting two finished poisons. Before each Duke kill, players may prepare enough poison for 2, 3, or 4 kills if they have Herblore level 62, 70, or 80, respectively. Mushrooms will only last for eight picks, after which they will respawn once Sucellus awakens. The salt does not share this limitation, although players will stop mining it if they have done so for over five minutes without clicking it again.

tactics.heading: Advanced tips
tactics.text:
Players looking to speed up the preparation process may opt to use tick manipulation by performing an action to delay the skilling timer (such as cutting a celastrus bark). By running towards the resource and performing the action before a specific tile, and then instantly clicking on the resource, players can gather double the resources.

Rather than making the Arder-musca poisons, the player can alternatively grind mushrooms to obtain 40 powder of its respective type, then feed it directly to Sucellus. While each powder only deals 5 damage, the player can rapidly feed him once per tick, filling up the bar much faster. The advantage of this method is that it significantly reduces the amount of run energy expended, making stamina potions completely unnecessary with 70+ Agility. However, it is very click-intensive, and after the changes on 25 June 2025 makes this method rather redundant.

tactics.heading: Battle phase
tactics.text:
Duke Sucellus has 485 health and attacks on a five-tick cycle (3.0s). It is highly recommended that players melee Sucellus, as he is weakest to slash attacks.

In addition, unlike other demonic monsters, Duke Sucellus only has a 70% vulnerability to demonbane weapons; Arclight gives a 49% boost to accuracy and damage as opposed to the usual 70%. The Ward of Arceuus spell can be used to reduce the damage of Sucellus' regular attacks (though the 10% damage reduction from the spell does not reduce damage of normal icicle attacks when using protect from melee as it is capped at 5), and the benefit does not apply to peripheral forms of damage like those inflicted by gas flares or extremities.

When in melee range (including diagonally across), Sucellus will raise his arms, causing icicles to spike up from the ground. These icicles have a 3x3 AoE and will deal up to 11 damage if Protect from Melee is not active, or 5 with. This is a standard attack and can occasionally miss, though Sucellus' high stats means this is very unlikely. Shortly afterwards, he will slam his arms back down, shattering the icicles in a 1x1 AoE on them. Getting caught in this slam will deal up to 56 damage without prayer, or 42 with, and will always hit regardless of the player's bonuses.

If outside of melee range, Sucellus will instead launch a blue projectile, which deals up to 48 damage if not protected against, and deals slightly less damage with Protect from Magic, though will generally deal significant damage. The damage only applies upon impact. However, getting hit by this attack, even if protected against, will disqualify the player from a "perfect" kill.

Due to the high, unblockable damage of Duke's magic projectile and slam attacks, players learning the Duke fight are recommended to stand directly behind the pillars on either side of Duke whenever they are not attacking. Standing behind these pillars will cause Duke to do his melee cycle, but because his slam attack does not reach diagonally, players will only take icicle chip damage.

Duke Sucellus has two special attacks:

• Freezing Gaze - Every fifth standard attack, he will open the eye within his body, indicated by the game message If the player is not standing directly behind a pillar 5 ticks (3 seconds) after the attack is initiated, the player will take up to 101 damage. This is almost assured to kill the player, so avoiding it is essential. This attack takes 6 ticks in total.
  • Players can quickly get one more hit off shortly after the first game message appears, or resume attacking the instant the game message appears.
• Gas Flare - He will launch gas towards the vent closest to the player, leaving dangerous gas there for a few seconds. The gas deals up to 12 damage, which can be reduced with a slayer helmet or gas mask. Avoid them by moving to the opposite pillar.
  • The Gas Flare attack will always be launched three standard attacks after the first Freezing Gaze. If above 75% health, Sucellus will use this attack after every five standard attacks, four above 25%, and three below 25%. However, Sucellus will never use this attack immediately after a Freezing Gaze, in which case it will do an extra standard attack. Once the 75% threshold is crossed (and 25% for enraged phase), the change in frequency of the Gas Flare attack will apply after the next gas flares are launched. If above 50% of his health (242 hitpoints), he will spit out one Gas Flare, and two otherwise.

tactics.heading: Enrage phase
tactics.text:
Upon reaching 25% of his health (121 hitpoints), Sucellus will enter an enrage phase, attacking one tick faster to start on a 2.4 second (4 tick) cycle.

If using a five-tick weapon, you will only be able to safely attack Sucellus every two attacks, as the third attack will result in the player getting hit by his slamming attack when they do so. Should the player wish to, they may switch to a four-tick weapon such as Arclight or Emberlight to match his attack speed, however it is not necessary in normal mode.

tactics.heading: Post fight
tactics.text:
If you wish to continue killing Sucellus after using up all of your Arder-musca poisons, run towards one of the mushroom spawns to immediately prepare picking them, as he will "respawn" shortly before one of them is reached.

When picking up drops, be mindful of mist rune and chaos rune drops if using the Arceuus spellbook, as these will cause other spells to become available, such as Vile Vigour and medium-tier thralls, potentially causing problems with muscle memory when spellbook filtering is enabled. These should be left on the ground until the trip concludes.

tactics.heading: Awakened mode
tactics.text:
In Awakened mode, Duke Sucellus has the following changes:
• The boss' health increases from 485 to 1,697.
• The boss is immune to stat drains.
• The boss' poison tolerance meter increases from 200 to 370, requiring three poisons to wake him up.
• Upon reaching less than 76% of his health, he will launch four Gas Flares in a row; above that, only once. The gas' damage is also increased to ~26 or 27 if hit without proper face covering.
• Around 32% health, a black orb will move from side to side in front of him that deals up to 27 damage and drains all stats by 8.
• Enraged phase starts at 440 health (25.9%).
• Periodically, Duke Sucellus will cover the player in bile, resulting in the player leaking poison for 15 ticks. If standing in a poison pool, the player will take 9-12 poison damage every tick and be poisoned starting at 2 damage if no poison immunity is present.
• The black mask and Slayer helmet do not apply their usual on-task damage and accuracy bonuses while on a Duke Sucellus boss slayer task.

Before starting the fight, drop supplies on the pillars closest to Duke Sucellus, enough so that the mushrooms, salt, and poison can be picked without juggling. The damage dealt from ice falls and extremities are the same as in normal mode, though much more care is recommended to avoid unnecessarily draining supplies before even fighting the boss. Drink potions and heal up as needed before using the final poison on him to begin the fight. As with normal mode, players must always force the Duke to use melee, as his magic attacks can hit very hard; up to 36 through prayer, and 71 without. The melee chips are still the same as in normal mode, though the melee attack does hit significantly harder, up to 81 without prayer and around 60 with.

While not necessary, a Menaphite remedy can be helpful in restoring drained stats every 15 seconds. The player's primary form of healing pre-enrage should be solely Saradomin brews, as damage during this time should only be from the chip damage caused from icicles. Solids are much more helpful in the enrage phase when some recoverable mistakes are made.

Flick Duke Sucellus as required; it is highly important that the player does not get caught by his Freezing Gaze, as it has a significantly higher max hit and can potentially kill in one hit. Once Duke Sucellus starts spitting out multiple Gas Flares (around 75% of his health), run south to the middle row of vents and wait for the last spit to appear before moving back in, as it is important not to let the row in front of him be immersed in dangerous gas, especially with poison and enrage. Around 65% of his health, Sucellus will perform Gas Spits one auto-attack after Freezing Gaze.

When Duke Sucellus splatters the player in bile, the player will be notified with the message "Duke Sucellus covers you in bile. It slowly drips off your body and onto the floor.", resulting the player leaking poison for 15 tiles if walking (or one tick running). This attack will begin to be used upon reaching 65% of his health, and will always occur after Gas Flares, though it is not guaranteed each time. If the bile does appear, use the walking method with the tiles indicated on the picture to the right; pre-enrage, the player must walk four tiles and then be next to Sucellus on the fifth tile to avoid getting hit by magic, while post-enrage, the player must walk three tiles and be next to Sucellus on the fourth tile.

Upon reaching ~32% of his health, an Orb of Darkness will begin to appear in the row in front of Sucellus from either side of the first set of pillars, which deals up to 27 damage and drains all stats by 8 if hit. These orbs will continually spawn until the encounter ends, and will appear every ~10 or so seconds regardless if the player is hit by it or not. These should be avoided whenever possible; though if there is no other choice, it is recommended to tank the orb, as it is much less dangerous than trying to tank one of Sucellus' auto-attacks.

Once the enrage phase begins, it is important to sync with Sucellus' attacks so that the player will not make mistakes as the chances of dying significantly increase, as it is possible to get biled twice in a single attack rotation. If the second bile occurs, players will always take damage at some point from the pools, due to the Freezing Gaze attack being lined up one auto-attack after the second Gas Flare. Therefore, minimise time spent in the phase by dumping special attacks to reduce the boss' health.

gearNotes.text:
The confliction gauntlets (+7%) or tormented bracelet (+5%), occult necklace (+5%), Virtus robes (+5% each when using Ancient Magicks) or Ancestral robes (+3% each), and imbued god capes (+2%) increase the maximum hit of the player's Magic spells. However, the tormented bracelet is generally inefficient to use as the bracelet of slaughter will increase the task's length and maximise overall Slayer experience rates.

It is recommended to use a staff or wand that can autocast Ancient Magicks. Kodai wand provides +15% magic damage bonus as well as infinite water runes and a chance to save runes, making it the most effective.

A goading potion, darts, knives, or a blowpipe may be used to lure. The special attack of the Dinh's bulwark in conjunction with a Lightbearer may also be used to lure, however it may cause stamina issues due to its weight for players with lower agility levels.

A Hunters' crossbow or Hunters' sunlight crossbow is also an effective luring weapon, having the same speed as shortbows and 1 more tile of range. It is also 1-handed, so magic off-hands aren't unequipped. Kebbit bolts and sunlight antler bolts are much more expensive than the cheapest arrows and darts, however Long kebbit bolts are a lower cost alternative.

tactics.heading: Overview
tactics.text:
Dust devils can be assigned as a slayer task by various medium and high-levelled Slayer Masters upon reaching 65 Slayer and 70 combat. In order to obtain these as a Slayer task, the player must have started Desert Treasure I.

Dust devils are an incredibly popular task amongst most slayers, as they have a superior, the choke devil, and are often found in multicombat areas which allows for chinning and burst/barraging. They have relatively decent drops which usually covers the cost of supplies.

Unlike most monsters, dust devils attack with ranged melee; their attacks are considered melee, but they roll on the player's ranged defence rather than melee. They have low defence but are surprisingly accurate for their level.

Players have three options to choose from when slaying dust devils:

• Catacombs of Kourend - this is the most easily accessible location. Dust devils here have access to the Catacombs of Kourend drop table.
• Smoke Dungeon - a more remote, quiet location. A multicombat area can be found to the west for on-task purposes.
• Wilderness Slayer Cave - a somewhat busy location, can only be killed on-task. This location is in level 25-28 Wilderness, so do not bring items you are unwilling to lose. A large amount of costs can be lowered via Blighted ancient ice sacks and the dust devils here have access to the Wilderness Slayer Cave drop table.

Unless killing them as part of Konar quo Maten or Krystilia's Slayer tasks, the Catacombs of Kourend are highly recommended for their ease of accessibility.

gearNotes.heading: Equipment
gearNotes.text:
Ancient Wyverns, Taloned Wyverns, and Long-tailed Wyverns have a typeless ranged attack that bypasses protection prayers and hits for up to 10 damage. As the attack is weaker than their melee attacks and cannot be prayed against, praying Protect from Melee while wearing gear that provides ranged defence can minimise the amount of damage taken. High-level food like anglerfish or sharks is recommended. The player's Prayer points can also/instead be used on Piety, and bringing at least two prayer potions is strongly advised, as well as being easily paid for by the wyvern bones collected.

Note: The ancient wyvern shield is the only shield that grants immunity against the freezing effect from a wyvern's icy breath. The dragonfire shield, mind shield, or elemental shield can be used, but you will occasionally become frozen. The Anti-dragon shield and regular antifire potions have no effect against the icy breath.

tactics.heading: Overview
tactics.text:
All Fossil Island Wyverns may be killed in this same fashion. However, the lower-level Spitting, Taloned and Long-tailed wyverns require 66 Slayer.

Ancient wyverns are the strongest species of wyvern. They possess very high Defence, Attack, and Hitpoints, thus making them very powerful foes. Like other wyverns, they require an elemental, mind, dragonfire ward, dragonfire, or ancient wyvern shield to be equipped in order to be slain, or the player will suffer devastating damage from their unique icy breath. The ancient wyvern shield is the only shield that will grant immunity against the freezing effect from a wyvern's icy breath. Ancient wyverns and taloned wyverns can use a typeless ranged attack from any distance. Long-tailed wyverns can also use a typeless ranged attack but only when the player is outside of their melee distance.

Note that after Bone Voyage, a Slayer level of 82 is required in order to deal damage to ancient wyverns (not withstanding the effects of a poisoned weapon). Otherwise, eating a wild pie at 77 Slayer will do, though kills will be extremely long.

Quick travel tip is to use the Digsite pendant, which should be used on the strange machine at the House on the Hill, to teleport directly to Fossil Island. Should players already have unlocked the teleport, they may use a mounted digsite pendant within their Portal Nexus room instead if they have one. Run south-east to the cave entrance. For Slayer tasks, you can use the Magic Mushtree adjacent to the House on the Hill teleport location to appear just north of the task-only wyvern Cave under the Mushroom Meadow. Alternatively, the player can teleport to the Digsite, use the barge, and run east past the bank and then south-east into the cave.

tactics.heading: Overview
tactics.text:
Fossil Island Wyverns are a Slayer monster requiring 66 Slayer to kill. A combat level of 60, as well as the completion of the quests Elemental Workshop and Bone Voyage, is required for them to be assigned as a slayer task.

Similarly to their skeletal cousins, Fossil Island Wyverns use both melee and an icy breath. The icy breath requires the use of an elemental shield, dragonfire shield, dragonfire ward, or ancient wyvern shield in order to take reduced damage from the breath; the latter also provides immunity from being frozen. Protect from Magic can also be used but only provides half the damage reduction of the prior protections. Antifire potions of any type and the anti-dragon shield do not work to mitigate icy breath.

There are four types of wyverns that fall under this category, of which three can be fought at 66 Slayer and the other at 82 Slayer.

For players seeking a quick clear of the task, Spitting Wyverns are the best to kill, as they can also use a very weak ranged attack in place of the ice breath. Long-tailed Wyverns can also be killed and while they have a typeless ranged attack, they will only use it if the player is not in melee distance. Taloned Wyverns should be avoided, as they can use their typeless ranged attack even when the player is in melee distance. Many players also wish to purchase the Stop the Wyvern reward as a way to block the task without using the blocklist. This is because the Wyverns on fossil island are not particularly profitable, do not give good experience, and aren't the best for points.

At level 82 Slayer, the Ancient Wyvern can be killed for the purposes of this slayer task. These, much like the Taloned Wyvern, are often ignored, as they are a much stronger version of them with higher stats. They can also use a typeless ranged attack from any distance.

Wyverns may drop Fossil Island fossils of various sizes. Both caves have a Fossil Storage box by their respective entrances.

gearNotes.heading: Equipment
gearNotes.text:
Like most dragons, frost dragons are weak to stab and dragonbane. However, due to their icy bodies, frost dragons are also extra weak to crush.

In max, one of either Inquisitor hauberk or plateskirt should be worn, with the other piece being Torva, to retain a max hit of 61 with the dragon hunter lance. Hauberk is marginally better.

Like most dragons, frost dragons are weak to bolts and dragonbane. However, they are less resistant to arrows (compared to bolts) than other dragons.

Frost dragons are incredibly weak to fire spells, making them a powerful option.

tactics.heading: Overview
tactics.text:
With level 87 Sailing, Frost dragons can be fought within the Grimstone Dungeon.

They may be assigned as a Slayer task by Nieve/Steve or Duradel/Kuradal. Being on task increases the drop rate of dragon metal sheets from 1/100 to 1/40.

Unlike chromatic dragons, frost dragons are weakest to crush, then stab, rather than stab alone. They have a 100% elemental weakness to fire spells rather than the usual 50% to water, and while heavy ranged remains the best ranged option, they are more resistant to ranged attacks overall. As with all dragons, they are weak to dragonbane weapons.

tactics.heading: Attacks
tactics.text:
Like chromatic dragons, frost dragons only use melee and short-ranged dragonfire, meaning they can be safespotted. Alternatively, Protect from Melee combined with full dragonfire protection will nullify all damage.

Their dragonfire is icy, and will freeze the player for a short time if not protected against. Unlike wyverns, their icy dragonbreath is fully negated by normal means of dragonfire protection.

tactics.heading: Transportation
tactics.text: The fastest way to get to frost dragons is by using fairy ring DLP, after visiting Grimstone at least once. Grimstone can also be reached quickly via a boat moored at it with a greater teleport focus, or simply sailed to from a nearby port, such as Weiss.

gearNotes.heading: Common setups
gearNotes.text:
As gargoyles are weak to crush, many players bring a crush-focused weapon such as the Sarachnis cudgel for this task.

Praying Protect from Melee will negate all damage from regular gargoyles. If players have the Bigger and Badder slayer perk unlocked, there is a chance for marble gargoyles to spawn. These superior variants use both melee and ranged attack styles. Be careful, as getting hit by the special attack can be dangerous.

The toxic blowpipe in particular can provide comparable damage to melee setups. It can also envenom them, however this must be done upstairs as the basement gargoyles are immune to venom. Safespots are offered in both locations, but because of the many gargoyles in the area, it is less reliable to do so.

tactics.heading: Overview
tactics.text:
Gargoyles can be assigned as a Slayer task by various Slayer masters at level 75 Slayer, level 80 combat, and with completion of the Priest in Peril quest. They are only found in the Slayer Tower, either on the top floor or in the basement. The gargoyles in the basement of the Slayer Tower can only be killed while on a Slayer task, as Raulyn will stop the player if they attempt to fight them off-task. Gargoyles have a Superior slayer monster variant, the level 349 marble gargoyle. Unlike regular gargoyles, the marble gargoyle also utilises ranged attacks. It also has a special attack, launching a white-red orb that deals heavy damage and entraps the player if not dodged; this attack has a 1x1 AoE (in other words, it affects only the single tile where the player was standing).

Gargoyles are weak to both magic and crush attacks, but melee is commonly used due to the lack of safespots, less defence against their attacks and expenses for casting spells. They have -2 flat armour, so weapons such as Dual macuahuitl are recommended to make use of the extra damage. Even then, they are still easily fought with most standard weapons one might have available.

To kill a gargoyle, a rock hammer, a rock thrownhammer, or a granite hammer must be used when they reach 9 or lower Hitpoints. Normally, the item must be used on the gargoyle, but players can buy the "Gargoyle Smasher" perk from Slayer masters for 120 Slayer points, which will automatically smash the gargoyle when it falls to 9 or lower Hitpoints, provided that the player has a rock hammer (or equivalent) in their inventory. The granite hammer will automatically smash gargoyles even without the perk if it is equipped. The rock hammer is faster than the rock thrownhammer as it does not have travel time. If both are in the inventory, the rock hammer is used in melee distance, while thrownhammers are used outside of melee distance.

Gargoyles also have a boss variant, the Grotesque Guardians. In order to access them, the player must kill gargoyles on-task to obtain the brittle key, which unlocks the boss arena. The boss fight consists of two gargoyles; Dusk and Dawn. Players can choose between melee and a melee/range hybrid; the former requires a polearm weapon, while the latter has easier accessibility.

When considering whether to kill regular gargoyles or the Grotesque Guardians, it is worth noting that the normal gargoyles are much faster to kill and require less supplies and effort, whereas the Grotesque Guardians are more time-consuming, and require more effort and supplies to kill. The requirements for killing the Guardians are also substantially higher in terms of stats and gear. The drop table of the Guardians is not significantly better than gargoyles, especially considering that regular gargoyles have very decent drops as well. However, the Guardians are one of only two sources of granite dust, which is untradeable. The dust strengthens steel cannonballs, turning them into granite cannonballs with a max hit of 35 instead of 30.

It is recommended to kill gargoyles in the basement during a task, as there are many gargoyles in a fairly small area compared to the top floor. The basement is also large enough that the player can reset the aggression timer easily without leaving the area.

If killing the Grotesque Guardians, it is strongly recommended the player avoid purchasing Double Trouble, as this causes the boss to be counted as two kills per task rather than one, drastically reducing the amount of kills per task.

gearNotes.heading: Equipment
gearNotes.text:
When selecting gear, the primary consideration is maximising damage to increase experience gain. The crab's minimal defensive stats and high health make nearly all weapons viable for consideration; players are able to use whatever their best weapon is already. As the boss is intended to be fought AFK, not all recommendations are required to be followed if the player does not wish to afford the extra effort to use them, such as special attacks or the use (and upkeep) of Prayers; however they are still listed here if one wishes to use them.

Generally, the tabs in the following sections are ordered from least to most effective; or lowest requirements to highest.

gearNotes.heading: Melee
gearNotes.text:
The three strongest setups are the full Blood Moon armour set, an obsidian armour setup, and the dharok's armour set (past 90 Strength and Hitpoints). The Blood Moon set is the most powerful set, though it is more expensive () and has higher repair costs than the others. The obsidian setup is cheaper ( for the required items) and has no repair costs. Dharok's armour is powerful at high levels, though requires a bit more attention to maximise its damage.
If a player can't afford or obtain these sets, players should use their best fast attacking (4 tick) melee weapon with as much strength bonus as they can acquire in the remaining item slots. See the "Lower Level" section for item choices.
(Not included in these sets are the soul reaper axe and the uncharged scythe of Vitur. These outperform the other sets, but it's unlikely players training combat will have access to these. If they are available, use them with the highest strength bonus gear.)
For lower levelled players, some of the other armour sets may be too expensive. If that's the case, the primary weapon has the largest effect on damage and should be the focus for a budget. For the other item slots, the main stat to prioritise is Strength bonus, with a secondary focus on prayer bonus items (such as Monk's robes) if that's not available.

The obsidian set — composed of the three piece obsidian armour set, the berserker necklace and the toktz-xil-ak (not the closely named toktz-xil-ek) — gives a 30% damage boost and is the strongest set outside of Blood Moon armour and Dharok's equipment at high levels (90+ Strength and Hitpoints). The setup has no hourly costs, unlike the Blood Moon set and Dharok's equipment with and respective hourly costs.

While inferior to obsidian, the void armour set has a similiar strength scaling and can be used with any weapon (see the "Lower levelled" tab for weapon options), so is placed here for clarity.

The Blood Moon armour set with the dual macuahuitl is the strongest melee set at Gemstone Crab, outside of Dharok's at Hitpoint and Strength levels close to 99. The set is more expensive () than obsidian and Dharok the Wretched's equipment (which cost and respectively) and the full set must be used.
The set has an hourly repair cost, which is reduced by your Smithing level at an armour stand. The hourly cost is coins at level 1 Smithing, coins at 60 Smithing, and coins at 99 Smithing.

Dharok's equipment is a powerful option at higher Hitpoint and Strength levels. Dharoks matches obsidian sets at level 90 Hitpoints and Strength, and matches Blood Moon sets at level 97 Hitpoints and Strength.
Dharoks requires the player to stay at very low hitpoints (3-4) to maximise its effect. This can be done with items that deal damage to yourself, namely the locator orb and dwarven rock cake. To offset your natural Hitpoint regeneration, either periodically use a dwarven rock cake, or turn on and off the Rapid Heal prayer once a minute (which resets the natural regen's timer). This management takes a bit more activity than the other sets, although simply resetting hitpoints between each crab burrow still provides competitive damage.
The gemstone crab occasionally deals damage, so do not drain your Hitpoints down to 1 or 2 (the crab has a ~15% chance to hit in the minute between natural Hitpoint regenerations, and a 1% chance to hit twice). Bring a handful of multihealing food items (such as cake, Guthix rest, cooked giant crab meat) to heal in case of draining mistakes.

gearNotes.heading: Melee inventory
gearNotes.text:
Fighting the gemstone crab does not require any items, although some may be brought to increase damage dealt at the cost of reducing AFK time:
• Super strength potions, or Strength potions. Black warlock mixes can also be used, and will share the Strength buff to other nearby players (that have Accept Aid on), but have low trade volume. Several black warlocks spawn to the east of the southern and northern crab nests, and south of the eastern nest; with 55 Hunter they can be caught before initiating combat with the crab to boost Strength.
• Bring a method to reach the crab, such as a pendant of Ates, quetzal whistle, or runes for Civitas illa Fortis Teleport. Banking can be done in Tal Teklan, so holding onto it isn't necessary.
• (Optional) Prayer restoring items such as prayer potions if using offensive prayers to increase damage. Moonlight moth mixes can be used to restore your own Prayer and that of 3 other nearby players fighting the crab, and at lower levels can provide more Prayer restoration than potions. If fighting the crab with a group of friends, or multiple of your own accounts, the moths can be coordinated to maximise their effectiveness across the recipients of the restoration. (Requires Accept Aid)
  • If using prayer potions, bring a holy wrench or other items which share its effect.
  • If only using the lowest tier of Prayers, it can be more efficient to just restore Prayer at the altar in Tal Teklan, as it would only need to be done every 5-10 crabs.
  • Using the Saradomin Godsword or Ancient Mace special attack can restore low amounts of prayer, negating the need for prayer restoring items.
• (Optional) A special attack weapon, such as the dragon claws or dragon dagger to use up special attack energy for bonus damage.
  • A defender will be beneficial if using a two-handed main weapon with a one-handed special attack weapon. Ideally a dragon or Avernic defender.
  • If looking to conserve supplies or not worry about using special attacks frequently, using a Dragon battleaxe special attack at the start of each new crab fight can replace the need for Strength potions.
• (Optional) A pickaxe, to mine the boss after defeat and loot gems.
  • A gem sack may be brought to hold additional gems, or simply a chisel to cut them for Crafting experience and then dropped or alched.

gearNotes.heading: Ranged
gearNotes.text:
The strongest training weapons are typically darts, especially with a blowpipe or a ranged strength offhand (such as the twisted buckler). Darts are relatively cheap, have a high DPS from their fast attack speed, and their relatively low accuracy doesn't matter against the zero defence crab.
At level 46 Ranged, a crossbow firing ruby bolts (e) becomes the strongest weapon until level 65-70 Ranged, as the ruby bolt passive effect gives a huge chunk of experience when it activates. The eclipse atatl scales off your Strength level and bonuses, and can outperform darts if your Strength level is above your Ranged level.
Make sure you're using the "Rapid" weapon style when training Ranged, as this will increase your attack speed and greatly increase the damage dealt compared to the "Accurate" or "Longrange" styles.
Ranging potions () or Armadyl brews () should be used past level 20 Ranged. These can either be sipped every 5 minutes or when the crab burrows. Use whichever potion is cheaper. If you're using Armadyl brews, buy some restore potions to reset your other combat stats after training.
The prayer Sharp Eye is worth using around level 30 Prayer, as it drains very slowly and can be sustained by a trip to the Tal Teklan altar when the crab is nearby. The higher tier offensive prayers require prayer restoration to sustain and don't always give an additional max hit; their usefulness depends on your exact weapon, Ranged level, and budget. You can experiment or use the wiki's DPS Calculator to check if your max hit increases with a higher-tiered prayer.

gearNotes.heading: Equipment
gearNotes.text:
At level 30 Ranged, obtaining an Ava's attractor is a high priority, as it automatically picks up the majority of your ammunition. At level 50 Ranged, it should be promptly upgraded into an Ava's accumulator (which has an enhanced ammuniation saving effect).

Lower-levelled Ranged armours only provide ranged accuracy, which has little impact on the Gemstone Crab that has zero defence. As such, the more useful pieces of equipment are items that grant prayer bonus (such as monk's robes), which make using offensive ranged prayers more convenient.

gearNotes.heading: Weapon
gearNotes.text:
Before level 46 Ranged, use mithril darts or steel darts. These darts are very cheap and, because of their fast attack speed and the crab's low defence, will outperform shortbows. Adamant darts can optionally be used at level 30. It takes around 5,000 darts to go from 5 Ranged to 46 ranged (with an Ava's attractor).

At level 46, the strongest weapon becomes an adamant crossbow firing ruby bolts (e). The ruby bolts (e) passive effect hits for 60 damage every ~20 attacks on average, giving a huge chunk of experience. Make sure your ruby bolts are enchanted (have an (e) at the end of their name), as the unenchanted version will be worse than using darts. The ruby bolt effect damages the player for 10% of their current Hitpoints; this effect can't kill the player, and natural Hitpoint regeneration will nearly offset the damage, but the effect will deactivate at 1 Hitpoint. As such, stay out of the crab's melee range and bring some cheap food items to stay above 4 Hitpoints.

Ruby bolts are comparatively expensive, costing per hour with an Ava's accumulator (at level 50) and per hour with an Ava's attractor. Adamant darts or mithril darts can be used as a budget alternative (with an hourly cost of and respectively).

At level 65, a rosewood blowpipe with adamant darts matches the ruby bolts with a crossbow, and overtakes them at level 70-75 Ranged. Using rune darts allows the blowpipe to easily surpass ruby bolts, although those darts are much more expensive to use (costing per hour).

The eclipse atlatl can outshine the dart-based options if your Strength level is above your Ranged level (and with melee gear). As a rule of thumb: with equal Ranged and Strength levels, an atlatl with "mid-game" strength items (around 40 strength bonus excluding the atlatl itself) matches an adamant dart rosewood blowpipe with elite void and no other ranged strength items. This atlatl configuration matches a rune dart rosewood blowpipe with 10 extra Strength levels, and it matches a twisted buckler firing amethyst darts with 15 extra Strength levels. Melee strength items tend to be easier or cheaper to obtain than ranged strength items, which allows the atlatl to reach most of its potential damage earlier.
Note: Use a (super) Strength potion and a Ranged prayer while using an atlatl.

The ideal weapons are dart firing: the toxic blowpipe, the twisted buckler or dragonfire ward, and the rosewood blowpipe. The toxic blowpipe is the strongest but far more expensive to use than other weapons, with an additional of hourly cost in Zulrah's scales. If a player is willing to spend an hour training Ranged, they should strongly consider training at e.g maniacal monkeys instead, which is a much faster training method (roughly three times as fast) with the same gold cost per experience. The twisted buckler and rosewood blowpipe are 5-10% slower but have far more competitive usage costs .
Void ranged and Masori both give max hits and are therefore ideal. Elite void is marginally better than Masori, though the latter can be purchased directly from the Grand exchange with no requirements (note: the Masori armour does not have to be fortified). Ava's assembler reduces ammunition costs by 30% from an Ava's accumulator.

gearNotes.text:
• Ranging potions, Divine ranging potions, Armadyl brews, or Lizardkickers
  • If using the Eclipse atlatl or hunter's spear, instead bring Super strength potions or a dragon battleaxe for its special.
• Teleport to the crab, such as a pendant of Ates, quetzal whistle, or runes for Civitas illa Fortis Teleport
• Food, especially if using ruby bolts (e)
• (Optional) Prayer restoring items such as prayer potions or moonlight moth mixes, if not using the altar in Tal Teklan
• (Optional) A special attack weapon, such as the magic shortbow (i)

  • A Gem sack may be brought to hold additional gems, or simply a chisel to cut them for Crafting experience and then dropped or alched.

gearNotes.heading: Magic
gearNotes.text:
The reduction in experience at the gemstone crab along with the lack of an elemental weakness means that the experience and cost-efficiency is not as good as other options. For example, Frost Crabs have a 100% weakness to fire spells, and allow the player to idle for 10 minutes at a time with a quick reset in between (the same as the gemstone crab). Rock Crabs are also available with a 20% earth weakness, for those without completion of The Heart of Darkness, and are otherwise nearly identical.

Generally, Magic is much faster and more cost-efficient to train on other monsters or with utility spells, since the gemstone crab has a negative experience multiplier, and does not possess an elemental weakness. One method of magic training that is recommended to be done at the gemstone crab for more active players is to weave in spellcasts while efficiently training one of the other combat styles.

High Level Alchemy is the most accessible spell, and can be cast in between hits. This does take a lot of effort, but can be done without losing any ticks. As an example, alching noted yew longbows profits per cast, granting the player up to per hour along with 78,000 magic experience per hour, if alching consistently. This can be done with a large variety of items, for variable profit.

The spell Telekinetic Grab can also be cast at most times as long as the player is not an Ironman. There is usually a pretty consistent stack of dropped ammunition under the boss from lower level players shooting it without a fully upgraded Ava's device. This can result in upwards of about 125k experience per hour on sufficiently populated worlds that are uncontested for picking up the ammo. Additionally one can profit from the resulting ammo picked up. If using the Eclipse atlatl method with a melee strength boosting cape instead of an Ava's device, this can be done on your own ammunition to not need to rely on other players.

Alternatively, the player can cast Magic Imbue on the Lunar spellbook. This can give passive magic experience at a cost of coins/xp. The spell, which costs and grants 86 experience every 12.6 seconds, adds an additional 24,500 magic experience per hour to the player's total experience, and requires half as many clicks as the previous spells per cast, and is cast less often.

If fighting the gemstone crab is still preferred, the following methods and equipment are recommended:

Low level magic is different to the other combat styles when facing the gemstone crab, in that magic accuracy bonus increases accuracy significantly, magnifying damage and therefore experience rates. With low-tier spells, magic strength bonus is unlikely to result in an increased maximum hit, so it is recommended to bring the best accuracy boosting gear available.

gearNotes.heading: Inventory
gearNotes.text:
• Magic potions or Wizard's mind bombs if 1-2 Magic levels below the next element of spell unlock. (i.e. if casting Earth Bolt at level 34 Magic, boosting to level 35 will increase the max hit to that of Fire Bolt.)
• Teleport to the crab, such as a pendant of Ates, quetzal whistle, or runes for Civitas illa Fortis Teleport
• Runes to cast the spell of choice, such as mind runes, chaos runes, and air runes.
• (Optional) a pickaxe, to mine the boss after defeat and loot a gem.
  • A gem bag may be brought to hold additional gems, or simply a chisel to cut them for Crafting experience and then dropped or alched.

Elder chaos robes provide a 3% magic damage bonus (1% per piece) and good accuracy, and require only 40 Magic and 1 Defence, making them a good low-mid level option for Magic. This magic damage is not enough on its own to grant a max hit, but with Mystic Lore active and casting Iban Blast, one can hit up to 26 damage. For those without access to Iban's staff, a smoke battlestaff in conjunction with the whole set and Mystic Lore can allow Fire Bolt to hit up to 17 damage.
Elite void knight equipment is a strong option, offering a 5% magic damage bonus alongside increased accuracy, enough for a max hit without using Prayer; however obtaining the set requires a significant time investment. It also requires completion of the hard Western Provinces Diary, which requires 64 Magic; at which point Smoke Burst is available to players and can be used for much greater experience against monsters in multicombat.
While the twinflame staff might appear to be an appealing option due to its higher damage output; the reduced attack speed, and no experience for the second spellcast means it provides less experience than other options.

gearNotes.heading: Inventory
gearNotes.text:
• Teleport to the crab, such as a pendant of Ates, quetzal whistle, or runes for Civitas illa Fortis Teleport
• Runes to cast the spell of choice, such as fire runes and death runes.
• (Optional) Prayer restoring items such as prayer potions or Moonlight moth mixes, if not using the altar in Tal Teklan.

  • A gem bag may be brought to hold additional gems, or simply a chisel to cut them for Crafting experience and then dropped or alched.

For higher levels, it is best to bring the highest magic damage boosting gear available and cast the highest tier standard elemental spell you can. Usage of elemental tomes can improve experience rates, but may be more expensive to use than preferred, so a normal offhand can be brought. Augury or Mystic Vigour should be activated to further improve damage, along with Prayer restoration items in the inventory to sustain them.

tactics.heading: Transportation
tactics.text:
Children of the Sun must first be completed to access Varlamore.

After partial completion of Twilight's Promise, the quetzal transport system will become accessible to players. The Civitas illa Fortis Teleport or quetzal whistle can be used to reach the quetzal transport system quickly, which can be used to fly to Tal Teklan to reach the Tlati Rainforest for the first time. From there, run south to the crab nest. Each gemstone crab nest has a cave that leads to the location of the fight, or the next respawn location if between fights. If there is no crab at the location you arrive at, simply use the cave to reach the correct area. After each fight, this is also used to reach the next crab respawn point.

Other methods to reach the gemstone crab include:
• A charged Pendant of Ates can be used to teleport just north of Kastori after activating the Statue of Ates located there. From here, the player can run north to reach the eastern gemstone crab site.
• The Quetzal landing site that must be built at Kastori, which is about the same distance to the eastern crab nest as the Tel Teklan quetzal is to the southern crab nest.
  • The Hunter cape teleport to the Hunter's guild is also next to a Quetzal landing site
• Fairy ring code ais to Auburn Valley. From here, the player can run south west to Achilka, who can take them to both Tal Teklan or Kastori, with both boat endpoints being close to gem crab nests to their north.
• If lacking any of the methods above, walking from Civitas illa Fortis to the Quetzacalli Gorge is safe and there is a mountain guide who will take you to Nemus Retreat. From there you can walk south to Achilka and take her boat.

tactics.heading: Strategy
tactics.text:
Unlike most monsters, the crab does not die. It has effectively infinite health and remains in its nest for 10 minutes before burrowing. As a result, fighting it serves as an idle training method, allowing players to gain combat experience with minimal interaction and little to no downtime.

Almost any equipment can be used effectively, and players of all levels can participate. The crab has no defensive stats, and uses a melee attack that can only hit for 1 damage to players it is facing. As such, accuracy is unnecessary and damage increasing items (those with strength bonus or ranged strength bonus) should be prioritised as much as possible.

Players may wish to consider using low level prayers like Burst of Strength which will always increase max hit, while draining prayer extremely slowly.

Combat experience is reduced by 12.5%, but as there's very little downtime and no overkill damage experience rates are still favorable compared to e.g sand crabs. Melee is the most effective combat style when training against the gemstone crab. Ranged training can be worthwhile at lower levels or if less effort is desired, especially before unlocking better methods such as chinchompas. Magic is less recommended as it's inefficient at all levels (see the section on magic for more information).

The gemstone crab does not count as a crab for the sake of slayer tasks, and so the slayer helmet (i) provides no benefit here.

Turning on Accept Aid can be helpful for main accounts, in case nearby players use hunter's mixes, or, if training multiple accounts at once, to receive the mix's boost from your own accounts. However, this does open the door to having your attacks interrupted by teleother spells.

gearNotes.heading: Solo
gearNotes.text: Killing General Graardor with Melee solo is generally not recommended except if looking to complete The Frozen Door or if you are comfortable flicking prayers between minions and Graardor himself, as the damage taken is significantly greater than with magic or ranged options. If choosing this, an Osmumten's fang is strongly recommended, and all equipment and gear downgrades will significantly affect the amount of kills that can be obtained, down to as few as one per trip with no flicking and poor damage output.

gearNotes.heading: Inventory
gearNotes.text:

• Saradomin godsword or Elder maul/Dragon warhammer (for special attacks)

General Graardor can effectively be killed with Tumeken's shadow, due to its extremely high accuracy and damage. However, due to its multiplicative effect, small downgrades in gear and levels can have a notable impact on damage output, and it is strongly recommended, if not essentially required, to have access to gear such as Ancestral robes, an occult necklace and confliction gauntlets.

Pairing the Eye of Ayak with confliction gauntlets can be an effective strategy if freezing General Graardor due to the increased accuracy buff the confliction gauntlets provide as well.

While lower tier magic weapons can be used, they will be significantly less effective and should not be used except in combination with otherwise best-in-slot gear. With a 40% Earth spell weakness, Earth Wave or Earth Surge can be a competitive option for DPS, but being on the Standard spellbook means relying on other methods to restore health.

Tumeken's shadow is particularly effective against General Graardor, but lower tier weaponry can suffice in teams where another player is tanking the melee hits and catching a freeze is not required. Regardless, strong magic equipment such as an occult necklace and confliction gauntlets are strongly recommended, and players using the standard spellbook to take advantage of Graardor's earth weakness should be mindful of their limited access to heals without access to blood barrage.

tactics.heading: Overview
tactics.text:
This is a guide for killing General Graardor with Melee and Ranged. It has the basics of attacking and tanking, as well as providing a few examples of what equipment to bring.

Note that ranged is the most straightforward combat style to use for solo players, since with proper play it is possible to avoid all damage from Graardor. In teams, it is recommended to have one player tank with melee while the rest of the party uses either melee or ranged.

tactics.heading: Requirements
tactics.text:
• Completion of Death Plateau and partial completion of Troll Stronghold after defeating Dad.
• Alternatively, Ghommal's hilt can be used to teleport to Trollheim without requiring either quest
• One rope is required to access the dungeon for the first time.
• Level 70 Strength is required to enter Bandos' Stronghold (cannot be boosted).
• At least 43 Prayer for access to the protection prayers.
• A hammer (if not bringing an Elder maul or Dragon Warhammer).

tactics.heading: Attack Styles
tactics.text:
Graardor attacks with both Melee and Ranged:

• The melee attack consists of a simple punch that deals up to 60 damage. He has a 2/3 chance of using melee whenever he attacks.
• As his Ranged attack, Graardor slams the ground to emit shockwaves to all players inside his chamber, dealing between 15 and 35 damage on successful hits. Despite it being a Ranged attack, Graardor can only use it within melee range of his current target. He has a 1/3 chance of using Ranged whenever he attacks.

tactics.heading: Bodyguards
tactics.text:
Graardor is protected by three goblin sergeants:

• Sergeant Grimspike is the Ranged bodyguard, who throws axes at his target, dealing up to 21 damage.
• Sergeant Steelwill is the Magic bodyguard, who launches yellow projectiles at his target, dealing up to 15 damage.
• Sergeant Strongstack is the melee bodyguard, who attacks his target with his flail, dealing up to 15 damage.
• The sergeants tend to target the player who last damaged Graardor (on the minions' 5th tick), and the player who deals Graardor's final blow will likely be targeted. Effectively, players with a faster attack speed will tend to be targeted as their attack is more likely to land on their 5th tick. This also means a tank with a Dinh's bulwark on Defence mode will never be focused on, allowing for prioritising Ranged Defence.

tactics.heading: General Strategy
tactics.text:
General Graardor is a formidable foe, with high Defence, extremely powerful melee attacks, and Ranged attacks capable of hitting every player in the room at once. He is also accompanied by three goblin sergeants who use Melee (Sergeant Strongstack), Ranged (Sergeant Grimspike), and Magic (Sergeant Steelwill) attacks.

In terms of Defence, as the bulk of incoming damage potential comes from his melee and Ranged attacks, players targeted by him directly should use Protect from Melee while wearing equipment with high Ranged Defence and moderate Magic Defence; in groups, those not targeted by him directly should use Protect from Missiles.

When Graardor dies, his sergeants will all focus on a single player, typically the one who landed the killing blow on Graardor. With most setups leaving players the most vulnerable to Magic, the targeted player should first switch to Protect from Magic and focus on killing Steelwill. After that, switch to Protect from Missiles so as to block Grimspike's powerful and accurate attacks, leaving Strongstack - the least threatening of the three - for last.

tactics.heading: Solo
tactics.text:
In solo encounters, the player has the option of choosing between all three combat styles; however, Ranged is only used for advanced methods that involve kiting Graardor due to the armour's terrible Ranged Defence. Melee is the simplest way to fight Graardor, but typically involves short trips and the slowest kills overall.

Without justiciar armour, the player will need to bring a ranged body as to protect from Steelwill's attacks as much as possible. Protect from Melee is mandatory to avoid getting killed by Graardor's melee attacks. The player should keep their health above 60 to prevent getting combo'd by Graardor and another sergeant as they will be frequently hit by ranged attacks. With justiciar, the full set can be taken with a spectral or elysian spirit shield, as it provides very high ranged defence and minimises the damage taken from any that should hit, along with reducing Steelwill's accuracy/damage respectively. Grimspike is unlikely to hit as hard in the process. An amulet of blood fury is usually prioritised over offensive alternatives. After killing Graardor, kill Steelwill and then use Guthan's or barrage stack Grimspike and Strongstack as needed.

Graardor has an attack speed of 6, or 3.6 seconds between attacks. 4-tick weapons attack once every 2.4 seconds, so the player can attack Graardor twice before he can attack. After attacking Graardor twice, walk under before attacking him again. If using both a shield and defender, the defender can be used on every odd-numbered attack, provided there is no interruption.

As magic, the player will need to be on the Ancient Magicks and cast Ice Barrage to freeze Graardor, ideally with an Ice ancient sceptre as it is 10% more accurate against an unfrozen target and binds them for 21.6 seconds. Once Graardor is frozen, attack him from a distance until he breaks free, after which the player should barrage him after a few seconds have passed, as subsequent freezes will not bind briefly once it wears off. If Graardor gets too close to the player, swapping to Protect from Melee is beneficial. Alternatively, advanced kiting methods can be utilised if using Tumeken's shadow for quickest kills.

When Graardor dies, players should ideally kill off Steelwill first, then lure Strongstack over to Grimspike, and use Blood Barrage to heal off both of them. Try to ensure that both attack on different ticks to avoid unnecessary damage while healing. A Blood ancient sceptre can be useful for this, as it allows the player to overheal 10% of their base hitpoints (108 hitpoints at level 99) while also healing 2.5% more effectively than a normal blood spell.

Graardor and his bodyguards drop bones upon death, so Bones to Peaches can be used to restore 32 health after each kill. Graardor drops Super restores and his bodyguards drop kebabs, chilli potatoes, and sharks as food to help prolong trips.

tactics.heading: Altar-door
tactics.text:
The altar-door (or door-altar) method is one of the solo ranged kiting methods. It involves attacking in between Red-Xing the Bandos altar and the entrance door, which, if done correctly, will cause Graardor to never attack the player. This method requires a weapon with an attack speed of 4 to work; the most commonly used weapon for this method is the bow of Faerdhinen on rapid. It is strongly recommended to have the "Highlight current tile" setting enabled if playing on the official client, or the "Current tile" setting on the Tile Indicators plugin enabled if playing on RuneLite.

Middle row (subsequent kills:)
• Pray Protect from Missiles. Stand on the southmost tile. Shoot Graardor right as he spawns, then click the altar.
• Shoot Graardor when your true tile is on the red tiles marked "A". After shooting him, click later along the row or on the wall.
  • If you need to heal, do so between the second and third attack, or between the third and fourth attack in the cycle. You cannot heal during the red-x click.
  • If you have made a mistake and need to get back in cycle, skip attacking on the other tiles and run straight to the "Shoot-Door"/"Shoot-Altar" tile while praying Protect from Melee. As soon as Graardor's attack lands, click on the door/altar. Shoot on the next tile as normal. Switch back to Protect from Missiles whenever safe to do so; it is recommended to set your quick prayers to Protect from Missiles and Eagle Eye/Deadeye/Rigour.
• Once you have reached the tile marked "Shoot-Door", shoot Graardor, then click the door.
• Shoot Graardor when your true tile is on the green tiles marked "D". After shooting him, click later along the row or on the wall.
• Repeat steps 2-4 until Graardor is dead. Stack the minions and kill them with Blood Barrage.

West row (first kill:)
• Enter the room, praying Protect from Missiles. Spam-click the tile labelled "Shoot-Door" on the west row.
• As soon as your true tile is on that tile, shoot Graardor, then click the door. Carry on from step 2 above, as you would for subsequent kills.
  • The west row can be used for subsequent kills, though it will be slightly slower than the middle row due to having to spam-click the "Shoot-Door" tile every time, which causes you to begin attacking later. However, this is safer for players inexperienced with the method, as getting out of cycle at the start of the middle row risks taking a melee attack from Graardor, thus requiring to get back in cycle and likely negating some of the time saved.

tactics.heading: Team
tactics.text:
Team settings allow for more flexibility at Graardor as more players will be damaging him, reducing the frequency of ranged attacks in general. Tanks can follow the conventional or justiciar melee setup to tank; due to the extra DPS, they will typically prioritise ranged defence over magic as the bodyguards prioritise those that damage Graardor. An ideal form of tanking is to bring full justiciar with Dinh's bulwark for even more ranged defence, although they are unlikely to gain any personal kills doing so.

Attackers can also prioritise offensive capability over defensive, although they will probably have to watch out for Steelwill who will hit more frequently. Do not attack Graardor until the base tank has obtained his attention, or you will likely have to tank for the duration of the encounter.

After Graardor dies, kill Steelwill, Grimspike and Strongstack in that order. It is common courtesy for the base tank to fight Strongstack alone with Guthan's; unless requested otherwise, Grimspike is also killed by the DPS.

A useful strategy for teams is to drop an item underneath Graardor's spawn spot and have everyone fight him in melee distance. When Graardor focuses on a player, that player will rapidly click on the dropped item. Due to unique mechanics similar to the chinchompa method for Kree'arra, Graardor will be stuck on the spot and be unable to attack. Everyone can attack Graardor in turn until he focuses on another player, in which that player goes under and rapidly clicks on the item until Graardor is killed. This is restricted to melee only, however.

Dolo

Killing General Graardor at max efficiency (50+ kills per hour) entails fighting him on two accounts at the same time (“dolo’ing”) and hopping between two worlds to avoid waiting out the respawn timer.

While various setups can be used to dolo Graardor, the most efficient method is to tank using blood barrage and DPS using max mage. The main account should be equipped with a Tumeken’s shadow and the best magic damage boosting gear possible. The alt account should be equipped with a staff or wand that can auto-cast ancients (such as a Kodai wand), as well as decent tank equipment that has minimal negative magic bonuses (a Bandos chestplate with an Elite void robe bottom is a good option).

Pray ranged on the main and pray melee on the alt. Upon entering the room or when General Graardor spawns, attack him on the alt account, then locate a mage or ranged minion that is not near the north or east walls of the boss room. Move the alt next to this minion, on its south side. This will drag the melee minion and General Graardor’s south-west tile (which determines if he is hit by the blood barrage or not) into a stack on top of the ranged or mage minion, and all three can then be barraged on the tank alt to heal over incoming damage.

Once the blood barrage stack is set and the tank is attacking it, move the main to DD (stand under) the tank account, then attack Graardor on the main. This ensures that the stack does not come apart if minions switch aggro. Continue to attack on both accounts until the boss and all minions are dead, then prepare to switch worlds and repeat the process.

A third account can be used to resupply the two accounts when necessary, avoiding unnecessary time spent gathering kill count.

tactics.heading: Tips
tactics.text:
• Goblins are an easy target for Bandos killcount, and also have a chance to drop a hammer (approx. 1/15, or 1/2 if you don't have one in your inventory).
  • You do not need a hammer to bang the door if bringing a dragon warhammer or elder maul.
• Walking under Graardor can buy a tank some time to eat food without taking unnecessary damage. It can be also done at certain intervals to make Graardor "miss" an attack.
• Experienced players can "tick eat"; tick eating is healing on a critical level of health right before taking damage, essentially surviving a hit that would have normally killed the player.
• Bones to Peaches can help extend trips; each kill rotation yields 32 Hitpoints worth of bones.
• The minions will drop chilli potatoes and sharks. If there is an excess of food, continually pick up and drop food again to prevent it from disappearing (aka "juggling"). This is not necessary if utilizing a private instance, as the despawn timer for dropped items becomes 3 hours inside instances.
• Guthan's equipment may be used to heal on the melee and ranged minions if desired. Cooperate with your team to maximise healing opportunities. Bring fewer brews and more restores if you choose this method of healing. Guthan's armour also doubles as good primary equipment for tanks.
• If you are assigned General Graardor as your Slayer task, use your Slayer helmet variant of choice to take advantage of its accuracy and damage boost.
• An Amulet of blood fury is generally ideal for tank setups as it emphasises healing, defensive bonuses and prayer bonuses.
• During the fight, the bodyguards will target the most recent player who attacked Graardor. Because of this, weapons with a slower attack speed will result in the player being targeted less often in a team. This can be useful in a team where some players have significantly lower defences.
• Boost Potion Share and Stat Restore Pot Share can be used in teams to significantly extend trips, especially in duos, and the Holy wrench or items which share its effect are recommended on the player sharing the Super restores.

tactics.heading: Overview
tactics.text: The Giant Mole is a simple low-level boss that can be found under Falador. It is killed for its mole claw, mole skin, immaculate mole skin, and Baby Mole drops.

tactics.heading: Suggested skills
tactics.text:
• 60+ Attack
• 60+ Strength
• 60+ Defence
• 60+ Hitpoints
• 60+ Ranged (If using ranged)
• 60+ Magic (If using magic)
• 43+ Prayer for Protect from Melee (44+ Eagle Eye, 70+ Piety, 74+ Rigour)

tactics.heading: Transportation
tactics.text:
The Giant Mole is located in the Mole Hole under Falador. The entrance point is located at Falador Park, where there are mole hills scattered on the west side. The closest teleport is the Falador Park option(3) on the ring of wealth. Players must bring a spade to dig underground and a light source of some type is required or they will be constantly bitten by bugs. A Fire of Eternal Light can be lit inside the cave after completing the Making Friends with My Arm quest which provides permanent light inside the cave.

In the north-west of Falador park is a mole hill with a spade. This allows access to a private instance of the mole hill for 25,000 coins. Players who have completed the Hard tier Combat Achievements will receive a reduced price of 12,500 coins. Also, the price is halved for Ironman accounts, reducing the cost to either 12,500 coins or 6,250 coins for those who have completed the Hard Combat Achievements.

tactics.heading: Attacks and abilities
tactics.text:
• Melee attack: The mole swipes a claw at its target, dealing up to 21 damage.
• Burrow: When the mole's health is between 5-50%, there is a 25% chance for any incoming attack to cause it to burrow away into another location. There is also a chance that the dirt she digs while burrowing to escape can extinguish the player's light source (shown with dirt splatters on the player's screen), though covered light sources will be unaffected by this. Note that splashed magic attacks cannot trigger her to dig, making weapons such as the Tumeken's Shadow particularly good for fighting the mole.

tactics.heading: Guide
tactics.text:
Combat with the mole is straightforward, as it doesn't have any unique attacks or abilities that can endanger the player.

For low levelled players, the mole can be safespotted with many of the cavern walls. Maging with earth spells is highly recommended when safespotting. The mole has 50% elemental weakness to earth spells, and splashes cannot trigger the mole to dig. Players meleeing it should activate Protect from Melee and use stab weapons, as it has lower stab defence compared to slash and crush.

For high levelled players, the mole can be killed quickly with Dharok the Wretched's equipment, as it is easily possible to kill her within 2-3 hits depending on the player's strength boosting equipment. Simply lower your health to 1 with the Locator orb or Dwarven rock cake, activate Protect from Melee and flick Piety.

When the mole reaches half health and lower, there is a chance that it will dig away to another location in the lair. Without the Falador shield 3 or 4, it can be a tedious task, as players may have to navigate through the whole lair to find the mole. The mole also loses aggression towards the primary target when burrowing away. Thralls can be used as a makeshift substitute for the Falador shield, as they will begin to path towards the mole's new location after she digs in order to attack her, but as thrall's max hit is 3 and they can make the giant mole dig, this is not recommended.

Completion of the hard Falador diaries is highly recommended, as players with the shield can locate the mole whenever it digs away. It also notes the 100% drop of mole skin and claws, prolonging trips.

Poison is a fantastic tool against the Mole, since she will not burrow from poison damage, significantly shortening kill times. For ironmen without the herblore required to make their own, Poison(++) can be acquired as a fairly common drop from stingrays. Another alternative is completing the Tai Bwo Wannai Trio quest and speaking to Tamayu, who will reward the player with a rune spear (kp). This karambwan-poison-coated weapon has the same poison strength as Poison(++).

gearNotes.heading: Equipment
gearNotes.text: Melee is one of the best ways to kill green dragons at any levels, and becomes the most effective way in terms of kills per hour and cost when using a dragon hunter lance. Setups can vary depending on the player's equipment, stats and how much the player is willing to risk in case of a death. With dragon hunter lance, high stats and the Wilderness elite diary completed (for noted bones) the player can kill up to 300-330 dragons per hour.

gearNotes.heading: Equipment
gearNotes.text: Viggora's chainmace offers the highest damage output, but due to the cost of using revenant ether it is best to use the dragon hunter lance for better profit per hour. Proselyte armour is recommended for its prayer bonus if using damage-boosting prayers such as Piety. Otherwise, the player should wear cheap defensive armour (such as dragonhide or rune armour) for extra defence against the dragons and player killers. Dragonfire shield is strongly recommended for its strength bonus and good defensive stats.

gearNotes.text:

• 1-dose extended antifire or 2-dose antifire potion
• 2-3 prayer potions

• Looting bag
• A teleport for banking and restoring stats such as a ring of dueling or a teleport to house tablet

The Webweaver bow, Craw's bow, and toxic blowpipe offer slightly higher kills per hour than using a dragon hunter lance, but due to the high cost of using these weapons it is only recommended for Ironmen who wish to bank dragon bones for Prayer experience. Otherwise, melee usually offers higher kills and better profit per hour.

gearNotes.heading: Equipment
gearNotes.text: Void Knight equipment is the best option due to its damage-boosting set effect. If wearing full Void Knight equipment however, it is recommended to only use the spot west of Dark Warriors' Fortress between level 12 and 14 Wilderness, as you will not risk untradeable items on death. If wearing black d'hide, it is recommended to use the spot east of black salamanders in level 20-22 Wilderness as there are more green dragon spawns. If not wearing an anti-dragon shield, the player must use Protect from Magic or extended super antifire potions.

tactics.heading: Requirements
tactics.text:
Green dragons are fairly easy monsters to kill for profit, even for lower level players. Killing them is also the fastest way of banking Prayer experience on an Ironman account. It is recommended to have at least level 70+ in all Melee skills or Ranged for reasonable kills per hour. Gear setups can vary greatly depending on stats, how much money the player has available and how much one is willing to risk in case of a death. As the green dragons are located primarily in the Wilderness, players should only take equipment and items that they do not mind potentially losing.

Completing the elite tasks in the Wilderness diary grants noted bones in the Wilderness.

tactics.heading: Transportation
tactics.text:
Getting there is quite simple, as the games necklace offers a teleport to the Corporeal Beast's lair. Clicking on the opening in the wall, the player will enter the Wilderness and only has to run west to reach the dragons, which are located north of the Graveyard of Shadows. Players can also use obelisks, or simply walk north from Ferox Enclave.

Players can also use a canoe to get to the lava maze and safespot them from inside. You will need to take law and air runes to telegrab the drops.

Green dragons can also be killed in Wilderness Slayer Cave which offers considerably lower risk of getting PK'd as you can use teleports below 30 Wilderness. They can easily be safespotted here, as there is a corridor too narrow for the dragons to walk through.

gearNotes.text: During the fight, players will need a rock hammer, granite hammer, or rock thrownhammer to deal the final blow. Magic is not recommended as Dawn is more resistant to magic than the other forms of damage she is susceptible to: Ranged and melee with halberds. An eternal slayer ring is highly recommended for fairly quick banking and access to the bosses.

gearNotes.text:
A form of sustain, such as a blood fury, full guthans, or a saradomin godsword with a lightbearer can be brought over food, as it is very easy to heal due to the bosses' incredibly low defence. Alternatively, the bosses commonly drop mushroom potatoes which can extend trips, although this is not guaranteed.

If no sustains are used, super restores are recommended over prayer potions to make use of saradomin brews, though these are not always dropped alongside combat potions and will require the player to boost it back up if the brews are drunk. However, the bosses can drop (regular, not divine) 2-dose super combat and ranging potions.
