tactics.heading: Overview
tactics.text:
The Grotesque Guardians are a pair of gargoyle slayer bosses that reside at the roof of the Slayer Tower: the Guardian of Dusk and Guardian of Dawn. In order to access and fight them, players must first acquire a brittle key from regular gargoyles (or their superior variant). The key is only obtainable as a drop whilst assigned gargoyles as a slayer task, which is dropped at a rate of 1/150.

After obtaining the brittle key, players can unlock the tower's rooftop entrance on the (right next to the gargoyle area), permanently unlocking access. However, the player must additionally be assigned gargoyles or the Grotesque Guardians themselves as a slayer task or boss task respectively.

If the player dies while fighting the Grotesque Guardians, lost items are placed into the magical chest near the rooftop entrance, where players must pay a fee of 50,000 coins to reclaim their items. Note that dying an unsafe death before reclaiming lost items from the chest will result in permanent loss of all the items inside; as such, unless the player has level 81 Agility (can be boosted) to climb the Ivy agility shortcut found west of the slayer tower's entrance, which leads up to the start of the top floor, it is highly recommended to bring a nosepeg or equivalent item to protect from aberrant spectres on the way back.

As with all other gargoyles, players must bring a rock hammer, granite hammer, or rock thrownhammer to finish them off.

Note that unlike other instances, players are kicked out of their instance after five minutes of inactivity; players are warned when there is one minute remaining, and another when thirty seconds remain. Players can reset this timer by ringing the Cloister Bell.

tactics.heading: Requirements
tactics.text:
• 75 Slayer and a gargoyle slayer task
• Completion of Quest Priest in Peril to access Morytania
• A rock hammer or thrownhammer
• Unlocked the Slayer tower rooftop with a brittle key
• Melee equipment, plus Ranged or Magic if not using a halberd

tactics.heading: Recommendations
tactics.text:
• 75+ Attack
• 75+ Strength
• 70+ Defence
• 75+ Ranged
• 75+ Hitpoints
• 70+ Prayer for Piety, (74+ for Rigour)
• 81 Agility+ for shortcuts

tactics.heading: Transportation
tactics.text:
There are several ways to access the Slayer Tower:
• The slayer ring teleports players to the main entrance.
• The fairy ring code CKS is south of the Tower.
• Casting Salve Graveyard Teleport will also take players south of the Tower.
• Casting Kharyrll Teleport will take players to Canifis which is a short distance from the bank.

Players with level 61 Agility can climb up the spikey chain on the (marked by a icon) to reach the next level; if not wearing a nosepeg or equivalent item, players are warned to wear one beforehand. Upon climbing up the chain, players can then climb the staircase to the south-west to reach the rooftop entrance.

Alternatively, players with 81 Agility can use the Ivy outside of the tower entrance to immediately get to the rooftop. This shortcut is recommended for players who find themselves dying multiple times to the Guardians; it removes the risk of dying a second time from aberrant spectres or other monsters on the way to the magical chest, and potentially losing valuable items.

tactics.heading: Fight overview
tactics.text:
The fight is started by ringing the Cloister Bell, which initiates a cutscene in which the Guardians awaken and face the player; upon reaching five kill count for the boss, the bell gains a "Quick-start" option to start the fight immediately.

During the first three phases, Dusk uses a slash-style attack that deals up to 15 damage; Protect from Melee will reduce the damage dealt by 80%. Meanwhile, Dawn uses a ranged attack that deals two separate hits, both with a max hit of 9. If within melee distance, she may also kick the player for up to 15 damage. The attacks are partially blocked by prayer; praying against melee reduces the max hit of the melee attacks to 2.

tactics.heading: Phase 1
tactics.text:
Dusk is immune to all damage during this phase, so the player must fight Dawn first. As she is airborne, the player must attack her with ranged, magic, or with a halberd; she is immune to non-halberd melee attacks.

Aside from her standard attacks, Dawn may launch a Stone Ball which has a 3x3 Area-of-Effect (1 tile from the centre). If struck, the player will become encased in stone, similar to the marble gargoyle's special attack, which acts as a freeze for 10 ticks (6 seconds) and deals up to 15 damage.

You can minimise damage by starting the fight from the left-most tile next to the bell, as this will automatically off-tick the Guardians.
Start with Protect from Missiles, switch to Protect from Melee when Dawn's attack animation starts, and switch back to Protect from Missiles immediately after Dusk's attack animation starts.
For less effort you can use Protect from Melee and stand next to Dawn, which will cause her to occasionally use melee attacks. Players can also dance under Dusk and use Protect from Missiles if desired.

The optimal method to attack Dawn with ranged is to stack both her and Dusk on top of each other, then using the venator bow. When charged, it will ricochet the shots and hit Dawn twice. Players can use a toxic blowpipe to attack Dawn whilst waiting for Dusk to approach. If using melee, a noxious halberd is required, as all other halberds hit too slow.

Upon reaching 55% health, she will ascend to the sky, beginning the next phase of the fight.

tactics.heading: Phase 2
tactics.text:
Dusk becomes attackable during this phase. Dusk's armour protects him from both magic and ranged attacks, so players must use melee on him. Additionally, burn damage has no effect against him. Dusk has -1 flat armour, encouraging the use of multi-hit weapons, although his abysmal Defence and bonuses make any weapon viable to use.

After attacking once, he will start to charge his blinding attack, indicated by his missing wing starting to glow; simply move one tile away from Dusk to avoid the attack. Otherwise, the player will be knocked back and dealt damage in the high 20s. The player will be able to attack three times with any four or five tick weapon before needing to back away.

The knockback animation will only occur if players are right next to or under him. The timeframe to get hit by this attack is relatively short; it is safe to return back and attack Dusk once his wings cover his face, though running back to him just as he expands his wings will result in getting hit.

Throughout this phase, Dawn will also occasionally use a rockfall attack, throwing down 9-10 pieces of debris into the roof at four different speeds, indicated with looming shadows over the targeted tiles. Like Stone Ball, these rockfalls have a 3x3 AoE. Getting caught in the edges can deal up to 22 damage, while being caught directly in one will also knock the player out, stunning them for 10 ticks (6 seconds).

Lastly, standing under Dusk during this phase can result in him trampling the player for up to 40 damage and should be avoided at all costs.

When Dusk reaches 55% of his health, Dawn will descend, beginning the third phase of the fight.

tactics.heading: Phase 3
tactics.text:
Dusk will quickly fly over to the west, then the pair will begin to charge up a lightning attack, discharging bolts of lightning that deal 5-10 damage per tick if the player is standing on or adjacent to the vortices. The vortices spawn anywhere on the rooftop, with one always targeting the tile the player is standing on. They do not stack on each other, although up to three circles may be in close proximity to each other.

There is a one-second warning frame indicated with a vortex of the respective colour before the player starts taking damage. Stand in a spot clear of any vortices; although some vortices appear later than others, they will all expire once the pair become attackable.

Once the attack ends, Dawn becomes attackable whilst Dusk returns to being invulnerable. She will start off by launching three energy spheres across the rooftop in an attempt to heal herself. There are three charge stages for these spheres, each advancing to the next after a few seconds. The player can absorb these spheres by walking into them at any time without penalty; if Dawn absorbs them once they fully charge, they will each heal 90 hitpoints.

Dawn will use the same attacks as she did in phase 1. Players can pray against both attacks by being one tile west from the eastern wall (not under or next to Dawn) right after the lightning AoE. Start by praying melee, then ranged and so on. If you notice you don't have enough DPS to skip the orbs, prioritise absorbing those, then finish the kill by standing next to Dawn and praying melee.

Once Dawn reaches less than 10 health, use the rock hammer on her (unless the Gargoyle smasher ability is unlocked). Dusk will absorb the remnants of her essence, empowering himself in the process, and initiate the final phase of the fight.

Players with 90+ Ranged or 90+ melee stats should be able to "orb skip", or kill Dawn before she has a chance to absorb any orbs. To do this with ranged, either a toxic blowpipe or venator bow, coupled with amethyst ammo or better, should be used on Dawn. The blowpipe has a ~75% chance of an orb skip, while the venator bow has a ~80-85% chance of an orb skip. When using melee, a noxious halberd is still required, though a crystal halberd can be used as a finisher. With a lightbearer, players should not worry too much about special attack; Death Charge can also be used, but this will likely shorten trips due to the rune equipment drops the boss frequently drops.

tactics.heading: Phase 4
tactics.text:
As Dawn shatters into bits, Dusk will absorb the leftover remains of her essence. Dusk's Attack level increases to 300, with Strength, Magic, and Ranged increased to 250, Defence to 150, and add one flat armour. Upon transforming, he will immediately use his prison attack, dragging the player somewhere within the arena and trapping them in a barrier of blue flames. One of the flames is missing, which is the first tile the player can stand on to avoid damage. If the player does not escape from the 3x3 "cell" within 5 ticks, they will take up to 65 damage, and the damage dealt by this attack will heal Dusk. Dusk's size is additionally increased from a 5x5 to a 6x6 monster.

Sometimes, Dusk may drag the player to the edges, then create a barrier where the exit cannot be used because there is no space to escape. In this case, simply running into the missing fire tile will prevent Dusk from damaging the player and healing himself. When he first uses this attack, he is invulnerable, but he can still be attacked in subsequent drag attacks. In these cases, the player can simply attack Dusk to path out of the prison, though it is still encouraged to click on a safe tile first.

As with the previous phases, Dusk is immune to magic and ranged attacks and his trample attack is reactivated. Be careful not to click on Dusk until his prison attack animation is fully complete or you may accidentally run under him and be trampled.

Dusk's attacks are improved upon, now using both melee and ranged much like Dawn did. The melee attack can deal up to 26 damage, while the ranged attack hits twice, with a max hit of 15 each for a total of up to 30 damage.

The ranged attack has a unique form of damage calculation. If Dusk succeeds the ranged accuracy check, the first orb will always hit for 60% of his max hit, or half of that number if the player is praying correctly. The second orb meanwhile will carry out a random damage roll upon succeeding the accuracy check, yet goes on to make a second damage roll ranging between 0 and the damage value rolled directly prior.

Prayer reduces the strength of Dusk's melee attack by roughly 80%, and ranged by 55%, which in turn reduces the max hits to around ~4 and 14 (7 x 2) respectively. For his first attack at the start of the phase, there is a 2/3 chance Dusk will use the opposite attack style of the one the player is praying against. Afterward, he has a 1/6 chance to alternate attack styles every time he attacks; if using the matching protection prayer, he will instead have a 1/3 chance to switch attack styles. For simplicity, as it is hard to predict Dusk's attacks when in melee range, it is best to pray against the style of the attack he previously used.

When Dusk attacks the player, halberd-using players are encouraged to stand one tile away from him when possible. Dusk will stay still when attacking with ranged and close the distance when attacking with melee.

When Dusk reaches less than 10 health, the player should use the rock hammer on him (unless the Gargoyle smasher ability is unlocked). It is possible for Dusk's second-phase special attack to happen as or shortly after Dusk is killed with a rock hammer; the player can still take damage from the special attack after Dusk dies. Additionally, if the player is inside the barrier and Dusk is at low enough health to be smashed with the Gargoyle smasher ability, the player may path directly to Dusk instead of trying to exit the barrier first, or may not move at all.

gearNotes.heading: Equipment
gearNotes.text:
Hespori can easily be tackled with low cost equipment. Use knives, darts, or a powered stave to attack the flowers that Hespori spawns at 100%, 66%, and 33% health, and use special attacks such as a dragon dagger where possible to speed up the fight. At lower levels you will encounter Hespori's immobilizing special attack at least once per fight, and it is important to click away repeatedly or risk taking a large amount of damage at once.

Thralls and Death Charge can be used on the flowers for additional damage and access to an extra special attack or two during the fight.

gearNotes.heading: Inventory
gearNotes.text:
• Dragon dagger for special attacks
• Hespori seed, spade, and, if the barehanded planting section of Barbarian training is incomplete, a seed dibber to harvest and replant Hespori
• Super combat potion or a super set
• Knives or darts to quickly kill flowers
• Rune pouch and Book of the Dead to use Thralls
• A prayer potion in case of a long fight, or at lower prayer levels
• Any form of antipoison
• Cooked food for remaining inventory spaces

gearNotes.heading: Notes
gearNotes.text:
• If casting a thrall, do so after waking Hespori.
• Hespori is immune to the ring of recoil.

With high combat stats and good equipment, little to no food or prayer restore will be needed when fighting hespori.

Blisterwood stake is an easily renewable "free" dart that has long range, allowing the player to stand still during the fight.

With the rite of vile transference unlocked, the upgraded Death Charge can be used on the second set of flowers, along with a dose of surge potion at 81 Herblore, for a total of 155 special attack energy.

Due to Hespori's elemental weakness to fire spells, maging Hespori is viable, especially at lower levels and with access to gear that boosts elemental spell damage, such as the Harmonised Nightmare staff, Twinflame staff, and Smoke battlestaff or Tome of Fire. However, meleeing Hespori provides access to thralls and better special attack weapons, and will typically be cheaper especially if using Sunfire runes or pages.

tactics.heading: Overview
tactics.text:
Hespori can be periodically killed in the Farming Guild, grown from a hespori seed.

Typically, a melee slash weapon is used to kill Hespori.

tactics.heading: Requirements
tactics.text:
• Level 65 Farming
• One hespori seed for each kill

tactics.heading: Suggested skills
tactics.text:
• 60 Attack+
• 60 Strength+
• 60 Hitpoints+

tactics.heading: Mechanics
tactics.text:
The Hespori is benign until the player attempts to harvest it. You can enter the cave, drink potions and enable prayers before starting the fight.

The Hespori is surrounded by four flower buds that keep it invulnerable while it attacks the player. These buds open three times during the fight, on initiation of the fight and again when the Hespori has 66% and 33% health remaining. Each bud has 10 hitpoints but will die in one hit from any weapon.

The Hespori has a ranged attack, a magic attack, and a special attack:

Ranged Attack:

Throws green spores that hit twice with a max hit of 8+8 (reduced to 2+2 with Protect from Missiles).

Magic Attack:

A green wave with a max hit of 14 (reduced to 3 with Protect from Magic).

Special Attack:

will appear in the chatbox when the Hespori uses this special attack, with roots immobilizing the player preventing movement and attacks. After 6 seconds (10 ticks) the player will take 40+ damage unless they break free early by clicking repeatedly on either a new tile or the Hespori. As you click, will appear in the chatbox. After this message appears for the 5th time, clicking once more will prevent the special attack and allow the player to move and attack again.

gearNotes.heading: Inventory
gearNotes.text:
• Some type of weapon switch.
• Some type of anti-poison.
• Some type of prayer restoration.
• Whatever food you enjoy to eat.

tactics.heading: Requirements
tactics.text:
and a Kourend echo orb, which is a guaranteed drop from Hespori.

Bring a Spade to collect the drops.

tactics.heading: Ranged attack
tactics.text: The Echo Hespori attacks with a two-hit ranged attack that applies poison similar to that of the regular Hespori.

tactics.heading: Magic attack
tactics.text: A blue wave that must be prayed against before it hits the player and can deal over 50 damage.

tactics.heading: Special attack
tactics.text:
A slow-moving projectile that targets the quadrant of the arena where the player is standing and causes the targeted area to explode for significant (30+) damage.

A shadow on the ground is visible when her special attack is launched.

tactics.heading: Flowers
tactics.text:
The Hespori is surrounded by 14 flowers, split into 2 W-shaped patterns of 5 on the north and south sides of the arena, and a cluster of 4 on the eastern wall of the arena.

At 75, 50 and 25 percent of the Hespori's health, some or all of the flowers become active and the boss becomes invulnerable until all active flowers are killed.

• At 75 and 25 percent, all flowers become active. The flowers on the north and south sides are protected from non-melee styles, and the flowers on the east side are protected from melee.
• At 50 percent, all flowers on the east side and 4 to 6 random flowers on the north and south sides become active. All active flowers are protected from melee.

Active flowers can be attacked with no attack delay, and always die to any attack with the appropriate style. While flowers are active, the Hespori will not use its magic attack.

gearNotes.heading: Equipment
gearNotes.text:
Melee is the simplest and lowest requirement style for effectively killing jellies. Using Protect from Melee will negate all damage taken. Their attacks are magic-based melee, so if you're not praying against their attacks, you'll need to wear armour that is resistant to magical attacks. Wearing armour with high magic defence (such as Karil's armour or black dragonhide armour) will suffice. Higher combat level players may find a small amount of food to suffice for fighting regular jellies (not Warped jellies) instead of using prayer.

The Ring of wealth may be considered as coins are a common drop, though a combat-boosting ring such as a berserker ring may be preferable for more experienced players.

Jellies may be killed with Magic for the fastest possible kills in multicombat areas (particularly within the Catacombs of Kourend), by using multi-target Ancient Magicks such as Ice Burst or Ice Barrage. Using Protect from Melee to mitigate all damage taken is highly recommended.

Knives or Darts (preferably the cheapest available, such as Bronze or Iron) are recommended for quickly tagging non-aggressive monsters to stack for multi-target spells. The Dinh's bulwark, especially in combination with a Lightbearer, can be used in addition to darts/knives to quickly tag many monsters even faster.

Ranged can be used with the Venator bow as an alternative to Ancient Magicks in multicombat areas. While it cannot achieve the same kill speed as Magic can with Ice Barrage, it requires significantly less effort to achieve considerably faster kills than Melee or single-target setups. Using Protect from Melee to mitigate all damage taken is highly recommended.

gearNotes.heading: Inventory
gearNotes.text:
• A Slayer ring or Dramen staff/Lunar staff for teleporting to the Fremennik Slayer Dungeon if killing regular Jellies.
• Runes for Kourend Castle Teleport or a Xeric's talisman with the Xeric's Heart teleport unlocked, for teleporting to the Catacombs of Kourend if killing Warped jellies.
• 1-2 divine super combat potions or super sets if using Melee; or 1-2 divine ranging potions or ranging potions if using Ranged.
• Some super restores, prayer potion, or food; to either negate damage with Protect from Melee, or heal damage taken.
• The rune pouch should be filled with runes for high alchemy if using Melee or Ranged, or Ice Burst/Ice Barrage if using Magic.
• Explorer's ring 4 to alchemise drops if using Ancient Magicks.
• A few empty inventory spaces for coins, and picking up higher value items to sell or alchemise.
• An empty space for brimstone keys is necessary if performing Konar quo Maten tasks.
• Gem bag for uncut gems drops

tactics.heading: Overview
tactics.text:
Jellies can be assigned as a Slayer task at level 52 Slayer and level 57 combat by various medium-level Slayer masters. They are found in the Fremennik Slayer Dungeon. They are popular to kill similarly to hellhounds due to their high drop rate of hard clue scrolls. While fairly weak, jellies have an unusually high Defence level compared to other similar monsters around their level.

It is not recommended to kill normal jellies in most circumstances as they have a fairly poor drop table and are very far from a bank.

Two stronger variants of jellies can be found on Zeah; the Warped Jelly in the Catacombs of Kourend, and the Chilled jelly in the Ruins of Tapoyauik/Grimstone Dungeon.

Warped jellies are in a Multicombat area and are popular for barrage tasks, along with having a better drop table and the Catacombs table. Chilled jellies are in a single combat area and require completion of The Heart of Darkness or level 87 Sailing; they have the exact same table as warped jellies (except without the Catacombs table and including frozen tear and moon tooth half drops if fought in the Ruins of Tapoyauik), but have a 50% susceptibility to fire spells. Despite their higher Magic level, they are still easy to hit with magic.

Players who are assigned jellies by Krystilia can kill them in the Wilderness Slayer Cave, where nine jellies can be found in a multicombat area. As this location is in the Wilderness, players should be mindful of the risk they bring and not bring items they are unwilling to lose, as the cave is a popular player killing hotspot. There is only one entrance to the jellies and they are below level 30 Wilderness, so players can easily escape with a one-click teleport such as a royal seed pod if any player killers arrive.

Magic = Tumeken's shadow provides the highest DPS against K'ril. Mage is not recommended with any weapon weaker than a Tumeken's shadow. Using the 5:0 method to avoid all damage from K'ril is highly recommended due to magic armour's low defences, while praying Protect from Range to protect against the range minion. Blood Barrage is used to heal off the melee and range minions in between kills.

A Purging staff can be used, but requires the player to bring a way to heal themselves between kills, such as Sanguinesti staff.

gearNotes.heading: Inventory
gearNotes.text:
• Staff to autocast Ancient magicks against the minions like Eldritch Nightmare staff, Kodai wand, or Blood ancient sceptre
• Saturated heart to boost magic level
• Sanfew serums, or Super restores and Antidote++
• Extended stamina potions or Stamina potions (it is unlikely that you will need any run energy restoration if you have a high enough agility level)
• Anglerfish or other high healing food (the better you get at performing the 5:0 method, the less food you will need to bring)
• Rune pouch with runes to cast Blood Barrage for healing and Ice Barrage to freeze Tstanon Karlak
• A Construction cape or house tab for escaping
• Explorer's ring 4 (for high alch and energy recharges)

tactics.heading: Overview
tactics.text:
This is a guide on killing K'ril Tsutsaroth. K'ril Tsutsaroth is commonly killed for his drops which include the Zamorakian spear, staff of the dead and the Zamorak hilt. He can be fought with any of the three combat styles and either solo or in a team.

The Zamorakian encampment, including K'ril Tsutsaroth's chamber, appears shadowy and dark; the farther down players venture, the darker it becomes, becoming near pitch dark when outside the door leading to his chamber and inside itself. This is purely a visual change and has no actual gameplay effects. The shadow effect can be removed by consuming a Saradomin's light.

tactics.heading: Requirements
tactics.text:
• Completion of Death Plateau and the start of Troll Stronghold to the point where you defeat Dad
• Alternatively, Ghommal's hilt can be used to teleport to Trollheim without requiring either quest
• One rope is required to access the God Wars Dungeon for the first time.
• 70 Hitpoints (boostable) are required to access Zamorak's Fortress.

tactics.heading: Attack Styles
tactics.text:
K'ril attacks with both Magic and Melee:

• K'ril swipes at his target with his scimitars for his melee attack, dealing up to 46 damage. The attack also has a chance of inflicting poison, even through Protect from Melee, with damage starting at 16. He has a 2/3 chance of performing a melee attack.
• K'ril raises both of his scimitars in the air before slamming them down as his magic attack, emitting a magical shock wave at his target. This attack deals a minimum of 10 damage and a maximum of 30 damage if it hits. He has a 1/3 chance of performing this attack.
• Both attacks are single-target.

tactics.heading: Prayer Smash
tactics.text:
K'ril has a 1/9 chance of using this attack instead of a melee hit if his target is using Protect from Melee. He will yell when using his prayer smash, always dealing 35-49 damage and draining his target's current prayer points by half, rounded down. Using a Spectral spirit shield halves the prayer drain to 1/4.
To fully avoid this attack, the tank should use Protect from Magic and maximize Melee defence; this also prevents damage being taken from the Magic-using Balfrug Kreeyath. This strategy will result in a much longer trip with your team.

tactics.heading: Bodyguards
tactics.text:
K'ril is protected by three demons:

• Balfrug Kreeyath, the magic bodyguard; a black demon that launches fire spells at his target, dealing up to 16 damage.
• Tstanon Karlak, the melee bodyguard; a greater demon that uses melee, clawing his target, dealing up to 15 damage.
• Zakl'n Gritch, the ranged bodyguard; a lesser demon that throws snowballs at his target, dealing up to 21 damage.

The bodyguards will focus on a random player in the room when K'ril is killed, regardless of whoever deals the killing blow.

tactics.heading: General strategy
tactics.text:
K'ril attacks with both melee and magic, but his magic attack can only be used against players in melee range. As such, if using melee, it is recommended for solo players (or in groups, the tank) to wear armour with high magic defence and use Protect from Melee during the kill. While this approach does leave players susceptible to his occasional prayer smash attack, it is still generally more efficient than doing the opposite.

After K'ril has been killed, the minions each focus on a random player. Because of this, players should adjust their prayers accordingly and focus on killing minions which are focusing on the same player. As K'ril and his minions drop ashes, bones to peaches cannot be used, and players should manage their hitpoints adequately. In group encounters, using Guthan's is recommended; in solo encounters, Blood Barrage is more effective. When casting Blood Barrage, make sure to stack Tstanon on Zakl'n so both demons can be hit by the spell. Bringing water runes (or a Kodai wand) is optional for Ice Barrage, but can freeze Tstanon in place so the player doesn't have to flick between ranged and melee prayers as frequently.

Because bones to peaches cannot be used, it is worthwhile to bring runes for Boost Potion Share and Stat Restore Pot Share to extend trips when going in a team. If not using Lunar spells, players can use Ward of Arceuus to reduce damage taken, and Death Charge to boost special attack energy. In a team it is helpful (but not required) for one or more players to be on task.

tactics.heading: Solo
tactics.text:
A popular strategy for soloing K'ril is using a scorching bow with a lightbearer. The player can use the bow's special attack to bind K'ril in place and avoid all damage from him. This allows for long trips of up to 20-40 kills.

Players should pray Protect from Missiles to avoid damage from Zakl'n Gritch, and start each kill in the room's north-west corner (as this is far from where Tstanon Karlak spawns). One special attack from the bow will have the bind last for six attacks in total, so use it again on the seventh attack to reapply the bind, and move counterclockwise around the room to kite him and Tstanon Karlak. With good stats and gear, players should never run out of special attack energy, especially when on-task. Once K'ril is dead, kill Balfrug Kreeyath and then stack the other two minions to heal from Blood Barrage.

For those without access to a lightbearer, death charge can also allow for enough special attack energy replenishment for a long trip. As this requires the Arceuus spellbook, blood barrage will not be available and alternative healing sources such as Guthans or more brews will be needed, resulting in shorter trips.

Another strategy is to use the Tumeken's shadow in conjunction with the 5:0 method. Tumeken's shadow with max mage gear deals significantly higher DPS than other solo methods, but requires significantly more concentration, being tick perfect, and high click precision. Players can expect upwards of 30 kills per hour using this method, and if done correctly, can expect trips to last indefinitely if using a private instance to keep supply drops from despawning.

tactics.heading: Tank
tactics.text:
For tanks, K'ril Tsutsaroth can be extremely dangerous when using Protect from Melee, as there is a very slim chance to take incredibly high damage should K'ril's prayer slam and both Balfrug and Zakl'n hit on the same or near ticks. For this reason, the tank should bring typical tank setup as with Graardor.

Another alternative is to focus solely on melee and ranged defence, using Protect from Magic to cover the magic weakness, as K'ril will not be able to use his prayer slam, Balfrug becomes completely harmless while Tstanon and Zakl'n will have trouble hitting the player. This in turn means K'ril's melee attacks are the only thing to watch out for as a tank.

This defensive setup is particularly favourable using a full set of justiciar armour with echo boots or guardian boots; while the player will miss out on a slayer helm's bonuses if on a task, justiciar provides the best melee defence, which can be combined with an elysian spirit shield or dragonfire shield for very high defensive bonuses, complementing the set's passive damage reduction bonus, with the former adding onto it. The glove and amulet slots aren't as of much concern for a defensive setup, and should be focused on improving the player's accuracy.

Similar to tanking General Graardor, the player should hit K'ril Tsutsaroth twice for every hit he inflicts on them to avoid as much damage as possible. This means that a player using Melee will be hit every 8 game ticks, while a player using Ranged with an Armadyl crossbow will be hit every 10 game ticks. In a solo scenario, using Melee practically is the only viable option due to the high damage-per-second of the arclight compared to the Armadyl crossbow, however in a team, Ranged can also be used in combination with Armadyl armour for greater magic defence. Generally soloing K'ril Tsutsaroth is only viable on a Slayer task, and the same strategy should be used for soloing Graardor, see here. Finally the tank may use the Lunar spell Vengeance to occasionally reflect high amounts of damage back onto K'ril Tsutsaroth. Further details on each tanking strategy are given in the equipment tabs.

tactics.heading: Attacker
tactics.text: At the beginning of the fight, the attackers should all stand in one of the corners near the altar, as this both is the furthest away you can get from K'ril Tsutsaroth's spawn and allows prayer restoration in the last few seconds before the boss respawns. Attackers should only attack K'ril Tsutsaroth once the tank has hit him, this is especially important when the tank is using ranged as it takes a little more time for a ranged attack to hit K'ril Tsutsaroth compared to a melee attack. As K'ril Tsutsaroth's attacks only hit the tank, the attackers should pray against whichever minion does the most damage to their respective combat style, and wear armour to tank damage against the other combat styles. This effectively means that attackers take relatively small amounts of damage during kills, especially if their Defence is high. Players using Melee should use Protect from Magic, players using Ranged should use Protect from Missiles. It is important to note that should K'ril Tsutsaroth focus on you, the armour you are wearing is generally quite bad at tanking him and you will take excessive amounts of damage. Should this happen, players using Melee should use Protect from Magic, players using Ranged should use Protect from Melee. All attackers should also bring an antidote++, both for this eventuality and to share with the tank should they run out of antidotes.

tactics.heading: Suggested skills
tactics.text:
Tank:
• 90+ Hitpoints
• 90+ Defence
• 85+ Magic
• 85+ Attack and 85+ Strength or 85+ Ranged
• 70+ Prayer

Attacker:
• 80+ Hitpoints
• 80+ Defence
• 75+ Magic
• 85+ Attack and 85+ Strength or 85+ Ranged
• 70+ Prayer

tactics.heading: Killcount
tactics.text:
The 40 (35/30/25/15) Zamorakian followers kill count (reduced kill count requirement with the hard/elite/master/grandmaster combat achievements respectively) is quite easy to achieve although it will take longer than Bandos. There are several tips to get a quick kill count:

• Main room: The place north and east of the rope has Zamorakian followers fighting both Bandosians in the north and Saradominists in the east. There are two imps which can be quickly killed, and other followers such as bloodvelds, goraks, werewolves and icefiends battling spiritual warriors and spiritual mages.
• Zamorak's Fortress: There are four imp spawns which can be quickly killed for kill count. Switching back and forth between two worlds while killing the imps with ranged attacks is the fastest way to gain kill count.

gearNotes.heading: Equipment
gearNotes.text:
• A Dragon warhammer or Elder maul is important for lowering Kalphite Queen's defence if using melee and ranged, making both forms much faster to kill.

• The Ring of suffering (ri) is useful here due to Kalphite Queen constantly hitting you for high damage, triggering the recoil effect. Alternatively, the Lightbearer can give additional follow up special attacks if you are not resetting every kill. Both are generally better than strength rings, as extra defence reduction and recoiled damage add up over both phases.

• It is still recommended to occasionally flinch the boss when you have to eat or if your supplies are low towards the end of a kill. Step under the boss to limit the amount of times that the Kalphite Queen can hit. This can be further optimised by using a fast weapon, (such as a blowpipe), followed by a slower heavy hitting weapon, (such as a crossbow) each time you step out from underneath KQ before returning underneath. You are effectively doing 7 cycles of damage vs. the Queen's 4, and will significantly reduce the amount of damage you take throughout the fight.

• An Anglerfish can be eaten before banking for the fight to boost hitpoints for a slight advantage.

• Using a Slayer Helm (i) while on task provides a far greater bonus to DPS than any other piece of gear. If you are struggling, do Slayer tasks until you receive a kalphite task. This will massively improve your chances of success.

gearNotes.heading: Pre-Elite Desert Diary
gearNotes.text: Players may need to complete up to 256 killcount before receiving the kq head or tattered kq head to complete the Elite Desert Diary and unlock the shortcut at 86 Agility. Until then, it is generally better to maximise kills per trip by minimising extra switches and/or flinching the boss.

gearNotes.heading: Post-Elite Desert Diary
gearNotes.text:
With the desert elite diary completed, it becomes much more beneficial to focus on high damage output as it is quick to return to the lair after restoring stats at your POH with the agility shortcut. This method capitalises on maximum Melee and Ranged/Magic attack bonuses, and every kill will start with full health, prayer, and special attack.

Having a Kalphite Slayer task to use the Slayer helmet is strongly recommended for saving an inventory space and significantly boosting damage.

With the recoil enabled, ring of suffering (ri) deals a lot of damage due to the frequency and severity of the Queen's attacks. An ultor ring with a scythe or partisan of breaching are an exception due to their unique damage scaling, but the suffering provides extra damage during both phases and when not using melee.
If you take too much damage, step under the boss to heal. Otherwise, heal during the phase transition.

tactics.heading: Overview
tactics.text:
The Kalphite Queen is a boss located in the Kharidian Desert. She is stronger than her combat level suggests due to her damage output ability.

If using the non-instanced version of the Kalphite Lair, players may fill a looting bag and their inventory with supplies and die within the lair, leaving a pile of supplies on the ground for 60 minutes which allows much longer trips.

tactics.heading: Suggested stats
tactics.text:
• 80+ Hitpoints (93+ if using anglerfish)
• 75+ Attack
• 75+ Strength
• 70+ Defence
• 75+ Ranged
• 70+ Prayer for Piety (74+ for Rigour)
• 86 Agility for the shortcut after the Elite Desert diary

tactics.heading: Transportation
tactics.text:
The Kalphite Queen is located at the end of the Kalphite Lair. It is highly advised to complete both the Elite Lumbridge & Draynor Diary and at minimum, the Hard Desert Diary. The former avoids the need to bring a dramen or lunar staff, as the lair is very close to the BIQ ring. The latter avoids the need to continually bring ropes (though two will be needed to set the ropes in place). While the Elite Desert Diary unlocks a shortcut that is usable at 86 Agility, one of the tasks needed requires the player to speak to a mounted head inside their player-owned house, which essentially locks the shortcut until the kq head is obtained. Once the Elite Desert Diary is completed however, the shortcut becomes usable with the appropriate Agility level, which is essentially required for long-term farming, especially for those seeking the Kalphite Princess.

From the surface area, players go west of the Shantay Pass until they find a bulging tunnel; this is where the first rope is needed for players. Once in the lair, players will go around a fairly large tunnel section with hostile soldiers, which can poison if they damage you. At the end is a chamber with two Kalphite guardians and another bulging tunnel; this is where the other rope is used. Like the soldiers, the guardians can poison, so being under the effects of an anti-poison potion is recommended so the player does not get hit with poison while fighting the Queen.

The Dorgesh-Kaan South Dungeon provides an alternative route to get to the Kalphite Lair. Players taking this route will require a light source, but will save on one rope and do not need a dramen staff if entering via the city. This can save one inventory spot for players getting their first kill for the hard desert diary, although this is generally not necessary as supplies are not the limiting factor for this.

After going down, there is another set of guardians. On the other side is the Queen; drink potions and put on protection prayers before charging in.

tactics.heading: The fight
tactics.text:
Tip: Unless wearing a serpentine helm for the duration of the fight, either sip an antidote++ before going to the lair to save an inventory slot, or bring the potion in with you during the fight.

The Kalphite Queen has 510 Hitpoints, split across two phases. Her Magic and Ranged attacks will always land as successful hits. While unlikely, it is possible for them to land but deal no damage. Her Ranged attack will drain 1 prayer point if it rolls more than 0 damage, even if the player prevents the damage with Protect from Missiles. Her Melee attack does not share the unique accuracy mechanic, and is treated as a standard attack meaning that standing next to her will decrease her DPS. Unlike the soldiers and guardians, this melee attack does not poison. When standing in melee range of the Kalphite Queen, she has a 1/2 chance of doing a melee attack, while her Magic and Ranged attacks each have a 1/4 chance of triggering.

There are two phases of the fight, similar to Vet'ion. While in her grounded form, the Kalphite Queen has Protect from Magic and Protect from Missiles active; however, they only add increased Defence to those styles rather than full immunity like the player versions of them.

When her first form falls at zero health, her chitin will crack open to reveal her second form, a wasp-like creature. This airborne form has Protect from Melee active; however, like the first form, this only provides increased Defence.

Note: Upon triggering the second form, there is a time limit of 20 minutes for defeating it. If not defeated within this time frame, the Kalphite Queen returns to the first form, though she carries the health she had left in her second form upon reverting back.

Her ranged attack will hit players close to the main target. To avoid this, players in a group can stand on opposite sides of her. This positioning (combined with Protect from Magic) will greatly reduce the amount of damage taken over the course of the fight.

Throughout the fight, if the Kalphite Queen is near any of the bulging cocoons, there is a 1/20 chance it will hatch an aggressive Kalphite Worker each time the Queen is hit. These only stay for a while before despawning. It is advised to get the Queen near them so the workers will spawn. This is because if there are plenty of workers around her, she will be unable to move at all while they are present, and allow the player to easily flinch her for longer trips. This is only viable with melee, since melee attacks land instantly, while Ranged or Magic projectiles do not land quickly enough to flinch the boss. An exception to this are salamanders, which work like a melee weapon and can deal magic damage.

Her attacks can be tick-eaten, however her ranged and magic attacks do have different projectile speeds and as such, it is advised to always make sure to heal up when below 31 Hitpoints to prevent the risk of dying. It is recommended to step under her during this to not take more damage.

tactics.heading: First phase
tactics.text: During both phases, it generally does not matter whether you pray Protect from Magic or Protect from Missiles, but Protect from Magic is still preferred in case another player crashes you as it can bounce between players. Also, Piety (or Mystic Vigour/Augury for magic) is strongly recommended to speed up kills. Immediately run under her again after killing off her first phase, heal up, and prepare for the second phase.

tactics.heading: Second phase
tactics.text:
Players should continue to pray Protect from Magic during phase 2. Players should walk under her as soon as this phase begins, otherwise she will get an extra attack on you first. Use a DPS calculator to determine how accurate her melee attacks during this phase will be; stand within melee range if more than 50% of her melee attacks will miss on average.

Flinching the Kalphite Queen is a slower method than conventional methods, however it requires much fewer resources per kill, allowing even low level players to do extended trips of 5 or more kills. This method is more easily employed by ironman players, as due to the Kalphite Queen's lair being instanced, they can leave and re-enter the instance to reset all the spawns, making it much quicker to set things up again.

Due to the slow nature of flinching, it is highly recommended to have a Kalphite Slayer task, as the Slayer helmet can give very large bonuses. Verac the Defiled's equipment can hit through the Queen's high defences on both phases incredibly well even without a slayer task. Otherwise, the Zombie axe or Keris partisan of breaching have the highest expected hits for both phases.

tactics.heading: Setting up
tactics.text:
Make sure you have around 70% run energy before you head into the lair. You'll need to do some running to attract the Kalphite Guardians and the Kalphite Queen, and running out of run energy can force you to tank more hits from the Queen herself. Since you probably don't have the elite Desert Diary done, you'll have to take the long way around - walking this part helps conserve run energy.

It is advisable to watch a video on the below method on setting up the Kalphite Queen, such as this one.

Turn on Protect from Melee as you go into the lair and attract the two Kalphite Guardians near the entrance. Run back to the entrance rope and stand two tiles to the south of it - this should cause the two Guardians to stand one behind the other in a line. With this done, turn on Protect from Missiles and find the Kalphite Queen to attract her attention (do not attack the Kalphite Queen if using a bone dagger as your special weapon), then run back to the entrance and stand two tiles west and one tile north of the entrance rope. If done correctly, the two Kalphite Guardians and the Kalphite Queen will be stood in a line facing you, with the Kalphite Queen out of attack range. If the Kalphite Queen gets stuck on the cocoon in the middle after attracting her attention, walk diagonally south-west 2 tiles and then back to release her.

With the Guardians and the queen in a line, turn on Protect from Missiles then run 3 tiles south of the Kalphite's Queen south-western tile, then immediately run under her. The Guardians should now position themselves to trap the queen against the cocoon in the middle, and she is unable to move to attack to you while stood under her.

tactics.heading: Flinching
tactics.text:
With the Kalphite Queen stuck, all you have to do is flinch the Kalphite Queen with your melee weapon until she is dead. It is highly recommended to summon thralls, as they will significantly increase kill speed, as they will be able to do damage while you are waiting for your next attack.

Due to the Kalphite Queen's attack speed, you can attack once every 10 ticks without her retaliating against you. If using thralls and/or poison, the usual method of waiting for the enemy's hitpoints bar to disappear will be inaccurate (it can still be used, but will take longer than necessary). In such a case, a good proxy for this is to attack again once your thrall stops attacking.

tactics.heading: After the kill
tactics.text:
After the kill, the flinching safespot will need to be set up again.

If playing as an ironman, simply leave the lair and re-enter, as this will reset the instance to a fresh state.

If playing on a standard account, the Kalphite workers which spawned during the fight will need to be defeated before trying to set up the flinching safespot again, or you may choose to hop worlds to look for a fresh lair.

gearNotes.heading: Equipment
gearNotes.text: Warning: Bear in mind that, since the Wilderness is used to reach the King Black Dragon Lair, only the player's three most valuable items (four with Protect Item activated, none if skulled) are kept on death if the player dies on their way to the King Black Dragon's lair. Therefore, it is recommended not to bring any items you're not willing to lose.

gearNotes.heading: Melee
gearNotes.text:
This gear minimises the risk associated with the short trip through the wilderness while optimising DPS. Proselyte can be used for less prayer potion usage and potentially longer trips. The dragon hunter lance scales well with gear upgrades, but the Osmumten's fang can perform better with less equipment strength bonus.

Notes
• Bring antidote++ and extended antifire potions for poison and dragonfire protection respectively.
• Extended super antifire potions can allow the use of Defenders but you will take more damage overall.
• Bring a right balance of super restore potions and food to sustain for one trip at the King Black Dragon.
• Bring a means of teleporting to the King Black Dragon Lair.
• Bring a teleport to house tablet to teleport out at the end of the trip.

gearNotes.heading: Equipment upgrades and downgrades
gearNotes.text:
This is the best-in-slot available equipment for meleeing the King Black Dragon. It is only worth the time if you plan on spending a lot of time at KBD at once.

Notes
• While transporting items to the King Black Dragon Lair via the gravestone method, make sure to bring enough food on these trips to be able to sustain for one hour at the King Black Dragon.
• Bring enough super restore potions to be able to sustain for one hour at the King Black Dragon.
• Both the 4-dose antidote++ and extended antifire potions give a total of 48 minutes of protection. Therefore take one sip of each potion at the bank right before starting the actual trip.
• Extended super antifire potions can allow the use of Defenders but you will take more damage overall.
• Bring enough super combat potions to last for one hour.
• Bring a means of teleporting to the King Black Dragon Lair.
• Bring a teleport to house tablet to teleport out at the end of the trip.

gearNotes.text:

Notes
• Bring antidote++ and extended super antifire (or extended antifire with an anti-dragon shield) potions for poison and dragonfire protection respectively.
• Pray magic instead of melee to reduce dragonfire damage considerably. Swap shield between attacks if using a bow of Faerdhinen while praying melee to reduce damage further, however this risks taking extreme damage if done incorrectly.
• Bring a right balance of super restore potions and food to sustain for one trip at the King Black Dragon.
• Bring a means of teleporting to the King Black Dragon Lair.
• Bring a teleport to house tablet to teleport out at the end of the trip.

Utilising a dragonfire ward or anti-dragon shield reduces the amount of damage taken overall when praying protect from melee.

• Bring a right balance of super restore potions and food to sustain for one trip at the King Black Dragon.

gearNotes.heading: Equipment upgrades and downgrades
gearNotes.text:
This is the best-in-slot available equipment for ranging the King Black Dragon. This method takes considerable setup, so only plan on bringing this gear if you intend to stay at KBD for an extended period of time.

Notes
• If killing the King Black Dragon in a small team or with alt accounts, using the Twisted bow may result in lower kills per hour than a high-end shield setup due to increased occurrence of the Icy Breath attack's freeze effect when not equipped with a form of anti-dragon shield.
• While transporting items to the King Black Dragon Lair via the gravestone method, make sure to bring enough food on these trips to be able to sustain for one hour at the King Black Dragon.
• Bring enough super restore potions to be able to sustain for one hour at the King Black Dragon.
• Both the 4-dose antidote++ and extended antifire potions give a total of 48 minutes of protection. Therefore take one sip of each potion at the bank right before starting the actual trip.
• Bring enough ranging potions to last for one hour.
• Bring a means of teleporting to the King Black Dragon Lair.
• Bring a teleport to house tablet to teleport out at the end of the trip.

gearNotes.heading: AFK Magic
gearNotes.text:
Using the passive damage bonus from the dragon hunter wand, it is possible to outheal the chip damage dealt by the boss and thus the only interaction needed is drinking potions every 5 minutes or so to maintain antifire protection and prayer. This is a very effective method for pet hunting due to the extremely long trip lengths and low interaction requirements, however can be costly due to the high cost of blood barrage. Due to the high cost of items used, it is strongly recommended to use the following method to move gear inside the KBD lair without risking being killed in the Wilderness:

• Enter KBD's lair with no armour equipped, and 4 low value items in inventory. Die to KBD to spawn a gravestone inside the lair.
• Withdraw all gear and potions required, and die a PvM death (e.g. to the Guard (Prifddinas) outside of the Prifddinas house portal with assistance from a locator orb). These items will be added to the gravestone within KBD's lair.
• Return to KBD's lair and withdraw all items from the gravestone.

Pray Protect from Melee and Mystic Might/Mystic Vigour, stay in melee range of the boss and enable auto retaliate, with Blood Barrage autocasting.

Notes
• It is not recommended to bank most loot from the boss using this method, as this will significantly reduce kills per hour.
• The best method to resupply is to die to the boss, and return to KBD's lair with only potions.
• The dragon hunter wand is required for this method. No other items are required (in particular, the ancient wyvern shield can be replaced with an anti-dragon shield), however if too many downgrades are made then it may not be possible to consistently outheal the boss.

tactics.heading: Overview
tactics.text:
Warning: While the King Black Dragon's lair is not considered to be a part of the Wilderness, you will need to cross a short distance in deep level 42-Wilderness that is commonly patrolled by Player killers. Do not bring any items into the Wilderness you are not willing to lose.

The King Black Dragon, commonly referred to as KBD, is a three-headed dragon located in his lair deep in the Wilderness. The King Black Dragon has a combat level of 276, which makes him one of the strongest dragons in Old School RuneScape. Players should always take an anti-dragon shield as his dragonfire breath is very deadly without protection. The King Black Dragon can also be killed as an alternative for a black dragon Slayer task, except those given by Krystilia.

tactics.heading: Requirements
tactics.text: There are no strict requirements to killing the King Black Dragon.

tactics.heading: Recommendations
tactics.text:
• High combat stats. Although not required, the skill levels below are advised:
  • If using Melee:
    • Level 80 Attack or higher
    • Level 80 Strength or higher
    • Level 70 Hitpoints or higher
    • Level 70 Prayer or higher for the Piety prayer
  • If using Ranged:
    • Level 80 Ranged or higher
    • Level 70 Hitpoints or higher
    • Level 74 Prayer or higher for the Rigour prayer
• Partial completion of Quest Dragon Slayer I for access to anti-dragon shields.
• Completion of Quest Slug Menace for access to proselyte armour.

tactics.heading: Transportation
tactics.text:
The King Black Dragon resides in the King Black Dragon Lair, which is not in the Wilderness, so teleports can be used inside if needed. However, its lair can only be accessed by travelling through the Wilderness, so take precautions and don't bring any items you're not willing to lose. In the event that you are teleblocked, you cannot use the lever to escape.

Using any of the following methods, ordered from quickest to slowest, will lead players to the King Black Dragon Lair:
• Burning amulet
  • Use a burning amulet to teleport to the Lava Maze.
  • Run west and then north along the fence.
  • Go through the gate and climb down the ladder.
• Player-owned house obelisk - Requires completion of the Diary hard Wilderness Diary or better for effective use
  • Select level 44 as the teleport destination of the obelisk in the superior garden.
  • Right-click the Wilderness Obelisk and select teleport to destination.
  • Run south-east, go through the gate and climb down the ladder.
• Ghorrock Teleport (tablet) (portal) - Requires completion of the Quest Desert Treasure I quest.
  • Use the Ghorrock Teleport (or tablet or portal) to teleport to the Frozen Waste Plateau, near the (level 44) Wilderness Obelisk west of the KBD lair.
  • Run south-east, go through the gate and climb down the ladder.
• Games necklace and Wilderness Obelisk - Requires completion of the Diary hard Wilderness Diary or better for effective use
  • Use a games necklace to teleport to the Corporeal Beast's lair.
  • Leave the cave and run south-east to the Wilderness Obelisk.
  • Select level 44 as the teleport destination of the Wilderness Obelisk.
  • Right-click the Wilderness Obelisk and select teleport to destination.
  • Run south-east, go through the gate and climb down the ladder.
• Waka canoe - This requires a woodcutting axe as well as level 57 Woodcutting or better.
  • Use the canoe station in Edgeville to travel to the Wilderness pond in level 35 Wilderness.
  • Run west-north-west to and then north along the fence.
  • Go through the gate and climb down the ladder.

Down the stairs, there is a lever players can pull to enter the King Black Dragon Lair.

tactics.heading: Attack styles
tactics.text:
The King Black Dragon attacks with Melee and dragonfire attacks. King Black Dragon will use a melee attack 1/3 of the time provided the target is in melee range. Otherwise, a dragonfire attack is used with a 50% chance of a special dragonfire attack. All three special dragonfires (Toxic, Shocking, and Icy breath) are equally common, each with a 1/9 incidence in melee range or a 1/6 incidence outside of melee range.
• The Melee attack is only used when the player is standing in Melee distance and can hit up to 25.
  • The Protect from Melee prayer will negate all damage from this attack.
• The fiery breath attack can deal up to 65 damage. Antifire shields, antifire potions, and Protect from Magic, or a combination of these, will partially negate the damage from this attack.
• There are three different special dragonfire attacks. Each of these attacks can deal up to 50 damage and have a 50% chance upon a successful hit to inflict a unique effect. Antifire shields and Protect from Magic, or a combination of these, will partly negate the damage from this attack and reduce the effect chance to 1 in 8.
  • Toxic breath inflicts poison to the player, starting at 8 damage.
  • Shocking breath drains two levels off of all the player's stats.
  • Icy breath freezes the player for 10 ticks (6 seconds).

tactics.heading: Dragonfire
tactics.text:
The King Black Dragon uses several kinds of dragonfire attacks. Dragonfire is a fiery breath attack that can deal considerable damage to players. However, there are a few precautions players can take to negate most of this damage, being:
• Antifire potions: (extended) antifire potion and (extended) super antifire potion
• Anti-dragon shields: anti-dragon shield, dragonfire shield, dragonfire ward, and ancient wyvern shield
• Protection prayers: Protect from Magic

See the table below for an overview of the maximum damage with (combinations of) the above-mentioned precautions.

tactics.heading: Protection prayers
tactics.text:
It is recommended to fight the King Black Dragon in Melee distance with the Protect from Melee prayer activated. This lowers the chance of the King Black Dragon using its unblockable special dragonfire attacks, while being able to negate all damage from its Melee attacks.

However, when a player is using a two-handed weapon, such as the twisted bow, the Protect from Magic prayer is necessary to partly negate the damage of the dragonfire attacks.

tactics.heading: Draconic
tactics.text: The King Black Dragon is considered to be a draconic creature, which means that it is weak against dragonbane weapons.

tactics.heading: Instance
tactics.text:
The King Black Dragon is a popular boss, therefore it may be hard to find an empty world. To combat this, players can create an instance for . This money does not have to be in your inventory and will automatically be taken out of the player's bank.

Note that the instance will collapse if the player dies. This means that all unprotected items will be added to a gravestone outside the lever on death. Therefore an emergency teleport is highly recommended.

tactics.heading: Gravestone method
tactics.text:
Important: There is currently a bug that a player-killer can exploit to get the items in your gravestone if you are killed.

Since the Wilderness is used to reach the King Black Dragon Lair, only the player's three most valuable items (four with Protect Item activated, none if skulled) are kept on death if the player dies on their way to the King Black Dragon's lair. Therefore, it is recommended to only bring items you are willing to lose. However, it is possible to 'smuggle' more than four valuable items into the public instance utilising gravestone mechanics, and additional supplies if a looting bag is brought too.

• (Optionally) fill a looting bag with potions and food.
• Fill the inventory with the looting bag, a burning amulet, desired supplies and the four valuable items you are 'smuggling' into the King Black Dragon Lair.
• Activate the Protect Item prayer and head to King Black Dragon's lair.
• Die to the King Black Dragon, so that all items in the inventory and looting bag drop onto the ground. These items will stay in your gravestone for exactly 15 minutes. If not retrieved in 15 minutes they will be transported to Death's office.
• Die again to send additional items to your gravestone. This does not have to be a death to the King Black Dragon, so it may be easier to die to the Corporeal Beast, or any other high hitting and easy to reach monster.
• Collect items from the gravestone within the public instance of the lair.

Warning: This method is not risk free, as there still is a chance of encountering player-killers before reaching the lair. It is strongly recommended to carry a means to restore prayer to keep Protect Item up continuously if carrying four items.

tactics.heading: Smuggle method
tactics.text: An alternative method of bringing many powerful but valuable items into the KBD lair is to use other players or alt accounts to trade with the main account once inside. This eliminates the gravestone reclamation fee but requires much more coordination. Due to the time and difficulty of this method, it is generally only done by pet hunters.

tactics.heading: Walk-under method
tactics.text:
If using a twisted bow, dragon hunter crossbow, or Osmumten's fang, the player's attack speed is slower than that of the King Black Dragon: the fang and bows (on rapid) attack every 5 ticks, whereas the dragon attacks every 4 ticks. When walking under the King Black Dragon immediately after performing an attack, the player is able to hide from the King Black Dragon's attacks until they step out to perform another attack, thus effectively slowing down its attack speed. When utilising this method correctly, the King Black Dragon will only perform 1 attack for every attack the player performs, reducing the damage taken by 20%. Players need not walk under the KBD after each attack; they can keep the 1:1 ratio even when walking under after every second or third attack, so long as they wait 5 ticks after they walk under.

If using a twisted bow with this method, players could also choose to stand in Melee distance and pray Protect from Melee, and bring an anti-dragon shield to equip when the King Black Dragon attacks. This requires great focus and timing, as missing even once can allow the King Black Dragon to deal up to 50 damage with its fire breath.

tactics.heading: Bonecrusher necklace
tactics.text:
To save on super restore potions, players could consider bringing a bonecrusher necklace. With this necklace equipped, players can bury the dragon bones to restore 4 prayer points.

In order to benefit from both an offensive necklace as well as the bonecrusher necklace's effect, players could wear their offensive necklace during the kill and then swap to the bonecrusher necklace once the final damage is dealt. Then re-equip the offensive necklace.

One thing to consider is that this method requires taking an additional valuable item () through the Wilderness.

gearNotes.heading: Equipment
gearNotes.text: Magic equipment, while providing less defence against the Kraken's attacks, is offset by the damage bonus provided from higher tier sets. It is only recommended to bring magic armour if it is Virtus or ancestral; otherwise, use the best ranged armour instead, as the damage bonus provided by other robes is not worth the tradeoff.

gearNotes.heading: Inventory
gearNotes.text:
• Fishing explosive to quickly start the fight
• Teleport out, such as Teleport to house (tablet), Explorer's ring 4, construction cape, or max cape
• Teleport to Kraken Cove, such as a Piscatoris teleport, or Teleport to house (tablet) with a fairy ring in your house for fairy ring akq (and Dramen staff without completion of the elite Lumbridge & Draynor Diary)
• Special attack weapon (optional)
• Rune pouch and either:
  • Book of the Dead and runes to use Thralls and/or Death charge
  • Autocast weapon such as an Ancient sceptre with runes for Blood barrage
  • Runes for earth spells and high alchemy
• Bracelet of slaughter (optional)
• Magic boost, such as Saturated heart, Ancient brews, or magic potions for higher defence and slightly increased accuracy (optional)
• 8-10 Prayer potions for use of offensive prayers and Preserve (optional)
• The rest Cooked karambwan or better
The Rondache reduces the chip damage received by the tentacles to 0. The remaining damage Source is the Kraken itself, which in max mage defence gear barely hits. The following Equipment allows for maximum sustaining. The Rondache is mandatory.

gearNotes.heading: Inventory
gearNotes.text:
• Fishing explosive to quickly start the fight
• Sanguinesti Staff for healing
• Teleport out, such as Teleport to house (tablet), Explorer's ring 4, construction cape, or max cape
• Teleport to Kraken Cove, such as a Piscatoris teleport, or Teleport to house (tablet) with a fairy ring in your house for fairy ring akq (and Dramen staff without completion of the elite Lumbridge & Draynor Diary)
• Special attack weapon (optional)
• Rune pouch and either:
  • Book of the Dead and runes to use Thralls and/or Death charge
  • Autocast weapon such as an Ancient sceptre with runes for Blood barrage
  • Runes for earth spells and high alchemy
• Bracelet of slaughter (optional)
• Magic boost, such as Saturated heart, Ancient brews, or magic potions for higher defence and slightly increased accuracy (optional)

gearNotes.heading: Notes
gearNotes.text: With Max gear, dropped sharks should be enough to sustain any damage taken by the Kraken. IF sustainability needs to be ensured, it is recommended to bring a Sanguinesti staff and use it whenever health drops below 50. Blood barrage or blood blitz can also be used to make food optional, however it is expensive. Health can still be restored even when casting on the Kraken while it is submerged, if needed.

tactics.heading: Overview
tactics.text:
The Kraken is a Slayer boss and can therefore only be killed while on a Slayer task to kill it, or (cave) kraken. The Kraken is located in the Kraken Cove.

It is recommended to use the Magic attack style to fight the Kraken, as Ranged deals 1/7th of its normal damage and it is immune to Melee, due to the fact that it cannot be reached by Melee attacks. As there are no complex mechanics, the Kraken is a popular boss (therefore it may be hard to find an empty world). Players can alternatively create an instance for 25,000 coins coins, which lasts until the player leaves or logs out.

tactics.heading: Requirements
tactics.text: • Level 87 Slayer and a Cave kraken task (requiring 50 Magic)

tactics.heading: Suggested skills
tactics.text:
• 75+ Magic
• 70+ Defence
• 75+ Hitpoints

tactics.heading: Transportation
tactics.text:
The Kraken is located in a separated section of the Kraken Cove. The quickest way to get to this dungeon is via fairy rings:
• Use the code AKQ, then run west to the dungeon entrance.

Run west after entering the Kraken cove to find the entrance to the Kraken's lair.

tactics.heading: Releasing the Kraken
tactics.text:
To disturb the Kraken and start the fight, a fishing explosive should be used on the large whirlpool, which will cause the Kraken and all four tentacles to emerge and attack at once. A fishing explosive only costs 60 coins and can be easily bought from any slayer master. Without this, the player must first disturb the smaller whirlpools, which will each spawn an Enormous Tentacle. The tentacles can be killed, but this is ill-advised as they have high hitpoints and are unaffected by slayer task bonuses. Once all four small whirlpools are disturbed, the player can then disturb the larger whirlpool, which will cause the Kraken to emerge and attack; disturbing the larger whirlpool without disturbing all four smaller ones will not produce a response. A ranged weapon with a range of 7 or more tiles is needed to reach the back two whirlpools from the bridge without having to move.

During the fight, it is best to focus on the Kraken and tank the hits from the smaller tentacles. The Kraken is very unlikely to kill the player unless they are extremely unlucky, as its attack has such poor accuracy despite having a high max hit, even in magic robes. It is still best to stay above 45 hitpoints to avoid the risk of getting killed.

tactics.heading: Attack styles
tactics.text:
During the fight, the player will be attacked by four Enormous Tentacles and by the Kraken itself:
• The Kraken and the tentacles only attack with a typeless magical ranged attack:
  • 'Typeless' means that protection prayers will not have any effect.
  • 'Magical ranged' means that the attack accuracy is decided by the ranged attack bonuses of the Kraken and the magic defence bonuses of the player.
  • The max hit of this attack is 28 from Kraken, and 2 from each tentacle. Unlike most monsters, damage will be inflicted before the projectile reaches the player, rather than on impact.
  • The attacks have an attack speed of 4 (i.e. every 2.4 seconds). Kraken's attacks are fairly inaccurate, but the tentacles are relatively accurate.

tactics.heading: Tips
tactics.text:
The Kraken is a popular boss, therefore it may be hard to find an empty world. To combat this, players can create a private instance for 25,000 coins coins.

An advantage of a private instance is that dropped items stay on the ground for a longer period of time. Normally, items disappear after two minutes upon being dropped and other players can see it after one minute. However, this is not an issue if instancing, as dropped items disappear in 3 hours within the Kraken Cove instance. As the Kraken regularly drops a generous amount of food in the form of 5 edible seaweed or 5 sharks, the instance makes it a lot easier on the player to juggle these food sources before they disappear.

Players attempting long trips or the Kraken's stamina-based Combat Achievements (e.g. One Hundred Tentacles) may benefit from using the Sanguinesti staff or blood barrage, as their passive healing greatly reduces the dependency for food drops.

It is highly recommended to turn Auto Retaliate off when fighting the Kraken, as the tentacles continue to attack the player after it has been killed. With Auto Retaliate off, after a fishing explosive is used, the player will automatically attack the Kraken when vulnerable.

When exiting the instance, either by leaving, dying, or logging out, all items on the ground will be permanently lost. If a player dies, all items carried will be moved to a gravestone outside the instance.

gearNotes.heading: Equipment
gearNotes.text: Tumeken's shadow is currently the only weapon capable of killing Kree'arra directly that is competitive with black chinchompas. Note that it is dramatically more effective than any other magic weapon in this encounter, dealing roughly three times as much damage as the next strongest option. As such, no other magic weapons are recommended for killing Kree'arra directly.

gearNotes.heading: Inventory
gearNotes.text:
• Eldritch Nightmare staff to autocast Ancient Magicks or something else such as a Kodai wand or Blood ancient sceptre
  • The eldritch Nightmare staff not only autocasts Ancient Magicks, but also has a special attack that restores Prayer which can be used on the melee or ranged minion
• Elidinis' ward (f) to pair with the Ancient Magick switch
• Ecumenical key to get into the room
• 3-5 Saradomin brews
• 5-7 super restores
• High-healing food such as anglerfish or manta rays
• Any crossbow with a mith grapple to get to the lair, if not already using a crossbow
• One-click teleport
• Rune pouch with necessary runes to cast Blood Barrage to heal off the minions and ice spells to freeze Flight Kilisa.
• Imbued heart or its saturated version to boost Magic level.
• Any necessary god items and/or secondary bolt if using any (optional)
• Trollheim Teleport

By using chinchompas, one can kill Kree'arra quickly even if they are soloing, though it is also expensive.
To use this method, stand in the south-western corner of the room and wait for both Kree'arra and Flight Kilisa, the melee bodyguard, to close in on you.
When both are in position, start throwing chinchompas at Flight Kilisa; the chinchompas will almost always hit her due to her lower Defence, and the AoE damage will hit Kree'arra.

gearNotes.text:
