• Bow of Faerdhinen to hit Kree'arra when he and Flight Kilisa are not stacked, which happens at spawn and if Flight Kilisa dies before Kree'arra
• Blood ancient sceptre or something else to autocast blood spells such as a Kodai wand or ancient staff
  • The eldritch Nightmare staff not only autocasts Ancient Magicks, but also has a special attack that restores Prayer which can be used on the melee or ranged minion
• Ecumenical key to get into the room
• 2+ bastion potions or ranging potions
• 6-10 Saradomin brews depending on your combats and if you are using Blood Barrage
• 11+ super restores
• Bones to peaches tab for extra healing
• Any crossbow with a mith grapple to get to the lair, if not already using a crossbow
• One-click teleport
• Rune pouch with necessary runes to cast Blood Barrage to heal off the minions
• Any necessary god items and/or secondary bolt if using any (optional)
• Trollheim Teleport

gearNotes.heading: Inventory
gearNotes.text:
• Mith grapple
• One-click teleport (such as ectophial or teleport tabs)
• Any necessary god items
• 12-16 Saradomin brews
• 6-8 super restores
• 2-3 ranging potions
• Ecumenical key (optional)
• Trollheim Teleport

The Twisted Bow and Bow of Faerdhinen are both viable methods for killing Kree'arra. While weaker than Black Chinchompas, they're much cheaper to use and less click intensive.
Twisted Bow is stronger than the Bow of Faerdhinen if the player has Masori armour (f) and Dragon arrows—if missing two of those three items, the Bow of Faerdhinen with Crystal armour is stronger.
Players should stand under Kree'arra after each hit to minimise the amount of attacks Kree'arra can use against the player, especially if using a Twisted Bow as its attack speed is slower than Bow of Faerdhinen

gearNotes.heading: Inventory
gearNotes.text:
• Toxic blowpipe for killing the minions and specs
• Blood ancient sceptre or something else to autocast blood spells such as a Kodai wand or ancient staff
  • The eldritch Nightmare staff not only autocasts Ancient Magicks, but also has a special attack that restores Prayer which can be used on the melee or ranged minion
• Ecumenical key to get into the room
• 2+ bastion potions
• 6-10 Saradomin brews depending on your combats and if you are using Blood Barrage
• 8-10 super restores
• Bones to peaches tab for extra healing
• Any crossbow with a mith grapple to get to the lair. The grapple can be held within Dizana's quiver if owned.
• Rune pouch with necessary runes to cast Blood Barrage to heal off the minions
• Any necessary god items
• 2 Trollheim Teleports - Revert one after teleporting Trollheim to get a house teleport back.
• Bracelet of slaughter to extend slayer tasks if applicable

Even though Kree'arra has extremely high melee defences, the special attack of the soulflame horn can be used to make the player's next melee hit always land. Since the horn's special attack only works if another player is near the user, it is mandatory to kill Kree'arra in a small team with this method, with duos and trios working the best. Additionally, the player must be using a halberd since Kree'arra is airborne; the noxious halberd is the only viable halberd for this method.
All players should stand under Kree'arra after every attack, and use the soulflame horn's special attack while under him. While it is possible for a team to use only one soulflame horn and simply trade the horn between players after killing the minions, it is recommended for all players to have a soulflame horn in the event the player currently using the horn uses all of their special attacks (and thus guaranteed hits for the party) before Kree'arra is dead.
Despite melee armour giving high ranged defence bonuses, it is still recommended to pray Protect from Missiles to avoid potentially getting comboed by Kree'arra. Switch to Protect from Magic after Kree'arra dies to kill the magic minion.

gearNotes.heading: Inventory
gearNotes.text:
• Soulflame horn
• Lightbearer to switch to after a kill if using another ring (e.g. ultor ring)
• Rune pouch with necessary runes to cast Blood Barrage and Ice Barrage if using Ancient Magicks, or Death Charge if using the Arceuus spellbook
  • While water runes for Ice Barrage are optional, it allows players to avoid damage from the melee minion by freezing them on top of the ranged minion
• Magic gear switch and a weapon that can autocast Ancient Magicks (e.g. blood ancient sceptre, kodai wand)
• Ecumenical key to get into the room
• 2+ super combat potions or divine super combat potions
• High-healing food such as manta rays or tuna potatoes
• 8 super restores
• Bones to peaches tab for extra healing
• Any crossbow with a mith grapple to get to the lair.
• Any necessary god items
• Ghommal's hilt or Trollheim Teleport

tactics.heading: Overview
tactics.text:
This is a guide to defeating Kree'arra, the Armadyl-aligned general in the God Wars Dungeon.

As Kree'arra is airborne, regular melee attacks will not work; instead, Ranged or Magic must be used to fight him. Halberds and salamanders are the only melee options, but due to Kree'arra's extremely high melee defence, this is not generally recommended unless using the soulflame horn in small teams.

Kree'arra and his minions count toward aviansie Slayer tasks; Slayer helm (i) and black mask (i) both give the 15% accuracy and damage boost to those on task.

tactics.heading: Quest requirements
tactics.text:
• Death Plateau and Troll Stronghold to the point where you defeat Dad.
• Alternatively, Ghommal's hilt can be used to teleport to Trollheim without requiring either quest

tactics.heading: Other requirements
tactics.text:
• 40 Armadyl Kill count in the godwars dungeon (lower with varying tiers of Combat Achievements) or an Ecumenical key
• A crossbow of any type
• Mithril grapple.

tactics.heading: Suggested skills
tactics.text:
• 85+ Combat (Required, 100+ Recommended)
• 70+ Ranged (80+ Recommended)
• 70+ Defence (80+ Recommended)
• 92+ Magic (Blood Barrage)
• 70+ Hitpoints (80+ Recommended)
• 44+ Prayer (Eagle Eye)

tactics.heading: General Strategy
tactics.text:
When starting a trip at Kree'arra, many players prefer using an ecumenical key to skip kill count, as Armadylean kill count is very slow and requires the use of prayer. Kree'arra is also commonly killed on a Slayer task of Aviansie, so skipping kill count is even more desirable in this case as the player will progress their slayer task if they kill Aviansie for kill count, reducing the overall number of Kree'arra that can be killed on-task.

Kree'arra, unlike the other generals, utilises all three forms of combat. By default, he attacks with ranged and magic. The ranged attack consists of grey dust tornadoes, while the magic attack is a blue dust tornado. Kree'arra's magic attack is classified as ranged magic, meaning that its accuracy rolls against the player's ranged defence bonuses, rather than magic. The ranged attack can deal up to 69 damage, while his magic attack deals up to 21. Both of these attacks hit all players in the room, and can knock the player back a tile unless they are standing in the corners of the chamber. It is important to keep Protect from Missiles on at all times while Kree'arra is alive, or players will likely meet a swift death.

Should Kree'arra not be targeted, he will go up to his target and swipe his talons at them, dealing up to 26 damage.

Kree'arra has three bodyguards; Flight Kilisa, Wingman Skree and Flockleader Geerin, who use melee, magic and ranged respectively, capable of dealing up to 15, 16 and 25 damage respectively. Only Kilisa will be a threat, as Skree is generally inaccurate and the player is protected from Geerin's attacks.

When killed, Kree'arra and his bodyguards will drop bones, which can be converted into peaches with bones to peaches tablets. Peaches heal for 8 health, so the player can heal for 32 health after each encounter with Kree'arra and his bodyguards. The bodyguards occasionally drop two manta rays or three mushroom potatoes, which heal for 44 and 60 health respectively. These should be juggled if inventory is full.

Regardless of the method used, it is recommended to bring a staff that can autocast ancient spells to heal larger amounts after Kree'arra dies, conserving food for later kills.

tactics.heading: Tumeken's Shadow
tactics.text:
Tumeken's shadow, with its passive effect enhancing powerful magic gear, is the strongest weapon for conventional methods of killing Kree'arra, and it is far cheaper and more efficient than throwing chinchompas. Additionally, the combination of Blood barrage to heal off the bodyguards and the special attack of an Eldritch Nightmare staff, especially with the reduced cooldown granted by the Lightbearer, can allow players to remain in Kree'arra's lair indefinitely, limited only by runes and weapon charges.

However, it should be noted that this strategy requires near-max magic gear. Downgrades will significantly impact kill times and trip length, due to the multiplying effect Tumeken's shadow has on the magic stat bonuses of other pieces of equipment.

As ancestral armour has less defence bonuses than conventional ranged options, players will take more damage from Kree'arra's magic attacks and Kilisa. It is recommended to freeze Kilisa whenever possible and go under Kree'arra after every attack made, as he attacks on a 3 tick cycle compared to the staff's 5 tick cycle.

tactics.heading: Chinchompas
tactics.text:
Because of Kree'arra's exceptionally high defensive stats, one of the most effective ways to kill him is by dealing indirect damage using red or black chinchompas. Hitting Kree'arra directly is significantly harder compared to the other generals with most weapons. Chinchompas roll accuracy based on the player's current target; if the hit is successful, then all other monsters in range will generally take damage regardless of their Defence level and bonuses. This method is primarily preferred for players without access to strong weapons such as a Bow of Faerdhinen.

To utilise the chinchompa method, the player must have both targets near or directly on each other. Monsters with a size of 2x2 tiles or larger have their hitboxes placed on the south-western most tile, which is also where any items dropped upon their death will appear.

Kree'arra must be targeted off-tick (when the player is not attacking) or he will attempt to use Melee. To achieve this, simply left-click Kree'arra after throwing a chinchompa at Flight Kilisa while using the Medium Fuse attack style, then left-click Kilisa again just before your next attack. This cycle will ensure you take no melee damage from Kree'arra.

When an untouched room is entered, Kree'arra and his minions will be wandering around. Players should move to the south-western corner of the chamber to line up both Kree'arra and Kilisa. The player throws the chinchompas at Kilisa, allowing the chinchompas to damage Kree'arra in the process. Kilisa will clearly die before Kree'arra does at the start of the encounter, so switch to your crossbow or bow to kill Kree'arra while waiting for Kilisa to respawn, if she does so. On rapid, a crossbow will fire at a rate of 5 ticks (3.0 seconds), a twisted bow 5 ticks (3.0 seconds) and a bow of Faerdhinen 4 ticks (2.4 seconds), so walk under Kree'arra after every attack to reduce the frequency of his own attacks.

When the room is cleared and Kree'arra respawns, when he attempts to melee the player, his hitboxes will also collide with Geerin, allowing chinchompas to be used on both of them for equal effect. The primary advantage of two chinchompa targets allows players to maintain more consistent damage, although there are also a few disadvantages in doing so; if the player's reflexes are too slow, Kree'arra will move out of the chinchompa's AoE, forcing the player to fully lure Kree'arra onto Kilisa and reducing the overall amount of health healed if Geerin does not respawn before Kree'arra dies.

When Kree'arra dies, switch to your toxic blowpipe and kill off Skree. Kilisa and Geerin can be stacked for Blood Barrage, unless Kilisa is dead or on low health, in which the player should use Blood Blitz on Geerin instead. Geerin and Skree will generally attack on different ticks (as Skree spawns all the way to the east, out of visible range when standing on the western edge), allowing their attacks to be flicked. It is also possible to flick all three bodyguards' attacks if they attack on different ticks, which saves even more food.

tactics.heading: Team
tactics.text: In team encounters, all players will take damage from Kree'arra's attacks, so there is no designated tank. Due to the extra players, chinchompas are unnecessary and players should bring their best ranged weapon.

gearNotes.heading: Common setups
gearNotes.text:
Kurask are weakest to stab, although slash is still better with the leaf-bladed battleaxe due to it having a much higher max hit.

Praying Protect from Melee will negate all damage from kurask. If players have Bigger and Badder unlocked, king kurask may spawn during kurask tasks, but have no additional mechanics.

Kurask possess a very low magic level whilst having no magic defence bonuses, this allows for Magic Dart to be used to high effect. Equipment should be prioritised for magic damage bonus and prayer.

tactics.heading: Overview
tactics.text:
Kurask can be assigned as a Slayer task by various medium and high levelled Slayer masters upon reaching 70 Slayer and 65 combat level.

Kurask are found in the Fremennik Slayer Dungeon, the Iorwerth Dungeon after completing Song of the Elves, and in the Kurask Lair on Laguna Aurorae with 58 Sailing. In the Fremennik Slayer Dungeon, there is also a separate task-only area. There are two 3D models for kurask, normal and big, but this is merely a cosmetic difference as there is no difference in stats.

Kurask attack with somewhat inaccurate crush attacks that can hit up to 11. Protect from Melee will negate all their damage. For players with at least 75 Defence, there is a viable strategy to not pray against them, and instead collect their bones and occasionally cast Bones to Peaches (unlocked from the Mage Training Arena) to restore health at a significantly lower cost at the expense of moderately more attention required.

The king kurask is the superior version of the kurask unlocked with Bigger and badder. It has no special mechanics, but is significantly more accurate and has a max hit of 33. If players are using the Bones to Peaches strategy, it is advised to turn on Protect from Melee and bring at least one prayer potion in case the superior spawns.

They are weakest to stab, ranged, and magic attacks, but similarly to turoth, kurask have the leafy attribute, meaning they can only be damaged with leaf-bladed weapons (the leaf-bladed sword, battleaxe, and spear), broad-tipped ammunition (broad bolts and arrows), or the spell Magic Dart. All other weapons, spells, and other sources of damage, including cannons and thralls, will not deal any damage. However, the special attacks of the Saradomin godsword, ancient godsword, and toxic blowpipe will heal the player as if the attack performed its rolled damage. The set effect of Guthan's equipment will not activate. The Burning Claws special attack will not deal damage but it does apply burn.

Kurask can be a profitable task, as they frequently drop weapons and armour suitable for High Level Alchemy, as well as the requisite nature runes. Players should bring a herb sack as kurask always drop three herbs when they roll the herb drop table. They also drop seeds, worthwhile quantities of coins, and valuable noted stacks of white berries, big bones, coconuts, and papaya fruit. Kurask in the Iowerth Dungeon additionally drop crystal shards.

gearNotes.heading: Equipment
gearNotes.text:
Lava dragons attack with both Melee and dragonfire, so as long as you maintain distance, you'll be safe from their attacks. As you'll be safespotting, your biggest threat is player killers. You want to keep risk to a minimum at all times!

The accursed sceptre is the most effective magic weapon to use against lava dragons. Due to the fact that Lava dragons are very weak to Magic, it's also most effective weapon outclassing ranged alternatives. However, the revenant ether adds a considerable amount of risk, making the player a somewhat lucrative target to player killers. This is somewhat mitigated by the fact that only gear with Magic damage bonuses matter for maximizing DPS (Occult necklace, Imbued god cape, etc.) and the rest can simply be tank gear or Prayer bonus equipment. In addition, the high magic bonus from this equipment enables players to escape from PKers more easily by using Entangle or Ice Barrage.

A strong alternative is the Eye of Ayak, providing similar dps while avoiding the risk revenant ether.
Note: Only bring items that you are comfortable with losing. Ensure PK skull prevention is turned on in the settings as added security. It is recommended that the player only brings three items of high value, to ensure they are protected. Four can be brought if using Protect item with blighted super restore, though as the isle is multi-combat, you may be easily Smited for the fourth item. While bloodbark is recommended, it does have a relatively high cost so keep this in mind and check items lost on death before entering the Wilderness.

gearNotes.heading: Additional gear
gearNotes.text:
In their inventory, the player may choose to bring the following to use when attacked by other players:

• Black d'hide body
• Black d'hide chaps
• Dinh's bulwark

----

gearNotes.heading: Notes
gearNotes.text:
The webweaver bow is most effective ranged weapon to use against lava dragons although it is not as accurate as Magic. However, the revenant ether adds a considerable amount of risk, making the player a somewhat lucrative target to player killers.

----

gearNotes.heading: Notes
gearNotes.text:
The Ursine chainmace offers high accuracy against lava dragons when set to the stab attack style. While the lava dragons cannot be safespotted using melee, praying protect from melee and using a super antifire potion offers complete protection from damage, and the chainmace offers better DPS than comparable Webweaver bow setups. The DPS of the chainmace is still inferior to magic setups using the Accursed sceptre, however.

----

gearNotes.heading: Inventory
gearNotes.text:
For the inventory, you want to bring some food, runes if not using a powered staff or Ranged, a looting bag, pestle and mortar (to grind up scales, but optional), and a games necklace if teleporting to the Corporeal Beast cave. A stamina potion could help for running, but if taking potions, it's recommended to take a stamina, saradomin brew, super restore, and a ranging potion if ranging with the latter omitted if maging instead.
As for food, it is recommended to take four to six lobsters or better.

tactics.heading: Overview
tactics.text: Lava dragons reside on Lava Dragon Isle in the Wilderness (between level 36 and 42 Wilderness) and have low Magic resistance, making spells as low as Water Bolt sufficient enough to kill them due to their Elemental weakness to Water. Despite the dangers involved, willing players can travel there and safespot them in hopes of the highly elusive draconic visage.

tactics.heading: Transportation
tactics.text:
There are two entrances to Lava Dragon Isle: The main gate on the north side and an Agility shortcut, a stepping stone, on the southern side requiring 74 Agility to use.

• The fastest teleport is a revenant cave teleport and then go north-east to the main entrance.
• Minigame Teleport to Last Man Standing (Ferox Enclave) and then go north to agility shortcut.
• Annakarl teleport and go west to the main entrance.
• Games necklace teleport to the Corporeal Beast lair, or make a waka canoe (requiring 57 Woodcutting and an axe), and go north to use the Agility shortcut.
• The Wilderness lever, requiring a weapon with slash bonus or a knife to cut a web, run south through the deep Wilderness gate to the northern entrance.

Banking can be done at the Mage Arena bank or via an amulet of glory by going south to level 30 Wilderness and teleporting to Edgeville.

tactics.heading: Requirements
tactics.text:
As always, only bring items you are willing to risk. It is therefore strongly recommended to only bring 3 or 4-item with a top, bottom, weapon and shield, preferably an anti-dragon shield. Anything else should be expendable and easily obtainable, such as God cape, book, or diary items.

At 74 Agility, an Agility shortcut becomes available for back-door access in the south. Furthermore, completion of the elite Wilderness Diary grants noted bones in the Wilderness.

tactics.text:
• 70+ Magic or (80+ Recommended)
• 43+ Prayer
• 70+ Defence (optional)
• 74+ Agility (optional)

gearNotes.heading: Equipment
gearNotes.text:
Using Ranged is recommended as this allows better manoeuvring, although Melee is also viable. Lizardman shamans are weak to both combat styles; specifically, they have negative stab defence and no ranged defence bonuses. Slash, crush, and magical attacks are not recommended as they have high defensive bonuses against those styles.

If killing lizardman shamans on task, it is strongly recommended to have completed the hard Kourend & Kebos Diary to add the Shayzien armour effect to your Slayer helmet via Captain Cleive. Warning: This will not happen automatically! You need to actively speak with Captain Cleive to trigger the change. If you do not have the diary completed, you will take some damage from the acid spit attack if wearing the Slayer helmet, and it can deal a lot of damage over time.

If you have not completed the diary, it's best to wear the Shayzien helm (5) regardless of combat class.

Activate Protect from Missiles and your best offensive prayer, and if using, set up your dwarf multicannon in the north-west corner near the obstruction in Lizardman Canyon as indicated in the image above. Focus primarily on killing the north-west and south-west spawns.

Always pay attention to all special attacks, namely leaping and summoning minions. Move out of the way as soon as you see them jump, and dodge the minions by manoeuvring around an obstacle or moving a few spaces away. The jump hits a 3x3 area in the Lizardman Canyon and 2x2 in the Lizardman Temple with the north-east tile targeting the player's tile. As a ranger, always keep distance, and work the obstacles. Note that hugging the obstacle or wall in the canyon prevents the shamans from jumping. As for the shaman temple, only the western and southern walls will prevent them from jumping.

Activate Protect from Melee, and if using, set up your dwarf multicannon north-west by the obstruction in Lizardman Canyon, or set up your cannon in the open area south-west.

Always pay attention to all special attacks, namely leaping and summoning minions regardless. Move out of the way as soon as you see them jump, and dodge the minions by manoeuvring around an obstacle or moving a few spaces away.

If using the noxious halberd, stand one tile away, allowing you to avoid the melee attacks and pray Protect from Ranged.

tactics.heading: Overview
tactics.text: Lizardman shamans are popular monsters hunted by players for their renowned dragon warhammer drop, which has a useful special attack for high level PvM encounters. This guide will give a few tips and some setups to help out with your kills.

tactics.heading: Location
tactics.text:
Lizardman shamans can be found in three locations:
• Western side of the Lizardman Canyon - contains three shamans in a large, multi-combat area. They won't attempt their stomp attack if you stand in the south-west corner.
• Lizardman Caves on the northern end of the Lizardman Settlement - contains eight shamans in a small, single-way area, with two shamans in each room. These can only be killed while on a lizardman Slayer task.
• Lizardman Temple beneath Molch - contains six shamans in a small, single-way area, with two shamans in each room.

tactics.heading: Attacks
tactics.text:
Lizardman shamans use the following attacks:
• Melee attack - a standard melee attack sharing the same animation as the other lizardmen.
• Ranged attack - a standard ranged attack sharing the same animation as the other lizardmen. This attack can poison.
• Special attacks - Lizardman shamans have three special attacks that can be used without cooldown:
  • Acid spit - The shaman spits a large ball of acid at the player's current location. This will deal unblockable poison damage for up to 30 damage. This attack can poison. The damage reduces if you wear a full set of Shayzien armour, obtained from fighting the soldiers in the Combat Ring. Wearing the full tier 5 Shayzien set negates all damage done by this attack, though you can still be poisoned.
  • Jump - The shaman jumps into the air before crashing down at the player's location when they jumped. This can be avoided by moving out of the way. If the shaman stomps you, you will take heavy damage which cannot be blocked. They will not attempt this attack if they cannot land on the players location. This can be taken advantage of by ensuring you have a wall blocking the tile to the south or west of you.
  • Spawns - The shaman summons three spawns - two next to the player and one under the player, who will follow the player upon spawning, unless the spawns are summoned in a position where they cannot see the player. After several seconds, the spawn will explode, dealing 8-10 damage to players that are two spaces or less from it when it explodes. The minion who spawns under the player will always explode first.

Lizardman shamans have an attack range of 8, which means that weapons like longbows, composite bows, the crystal bow, and the Bow of Faerdhinen can outrange it on rapid, and weapons like shortbows, crossbows, and Karil's crossbow can outrange it on longrange.

• 80+ Strength
• 20+ Defence (60+ Recommended)
• 60+ Ranged
• 40+ Prayer (43+ Recommended)

gearNotes.heading: Equipment
gearNotes.text:
Melee is the simplest and most effective way to kill the Mad Angel. Due to its golembane weakness, a granite hammer is particularly effective, although many other crush weapons are viable.

Lower tier options still perform relatively well since accuracy is guaranteed after perfectly dodging the sweep attack and max hits are guaranteed on the first hitsplat after perfectly praying against the smite attack. Lower damage setups will find swapping weapons throughout the fight to be worthwhile. For example, using the dual macuahuitl when accuracy is guaranteed, but using a higher accuracy weapon during other parts of the fight.

Most other ranged and magic setups will not perform well due to the boss's defence; however, the twisted bow can take advantage of the opportunities to hit with guaranteed accuracy.

gearNotes.heading: Inventory
gearNotes.text:
• 1 divine super combat potion
• Food
• Prayer potions or super restores
• Crystal dust to convert dropped 1 dose super combat potions into their divine version (optional, requires 97 Herblore)
• Special attack weapon
• Ardeaglais teleports and a teleport for banking such as teleport to house tablets
• Divine rune pouch and Book of the Dead with runes for thralls and Death Charge

The Mad Angel can be killed effectively with lower tier weaponry when countering its mechanics correctly due to the guaranteed max hits and accuracy granted throughout the fight. Lower level players looking to take on the boss should prioritise using the best weapon they have available to them, and should consider using the full blood moon set where possible. Utilising special attacks after the smite attack is also particularly effective, although this requires good timing to execute.

gearNotes.heading: Inventory
gearNotes.text:
• Special attack weapon, such as the dragon mace
• Combat boosting potions, such as divine super combat potion, or divine super strength potion
• Prayer potions
• Runes to cast thralls with Book of the Dead, and ideally also Death Charge
• Teleport to the boss such as necklace of passage or Slayer ring
• Emergency teleport/a way to restore stats and bank, such as teleport to house (tablet) or ring of dueling
• The rest food, such as karambwans or better

tactics.heading: Overview
tactics.text: After completion of Fallen From Grace, a stronger version of the Mad Angel can be awoken and fought again in Ardeaglais.

tactics.heading: Requirements
tactics.text: • Completion of Quest Fallen From Grace

tactics.heading: Recommendations
tactics.text:
• 60 Attack
• 60 Strength
• 43 Prayer minimum for Protect from Melee / Protect from Magic
  • 70 Prayer and 70 Defence for Piety

tactics.heading: Transportation
tactics.text:
• The fastest route to the cathedral in which the Mad Angel resides is via Ardeaglais teleport.
• Alternatively, use a Slayer ring to teleport to the cave underneath the boss. Then either interact with the golem to the north and climb the stairs to the boss, or exit the cave to the west and run to the boss.
• You may also use a necklace of passage, then run west and climb the rocks to reach the front door to the cathedral. This requires you to have mined the rocks at the top of the shortcut, as well as 54 Agility.

tactics.heading: Fight overview
tactics.text:
Auto-retaliate should be disabled or you risk being dragged during the blast attack, which can result in failing the mechanic.

The Mad Angel attacks primarily with melee, and is weak to golembane weapons.

Protect from Melee will reduce the max hit of its standard attacks from 31 to 5. After three standard attacks, it will perform a special attack.

Upon reaching 350 Hitpoints (~45%), the Mad Angel will enter the enrage phase at the next available opportunity, denoted by a overhead message. During this phase, its special attacks are performed quicker, requiring quicker reaction times to counter them. Additionally, it will use all three of its specials consecutively at the start of this phase.

Since the blast attack damage mechanic always deals a fixed 18-22 damage, players with high damage setups can intentionally fail this mechanic for the next sweep/smite attack punish to occur sooner. When done strategically, this leads to faster kill times but possibly lowers kills per trip if supplies are an issue.

gearNotes.heading: Equipment
gearNotes.text:
The Maggot King is weakest to crush and heavy ranged attacks. Although it possesses a relatively high Magic level and defence (200 Magic and +150 magic defence), it also possesses an 80% susceptibility to fire spells, which can be feasible for maging players utilising a harmonised Nightmare staff, tome of fire and confliction gauntlets. Furthermore, successful attacks with fire spells deal an additional (stacking) 5 burn damage to the boss. It is recommended to use fire spells with either the harmonised Nightmare staff or the twinflame staff, as not only does the boss's magic defence get reduced by 20 per burn stack, but failed casts will also benefit from confliction gauntlets, whereas Tumeken's shadow gains none of these benefits. The harmonised nightmare and twinflame staffs also output fire hits at a higher rate than standard autocast staffs such as the Purging staff, ensuring the boss gets to full burn stacks more quickly and stays there more reliably.

Perfect kills will require minimal sustain, as the boss deals very little chip damage when walking onto acid/bile pools and being hit by small carrion bits. While not necessary, an amulet of blood fury switch can also be used to heal off of any damage taken during the fight. The boss frequently drops a dull ancient medal and 2-4 stymphike tartares, which help restore prayer, has a 3/7 chance to provide combat stats and heal a good amount of health, which often adds an extra kill into trips.

Fire spells are especially powerful, causing both a damage-over-time effect and lowering the boss's magic defence. Generally, fire surge with a tome of fire and sunfire runes or searing pages will outperform the Tumeken's shadow. This is much more beneficial than thralls and Death Charge, as the only special attack needed is the Accursed sceptre or Eye of Ayak to lower the boss's magic defence, which costs 50% energy and is easily restored over the course of a single kill. Apply the Ayak special when the boss has 5 burn stacks.

Heavy ranged options, which require bolts, are the most effective ranged weapons to use on the Maggot King. While cheaper than magic, players will usually have longer kills and shorter trips as damage leading up to the melee phase is heavily reliant on enchanted ruby bolts, which forces the player to keep health low to avoid as much self-damage as possible. A hunters' sunlight crossbow can serve as a budget option, as it is better than a twisted bow here with enough components of max range gear. Additionally, a standard ranged weapon is required to deal with ur-maggots. Dizana's quiver allows bringing both ammo types without using extra switches or inventory slots but caution is advised if the player brings a melee cape switch, as failing to switch back to quiver can result in failing to fire. A charged bow such as a Bow of Faerdhinen, Crystal bow or Webweaver bow is a good way to get around this problem while also providing a nine to ten tile range to hit larvae. A venator bow is another option for killing larvae as the shots can bounce to the boss for extra damage, and also bounce to other larvae spawns to kill multiple in 1 click. It does have slightly less range than other bow options however so take care to not be dragged into hazards.

Melee punishes are not affected by a weapon's attack speed. Slow, higher hitting weapons are preferred, ideally alongside a faster weapon to create more opportunities to punish for extra damage. Weapons set to the crush style receive a significant accuracy boost alongside the normal 50% increased damage. If not switching weapons specifically for the punish, it is often better to only use the punish weapon and to maximise the amount of punishes. Damage special attacks are preferred over defence reducing special attacks as Maggot King resets its defence after melee phases. If you do use a defence reducing special attack then do it on a punish attack to increase your accuracy.

tactics.heading: Overview
tactics.text:
After completion of The Blood Moon Rises, players can fight the Maggot King in its lair, in which the entrance is accessed via some darkwood trees in the forest between Sangvesti and the Ruined Village.

If the player dies while fighting the Maggot King, they will respawn in Vampyrium by the portal back to Gielinor, with their grave appearing outside of the boss lair entrance. Players will have their reclamation fee reduced by 75% until they have five kills, after which the standard death cost will apply.

Should players not wish to make the trek from the portal to the boss lair, the aranei scout near the portal can be paid with one of three items to move the gravestone near them:

tactics.heading: Requirements
tactics.text: • Completion of Quest The Blood Moon Rises for access to Vampyrium.

tactics.heading: Recommendations
tactics.text:
• 85+ Ranged (if using Ranged)
• 75+ Magic (if using Magic)
• 80+ Attack
• 85+ Strength
• 74 Prayer and 70 Defence to unlock and use Rigour. Highly recommended.
• 70 Construction to build a bank chest in Sangvesti.
• 64 Agility for the bush shortcuts in the Sotfa Forest.

tactics.heading: Transportation
tactics.text:
Use Drakan's medallion to get to Castle Drakan, enter Vampyrium, and then run east. Before fighting the boss, players should unlock a quick-travel method by rescuing an aranei scout south-east of Sangvesti.

This scout will initially be attacked by sanguidae; kill all three of them, then talk to the scout again, who will then be found south of the bank chest by the map icon and will take players just east of Sangvesti. Two agility shortcuts can be used to traverse the woods more quickly, both requiring level 64 Agility; It is recommended to only use the shortcut furthest away from the scout, as the closer shortcut is a longer path to the boss and the player is likely to be attacked by an Ancient feral vyre.

Lastly, to use the bank chest, it must first be built with level 70 Construction (boosts can be used) using a hammer and saw, 1 magic stone, 2 cupronickel bars, 2 adamantite bars, and 4 ironwood planks. If the player is not using this chest to bank, they may rebank at their desired location, then utilise a shortcut south of Safalaan to quickly reach the scout.

Regardless, both routes will usually result in the player running into the nearby dire bat which is the only nuisance on the way to the scout.

tactics.heading: Fight overview
tactics.text:
The Maggot King is initially fought at a distance, requiring players to attack with either ranged or magic attacks from their side of the arena; heavy ranged attacks and fire spells work best, with fire spells dealing an additional (stacking) 5 burn damage to the boss and reducing its magic defence by 20 per burn stack.

The Maggot King's basic attacks cover all three combat styles. Both the magic and ranged attacks can deal up to 46 damage, and are fully blocked by prayer. The melee attack is slightly stronger, dealing up to 55 damage, and prayer does not fully protect against these attacks, instead reducing them by ~40%.
• Ranged - Green spit is launched at the player, leaving poisonous bile behind on the tile the player stood on when the attack lands, as well as on two adjacent tiles. The attack will also poison the player starting at 8 damage.
  • Standing on the poisonous bile will deal minor damage, as well as drain poison immunity by 45 seconds. It will remain there until it is covered over with carrion or when stepped on.
  • Using both the serpentine helm and anti-venom+ will provide immunity to poisonous bile.
• Magic - Yellow spit is launched at the player, leaving sticky bile behind on the tile the player stood on when the attack lands, as well as on two adjacent tiles.
  • Standing on the sticky bile will deal minor damage, drain Attack, Strength, or Defence, and delay the player's next attack by one tick (0.6s). The amount drained is based on the damage dealt by the bile. It will remain there until it is covered over with carrion or when stepped on.
  • An inoculation bracelet will provide immunity to sticky bile.
• Melee - The Maggot King walks up close and slams its head in a 3x4 Area-of-Effect.

tactics.heading: Attack rotation
tactics.text:
The Maggot King follows a rotation of attacks that it will use throughout the fight, with slight alterations at certain health thresholds.

When the fight begins, the Maggot King will always start with ranged attacks. It will use ranged/magic 4-8 times before using a screech attack, indicated by a white aura surrounding the boss. Players must turn off their protection prayer prior to this, otherwise they will take 15-25 damage per tick; players may take damage up to three times if it is not turned off at all, but deactivating it late will still reduce overall damage. Notably, during its screech attack, its Defence level is temporarily halved to 100, allowing special attacks such as the Zaryte crossbow to be far more likely to hit.

Alongside every screech, the Maggot King will throw piles of carrion into the arena. These target random tiles, after which they will splatter into smaller bits, wiping off any pools of bile that were previously occupying the tiles they landed on, making them safe to stand on again. Getting hit by the initial carrions will deal up to 25 damage, while getting hit by the smaller carrion will deal up to 10 damage. Additionally, the Maggot King’s attack speed will increase by 1 tick after the first screech.

Carrions can be avoided by spotting looming shadows on the target tiles, and the smaller bits will only target tiles adjacent to the initial target tiles. As piles of carrion tend to land next to each other, the secondary bits can overlap and target what would otherwise be "safe" tiles. For the highest chance to avoid damage it is best to look for the more isolated first shadows. Given that the smaller bits deal less damage, it may be be more beneficial to simply tank them.

Shortly after the carrions land, the Maggot King will switch to magic attacks until it screeches again, after which it will switch back to ranged. Lastly, any drained Defence levels will be restored after a screech, though defence bonuses will remain. Therefore, the Eye of Ayak will be more beneficial than an accursed sceptre, as the former's special attack will also stack with the magic defence reduction from using fire spells; a hit of 30 or more with the Ayak, coupled with 5 burn stacks, usually results in the boss having next to no magic defence.

tactics.heading: Ur-maggot larvae
tactics.text:
When the boss reaches ~1,250 (~83%) health, it will launch an ur-maggot larvae towards the arena whenever it uses its screech. If the larvae is hit with standard ranged (bow and arrows) before it lands on the arena, they will be instantly killed; this bow attack can be fired off instantly after attacking the Maggot King. This attack will incur its normal attack cooldown and will completely overwrite the cooldown of the previous attack. Therefore, a slower weapon's attack cooldown can be shortened by attacking the larvae with a fast attack speed bow. By weaving the bow attack between the player's first two melee attacks, the second melee attack can be performed before the Maggot King's first melee slam, even if the player is using a slow melee weapon like Dharok's greataxe. For this to work, a 3-tick or 4-tick bow must be used, with a 3-tick bow making this mechanic much easier.

If allowed to land onto the arena, the larvae will move back and forth horizontally over the row of tiles it landed on; if carrion are present on a tile they move to, they will eat it and heal the boss for 1 hitpoint. If they reach the player, they will stop moving and begin to chip at the player's health to heal the boss, starting at 3 damage and increasing by 1 every tick.

The first larvae will spawn on the west side of the arena, after which they will alternate back and forth (west > east > west > east) for the rest of the fight.

When the boss reaches ~299 (~19%) health, it will launch multiple larvae at once, with a maximum of four (for each row in the arena. Although multiple may stack on the same row) if there are none present. A venator bow is useful for this part as the bounces allow easier control of larger groups.

tactics.heading: Melee slams
tactics.text:
When the boss reaches ~980 (~65%) health, it will begin using melee attacks as part of its attack rotation. After using a screech, it will walk up to the bone wall separating the arena and position itself to align its centre tile with your current tile, then slam the 3x4 area in front of it, dealing up to 55 damage (reduced to 35 with Protect from Melee) as well as launching three poisonous or sticky biles within two tiles in front of it. As such, players must avoid the slams by moving towards its easternmost or westernmost tiles when it is about to attack. Additionally, the boss's magic defence will be temporarily increased from +150 to +400.

If the player attacks the boss the same time as it slams down, they will automatically attack the boss without incurring an attack delay alongside increased accuracy (85% reduced defence roll if using crush) and a 50% damage boost for that attack. Multi-hit weapons will only have the bonus applied onto the first hit. As such, slow weapons such as an elder maul or godsword can be used to particularly strong effect if the player is able to properly time their attacks; the timing for this melee punish requires the player to click the Maggot King on the same tick that it extends its head.

To effectively melee the boss, the player can wait for the slam, step out to attack, and then attack again to do a regular attack alongside the melee punish. Both 4 and 5-tick weapons can effectively melee punish, but with different methods; 4-tick weapons require the player to utilise a stepback method to avoid losing ticks from the boss moving into position, while 5-tick weapons can simply move east or west accordingly without tick loss. The 4-tick method may require the player to walk one tile accordingly as the stepback tile may be splattered in bile (subsequent stepbacks in that melee sequence are safe as normal), while the 5-tick method requires players to be mindful lest they step into bile while dragging the boss.

Upon screeching, it will retreat and resume attacking with either ranged or magic, depending on which style was used prior to it using melee. When the boss reaches ~305 (~20%) health, it will stop retreating and only attack with melee, allowing players to ignore the screech entirely since there isn't anything to pray against at this point in the fight.

tactics.heading: Dharok's punish
tactics.text:
Skilled players who wish to do the fastest kills may opt to use full Dharok's at very low hitpoints for both the melee punish and regular attack. This requires doing a 7-tick attack cycle that does not consistently align with The Maggot King's attack cycle, thus the player needs to alternate between dragging and stepping back towards the boss in order to align the attack cycles with the awkward 7-tick attack speed.

Usually, the player drags the boss by doing the exact same clicks as the 5-tick cycle and waiting to attack, but whenever your regular attack happens on the last tick before dodging the slam, you need to step back after the punish. This results in a cycle of drag-drag-stepback repeating every 3 slams. You can however enter the cycle in different parts at the start of the melee phase depending on your attack cooldown prior (due to shooting the ur-maggot larvae for example), resulting in drag-stepback-drag or stepback-drag-drag (which the player shouldn't really ever end up on).

Players using the Dharok method may wish to use low healing foods such as Guthix Rests, so that they maintain hp from 20-30 outside melee phases, and 1-15 during melee phases, having enough health to survive carrion falls during screeches. Camping high enough hp to survive a slam results in Dharok's being worse than other options for most players.

Hallowfell deals damage to two additional enemies for half the player's maximum hit (within the three front and two adjacent tiles to the player), which provides the highest melee experience rate in the game when consistently applied (as it will here).
High strength bonus should be prioritized for other item slots, with prayer bonus as a secondary focus. A bonecrusher necklace (or dragonbone necklace with a bonecrusher) is particularly useful here, as it restores 2 prayer points per monkey killed. Depending on prayer bonus and kills per hour, players may restore enough prayer passively to have permanent uptime on Piety without other prayer restoration methods; for those that cannot achieve this but wish to train passively, Chivalry can be used instead at the expense of slightly less experience per hour.

Players should bring super strength potions over super combat potions, as the extra accuracy is not needed against the very low defence monkeys.

gearNotes.heading: Higher Effort
gearNotes.text:
Players should aim to attack a maniacal monkey with full health. This minimizes the damage lost from overkill: hitting a weakened monkey with a damage roll higher than its current hitpoints "wastes" the excess damage, and this is more likely to happen with the full damage hit rather than the half damage splash.

As discussed above, the dragon/crystal halberd special hits up to 10 monkeys at once and provides a large increase in experience, upwards of an additional 50,000 experience per hour. This does require more active stacking of the monkeys.

gearNotes.heading: Lower Effort
gearNotes.text:
Alternatively: players can simply turn on auto-retaliate and reset aggression (every 10 minutes) as needed. This gives substantially less experience but is much less active.

A bonecrusher necklace for passive prayer regeneration is highly recommended to minimize interactions due to prayer drain. With Piety usage, some setups may require additional prayer restoration, such as the potions dropped by the monkeys. Switching to Chivalry, or trading out some equipment for higher prayer bonus gear, may allow the player to auto-retaliate for the full aggression timer without interruption.

tactics.heading: Overview
tactics.text: Killing Maniacal monkeys offers some of the highest experience rates in the game for training Magic (with Ancient Magicks burst/barrage spells), Ranged (with Chinchompas) and Melee (with a Hallowfell). The monkeys' extremely low Defence and high spawn density allow for consistent high-damage hits against multiple targets, and the frequent 1-dose Prayer potion drops minimise banking trips. They can be killed in an active manner (for higher experience rates) or in a semi-AFK manner with auto-retaliate (similar to Nightmare Zone).

tactics.heading: Requirements
tactics.text:
• Partial completion of Monkey Madness II (must have gained access to Kruk's Dungeon)
• 43 Prayer to use Protect from Melee
• 75 Attack to use Hallowfell
• 45 Ranged to use chinchompas
• 62 Magic and Desert Treasure I completion to cast Ancient Magicks burst or barrage spells (e.g. Ice Burst)
• A light source

tactics.heading: Recommended
tactics.text:
• 70+ Prayer for longer trips and access to Piety, Rigour, and Augury
• 80+ Ranged for effective use of Red chinchompas and faster XP rates
• 94+ Magic for efficient casting of Ice Barrage with high max hits and accuracy

tactics.heading: Transportation
tactics.text:
Maniacal monkeys are located in Kruk's Dungeon on Ape Atoll. The dungeon entrance is in the north-western part of the island. There are a few different methods to get there:
• After the completion of Monkey Madness II, players can use any gnome gliders to Ape Atoll and then run south.
• Players who have not completed the quest will need to wear a greegree while getting there to avoid damage from aggressive monsters. Players can get there via the Ape Atoll Teleport on the standard spellbook and running west, or Ape Atoll Teleport on the Arceuus spellbook and running north.
• The fairy ring CLR is south of the dungeon entrance.
  • Without a Ninja or Kruk monkey greegree, the player has to take damage to leave the Ape Atoll Agility Course.

To reach the best spot to kill maniacal monkeys, players should navigate through the second hole with vines (marked as 2 on the map) of Kruk's Dungeon, then they will need to climb down and head south-east until they reach a large room. It is advised to check if there are any other players currently present by right-clicking the hole and selecting the "Look-in Hole" option. Sharing a world is not recommended as it will reduce experience rates for both players.

tactics.heading: General information
tactics.text:
Use Protect from Melee at all times. Use the 1-dose prayer potions dropped by the maniacal monkeys to replenish Prayer points. Alternatively, players who have the bonecrusher can equip the dragonbone necklace or the bonecrusher necklace to restore Prayer points whenever needed.

When the maniacal monkeys lose aggression towards the player after roughly 10 minutes, they should run west along the south passage to the yellow box indicated on the map above. Once the adjacent maniacal monkeys become aggressive again, the aggression has been reset and the player may return to their training spot.

Players on a budget looking to recoup some of the money spent on runes or chinchompas can use Imp-in-a-box (level 71 Hunter) and bank 4-dose Prayer potions while dropping the leftover magic boxes. This assumes the bonecrusher necklace or the dragonbone necklace with a bonecrusher method is used, which removes the need for prayer potions. For example, a player ice bursting who leaves and returns after filling up on prayer potions after all the Imp-in-a-box have been used, can expect to be refunded about half the cost of the runes spent for that trip.

Even without the necklace, players may find it worth bringing a bonecrusher. Depending on the method used, a bonecrusher can provide as high as 40k Prayer experience per hour. Even on lower intensity methods, this will rapidly deplete charges at a minimum rate of 1200 per hour, so ensure the bonecrusher is adequately charged.

tactics.heading: Solo methods
tactics.text: There are different methods to stack the maniacal monkeys for solo players. See the gallery below for the three most common methods. Higher click-intensity methods may provide higher experience rates as you will hit larger amounts of monkeys, and are generally most efficient with weapons that can hit a higher number of targets. Using Hallowfell (Melee) can hit up to 3 targets, Burst and Barrage spells (Magic) can hit up to 9 targets, and Chinchompas (Ranged) can hit up to 11 targets, so stacking methods are much more impactful for Ranged and Magic than for Melee.

tactics.heading: Using 2 dancing accounts
tactics.text:
Maniacal monkeys can be stacked automatically by having 2 accounts follow each other in front of the player. This method allows the player to fully AFK without needing to run back and forth to stack the monkeys.

At first, the two accounts need to wait 10 minutes to lose the aggressiveness of the monkeys. After that, the second player should follow the first and then head to one of the stacking corners seen in the videos above. If the second player follows the first one at the right time, the characters will start moving around each other ('dancing'). This finishes the preparation, and now the account that wishes to train can run to one of the corners near the two dancing players, and the monkeys will be stacked automatically (this dancing movement is basically an automatic shuffling machine which stacks the monkeys).

To optimally shuffle, stand in one of the stacking corners. Visualise a 2x2 tile square wherein the player who is bursting is in the top right. The two accounts should be shuffling on the other 3 tiles. This can be done by simply having 1 stand still on the bottom right tile, one stand on the bottom left following the account on the bottom right tile, and the bottom right tile following the bottom left player. If done correctly, this can increase experience rates by up to 20%. This can be especially helpful if the player often finds themselves running out of run energy while stacking.

tactics.heading: Using the crystal halberd (All combat styles)
tactics.text:
Using the special attack of a Crystal halberd or dragon halberd when it is available can provide significant additional experience when training any combat skill: When training Melee, it will increase experience per hour for a minimal intensity increase. For Ranged and Magic, it can provide about 50,000 experience per hour in Attack, Strength, or Defence while only slightly reducing magic or ranged experience and supplies used per hour - this can be efficient depending upon the player's goals. If using this method and training Ranged or Magic, it is advisable to prefer melee strength over prayer bonus or magic/ranged accuracy in slots where gear would not increase the Magic or Ranged hit - for instance, using a Mixed hide cape or a Fire cape over Ava's accumulator, or a Berserker ring (i) over a Ring of shadows. Bringing divine strength potions, switching to an offensive prayer and wearing the best strength-boosting gear while using the halberd's special attacks is advised (or a Void melee helm if the player is using the void armour).

Players training Melee or Ranged may optionally cast the Death Charge spell from the Arceuus spellbook (with 80 Magic and completion of A Kingdom Divided) to regain special attack energy faster.

Only equipping the halberd when the player is able to get off at least 3 special attacks in a row minimise time spent switching. It is possible to achieve four consecutive halberd special attacks with the death charge spell off cooldown.

tactics.heading: Using Ahrim's set (Magic)
tactics.text: For low-budget/mid-level players who do not have the Ancient sceptre and high level armour such as Ancestral or Virtus, using the Ahrim's set with amulet of the damned can be a viable alternative. Not only does this provide the ability to autocast ancient magicks, the amulet of the damned also provides a 25% chance to do 30% more damage. Contrary to popular belief, barrows armour does not degrade based on the number of attacks. Rather, it degrades purely based on time in combat. This allows the player to pay an additional 12k/hr (Ahrim's and AotD degradation costs) in exchange for the ability to achieve high rates for a fraction of the barrier-to-entry cost.

tactics.heading: Detailed strategy by training method
tactics.text:
Maniacal monkeys have a Magic defence of 1 and so increasing magical accuracy will increase hit accuracy by no more than 1%. Therefore, the objective is to increase the max hit of the spell with the largest magic damage bonus.

The base hit of Ice Burst is 22. The maximum hit with all magic damage bonuses is 33.

Items to bring for Ice Bursting are prioritised as follows:
• Equipment that increases max hit
• Equipment that increases prayer bonus
• Equipment that increases magical accuracy

Players who have completed the Morytania Hard Diary also have the option of using a Bonecrusher necklace to completely remove the need to pick up prayer potions. This option is not fully AFK, however, as NPC aggression must be reset every 10 minutes.

tactics.heading: Prayer bonus vs Ranged attack bonus
tactics.text:
Maniacal monkeys have a Defence level of 10. Because of this, equipping best-in-slot ranged accuracy gear versus no items at a Ranged level of 80/99 will only increase accuracy by 0.75%/0.60%. In the worst case scenario, this translates to a negligible 14 missed hits per hour.

Because of this, prioritising prayer bonus over ranged accuracy results in 23-42 fewer prayer potions doses per hour or less time spent without a necklace of anguish or rupture equipped if using the bonecrusher method. If you instead use max ranged bonus gear and are able to pick up prayer potions and continue throwing chinchompas without losing any ticks or unstacking the monkeys significantly, you would gain no more than an extra 5,000 experience per hour. It is much more likely that players will spend more time picking up and consuming prayer potions than the minimal extra damage output of ranged accuracy gear. For this reason prayer bonus gear is considered superior to having higher ranged accuracy, and it also makes training less intense.

The lone exception to this may occur at certain ranged levels and with certain setups (DPS calculation required) when the player does not gain a max hit from wearing the necklace of anguish or rupture. In this specific case, wearing the bonecrusher necklace with a preference for high ranged accuracy equipment over prayer bonus (ex: pegasian boots, archers ring (i)) becomes slightly better, as your prayer will remain almost full the entire time due to the effects of the bonecrusher necklace.

While the monkeys do drop Bass, Rapid Heal will negate the divine potion damage.

gearNotes.heading: Equipment
gearNotes.text: Melee is an efficient way of killing them, especially with a Dragon hunter lance (the best stab weapon against Dragons and draconic creatures) and using Sunfire armour for Prayer or high-tier armour, such as Bandos or Barrows equipment, for Defence. The Dragon hunter lance is the best choice followed by Osmumten's fang. Other options include Ghrazi rapier, Zamorakian hasta and lastly Abyssal Dagger. Using slash weapons, such as an Abyssal whip, is not recommended due to their high slash defences. As their Defence is extremely high, the higher the stab bonus the faster the kills will be, thus using fewer supplies.

gearNotes.heading: Inventory
gearNotes.text:
• Holy wrench (optional)
• 2-3 Extended super antifires potions
• 1-2 Super combat potions
• 30+ Nature runes and 150+ Fire runes for Alchs (optional)
• Food is not necessary when fighting bronze, iron or steel dragons with protect from melee.

Ranged can be feasible and very economical if using broad bolts, but using Diamond bolts (e) can be faster at a greater cost. Always keep a distance of several spaces away from the dragon to avoid its melee attack. All you have to do is make sure your antifire is active, and snipe away at a distance.

gearNotes.heading: Inventory
gearNotes.text:
• 1 Extended super antifire
• 1-2 Prayer potions (optional) Unlike melee, Prayer potions are really not needed when using range unless Eagle Eye or Rigour is used
• 1-2 Ranging potions
• 30+ Nature runes and 150+ Fire runes for Alchs (optional)
• Food is not necessary when fighting bronze, iron or steel dragons from a distance.

Magic is one of the quickest ways to kill metal dragons cheaply, and can be done without taking damage. All the caster has to do is make sure their antifire is active, anti-dragon shield is equipped and attack them at a distance. Unless using a powered staff, earth spells should be used to take advantage of the dragons' earth weakness.
Although players can opt for better setups if maging, Void mage can be used as well for accounts below 70 Defence. However, Ahrim's robes will prove to be better when players have level 70 Defence or higher.

gearNotes.heading: Inventory
gearNotes.text:
• 1 Extended super antifire
• 1-2 Prayer potions (optional) Unlike Melee, Prayer potions are really not needed when using Magic unless Mystic Might or Augury is used
• Nature and Fire runes for Alchs (optional)
• Food is not necessary when fighting bronze, iron or steel dragons from a distance.

tactics.heading: Overview
tactics.text:
Bronze, iron, and steel metal dragons can be killed with all three combat styles.

As with chromatic dragons, metal dragons are weak to stab attacks and heavy ranged attacks. Unlike chromatic dragons, metal dragons are weak to Earth spells. Slayer masters can assign metal dragons, though many players tend to skip them, especially at lower levels where they do not have good gear, as metal dragons have higher Defence levels compared to their chromatic counterparts. If the player does not have any dragonbane weaponry, they are highly advised to use a magic setup, as they have a slightly lower Magic level compared to Defence, and they suffer 50% more damage and an extra 50% magic accuracy from earth spells.

tactics.heading: Suggested skills
tactics.text:
• 70+ Attack
• 70+ Strength
• 70+ Defence
• 70+ Ranged
• 75+ Magic (for slayer's staff (e))
• 70+ Hitpoints
• 44+ Prayer (Eagle Eye, 45+ Mystic Might, 70+ Piety, 74+ Rigour, 77+ Augury)

options.text: Elite void robe / Void knight robe
Dragon hunter wand / Harmonised Nightmare staff / Eye of Ayak
Trident of the Swamp / Mystic smoke staff
Trident of the Seas > Twinflame staff > Ahrim's staff
Lunar ring / Beacon ring / Explorer's ring 4
Moonlight antler bolts > Sunlight antler bolts
Zaryte crossbow > Armadyl crossbow > Dragon crossbow
Ring of suffering (ri) / Ring of shadows
Justiciar faceguard (only when wearing the full set)
Justiciar chestguard (only when wearing the full set)
Justiciar legguards (only when wearing the full set)

gearNotes.heading: Equipment
gearNotes.text:
Melee is a very effective method of killing mithril dragons with little upkeep cost, assuming that the player has high combat stats (at least 90+), and access to either the Osmumten's fang or a dragon hunter lance. If the player does not have either the fang or lance, ghrazi rapier and zamorakian hasta are still viable options, however Magic then usually becomes more effective, depending on the player's equipment. For the best damage output, it is strongly recommended to use a defender and use extended super antifire potions to negate the dragonfire damage, instead of an anti-dragon shield or dragonfire shield.

This specific setup focuses on an offensive approach, resulting in higher kills per hour, at the cost of requiring more attention and supplies than a tank-based method.

When meleeing, players take damage from two combat styles and will have to tank both in order to survive. It is best to wear Torva or Bandos armour for their strength bonus and good defensive bonuses, and use Protect from Magic. Players can also wear Eclipse Moon chestplate and Blood Moon tassets for a minimal loss of max hit, in exchange for gaining much higher Magic defence. If the player does not have Torva or Bandos armour, wearing armour with high Magic defence (such as Karil's armour or black dragonhide armour) and using Protect from Melee will suffice. Piety should also be used in conjunction with the chosen protection prayer for better damage output and higher Defence.

gearNotes.heading: Inventory
gearNotes.text:
• A games necklace
• A teleport
• 1-2 Divine super combat potions or super sets
• 1-2 super antifires (Regular antifire if using a shield for dragonfire protection)
• 4-5 prayer potions
• High-healing food for the rest

gearNotes.heading: Notes
gearNotes.text:
Magic is one of the most effective ways to kill mithril dragons with high-level equipment. With best-in-slot gear available, Tumeken's shadow offers the highest damage output off-task and second-highest on-task. Using the harmonised Nightmare staff and casting Earth Surge also offers good DPS due to the dragon's 50% elemental weakness to earth spells. Lesser powered staves, such as the sanguinesti staff or trident of the swamp are solid options as well, particularly at high Magic levels due to the way their damage scales with level. At lower Magic levels, it may be better to use strong earth spells to take advantage of the elemental weakness. Compared to Magic, using Melee is much more cost-effective, and the dragon hunter lance offers comparable or higher damage output in most cases.

Players should wear equipment that maximises Magic damage and accuracy bonuses. When maging, players should stand at a distance and use Protect from Missiles. Lastly, Augury, Mystic Vigour, or Mystic Might should be used for better damage output and higher Magic defence.

If the player is not wearing an ancient wyvern shield or an anti-dragon shield, players must use super antifire potions (or their extended versions) to negate the dragonfire damage.

gearNotes.heading: Inventory
gearNotes.text:
• A games necklace
• A rune pouch
• A teleport
• Imbued heart or magic potion(s) (optional)
• 1-2 antifires
• 4-5 prayer potions
• High-healing food for the rest

gearNotes.heading: Notes
gearNotes.text:
Ranged is a similar option to Magic in that damage taken will be largely prevented by Protect from Missiles and high magic defence bonuses from equipment. Due to the high ranged defence of Mithril dragons, the high Ranged Attack bonus granted against dragons by the dragon hunter crossbow is all but necessary. It is still possible to kill mithril dragons with other crossbows, but Melee and Magic set-ups will outperform the Ranged style with ease. Ruby dragon bolts (e) and diamond dragon bolts (e) are very effective, but come at a high cost and can only be used if using a Dragon crossbow or better. If using enchanted ruby dragon bolts, players should switch to their enchanted diamond dragon bolts at 100-150 HP. Amethyst broad bolts can be used instead as a more cost-effective ammunition alternative, but can significantly increase the time taken for a kill.

Players should use Protect from Missiles with Rigour or Eagle Eye. Since Ranged armour has high Magic defence, all magic damage should be tanked but Rigour will be a large boost as unlike Eagle Eye it provides some defensive bonuses of its own.

gearNotes.heading: Inventory
gearNotes.text:
• A games necklace
• A teleport
• 1-2 divine ranging potions
• 1-2 antifires
• 4-5 prayer potions
• High-healing food for the rest

gearNotes.heading: Notes
gearNotes.text:
While offensive armour is generally better for a high amount of kills per hour, focussing on defensive gear will allow the player to kill mithril dragons with relatively low effort and for extended amounts of kills per trip, making it a viable choice for those intending to grind out many hundreds or thousands of mithril dragons in their hunt for a dragon full helm or draconic visage.

The Osmumten's fang or dragon hunter lance are still the best choice for the weapon, but instead of offensive armour, Justiciar armour (only when wearing the full set) in combination with an elysian spirit shield can be used to effectively block out 15% + 17.5% of all incoming damage. Combined with optional recoil effects from the ring of suffering and echo boots, as well as the healing effect of the amulet of blood fury will make for an incredibly tanky setup that will allow for trips that are only terminated when the player runs out of antifire potions or prayer potions.

Using protect from Magic and piety as well as stat boosting potions will greatly help. When no or few specialized tanking equipment is owned by the player, they should consider focussing on offensive stats as listed in the 'Melee' style equipment tab instead. Where viable tanking options are lacking, the player might prefer to instead use offensive gear in that slot. Especially when justiciar armour or an elysian spirit shield is already used, it is still very viable to use a tank setup with more offensive hand, feet and jewellery slot equipment instead.

gearNotes.heading: Inventory
gearNotes.text:
• A rune pouch with teleports to the player owned house or house teleport tablets.
• 1-2 Divine super combat potions or super sets
• 1-2 super antifires (Regular antifire if using a shield for dragonfire protection)
• 6-7 prayer potions
• High-healing food for the rest
A bonecrusher (Or bonecrusher necklace) is very helpful to have in your inventory.

tactics.heading: Overview
tactics.text: At level 304, mithril dragons are the third strongest tier of metal dragons. They attack from all sides of the Combat triangle in addition to utilising extra long-ranged dragonfire. Players seeking to kill these powerful dragons will need to tank at least one combat style, or two when fighting within Melee distance.

tactics.heading: Dragonfire
tactics.text: It is not recommend to fight mithril dragons without full dragonfire protection, which can be achieved by drinking either a super antifire potion, or a regular antifire potion combined with a anti-dragon shield. Protect from Magic does not reduce the amount of damage taken from dragonfire attacks, as is the case for all metallic dragons.

tactics.heading: Suggested skills
tactics.text:
• 85+ Attack
• 85+ Strength
• 70+ Defence (85+ recommended)
• 75+ Magic
• 80+ Ranged
• 80+ Hitpoints (85+ recommended)
• 44+ Prayer (75 recommended)

tactics.heading: Flinching
tactics.text:
Flinching is a slow but safe method that allows players to kill mithril dragons without taking damage or using supplies.

Mithril dragons cannot attack players standing underneath them, so players can flinch them by standing inside their hitbox until they drop aggro.

If a player travels north upon entering the upper level of the ancient cavern, they can find a mithril dragon that is contained within a small room, giving the player multiple tiles that are permanently underneath the dragon and offer a safe and consistent flinching setup.

Flinching kills can be significantly increased by also using thralls.

A similar method is also possible by retreating down the stairs after each hit against the nearby mithril dragon, before it has a chance to retaliate, then climbing back up to hit again. Players must first spend 10 minutes in the areas to build up Tolerance so the mithril dragons upstairs and the brutal green dragons downstairs do not attack unprovoked, but afterwards can potentially achieve quicker kills than flinching, and can use ranged or magic attacks instead of only melee.
