gearNotes.heading: Equipment
gearNotes.text:
Ideally, use both Ranged and Magic, to exploit the weaknesses of both forms. Camping a single form will result in greatly increased kill times, with range camp generally being slightly more optimal. To a lesser extent, Magic-only setups with best-in-slot mage gear and a Tumeken's shadow are doable; a ranged swap may still be helpful for Muspah's smite phase.

Ranged setups employing Zaryte crossbow special attacks benefit greatly from using Surge potions.

The Arceuus spellbook is particularly useful against Muspah, and is strongly recommended. In addition to the use of thralls, Greater Corruption can be used for additional damage against Muspah's prayer shield. Ward of Arceuus can be used to protect the player from corruption. Vile Vigour can be used for additional run energy. Death Charge can be procced off Muspah to restore additional special attack energy, if not resetting between kills.

However, some players opt to use Ancient Magicks or Standard spellbook to simply freeze with Ice spells or Entangle Muspah to avoid its melee attack. Freezing the Muspah also makes the faster attack speed of the Eye of Ayak easier to take advantage of. Standard spellbook gives access to Wind spells, which Muspah is weak to.

Without reducing Muspah's defence, Melee setups perform poorly. A ranged swap should also be brought for use when Muspah is teleporting or shielded, and additionally may be helpful at the end of the fight if Muspah is surrounded by spikes.

Using Melee also requires familarity with the stepback method and can be harder to execute.

Muspah is most effectively fought with Magic and Ranged. Magic should be used on Muspah's Melee form, and Ranged should be used otherwise. Using sapphire bolts (e) with a crossbow is strongly recommended on Muspah's prayer shield, ideally in combination with Smite and Greater Corruption.

Ranged only setups are sometimes preferred for simplicity, especially if players aren't as comfortable with a large amount of equipment swaps.

Upon entering the boss arena, if Muspah spawns in Melee form, it may save time to leave and re-enter to spend more time overall hitting Muspah's ranged form, which has lower ranged defence. Alternatively, with a Zaryte crossbow, using a special attack with Ruby bolts (e) special on the first Melee phase can be beneficial.

Alternatively, some players prefer to use a Elder maul, Dragon warhammer, or Tonalztics of Ralos special attack to reduce Muspah's defence and speed up kill times.

Assuming a successful defence-reducing special attack has landed, a Scythe of Vitur can provide comparable damage to best-in-slot Ranged and Magic options. However, the reliance on this can make it a less effective option, and a ranged swap is still strongly recommended for Muspah's prayer shield and during the teleportation phase.

Mastering the step-back method in Muspah's melee phase is functionally required for this method.

tactics.heading: Overview
tactics.text: After completion of Secrets of the North, a stronger version of the Strange Creature can be fought again in the form of a Phantom Muspah (aka, "Muspah").

tactics.heading: Requirements
tactics.text: • Completion of Quest Secrets of the North to access the Ghorrock Dungeon

tactics.heading: Suggested skills
tactics.text:
• 85+ Ranged
• 85+ Magic (if using magic)
• 75+ Defence
• 74+ Prayer for Rigour (77+ for Augury)
• 82+ Construction for Ornate rejuvenation pool (with boost) or completion of the elite Desert diary for Desert Amulet 4
• 81+ Herblore for Surge potions (optional)

tactics.heading: Transportation
tactics.text:
The quickest methods of reaching Weiss, where the Phantom Muspah resides, are:
• Using the ring of shadows to teleport to Ghorrock Dungeon. Requires completion of Desert Treasure II - The Fallen Empire and the frozen tablet, obtained from Duke Sucellus.
• Using an icy basalt. Go through the gap in the fence.
• Using the Weiss teleport in the portal chamber or portal nexus of a player-owned house.
• Using Larry's boat north-east of Rellekka and sailing to Weiss from there. Fairy ring code DKS is the closest teleport to Larry's boat.
Once in Weiss, enter the salt mine (accessible from the staircase in Snowflake and My Arm's hut) and go deeper into the cave to enter the Ghorrock Dungeon. Then, run south.

tactics.heading: Forms
tactics.text:
Throughout the fight, the Phantom Muspah will switch forms after taking 100 damage in the Ranged form (barring the teleport attack) or 80 damage in the Melee form. After switching forms for the first time, it must also take damage at least four times before it can switch again. Thrall damage does not count towards these damage thresholds or hits, with the exception of the final stand transformation when the boss reaches ≤127 hitpoints.

During transformations, Muspah will slam the ground and spawn spikes around the arena, with a spike always appearing on the player's current position. Standing on a spike will knock the player back to a clear tile and heal the boss for ~75% of the damage dealt.

Muspah's defence can be reduced down to 125. The defence reduction will preserve between phases until the shielded phase, where Muspah's defence resets to 200.

tactics.heading: Ranged
tactics.text:
Muspah's Ranged form will attack with ranged, occasionally magic, and has a significantly lower ranged defence bonus compared to its magic defence bonus.

Ranged attacks are more common and calculated on attack start, therefore Protect from Missiles should remain active by default. This can deal up to 61 damage.

Occasionally, Muspah will charge up for a Magic attack, appearing to stand up and charge a purple orb before launching it at the player. It is imperative to swap to Protect from Magic immediately upon seeing this animation, as failing to do so can result in taking up to 72 damage. This will also apply corruption onto the player.

Unlike the other attacks, using Protect from Magic while the projectile is in transit will reduce a significant amount of damage, but the player will still be inflicted corruption.

Corruption

Taking damage from the Magic attack will also apply corruption onto the player that drains 3, 6, and 9 prayer points every 6 seconds, for a total of 18 prayer points over the course of 18 seconds. Players can cast Ward of Arceuus to become temporarily immune to being corrupted, or to nullify its effect after the fact. Ward of Arceuus is cheaper than a dose of Super restore, but 1 additional inventory spot for runes will take up more inventory per use unless a player is hit by 8 or more corruption effects per trip.

tactics.heading: Melee
tactics.text:
Muspah's Melee form will deal significantly increased melee damage the longer it stays still. It is imperative to maintain distance at all times and to not allow Muspah to chain melee hits. Muspah's melee hit can deal up to 34 damage. Muspah has a significantly lower magic defence bonus in this form compared to its ranged defence bonuses.

Easiest method to combat this form is to freeze Muspah with ice spells and damaging it from distance. For lower-level players who are struggling to freeze it, Muspah can be kited and attacked with ranged or magic to avoid damage from its melee form, similar to kiting Commander Zilyana. However, due to the Muspah’s larger size, an “octagon” run pattern works better than running in a square.

Players can get hit by Muspah and still avoid damage from melee attack entirely if praying protect from melee and Muspah was chasing one tick before the intended attack tick. This led to what is known as the step-back method, which involves moving away from the boss one tick before the intended attack. Below is a breakdown of events on each tick of a step-back method being executed during Muspah's 5-tick melee cycle.

  Tick 0: Muspah attacks player
  Tick 1: hitsplat fades
  Tick 2: nothing
  Tick 3: Click to step 1 tile away
  Tick 4: Player moves
  Tick 5: Muspah will chase and attack the player same tick, for 0 damage if protect from melee is active.
Note: With 3-, 4-, and 6-tick weapons, player needs to sometimes move 2 tiles away (instead of 1) a tick earlier to not lose any ticks attacking.

tactics.heading: Shielded
tactics.text: Muspah's Shielded form is a reinforced Ranged form that is immune to all regular sources of damage. This reinforced form reverts back to the normal Ranged form when the prayer shield is removed. Prayer-draining attacks such as Smite, Corruption spells, and enchanted sapphire bolts will drain the shield faster. Entering this form also ends an active homing spikes special attack, which otherwise lasts .

tactics.heading: Fight overview
tactics.text:
The Phantom Muspah can spawn in ranged or melee form, and will trigger special attacks at 75% and 50% health. Ranged spawns will trigger Lightning clouds at 75%, melee spawns will trigger homing spikes at 75%. The unused special will always occur at 50% health.

• Players may deal large hits at the end of a ranged form, which will count towards ending the melee form.
• Hitting Muspah below 637 HP before hitting under 650 HP prevents Muspah from entering ranged form before his lightning cloud special attack. This allows you a full 100 damage against range form instead of switching to melee immediately after.
• Large amounts of damage dealt during the lightning cloud special attack can potentially skip the entirety of the final melee phase.
• Lightning Clouds - Muspah will rapidly teleport around the arena and spawn lightning clouds that travel across the area.
  • Getting hit by a cloud will deal up to 20 damage, though they can be avoided by standing on a specific tile, provided with the button above. Players should avoid standing on this tile until the attack occurs, so that spikes aren't protruding on it.
  • Muspah will always appear to the north-east when the move is finished.
  • Muspah has combat stats equal to Range form, and can be attacked during this phase.
  • Damage dealt during this phase does not count towards the damage threshold for a form swap.
• Homing Spikes - The Phantom Muspah will slam the ground, causing 2-4 spikes to home in on the player.
  • Players can stand behind hardened spikes to avoid the homing spikes from reaching them if there's more than one spike grouped together.
  • The spikes move 1 tile per 2 ticks, do not move diagonally, and cannot pass through idle spikes.
  • After , the spikes harden and stop moving.
  • Spikes that are directly adjacent to the player and under the Phantom Muspah will never be chosen to home in on the player.

tactics.heading: Shielded phase
tactics.text:
Upon reaching less than 127 health, Muspah will teleport to the centre of the arena and unleash a massive shockwave that engulfs the entire arena. Players must stand behind a spike to avoid the attack, or it will deal up to 80 damage and the subsequent corruption will drain more prayer points compared to its magic attack. Players can place spikes on 8 specific tiles (also provided with the above button) to block the shockwave most efficiently. Spikes being on all 8 tiles is unlikely, but would completely negate a shockwave. Once Muspah finishes the attack, it will change into its shielded form, activating a prayer shield and Soul Split, as well as increasing the max hit and accuracy of its attacks.

The prayer shield has 75 health, and is drained by 2 after each attack. The Phantom Muspah will also heal itself for 50% of the damage inflicted, rounded down to the nearest whole number; e.g., a hit of 23 will cause it to heal 11 health. The player can further speed up the drain by using various prayer-draining methods, such as the Smite prayer or having a corruption spell active. If using a corruption spell it is recommended to activate Mark of Darkness first as it increases the effectiveness of corruption spells.

Using a crossbow with enchanted sapphire bolts or enchanted sapphire dragon bolts is highly recommended, as they have a 25% chance (27.5% with completion of the Hard Kandarin Diary) to activate their special effect against the prayer shield, draining around 33 prayer from it.

To successfully use Smite, players should avoid lining up their attacks with Muspah's ranged or magic attacks. Players can utilise the following five-tick cycle to determine when they can use Smite:

• Tick 1: Muspah's ranged attack damage is calculated (Protect from Ranged must be active on this tick to reduce damage)
• Tick 2: Empty (can use Smite)
• Tick 3: Empty (can use Smite)
• Tick 4: Muspah's magic attack damage is calculated (Protect from Magic must be active on this tick to avoid damage)
• Tick 5: Empty (can use Smite)

If the player is using a weapon with a five-tick attack speed, such as a crossbow on rapid, attacking Muspah on the first possible tick of the shielded phase will ensure that the player always attacks on Tick 2 of the above cycle, allowing them to flick Smite consistently. If players find themselves attacking on Tick 1 or Tick 4 of the cycle, it is advisable to delay their next attack by one tick to offset their attacks.

Note that because this attack cycle is one tick faster than in previous phases, there is one less tick between a magic attack landing and the next ranged attack being calculated. As a result, players should be prepared to switch prayers quickly after a magic projectile hits them.

Once the shield is depleted, Muspah will return to its ranged form—though still with a five-tick attack speed—and create a large number of spikes (including one on the player's position) before resuming combat as normal. The spikes will emerge every four attacks and cover more tiles, growing from existing clusters of spikes.

tactics.heading: Shield Skip
tactics.text:
For players attempting Phantom Muspah Speed-Runner, it is possible to bypass the shielded phase entirely. If Muspah's health reaches zero before the shield is applied, the shield phase is cancelled and Muspah instead restores 1 health. [Youtube]

To succeed in a shield skip:

• There is a 5-tick vulnerability between Muspah's teleport and shield application. 3-tick and 4-tick weapons can deliver two attacks in this timeframe.
• When Muspah teleports to the middle, you must be standing within 1-2 tiles of Muspah's 5x5 to prevent delays on ranged weapon damage [Youtube].
• Spam click to attack (Clicking before vulnerability will be lost, and will not cause a delayed attack at first vulnerability)
• Your first attack will land before the shockwave
• Your second and final attack will come after the shockwave
• If Muspah is at 0 Health pending a successful shield skip, any further damage will fail the shield skip (ex: Thralls).
• If successful, Muspah will not enter the shield phase, but exit with 1 health to be killed easily.

This skip requires 2 or 3 lucky hits, and is therefore very luck dependent.

• The hit which brings Muspah below 127 health is the most critical. If a player is unlucky and hits Muspah from 135 to 126, players must deal a full 126 damage in the hits to follow. Oppositely, if a player is lucky and hits 80 damage from 130 health down to 50, the player has two hits to deal only 50 damage.
• The first hit after Muspah teleports.
• If hit 2 did not bring Muspah to 0 health, the hit following the shockwave must do so.

options.text: Obligator > Scythe of Vitur > Inquisitor's mace
Bandos chestplate / Blood Moon chestplate / Fighter torso
Sanguinesti staff > Trident of the Swamp

gearNotes.heading: Equipment
gearNotes.text:
Upgrades to melee gear should be prioritised over magic upgrades, due to the emphasis on melee combat. Less experienced players can substitute some magic gear for extra supplies.

As the Totems possess no stats, magic accuracy is not beneficial. Prioritise adding as many magic damage switches as possible, as all magic damage is increased significantly.

• Note that Phosani's Nightmare is not undead, therefore items such as Salve amulet will have no effect on her.
• Although the Scythe of Vitur can deal more damage, it is less accurate and requires charges ( per attack), which increases supply costs.
  • The Inquisitor's mace has a similar damage output when worn alongside Inquisitor's armour, and does not require charges. With a high enough strength bonus from other item slots, the player can potentially negate the need to bring a strong two-handed crush weapon to one-shot parasites.
  • Overall, it is up to the player to decide which weapon they prefer; the scythe is more consistent for speed-based Combat Achievements.
• Aether runes as a combination of soul and cosmic runes. If not using, bring soul runes on the side.
• The crimson kisten has the strongest special attack for boss damage. The granite maul is an alternative budget-friendly option if using Inquisitor's armour, as long as the player is comfortable swapping to it and using its special attacks in between regular weapon hits.
• The Hallowfell (on crush) is the best weapon to kill Husks and Parasites. There is a 1/6 chance husks can spawn front to back requiring 2 hits to kill. In this situation, a Ham joint to hit the rear husk, then the hallowfell to hit nightmare with splash damage to the DDed husk can be used. In regards to the parasite, try to have the nightmare and parasite near each other, so that the splash damage hitting the parasite damages nightmare.
• An elder maul or godsword (on crush) can be used to kill parasites in one hit. With high enough strength bonus, the mace is also capable of this, but it is less convenient to do a full melee switch when the parasite spawns on pillar phase. Saradomin godsword can double as a special attack weapon and helping cover some mistakes due to guaranteed max hits on crush, additionally including its special attack.
• If using a powered staff for totems, an imbued or saturated heart should be used. The heart should not be brought if using Fire Surge.
• If using thralls, the ghostly thrall should be summoned as they benefit from doubled damage against totems. Focus on one totem at a time, otherwise the thrall will waste a lot of time moving between them.
• For killing the sleepwalkers, a weapon with long range, fast attack speed and fast projectile speed is highly recommended. Blisterwood stakes are cheaper and more efficient at sleepwalker clearing than a toxic blowpipe, sharing the same attack speed but with +1 range. These require partial completion of The Blood Moon Rises to the point where the player learns how to make them. Alternatively, the Eye of Ayak has the same attack speed and range, and doubles as an effective weapon for charging the totems.
• An amulet of blood fury can be useful for learners, but shouldn't be relied on, due to extremely high damage from off-prayer hits or special attacks.
• A surge potion can be used for additional special attacks throughout the fight. Following changes on 25 June 2025, the player will not be able to maintain 100% special attack energy for the final phase when using special attacks readily; as such, a surge potion helps offset some of this.
• If using a Harmonised Nightmare Staff casting fire surge, with an elemental amulet and tome of fire, the max hit of 118 can be achieved with a magic damage bonus of only 35%. This allows you to leave either the magus ring or imbued god cape behind, saving an inventory space/swap and the extra melee strength bonus will allow you to 1 hit the parasites with only a 1-way swap to an elder maul during the totem phase. However, this will prevent the use of thralls and Death Charge.

gearNotes.heading: Inventory
gearNotes.text:
While the fight has a low amount of guaranteed chip damage, the increased length caused by lower end gear can create more opportunity for mistakes.
Additionally, more than 4 parasites can spawn throughout the fight if the player is unlucky. An additional Sanfew serum is taken because of this.

tactics.heading: Overview
tactics.text:
Phosani's Nightmare is a solo boss located in the Sisterhood Sanctuary, a dungeon beneath Slepe in Morytania. It is the stronger version of the Nightmare.

Players can initiate the fight by entering the Pool of Nightmares which is located north of The Nightmare's arena on a raised area. As a solo instanced fight, players do not need to hop worlds.

Phosani's Nightmare awakens in 10 seconds upon entering the instance, compared to 30 at the original. After she is defeated, players can continue fighting her by disturbing her again.

Unlike most other bosses, players who die fighting Phosani's Nightmare are sent back outside to the Pool of Nightmares, and Sister Senga acts as an Item Retrieval Service for this purpose. Reclaims cost 60000 coins regardless of the equipment's value or amount of kills completed.

tactics.heading: Requirements
tactics.text: • Completion of Quest Priest in Peril to access Morytania.

tactics.heading: Recommendations
tactics.text:
• High combat stats. Although not required, see the skill levels below for an indication of the advised stats:
  • Level 95 Attack or higher
  • Level 95 Strength or higher
  • Level 85 Defence or higher
  • Level 95 Magic or higher
  • Level 95 Hitpoints or higher
  • Level 70 Prayer or higher
• Completion of Quest A Taste of Hope for the Drakan's Medallion, which is the quickest teleportation method.
  • Alternatively, completion of Quest Ghosts Ahoy for the ectophial, which is the second quickest teleportation method.

tactics.heading: Transportation
tactics.text:
The five quickest methods of reaching Slepe, where Phosani's Nightmare resides, are (from fastest to slowest):
• Teleporting directly to Slepe via Drakan's medallion after unlocking this teleport via Slepey tablet, which is a drop from Phosani's Nightmare.
• Teleporting to the Morytania Spider Cave with a spider cave teleport and running east to Slepe
• Teleporting to Hallowed Sepulchre using a Hallowed crystal shard, then running east to Slepe via an agility shortcut that requires 63 Agility and installing two Long ropes
• Teleporting to Ver Sinhaza via Drakan's medallion, then running north. Once players pass the small dock, run east to arrive at Slepe.
• Using the Ectophial to teleport to the Ectofuntus, then heading north to the small dock and paying Andras 10,000 coins to row to Slepe. The player will arrive at a dock just south-west of Slepe.

tactics.heading: Mechanics
tactics.text:
The fight is divided into four phases. Phases 1-3 consist of a shielded portion in which players must deal 400 damage to the boss with melee, followed by an unshielded portion in which players charge four totems in the arena's corners by dealing 200 damage to each totem with magic, followed by a set of sleepwalkers spawning. Phase 4 is a desperation phase with 150 hitpoints.

A total of 3,750 damage must be dealt across all phases. However, since totems receive double damage from magic, the effective total is 2,550.

tactics.heading: Standard attacks
tactics.text:
Unlike the normal Nightmare, praying against the attacks of Phosani's Nightmare will fully block damage. However, the attacks deal significantly increased damage in return if not protected against, with both the ranged and magic having a maximum hit of 80 and melee a maximum of 73.
• Ranged attack: Phosani's Nightmare will contort herself and shoot out projectiles toward players; having game sounds enabled will help as this attack performs a loud clicking sound per contortion. Players have 3 ticks (1.8s) to react with Protect from Missiles.
• Magic attack: Phosani's Nightmare will flail to the side surrounding herself with pink flower petals, then spin back shooting the petals toward players. Players have 3 ticks (1.8s) to react with Protect from Magic.
• Melee attack: Phosani's Nightmare will charge her claws and quickly scrapes the area in front of her. Players have 2 ticks (1.2s) to react with Protect from Melee. This attack will always hit regardless of the player's defensive bonuses if not protected against. The attack can also be avoided by walking one tile away from her just before the claws rise up.
The boss does not have trample damage, so it is safe to stand underneath her except during her Grasping Claws special attack.

tactics.heading: Special attacks
tactics.text:
Phosani's Nightmare will use one of her special attacks every few standard attacks.

The following special attacks are used randomly throughout all phases.
• Grasping Claws: Phosani's Nightmare will spawn a large black portal underneath her, and many more small portals around the player. After 3 ticks, claws burst out of each portal, dealing 50-65 damage if the player is standing on one. All the tiles under the boss except the corners will also deal the same damage when the claws burst out.
• Curse: A pink glow fills the player's screen and protection prayers are shuffled to the right. Using Protect from Melee will instead activate Protect from Magic, Protect from Magic activates Protect from Missiles, and Protect from Missiles activates Protect from Melee. After 5 attacks, the curse is lifted.
• Surge: Phosani's Nightmare will teleport to one of the four edges of the room, then immediately surge across to the opposite side in the direction she is facing, dealing up to ~80 damage if caught in her path. Move out of the way to avoid taking damage.
Each phase will feature three of the remaining special attacks. This will always consist of one "spawn" (husk or parasite), one paired with Grasping Claws (Corpse Flowers or Spores), and one miscellaneous special attack (Curse or Surge). Below are four possible sets of special attacks:

• A1: Spore/Husks/Curse
• A2: Spore/Husks/Surge
• B1: Flowers/Parasite/Curse
• B2: Flowers/Parasite/Surge

The first phase picks a random set (A or B), then every following phase alternates between the A and B sets, but randomly picks between 1 and 2. For example, a special attack set will go as follows: A1, B2, A2. The Nightmare will expend all special attacks first before she may use them again, and both the spawning mechanic and claw-accompanying mechanic cannot be used in consecutive phases.
• Husks: Two husks spawn next to the player. The player will be frozen in place until the husks are killed. The blue, skinny husk uses magic attacks, while the green, bulky husk uses ranged attacks.
  • The husks have 20 hitpoints, can hit up to 26, and players will always max hit on them when using the crush attack style.
  • Phosani's Nightmare will not spawn Grasping Claws portals under players frozen by the husks. However, if the player is under Phosani's Nightmare while frozen by husks, they will still take damage.
  • An advanced tactic to avoid all damage from husks is to kill the ranged husk first during Phases 1 and 2. The magic husk will hit before the Nightmare does, whereas the ranged husk will hit on the same tick as the Nightmare. During Phase 3, if the Nightmare uses melee, the magic husk must be killed first, as damage will register on the same tick.
• Spores: Mushrooms spawn around the arena. Standing within 1 tile of one will cause it to explode, causing the player to become weary; their run is disabled, their attack speed is lowered by 2 ticks, and every yawn will drain 6 prayer points.
  • While the mushrooms are present, Phosani's Nightmare will constantly use Grasping Claws instead of auto-attacking.
• Corpse Flowers: The room is divided into four quadrants with lines of flowers. The quadrant between the lines of white/pink flowers is safe, while the other quadrants (indicated by black/red berries) are dangerous. The dangerous quadrants cause rapid damage, heal the boss, and cause any damage to the boss to heal her further.
  • While the flowers are present, Phosani's Nightmare will constantly use Grasping Claws instead of auto-attacking.
• Parasites: Phosani's Nightmare impregnates the player with a parasite. After ~18 ticks (10.8s), it will grow and burst out of the player, dealing massive damage, and will then begin healing Phosani's Nightmare or a totem until killed.
  • Drink a dose of Sanfew serum or Relicym's balm (can also be done by clicking the HP orb) before it emerges to weaken the parasite and greatly reduce the damage taken when it bursts out.
  • A weakened parasite has 55 hitpoints, and players will always max hit on it when using the crush attack style.

tactics.heading: Additional mechanics
tactics.text:
• Sleepwalkers: At the end of Phases 1-3, after the last totem is charged, Phosani's Nightmare will summon sleepwalkers that walk toward her. Two are summoned after Phase 1, three after Phase 2, and four after Phase 3.
  • Sleepwalker die instantly upon taking any damage. They should all be killed with a fast ranged or magic weapon to reduce the damage of the resulting power blast. If all are missed, the blast will always kill the player.
• Prayer Deactivation: During Phase 3, Phosani's Nightmare will deactivate the player's protection prayer if they have the correct prayer active before the attack animation starts, making it critical to react to every auto-attack.
• Desperation Phase: After the final set of four sleepwalkers, Phosani's Nightmare begins Phase 4. She will heal 150 health and constantly use Grasping Claws instead of auto-attacking while sleepwalkers continually walk towards her. Each sleepwalker that reaches her deals 15 damage to the player. Simply ignore the sleepwalkers and attack the boss while dodging portals; special attacks are useful to finish the phase quickly.

tactics.heading: Fight overview
tactics.text:
Before heading to the boss, eat an anglerfish to overheal. If the player does not have the teleport to the Sisterhood Sanctuary with Drakan's medallion (via slepey tablet, acquired from the boss), it is required that players sip a stamina potion before leaving the bank, as their run energy will deplete before even reaching the sanctuary. If the player has the teleport unlocked, a stamina dose is not necessary.

The fight plays out very similarly to the original, though much faster. Phosani's Nightmare is significantly more punishing when a mistake is made, as its auto-attacks have the capability to kill players in two hits. Food that can heal 22 (ideally anglerfish for its overhealing capability) is recommended for mistakes and chip damage taken during the fight. Unlike the original, an amulet of blood fury is not mandatory, as an ideal kill will only see minor chip damage, dealt through phase transitions and parasites. Generally without a Saradomin godsword, up to three mistakes are allowed, after which the fourth one will likely kill the player when accounting for the best loadout.

When using a weapon on its crush setting, the player will be guaranteed a maximum hit on both husks and weakened parasites. When using a 5-tick or slower weapon such as a Scythe of Vitur, a goblin paint cannon or ham joint swap is generally encouraged due to their 3-tick attack speed. If using a 4-tick weapon such as an Inquisitor's mace, this is not necessary. For parasites, the player must have a minimum of 118 Strength, a strength bonus of 160 or more and Piety in order to one-hit weakened parasites. A godsword swap requires piety and a four-way swap of the weapon, cape, amulet and gloves. If the parasite is not weakened, the damage it deals to the player will be added onto its base health, and the player will not be able to land maximum hits on it even with crush weapons. An elder maul will not need any swaps, but the strength level and piety must be maintained. Alternatively, a hallowfell can kill all three, however this can occasionally require luring in order for it to hit them and the Nightmare at the same time.

Learning players will likely struggle against the Grasping Claws, as a late reaction by even a tick will deal heavy damage, and it also has the capability to kill players in two hits. It is important to quickly locate safe tiles; learners should prioritise dodging the pools over attacking the boss, as a few mistakes will quickly kill the player. A more advanced strategy is to "corner rift"; this method requires the player to stand underneath the Nightmare by the corners of her collision box, as standing anywhere else will result in damage. The player must quickly step out of the boss before the next set of pools form, or one will form in the corner. This allows players to maintain a cadence while minimising tick loss from not attacking the boss.

Before using Flower Power or Spores, the Nightmare will have a slight delay before actually using the attack alongside Grasping Claws. She will always teleport to the centre of the arena when performing these attacks.

As with the original fight, there are three iterations of Flower Power. Assuming she is not moved from the centre, two of these layouts will not require the player to move her. Some particular layouts will have spores diagonally across from her, which requires luring her away from the centre as they will severely restrict movement. If the player is tick perfect and moves as soon as the spores spawn, the boss can be lured to corner rift. It is usually more common to have late reactions, causing the boss to move one tile from the centre; while this does not allow corner rifting, it does give ample space to dodge claws.

At the end of each phase, the Nightmare will spawn a corresponding amount of sleepwalkers while charging up an attack. This attack will always deal 149 damage if no sleepwalkers are killed. Killing a sleepwalker will reduce the damage appropriately to the amount of sleepwalkers present; e.g with 4 sleepwalkers, each sleepwalker killed will reduce the blast damage by 36. If all sleepwalkers are killed before they reach the boss, the blast will deal 5 damage instead. Sleepwalker control can be dealt with using blisterwood stakes or a toxic blowpipe on the rapid style, but quick reactions must be maintained to avoid leaks.

tactics.heading: Phases 1-2
tactics.text:
The first two phases are very much like the regular encounter except the special attacks can be used randomly in any of these phases.

As the player progresses through the phases, sleepwalkers will spawn in to reach the Nightmare. Two will spawn at the end of phase 1 and an additional will spawn at the end of the phase.

tactics.heading: Phase 3
tactics.text:
Phosani's Nightmare will deactivate the player's protection prayers as soon as she starts her attack animation. Since the attacks have a slight delay and only deal damage upon being launched, this is mostly to keep players vigilant. She will also have a much higher chance of using melee attacks during this time, so players should prioritise activating Protect from Melee (or Ranged if Curse is active).

To avoid damage from husks during the phase when not using a Hallowfell, players should not have any overhead prayers active before they appear. Once the husks appear, pray magic, as both the Nightmare and the magic husk will attack on the same tick (although the magic husk will hit first). If the player prays against magic and the Nightmare uses a magic attack, the magic husk will likely hit the player. Even if the Nightmare uses melee, players can still flick against all three enemies at once by praying against magic, then melee and finally ranged within 1 tick of each other from the first prayer.

For sleepwalker control in this phase, players using a short ranged weapon like blisterwood stakes should stand next to one corner of the arena, as a sleepwalker is guaranteed to spawn on either side of the pillar. If using a bow, stand in the middle. Unlike the previous phase, there is a slight delay before the sleepwalkers start moving. In order to avoid damage from sleepwalkers, the player must kill at least two sleepwalkers before this delay lifts.

tactics.heading: Desperation phase
tactics.text:
Phosani's Nightmare will survive the final blast, and teleport to the centre of the arena. Lashing out to survive, she will unleash a desperate last stand by indefinitely using Grasping Claws, while sleepwalkers continuously spawn from the edges of the arena. Mastering the corner rifting technique will make this phase less hectic.

Unlike the previous sleepwalkers, these will only deal 15 damage upon reaching the Nightmare and has a 1-tick delay; damage is indicated when pink petals fall on the player. The first sleepwalker that spawns will deal damage ~20 ticks after spawning, allowing for four attacks with a four or five-tick weapon before this occurs. Focusing on ending the fight instead of dealing with the sleepwalkers is crucial.

Before the phase starts, the player should fully restore their health, ensure their melee stats are boosted, and their special attack energy is full. Although not necessary, standing underneath the boss before the phase starts will usually allow the player to dodge the first set of rifts. Immediately dump special attacks on the Nightmare to quickly damage her, if available. Redemption, although not needed, can be very useful in this phase if low on supplies or if the phase takes longer than usual.

The strongest special attack weapon to use is the crimson kisten, as it is very likely to hit and generally deals more damage on average compared to a voidwaker. Voidwaker is still strong for players who don't have a kisten, due to its guaranteed accuracy. If neither are available, dragon claws can perform relatively well despite the boss's high Slash defence, and finally, the ornate granite maul. While the maul should be better than dragon claws, it does require proper timing to avoid unnecessary tick delay.

tactics.heading: Hallowfell
tactics.text: Utilizing the Hallowfell to its full potential takes some planning to avoid the 1/6 bad husk spawn and 1/4 bad parasite spawn chances. The same trick will work for both situations; when standing next to a wall or against a corner, she cannot spawn either husk or parasite in a location that the Hallowfell will fail to provide area-of-effect damage. However, it is important to note that to effectively move the boss the player needs to be moving in between attacks or waiting for Surge, as both the magic and ranged auto-attacks have a rather lengthy animation that roots her in place.

tactics.heading: Tips and tricks
tactics.text:
• Before starting a trip, equipping Blisterwood stakes and the Book of the Dead can free up an inventory slot (if the player is using a 2-handed weapon), allowing for an extra piece of food or potion to be carried into the fight.
• During the last Grasping Claws after a Spore special attack, the rifts will never spawn on where a spore was, so the player can safely move to one of those tiles without the concern of being hit.
• Be sure to have 100% special attack energy at the start of the final phase, as it is imperative to kill the boss quickly during this phase.
• With lightbearer and double Death Charge (unlocked by reading the rite of vile transference from Yama), the player can spec twice per shield phase and twice in enrage.
• Keep in mind that in order to one-hit both husks and parasites, your max hit has to equal or be above their health (20 and 55 HP respectively). In order to guarantee a one-hit kill, make sure you are wearing your melee gear, praying Piety, and boosted by your combat potion. In this fashion, a Goblin paint cannon or Ham joint will not be able to kill the parasite seeing as the max hit will never be above 30. For this reason, a higher-hitting weapon must be used for the parasite.
  • Save enough special attack energy to one-hit parasites with a dragon mace or saradomin godsword with minimum gear, also helpful for completing Crush Hour Combat Achievement.
• Defence-reducing attacks can lower the boss's Defence level from 150 to a minimum of 120, and she recovers drained levels every 3 seconds (5 ticks) instead of every minute. Thus, she will always recover any drained defence levels within 90 seconds. However, because of the high crush accuracy of the dragon warhammer and elder maul, their special attacks can still be beneficial in combination with other damage-dealing specs for players with worse than entry level gear who aren't using voidwaker.
  • When using this strategy, it's best to wait until 100% special attack energy before reducing her Defence, ideally before a husk or parasite special so that Death Charge can allow for additional specials while her defence is lowered. Surge potions can also be used for extra specs during this window, but are best used only if the 5-minute cooldown between doses will expire before her desperation phase.

gearNotes.heading: Equipment
gearNotes.text:
Always minimise your risk in the Wilderness by limiting the amount of valuable items you bring to three (or four with the Protect Item) - for example a, good weapon along with some body and leg armour, such as black or blessed dragonhide - in addition to wearing a bracelet of ethereum and bringing a means of teleportation.

• As revenants have very high accuracy, the bracelet of ethereum is highly recommended when battling them.
• The amulet of avarice is the most powerful amulet for killing revenants, giving the same bonuses as a Salve amulet(ei) and a amulet of glory, but makes the player skulled until unequipped (and for 20 minutes thereafter), increasing your potential risk substantially and making yourself a target for player killers. However, you will receive many of the revenants' drops in noted form, along with an increased chance to roll on the drop table for a Wilderness weapon or additional amulet of avarice due to being constantly skulled. The decision whether or not to use this item should not be taken lightly.
  • If you do not possess or do not wish to use an amulet of avarice, Revenants are considered undead creatures, so the salve amulet and variants will work on them.

• The royal seed pod and any charged dragonstone jewellery are capable of teleporting non-teleblocked players to safety at level 30 Wilderness or below. The seed pod is a good option, as it is a one-click teleport and can be cheaply re-obtained, allowing an observant player to easily escape player killers. Since dying is highly probable, it is recommended to have spare bracelets, amulets and ether in the bank. A bracelet with 50 ether will suffice as the bracelet and its ether is always lost upon death and more can be obtained than what is consumed while fighting revenants.

• Any of the Wilderness weapons will drastically increase your kills per hour, but requires 1,000 ether to charge, plus additional ether for usage. No more than 500 is necessary per trip for a total of 1,500 ether. On death, the weapon will have to be recharged and reloaded. See the equipment section below for cheaper alternatives, albeit less kills and less profit.
• Appropriate Prayer switching, black dragonhide armour and Dinh's bulwark can be used to protect the player by lowering the accuracy of player killers, who bring teleblocks and freezes.
• Alternatively, monk's robes offer cheap prayer bonuses at the cost of less defensive and offensive (if using ranged) bonuses.
• Players can use the Toggle option on the bracelet of ethereum to make it so dropped ether is automatically added to the bracelet.
This setup aims to maximise DPS against the revenants while miminizing risk. Ranged can usually offer better dps against revenants with less gear used, and d'hide conveniently adds ranged accuracy while giving magic defence. However, you will be more vulnerable to incoming melee and ranged attacks from PKers without a shield.

gearNotes.heading: Inventory
gearNotes.text: Melee is generally less damage than ranged setups, but is tankier against revenants and PKers. You gain additional defence and utility from melee gear such as the serpentine helm and dragonfire shield.

gearNotes.heading: Inventory
gearNotes.text: Mage is not commonly used due to its average dps and poor defensive bonuses. However, the accursed sceptre will perform better than most other ranged or melee setups without their respective Wilderness weapons.

gearNotes.heading: Inventory
gearNotes.text:
This setup uses a ranged tank setup which aims to prioritise survivability with slightly increased risk, while maintaining high dps. This is achieved via a clever use of protected items with the most benefit, alongside cheap gear that provides a lot of defensive stats. This setup is mostly for higher levels with more to spend, but will work for anybody with high hitpoints and relatively high defence and magic levels. The risk is still extremely low due to the low cost of the tank items and the high chance of surviving.

Use the agility shortcuts and prioritise teleporting. If teleblocked, focus on running and eating. Ignore prayer switches but keep prayer points topped up. Summer pies can help reach the level requirement for the agility shortcuts.

To get there, teleport using the Revenant cave teleport scroll which leads to Revenant dragons. Ensure you have ether in your Bracelet of ethereum and have it toggled to collect ether.

• Never skull, use skull prevention.
• Always use Protect from Magic and Protect item. Switch from offensive ranged prayers to Augury when attacked. This is to avoid a full teleblock. You can survive a half teleblock quite easily even from somebody in max. It's also because the build is centred around providing bulk against melee/ranged so camping Protect from Magic and Augury prevents spells from landing.
• When attacked, switch to the tank legs, phoenix necklace and Dinh's bulwark. Often pkers will give up at this point.
• Check that you are always protecting your expensive items. For your fourth, it can help to bring a cheaper +1 as it's possible to get smited. But staying in singles should avoid this if you're vigilant.
• If you don't have fortified Masori, you can add Echo boots/Guardian boots alongside Blessed body or Karil's leathertop. Although it's usually not worth it to take Karil's top/skirt because the cost is not worth the added risk. If the enemy is catching a lot of freezes, you can add an Imbued god cape alongside a Blessed body.

The core items for this strategy are Masori body (f), Barrow's helm, Barrow's legs, Dinh's bulwark, Salve amulet(ei), Bracelet of ethereum, and Webweaver bow. If you have Avernic treads (max), use these and replace your Ring of suffering. If in need of melee defence, replace it with a Steel ring, or use a Ring of shadows for more Magic defence and ranged accuracy. A Granite ring works for the budget option, and adds ranged defence, but the Explorer's ring provides much more utility.

gearNotes.heading: Inventory
gearNotes.text:
• Take 6-8 Saradomin brews and a Sanfew serum for in case the player is attacked by a pker using venom.
• Summer pies can be used if the boost takes you to 75 agility, this also provides run energy.
• A Guthix rest or two can help restore run energy and provide delay-free healing for facing maledictus without it affecting your ranged level. These also lower venom.
• A Barrows gloves switch is worth it if the player has many Saradomin brews for the defensive stats alone.
• Stamina potions simply aren't necessary at higher agility levels, especially if the player has Summer pies and/or Guthix rest. The player can consider taking the Explorer's ring as a backup for run energy, as this also provides alchs, although this is rarely needed.
When a freeze is about to finish, the player can switch back to d'hide chaps before running to encourage splashing.

Soloing the maledictus is possible, though this will be the only time where you are truly vulnerable. Be very careful, as using protect from ranged against the maledictus opens you up to a full teleblock. Additionally, players will expend a lot of food to kill the maledictus. It can take at least 4 brews, and often even more than that. This is why it is recommended to take an excessive amount of brews if planning to kill a maledictus. A Ranging potion can help to top up your ranged level. Saving food when killing the boss can help retain the ability to combo eat against a pker.

Regardless of your inventory setup, you should have a teleportation item capable of bringing you to safety at or below level 30 Wilderness, such as a royal seed pod or charged dragonstone jewellery, in addition to the following:

• Dinh's bulwark (optional, but helps with tanking)
• Phoenix necklace (optional, for switching with Dinh's and emergency healing whilst tanking)
• A Ranging potion (if ranging)
• A Super combat/Super set (if melee)
• A Saturated heart or Forgotten brew (if maging)
• 2-5 Blighted super restore
• Stamina potion (optional)
• Looting bag
• Best food (sharks or better)
• Combination food, such as cooked karambwan
• 3-4 Saradomin brews for additional combo healing

tactics.heading: Overview
tactics.text:
Revenants are monsters that can be found in the Revenant Caves, which are located in singles-plus combat Wilderness. They have generous drop tables, consisting of valuable rewards, and are found within level 17-40 Wilderness in the Revenant Caves.

Warning: The entire area is within the Wilderness. Players will be able to attack you here and the area is a rather popular one to do so.

tactics.heading: Suggested skills
tactics.text:
• 60+ Attack
• 60+ Strength
• 40+ Defence
• 60+ Ranged
• 45+ Prayer (Protect from Magic, 40+ Protect from Missiles, 43+ Protect from Melee, 70+ Piety, Protect Item)
• 89+ Agility (optional, strongly recommended)

tactics.heading: Transportation
tactics.text:
• Walking west from Ferox Enclave, which can be reached via a ring of dueling or the Minigame teleport to Last Man Standing.
• Using a burning amulet, teleport to either outside the Lava Maze or the Bandit Camp.
• Use the Wilderness obelisks to teleport to the level 35 obelisk, before running north to find the high levelled entrance.
• With 57 Woodcutting, one can make a waka canoe to head into the Wilderness. Upon arriving, run north-west to the high levelled entrance.
• Teleporting to the level 27 obelisk and running east, leading to a chasm down to drop players in the middle of the caves. This is a one way entrance.
• A Revenant cave teleport brings you directly to any entrance of your choice; which entrance it goes to can be changed using the scroll's "Config" option.

Note: Without 75 Agility, (70 with a Summer pie, or 72 with an Agility Potion) using the lower levelled entrances are recommended, as the higher end of the cave has limited escape options without the level 75 and 89 Agility shortcuts. The level 89 shortcut is a good escape route for players if their aggressor lacks the Agility needed to cross it. The shortcuts do make the player vulnerable as they navigate it for a few seconds however.

tactics.heading: Mechanics
tactics.text:
Revenants use all three forms of attack. Their attacks have very high accuracy and will often deal high damage. They will react to a player's overhead prayers and defensive bonuses. By default, all revenants attack with Magic, but can quickly adapt based on the player's defensive bonuses and prayers.

A revenant's magic attack, which resembles a weaker form of Ice Barrage, can momentarily freeze the player for several seconds and hits up to nine other players on the same tile as their target. Revenants are also capable of healing themselves whenever their health falls below 50%. The exact healing mechanics are as follows:

• They recover 20 hitpoints each time they heal. This disregards their maximum hitpoints (e.g. a revenant imp will heal fully).
• They have a cooldown that begins once they have healed, preventing them from healing again for 15 ticks (9 seconds).
• They are guaranteed a heal whenever they attack while they're below half HP, so long as their heal is ready and not on cooldown.
• They can only heal themselves a total of 8-25 times before being unable to heal again - it being random (probability being uniform throughout).

To prevent most of a revenant's damage and aggression, a charged bracelet of ethereum must be worn at all times. The bracelet is charged by revenant ethers, which all revenants are guaranteed to drop. For each attack the revenant does, its damage is reduced by 75% by a charged bracelet, with each attack consuming one charge. Note that it will not prevent the freezing capability of a revenant's magic attacks. The bracelet is always lost upon death. If a bracelet is taken, it is only recommended to give it 100 charges as it automatically recharges itself with dropped ether.

tactics.heading: Strategy
tactics.text:
Revenants are relatively straightforward to kill, dealing minor amounts of damage and respawning quickly. Most of the strategy for revenants is deciding your risk tolerance with Pkers and your equipment. There are various levels of revenants across the caves, each with varying pros and cons. Generally, higher level revenants are more profitable yet have higher traffic from Pkers.

Revenants below level 30 Wilderness include a single hellhound, two imps, goblins, hobgoblins and demons, three pyrefiends, and four orks, while those above level 30 Wilderness consist of a single pyrefiend and hellhound, two imps, cyclopes, demons, dark beasts, knights and dragons. The dark beasts can be lured and fought in level 30 Wilderness, allowing players to maximise profits and safety at the same time, although they will have to loot the drops in level 31 Wilderness if not luring or telegrabbing them.

Revenant dragons and revenant knights are difficult to kill without a revenant weapon, are in a highly trafficked player killer zone above 30 wilderness, but give the most loot per kill.

tactics.heading: Handling player killers
tactics.text:
While killing revenants can be one of the most lucrative sources of income for any player who can survive being intercepted and interrupted by player killers, it is more beneficial for higher-level players with access to better tanking equipment and stats. Some knowledge of PvP tactics is helpful (such as the ability to fight back if anti-PKing), quickly reacting to and predicting incoming attacks, using Protect from Magic when running away, and not overbrewing to increase the chance of survival. Using Barrows armour alongside Dinh's bulwark or an elysian spirit shield further increases the chance of survival; with a good defensive setup, it should be very easy to escape most player killers, with some outright not attacking due to not being worth their time.

Saradomin brews are highly recommended for escaping player killers, with super restores to counter the Magic drain. The revenants drop plenty of blighted food as a tertiary drop, which helps extend trips.

Protect from Magic and Protect Item should be used at almost all times while in the Revenant Caves to reduce the overall damage of the revenants, (magic is their most accurate style), reduce the duration of teleblock by 50%, or reduce incoming magical attacks from pkers as they most often start by attempting to freeze their target with Ice Barrage. It is generally better to bring additional Prayer potions over Prayer gear, as Prayer gear such as proselyte is weak to Magic and monk's robes offer almost no defensive bonuses.

In all but the revenant knight and dragon areas, Pkers generally use the Standard spellbook as it would be very easy to teleport from them if they were using Ancient spells. If a player has completed the Hard Wilderness Diary, they should attempt to teleport away from pkers as soon as possible to avoid getting teleblocked. If the player isn't quick enough, does not have the diary completed, or is beyond 30 Wilderness in the northern part of the dungeon, some other strategies will have to be used.

• Attempt to outrun the PKer. By bringing high magic defence gear and praying Mystic Might or Augury, they can cover lots of ground in between the PKers entangle and freeze spells if they splash. Given enough time you could be able to run to the Wilderness Ditch and escape.
• Attempt to combat the PKer. A half-teleblock only lasts 2:30. Bringing good defensive gear and a ranged weapon to retaliate with can make the PKer think twice about trying to take your loot. Making them waste time by eating or brewing down their stats can give you enough of an edge to survive a player in more powerful gear than your own. With good timing of Vengeance and a powerful special attack weapon like an Armadyl godsword or Voidwaker, some PKers can be killed outright.
• Attempt to freeze-logout. By bringing Entangles, Ice Barrages, or another way of freezing a PKer will allow one to force them into a position where they cannot reach the player with magical or ranged attacks. This can be done by freezing the PKer and then running around a corner. This breaks line of sight and allows you to wait until 10 seconds are up to log out. A much riskier option is to freeze the PKer and attempt to stand underneath their player model. This can be done when sufficient cover is too far away, but runs the risk of the PKer using mithril or adamant seeds to move from underneath you and interrupt your logout.

If arriving to the revenants through the upper entrance via burning amulet, it is recommended to use Protect from Magic to avoid being seared by any potential green dragons the player may run past. The other entrances do not have this concern.

tactics.heading: Revenant maledictus
tactics.text: While revenants are being slain by players, there is a possibility of a revenant maledictus spawning in one of several locations across the caves. If the player has no intention to fight it, it is highly recommended to leave the area as it does hefty damage and will bring extra attention to the location it spawns in. Players killing revenant hobgoblins or knights do not need to worry about the maledictus, as it will only spawn in large areas, with both of these revenants being in cramped and narrow passageways.

gearNotes.heading: Equipment
gearNotes.text:
All three styles of combat are beneficial to the fight, so balancing the best equipment available with your limited inventory space is a concern. Bring switches that have high magic attack bonuses; spells will have a chance to splash on the minions if your magic attack bonus is below the following values: 70+ magic attack bonus (39+ magic attack bonus with void).

As the Titans are primarily fought with melee, prioritise melee strength bonus. For when the Titans are out of reach of melee, bring a ranged weapon and equipment.

Additional gear switches can make the fight faster if executed correctly, but may shorten trips due to fewer supplies. Because the giants can have very high ranged defence in some parts of each phase it's better to prioritise getting high-hitting melee attacks primarily, although with slower kills, ranged equipment becomes more important.

If choosing to kill the elementals, bringing an additional staff is recommended. Despite the low inbuilt accuracy, the Twinflame staff is highly recommended due to the passive effect automatically swapping between fire and water spells.

gearNotes.heading: On Slayer task
gearNotes.text:
Each boss counts as an ice giant or fire giant task respectively. The imbued slayer helm can boost damage on task.

The only slayer master that assigns both is Vannaka, and you can optimize his blocklist to be Titans specific.

Alternatively if you only need the fire giant task, Chaeldar, Nieve and Duradel can assign them, but without the possibility of ice giants.

gearNotes.heading: Low Level / Sustain
gearNotes.text:
When fighting the Titans solo or in a duo with low end gear and stats, it may be easier to bring fewer switches and more supplies so you can kill more Titans before you have to bank. With lower damage output, it is recommended to use the standard spellbook to deal with the elementals and barriers, as their damage will add up quickly.

Using Void knight equipment or Blue Moon armour can greatly reduce the amount of gear switches required to meet the magic accuracy threshold for killing the elementals. This also makes transitioning from melee to ranged much easier for those getting familiar.
• Using ranged armour throughout the fight also has the same benefits, as melee armour gives considerably less bonuses to attack. The Eclipse atlatl, which uses melee strength for calculating its maximum hit, is particularly effective for this approach as it requires fewer compromises on melee strength and ranged accuracy.

In order to determine which gear to use, it is important to look at the magic attack bonus of the total gear chosen.
For example, choosing a twinflame staff (+12) as your magic weapon with full void (+0), amulet of fury (+10), aranea boots (+5), Imbued god cape (+15), and a dragon defender (-3) provides exactly 39 magic attack bonus.

gearNotes.heading: High Level / Resetting
gearNotes.text:
When fighting the Titans in a duo with high end gear and high stats, damage taken from elementals per kill is very low. It is possible to forego use of fire and water spells for the elementals, and rely on thralls, especially if resetting health, prayer, and special attack energy between kills at the Nardah statue or an ornate rejuvenation pool. This strategy is most effective for maximising kills-per-hour, although the gear threshold required to execute this strategy is reasonably high.

If you instead opt for standard spells to kill elementals and remove barriers, reaching a magic attack bonus of a minimum of 70 is required. The most effective switches to reach this threshold are typically magic armour and a staff, with expensive gear such as ancestral robes / virtus robes (+61) only providing a modest accuracy boost over armour such as Ahrim's equipment (+52). If using amulet of rancour (-6) or ferocious gloves (-16), swapping to occult necklace (+12) / amulet of fury (+10) and barrows gloves (+6) / tormented bracelet (+10) might be required to hit +70 magic attack bonus.
Most Titans fights start with 1–2 melee hits, then transition to a ranged phase. Melee is still used frequently in the final stages of the fight.

tactics.heading: Overview
tactics.text:
The Royal Titans are a pair of ice and fire giant bosses located in the Asgarnia Ice Dungeon: the fire giant queen Branda and the ice giant king Eldric. There are no requirements to access or fight them. They can be fought in a duo or solo.

To reach the bosses, after entering the dungeon, players must run north past the pirates and muggers, then west. Alternately, players with 60 Agility can use a shortcut directly to the west of the entrance.

tactics.heading: Recommendations
tactics.text:
• Moderate combat stats in all styles
  • Level 70 Attack or higher
  • Level 70 Strength or higher
  • Level 70 Defence or higher
  • Level 70 Ranged or higher
  • Level 75 Magic or higher for a max hit of 40 with Fire Wave and Water Wave on elementals
    • Levels below this will not be able to 1-shot elementals
  • Level 70 Hitpoints or higher
  • Level 43 Prayer for protection prayers

tactics.heading: Transportation
tactics.text:
Players can use the tunnel shortcut just west of the dungeon ladder with 60 Agility to get to the boss room faster if they don't have the giantsoul amulet yet.
• The Giantsoul amulet will teleport the player directly outside the boss room.
• The fairy ring code AIQ is south of the dungeon entrance.
• The minigame teleport to the rat pits, Port Sarim spirit tree patch, and explorer's ring are north of the dungeon entrance.
• The Rimmington house portal is north of the dungeon entrance.

tactics.heading: Fight overview
tactics.text:
The fight against the Royal Titans takes place on a five-tile-wide strip of land between the Crandor and Karamja Dungeon and Asgarnian Ice Dungeon. The encounter is recommended for two players, though a player can fight the Royal Titans alone if desired. Most damage taken during the fight is avoidable, so the major difference a solo player can expect is a significantly lengthier fight.

All three combat styles have a purpose for the fight:

• Ranged - to attack titans (6x multiplier whilst in non-melee distance)
• Magic - to clear fire/ice obstacles and minions
• Melee - to attack titans

It's possible to kill the Titans with only melee or only ranged attacks, but it can be much slower than bringing both. It's possible to complete the fight without magic, but this is only recommended for higher-levelled players.

The Titans have 600 health each, with a Defence level of 100. They are slightly weaker to crush, though not significantly enough to prioritise a crush weapon over something stronger. Additionally, despite their high ranged defences of +700, players get a hidden +500% (a 6x multiplier) to ranged accuracy whenever the titans are out of melee distance. This lasts until the Titans turn around to start engaging in melee combat once again. This accuracy boost also applies during the entirety of the Elemental Blast attack, which includes the charging and a few ticks after the attack has completed.

Despite the strength of this boost, the Titans still have considerably lower melee defence and players are incentivised to attack with melee whenever possible.

tactics.heading: Attacks
tactics.text:
The titans use several different attacks during the fight:
• Stomp - a melee attack where a Titan stomps the ground (affecting the three rows in front of them), which can be blocked with Protect from Melee. Only used whilst in melee distance during phase 1 of the fight. This can deal up to 26 damage.

• Fire/Icicle Walls - a row of fire/icicles will begin to manifest, fully forming and blocking said row after four ticks. Standing on a targeted tile will deal up to 12 damage to the player, but prevents the obstacle from forming. They will dissipate on their own in time, but can be destroyed with their opposing element without incurring any attack delays, regardless of the player's magic attack bonus:
  • The fires are doused with Water Blast or greater, extinguishing the two others adjacent to the targeted tile. Ice spells are also effective.
  • The icicles are melted with Fire Blast or greater, melting the two others adjacent to the targeted tile.
• Fire/Ice elementals - The Titans will summon three fire/ice elementals that attack with melee. If not killed, they will self-destruct, dealing 8-10 damage in a 3x3 area around them.
  • Players with a +70 magic attack bonus (or +39 if wearing the full void mage set) are guaranteed a successful hit, dealing their max hit with water or fire spells, which uniquely attack in a 3x3 area around its primary target during this fight. The elementals also have an elemental weakness to their opposing element, taking double damage.
  • For each elemental killed, the player receives a 1-tick reduction to their attack delay, allowing spells to be cast consecutively much quicker than usual.
  • Elementals are instantly destroyed if they are hit by fire/icicle walls or elemental blast attacks of the opposing element.
• Elemental Blast - The Titans will blast the entire area with their respective elements three times, except for one safe tile, dealing up to 30 damage per blast. Only used once the Titans enter the second phase of the fight.

tactics.heading: Phase 1
tactics.text:
Upon entering the fight area, Branda and Eldric will briefly be in melee distance at the centre. Players have enough time to run from the entrance and strike one of them with any melee weapon (Eldric being easiest) before they distance themselves from the platform. When this occurs, the player's ranged accuracy is increased by 6x, lasting until the Titans start to move back within melee distance.

While out of melee range, the Titans will conjure icicles and fire walls, with elementals being summoned once one of the Titans have taken 100 damage. The elementals can stack on each other and do not have a clear indicator on when they self-destruct, so it is recommended to kill them, as the damage can quickly add up. It is also possible to lure the elementals onto an emerging wall of the opposing element, which will kill them instantly when it forms, although this is not a fully reliable strategy due to the unpredictable placement of the walls.

After roughly 20 seconds, they will enter melee distance and perform their stomp attacks. When one of the Titans drops to 210 (35%) health or below, the fight will transition to the second phase.

When soloing, it's advisable to try to stagger the melee/range phases for both Titans so that at least one of them is in melee range for as much of phase 1 as possible, with one titan entering into melee when the other one is just about to enter into ranged. This can be accomplished by staying as far away from a Titan as possible so that they have to walk the max distance to get to you upon transitioning to melee, delaying their sequence. When done correctly, there should barely be any situations where neither titan is in melee range, which increases DPS as you can just run back and forth without needing to switch to lesser ranged DPS.

If the player remains in the instance after slaying the titans, it's possible to use a four-tick weapon to attack each of the titans a single time before they walk away; Or a four-tick weapon followed by a halberd swap can allow two hits on a single Titan before it leaves melee range.

tactics.heading: Phase 2
tactics.text:
Both Titans will make their way onto the main fight area, occupying three rows at both ends. During this phase, the Titans will now use Elemental Blast (in addition to elementals and stomp) which can be safespotted using the marked tile that appears. The Titans will then begin charging their Elemental Blast attack after a short delay; the player's ranged accuracy gets a 6x multiplier during the charging, attack, and for a few seconds after.

Note: If a player is standing on the position a Titan will occupy, the player is knocked back and takes roughly 15-30 damage.

Try to leave the Titans' health as low as possible before subduing them, as defeating one Titan will result in the opposing titan's stomp attacks to deal up to 10 hitpoints of prayer-piercing damage and the safespot for the Elemental Blast always being placed at the furthest row from them. The Titans will generally sync their attacks, though this may desync once they fall below 100 hitpoints, such as one Titan stomping and the other summoning elementals rather than both stomping at once. Notably, the stomp will cover the entire arena.

During the Elemental Blast, there is one safe tick between each blast that the player can exploit with melee to attack once and then run back to the safespot. This is only damage-free if the safespot is two tiles away from the respective Titan so the player can return on the next tick, or the player will be hit by the following blast. If three tiles away, a halberd can be used instead. A useful indicator for timing this method is to attack immediately after a Titan raises its staff to perform the blast. Otherwise, attack them with ranged. Utilising this strategy minimises time spent swapping gear and prayers.

Depending on gear and attack styles, a player may wish to bring both Titans down equally to this point, or focus on a single titan to reach this phase as soon as possible. While the Titans will now always be in melee distance, lower-levelled players may find it more difficult to manage as the titans will now follow a more dangerous, albeit generally consistent attack rotation. If one of the Titans is subdued before the Elemental Blast fully charges, the blasts will no longer cover their corresponding area for that cast, thus making it a brief safespot for that instance.

gearNotes.heading: Equipment
gearNotes.text:
With base 90 Melee stats and Osmumten's fang or dragon hunter lance, using melee against rune dragons is a reliable option. With worse weapons, magic or ranged may be more effective. Rune dragons have accurate and strong attacks, so Bandos, Justiciar, or Barrows equipment is recommended along with Protect from Magic and Piety in tandem to reduce damage taken. Vengeance can be used against their healing Ranged attacks. As soon as a number appears in a purple hitsplat on the dragon, cast Vengeance.

Additionally, you may bring Thralls along with a Book of the Dead. Thralls deal 1-3 damage every couple of seconds so this adds up significantly.

A Dwarf multicannon may also be used against rune dragons with significant accuracy.

Inventory

• Digsite pendant or a mounted one in POH with house tabs
• Special attack weapon choice
• 1 divine super combat potion, super combat potion or super set
• 1 extended antifire, or extended super antifire if using a shield without dragonfire protection
• 3-4 prayer potions
• Rune pouch with runes to cast Vengeance or High Level Alchemy (set warning value to 162,000) (optional)
• One-click teleport (optional)
• Food (sharks / manta rays / anglerfish / karambwan)
• Bracelet of slaughter (optional, if on task)
• Dwarf multicannon (optional)
• Steel cannonball (about 400 per hour)

With level 90 Ranged and a dragon hunter crossbow, rune dragons can easily be killed due to the crossbow's passive effect, as well as circumventing their melee attack. Protect from Missiles is recommended with Rigour or Eagle Eye in tandem. Also, Vengeance could be used for dealing with their healing Ranged attacks, which hits through Protect from Missiles. As soon as a number appears in a purple hitsplat on the dragon, prepare Vengeance. Additionally, you may bring Thralls along with a Book of the Dead. Thralls deal 1-3 damage every couple of seconds so this adds up significantly. A dwarf multicannon may also be used with good accuracy due to ranged gear's high bonuses.

Inventory

• Digsite pendant or a mounted one in POH with house tabs
• 1 divine ranging potion or ranging potion
• 1 extended antifire, or extended super antifire if using a shield without dragonfire protection
• 3-4 prayer potions
• Rune pouch with runes to cast Vengeance or High Level Alchemy (set warning value to 162,000) (optional)
• One-click teleport (optional)
• Food (sharks / manta rays / anglerfish / karambwan)
• Bracelet of slaughter (optional, if on task)
• Dwarf multicannon (optional)
• Steel cannonball (optional, about 400 per hour)

Rune dragons have relatively low Magic defence. The most effective weapon for killing rune dragons across all styles is the Tumeken's shadow, surpassing even dragonbane weaponry.

For those without a Shadow, Earth spells can be a viable alternative, especially when used with a dragon hunter wand and/or while on a slayer task. Protect from Missiles is recommended due to the dragons' accurate ranged attacks.

Inventory

• Digsite pendant or a mounted one in POH with house tabs
• Saturated heart
• 1 extended antifire, or extended super antifire if using a shield without dragonfire protection
• 3-4 prayer potions
• Rune pouch with runes to cast the spell of choice
• One-click teleport (optional)
• Food (sharks / manta rays / anglerfish / karambwan)
• Bracelet of slaughter (optional, if on task)

tactics.heading: Overview
tactics.text: After completion of Dragon Slayer II, rune dragons can be found and fought in the Lithkren Vault. They are the strongest of all metal dragons, so caution should be exercised at all times.

tactics.heading: Attacks
tactics.text:
Similar to their mithril and adamant counterparts, rune dragons use standard dragonfire and attack from all sides of the combat triangle. They also have two unique special attacks:
• Electricity: Signalled by throwing two small balls that appear to be electricity on the floor, which will then arc to other tiles around the player, dealing rapid hits of 2-5 damage if the player doesn't move away. This can be reduced to 1-2 damage by wearing insulated boots.
• Life Leech: An augmented ranged attack, similar to the Life Leech effect of enchanted onyx bolts, that hits through Protect from Missiles and heals the dragon for whatever it hits on the player.

tactics.heading: Transportation
tactics.text: The fastest way to get to rune dragons is by using a digsite pendant to teleport Lithkren Vault directly. Alternatively, players can take the boat by Jardric, found to the north-west of Fossil Island, to Lithkren, and navigate the ruins there to reach the vault.

• 94+ Magic (optional)

• 70+ Prayer

Magic defence is prioritised due to two magic-using spawns that will appear during the fight. Aranea boots allow the player to avoid Sarachnis' web attack, but their cost may be prohibitive for lower level players.
