tactics.heading: Overview
tactics.text:
Sarachnis is a mid-level boss located in the Forthos Dungeon. She is often killed for her Sarachnis cudgel, pristine spider silk, and elite clue scroll drops.

Players can create an instanced version of Sarachnis' arena for 25,000 coins via the thick web opening to her lair, which lasts until the player leaves or logs out.

tactics.heading: Transportation
tactics.text:
The three easiest ways to reach the Forthos Dungeon include:
• Xeric's talisman - Teleporting to Xeric's Glade brings players just east of the eastern dungeon entrance.
• Kharedst's memoirs/Book of the Dead - Using the "Lunch by the Lancalliums" teleport brings the player by the River Hos just north-east of the dungeon entrances.
• Spirit tree (player-grown) just south of the dungeon entrance.

tactics.heading: Mechanics
tactics.text:
Sarachnis has several attacks that she will occasionally use other than the standard melee and ranged attacks. Her melee attacks consist of smashing the player with her legs, while she launches barbed projectiles as her ranged attack.

• Healing strike - Sarachnis' standard attacks will heal her on successful hits, indicated by a magenta hitsplat. She heals 5 health for every successful melee attack, and 10 health for every successful ranged attack, regardless of how much damage she actually deals, including zeros.
• Sticky web - Every four standard attacks, Sarachnis will screech out and shoot out a sticky web that leaves players bound for 6 ticks (3.6 seconds), then moving a short distance away from where she was before attacking the player. This attack can be completely negated by wearing aranea boots.
• Spawns - When Sarachnis reaches 66% and 33% health, she summons two Spawn of Sarachnis per player; a level 68 that uses Magic and has a maximum hit of 11, and a level 107 that uses Melee and has a maximum hit of 13. Both have 30 health.

tactics.heading: Suggested skills
tactics.text:
• 65+ Hitpoints
• 65+ Strength
• 65+ Attack (required to equip weapons like Sarachnis cudgel)
• 65+ Defence (to be able to tank some damage from minions)
• 60+ Magic (for magic defence against mage minion)
• 70+ Ranged (for magic defence armour)
• 43+ Prayer (for protection prayers, 70 recommended for Piety)

tactics.heading: Strategy
tactics.text:
Sarachnis is weak to crush weapons, and has high magic and ranged defence. Therefore, it is recommended to bring high strength bonus equipment and a crush weapon that can attack fast (such as an abyssal bludgeon).

Sarachnis attacks with melee when players are next to her, and Ranged when she cannot reach them; it is advised to pray Protect from Melee or Protect from Missiles accordingly, as these attacks can hit up to 31 if they aren't protected against, and also heal her if they do manage to hit. Her melee range is deceptively large, so players are advised to exercise caution when standing near her.

Additionally, lower-levelled players may wish to kill the blue magic-using Spawn of Sarachnis. The melee spawns may be tanked with sufficiently high defensive bonuses, but are not necessary to kill as the player should be praying Protect from Melee outside her web attack.

Players fighting Sarachnis can avoid getting snared by her web attack by wearing aranea boots throughout the fight. This allows the player to attack more frequently and avoid taking ranged attacks at all, avoiding prayer switches entirely. If these strategies are not able to be used, eating food only while bound by her web is recommended to maximise damage dealt.

All tiles directly adjacent to walls are out of Sarachnis's melee range. Standing on one of these tiles and praying Protect from Missiles will nullify all of her damage, but not the damage of her spawn.

When Sarachnis is killed, any remaining spawns will automatically die off with her. She will respawn in 17 ticks (10.2s).

gearNotes.heading: Equipment
gearNotes.text:
The setup primarily consists of only taking 3 or 4 expensive items as this boss resides in a multi-combat area in level 50+ Wilderness, meaning player killers may quickly kill off-guard players.

Scorpia is not immune to venom and poison; therefore, using a trident of the swamp will do some additional damage over the course of the kill. Due to her low magic defence, a minimally geared player will rarely miss, therefore magic damage and prayer bonus should be prioritised over magic accuracy to reduce risk and prolong trips.

If bringing a powered staff, a magic boost such as a Magic potion, forgotten brew, or saturated/imbued heart will provide additional magic damage.

gearNotes.text:

  • Forgotten brew can be substituted instead to reduce risk with an added benefit of boosting prayer above current level.
• 100+ casts of blighted ancient ice sack/blighted entangle sack for Ice Blitz, Ice Barrage, or Entangle. If lasting a full trip with the recommended inventory bring 300+ casts.
• 1 or 2 Stamina potions for escaping player-killers and during kills, especially if finishing a kill after running out of binds
• Wilderness sword 1 or better, knife, or slash weapon if running from Edgeville lever
• Lockpick, for escaping into the magic axe hut
• Black d'hide body and chaps, for tanking player killers
• Looting bag

tactics.heading: Overview
tactics.text:
Scorpia is a powerful Wilderness boss capable of poisoning her opponents starting at 20 damage as well as hitting up to 16 with melee. Her lair, located beneath the Scorpion Pit, is filled with many Scorpia's offspring, which use accurate ranged attacks with a max hit of 2 and inflict poison starting at 6 damage.

Once Scorpia reaches 99 health or lower, she will summon two Scorpia's guardians which will continually heal Scorpia when within 3 tiles of her until they are killed or despawned. The guardians will not respawn if killed, and will despawn if they are too far away to heal Scorpia for 15 seconds.

An effective strategy is to exploit her low magic defence by using Ice Barrage to freeze her (Ice Burst, Ice Blitz, or Entangle will also work fine), staying out of melee range while attacking her with magic, and praying Protect from Missiles to prevent damage from Scorpia's offspring. Once her guardians spawn, players should wait until Scorpia is about to become unfrozen, then quickly freeze both guardians and lure Scorpia far away from them. This should cause the guardians to despawn, allowing Scorpia to be easily finished off.

tactics.heading: Tips
tactics.text:
• If you are comfortable with it, set NPC attack options to "always right click" so you don't accidentally target the offspring, as this hinders your movement and wastes runes and Scorpion slayer kills. Alternatively, a plugin available in any approved third-party game client called "Menu Entry Swapper" will allow customizable left/shift click settings, allowing you to set the left-click option of the offspring as "Walk here".
• Consider using longrange/defensive casting. Standing further away makes positioning easier when Scorpia unfreezes.
• A good way to lure Scorpia away from her guardians is to position yourself at the side where you will be luring her just before she reaches half hp and freezing the healers immediately as they spawn. This requires careful timing, as Scorpia should ideally unfreeze very soon after you freeze both the guardians.
• If using Ancient Magicks, you may utilise manual casting of blood spells to heal yourself when Scorpia is frozen and minions are not around.
• Lower levelled players not using a toxic weapon may also try to poison Scorpia with a couple casts of Smoke Blitz/Barrage when starting the kill for a little bit of extra damage.
• The guardians give highly reduced experience. Do not rely on experience drops to see whether you hit them.

tactics.heading: Suggested skills
tactics.text:
• 70+ Magic for Accursed sceptre
• 40+ Prayer for Protect from Missiles

tactics.heading: Overview
tactics.text:
Within the Varrock Sewers, players can fight Scurrius, the Rat King. Players can make their way east from the sewer entrance just east of the Varrock Palace courtyard, then climbing through the broken bars. Players can right-click the bars to choose whether to enter the public area or create an instance, which is free.

The public area contains a much stronger Scurrius (having 1,000 more health and slightly higher combat stats), though it has a more generous experience multiplier. The private version of Scurrius is faster to kill, but is weaker and gives a lower multiplier.

The use of a Dwarf multicannon is prohibited in the arena. Attempting to place a cannon gives the message: "It's far too damp for you to set up a cannon here."

If the player dies while fighting Scurrius, their grave will appear next to Historian Aldo just outside Scurrius' lair.

tactics.heading: Recommendations
tactics.text:
• Moderate combat stats in any style
  • Level 50 Attack or higher
  • Level 50 Strength or higher
  • Level 50 Defence or higher
  • Level 50 Ranged or higher
  • Level 50 Magic or higher
  • Level 50 Hitpoints or higher
  • Level 43 Prayer for protection prayers

tactics.heading: Fight overview
tactics.text:
Scurrius uses several different attack styles during the fight:
• Tail Swipe - A melee attack where Scurrius strikes the player with his tail, dealing up to 13 damage; Protect from Melee negates all damage. Only being used during the first two phases, this is his fastest and most accurate attack, and no warning is given for it.
• Bolts of Electricity - A magic attack where Scurrius discharges lightning at the player, dealing up to 14 damage (8 in solo mode); Protect from Magic negates all damage. The attack will only deal damage on impact.
• Flying Fur - A ranged attack where Scurrius throws a stinky fur ball at the player, dealing up to 13 damage (7 in solo mode); Protect from Missiles negates all damage. The attack will only deal damage on impact.

tactics.heading: Special attacks
tactics.text:
• Healing - Upon reaching 80% of his health, Scurrius will occasionally move to a Food Pile, eating and restoring 5 or 10 health every few seconds. During this time, he will only use magic and ranged attacks, along with the Falling Bricks attack. This will stop upon reaching 30% of his health.
• Minions - Scurrius will screech, causing six level 46 giant rats to appear around the arena. The rats are very accurate and hit 0-1 through Protect from Melee, but players will always instantly kill them upon attacking them, Protect from Melee is recommended as the rats can hit up to 4 without it. Hitting the rats with any of the rat bone weapons will incur no attack delay. The rats will persist even after Scurrius is slain, and can prevent players from healing with the Food Piles.
• Falling Bricks - Scurrius will jump on the spot, causing rubble to fall down on the arena. One piece will always target the player's current tile when it was used, while others will fall randomly around the arena. This is indicated with a looming shadow on the targeted tile. Getting hit by the attack will deal 15-24 damage (15-22 in solo mode).

tactics.heading: Phase one
tactics.text:
At the start of the fight, Scurrius will be in the east side of the chamber and attack with melee by sweeping his tail, and occasionally use his Falling Bricks attack.

Upon reaching 80% of his health, Scurrius will move towards one of the Food Piles. He will break free of any binds in the process. The food pile selected is random, though usually one close to him. He may either walk or run towards the pile.

tactics.heading: Phase two
tactics.text:
At the food piles, Scurrius will eat every few seconds, healing 5 or 10 hitpoints per player in the arena. While the animation will show him eating ten times, he will only heal five times. After the tenth eating animation, he will stop and resume attacking players with melee. Scurrius can continue to use his Falling Bricks attack, attack with magic or range, and summon giant rats.

The healing that occurs during this phase is affected by the smoke ancient sceptre if Scurrius is poisoned (in that case he will heal for only 4 or 8 hitpoints per player).

tactics.heading: Phase three
tactics.text: After reaching 30% of his health, Scurrius will move to the centre of the arena, attacking the player exclusively with ranged and magic at a faster rate than during the first two phases. He can also use the Falling Bricks attack and summon minions during this phase. Notably, he can use the Falling Bricks attack multiple times in a row during this phase, so players should pay attention to the shadows on the ground and move as necessary to avoid heavy damage. If Scurrius heals above 30% of his health, he will reset back to phase 2 and attempt to heal again. This will continue until Scurrius is dead.

tactics.heading: Strategies
tactics.text:
Until Scurrius reaches 30% of his health, the player should use Protect from Melee, as it is Scurrius' fastest and most accurate attack, due to his Attack level of 300 and +150 melee attack bonus. The ranged and magic attacks are generally less accurate (as he is level 50/100 in those stats), and can be blocked with late reactions. Avoid falling rubble as necessary. If the player is using mage or range attack styles and does not wish to prayer switch, they may pray against whatever their equipment is weaker to when Scurrius is at the food piles as he will not perform melee attacks during this period.

When the giant rats appear:
• If the player possesses a rat bone weapon, it is recommended to attack the giant rats using the no attack delay if you are trying to get the best experience per hour.
• If the player does not possess a rat bone weapon, viable alternatives include a charged Venator bow or the special attack of the Rune thrownaxe or Dinh's bulwark.
• Otherwise, try to trap them using Scurrius and themselves to minimize the amount of rats appearing, as they are rather accurate and bypass prayer.

Once Scurrius reaches 30% of his health (150 for solo/450 for group), he will head to the centre of the arena and continually drop rubble. He will no longer use melee attacks, instead throwing ranged and magic attacks until slain. Scurrius will also continue to summon waves of rat minions. He will do this up to 12 times, after which there will be no more additional rat waves.

After Scurrius dies, kill off the other rats. If the player is using a rat bone weapon, they will be able to attack the giant rats with no delay. Attacking Scurrius and then swapping to a minion will still incur normal attack delay.

You can eat from the Food Pile once every 10 minutes to heal to full outside of combat. This cannot be done for a couple of seconds after being attacked, but you can eat while Scurrius or the rats are still alive.

gearNotes.heading: Equipment
gearNotes.text:
Since the Shellbane Gryphon's knockback is effective against players with less than 40 kg of worn equipment, some of the best options do not necessarily provide the highest damage, but rather a balance between strength bonus and heavy weight.
A 40kg+ setup can be easily achieved with most melee armour coupled with both a tortugan and dragonfire shield, even when using a slayer helmet. If a black mask is used, its higher weight over the slayer helmet means that the player can slot in an avernic defender for better DPS. If not being used, the dragonfire shield is recommended to meet this requirement.
If using low-level gear, adamant armour may be preferred to rune as it is heavier.

gearNotes.heading: Inventory
gearNotes.text:
• Special attack weapon such as a dragon dagger. If using the Arkan blade as a main-hand damaging weapon, its special attack will suffice.
• Divine super combat potions / super combat potions; or super attack potions + super strength potions if those are not available.
• Means to teleport to house, such as Teleport to house (tablet) or Construction cape
• Rune pouch, with runes to cast Resurrection spells and a Book of the Dead.
  • If A Kingdom Divided has not yet been completed, simply bring nature runes and fire runes for High Level Alchemy.
• Explorer's ring 4 if high alching runite item drops and using the Arceuus Spellbook.
• Herb sack if collecting herb drops.
• Bonecrusher or bonecrusher necklace for Prayer experience and to reduce number of items on ground.
• A bracelet of slaughter to switch to as the boss dies, if wishing to prolong Slayer task.
• Some food to heal from occasional off-prayer attacks or mistakes. If no longer getting hit by special attacks in the fight, cheaper food may be brought.

High-level players may forgo food by using the Saradomin godsword's special attack to heal.
Low-level players may use a knife on the watermelon drops to eat watermelon slices, or bring a tinderbox and filled log basket or axe to cook the raw food drops outside of the cave.

Due to Shellbane gryphon's cave's proximity to fairy ring CJQ, players who have ornate rejuvenation pool and fairy ring built in their player-owned house can teleport out between kills and restore their hitpoints, special attack, and prayer points. This has three major benefits:
• Less supplies used
• Allows special attacks to be used more often
• Allows player to bring better equipment
  • The weight aspect of gryphon's knockback can be ignored, since it's unlikely that the gryphon will do that more than once per kill and the damage taken is only moderate.
~50-65 kills per hour can be achieved with this method, depending on what gear player has access to, and how attentively they are playing.

tactics.heading: Overview
tactics.text: After completion of Troubled Tortugans, the Shellbane Gryphon can be fought again, but requires the player to be assigned a gryphon slayer task, or to have an elite clue directing them to kill the Shellbane Gryphon (in which case the player will be only be able to kill the boss once).

tactics.heading: Requirements
tactics.text: • Completion of Quest Troubled Tortugans

tactics.heading: Recommendations
tactics.text:

• 43 Prayer minimum for access to Protect from Melee
  • 70 Prayer and 70 Defence to unlock and use Piety

tactics.heading: Transportation
tactics.text:
• The fastest way to the shellbane gryphon's cave is by using fairy ring cjq, then running north.
• Players without access to fairy rings may opt to use a charter ship to reach the Great Conch, with the cost dependent on the departure location.

tactics.heading: Fight overview
tactics.text:
Like normal gryphons, the shellbane gryphon is primarily weak to melee, but magic can also be effective due to its elemental weakness to wind spells; however, due to one of its special attacks, this is not entirely practical. Additionally, a tortugan shield is recommended for the encounter with the shellbane gryphon, otherwise the player will take heavy damage from gryphon's melee attacks even through Protect from Melee, and receive a game message stating Using Protect from Melee whilst having the tortugan shield equipped will fully negate all melee damage dealt.

The shellbane gryphon primarily attacks with melee, but also uses a ranged attack occasionally. It also has three special attacks:

• Knockback - The boss will throw the player backwards, dealing up to 30 unavoidable damage. Despite the audio from this attack, the player is not stunned and can immediately resume attacking. The knockback is countered by having the player's equipped weight be ≥40kg, which also causes the boss to prioritise using its other two special attacks.
  • Negating the knockback stuns the boss for 2 ticks (1.2s). During this short window, the player can quickly click to attack the boss to knock it back one tile and grants player one additional attack free of attack delay. However, if the player does not click to attack the boss while it's stunned, they will be knocked back regardless of equipped weight, indicated by the game message
  • Players may not be able to perform the knockback in time if their attack is delayed by eating food.
• Corrosive spit - An orange blob is launched, which corrodes the player's worn equipment if they do not move one tile away from where they stood. This causes a player to take 3-12 damage 6 times (18-72 damage total) over the course of 32 ticks (19.2s), which can be interrupted by quickly unequipping all of the player's items.

• Whirlwind - Whirlwinds begin to form at the player's current position, indicated by the game message
  • The boss will form a whirlwind every 3 ticks (1.8s), up to a maximum of 5. If a whirlwind would have formed on top of an existing whirlwind, that whirlwind instead grows more powerful. 6 ticks (3.6s) after the last whirlwind forms, all whirlwinds will begin damaging every tick the player stands on them.
  • 15 seconds after that, all summoned whirlwinds will burst and deal large amounts of damage, indicated by the game message As such, its recommended to move one tile every attack in order to avoid whirlwinds stacking and increasing their size, resulting in less damage received.
  • When countering the knockback attack, players should be cautious on where they move to, as a whirlwind may inadvertently end up in range of damaging the player upon shoving the boss.

Therefore it is recommended to use a dragon hunter crossbow or dragon hunter lance if any of these weapons are available. They are also one of the few draconic creatures that are affected by the enchanted dragonstone bolt effect, Dragon's breath.

tactics.heading: Overview
tactics.text: Skeletal Wyverns are level 72 Slayer monsters found in the Asgarnian Ice Dungeon.

tactics.heading: Requirements
tactics.text:
• Level 72 Slayer to damage skeletal wyverns. This can be boosted.
• Completion of QuestElemental Workshop I or II for access to the elemental or mind shields respectively. These shields offer protection from the wyverns' powerful icy breath attack.
  • Alternatively, the dragonfire shield, ancient wyvern shield and dragonfire ward also offer the same protection, all requiring having started Dragon Slayer I.

tactics.heading: Recommendations
tactics.text:
• High combat stats. Although not required, see the skill levels below for an indication of the advised stats:
  • If using Melee:
    • Level 75 Attack or higher
    • Level 75 Strength or higher
    • Level 70 Hitpoints or higher
    • Level 70 Prayer or higher for the Piety prayer
  • If using Ranged:
    • Level 70 Ranged or higher
    • Level 44 Prayer or higher for the Eagle Eye prayer
  • If using Magic:
    • Level 75 Magic or higher for the Fire Wave spell

tactics.heading: Transportation
tactics.text:
Skeletal wyverns are located in the Asgarnian Ice Dungeon. The entrance to this dungeon may be found south of Port Sarim and north of Mudskipper Point. The quickest ways to travel here are:
• Using the Giantsoul amulet, teleport to Branda and Eldric's Lair and run east.
• From the fairy ring at Mudskipper Point, using the code AIQ, and running north.
• From Rimmington, via the Teleport to House spell or a Rimmington teleport tablet, or Captain Barnaby, and running south-east.
• From Port Sarim, using the spirit tree, an explorer's ring, or the Minigame Port Sarim Rat Pits minigame teleport after the completion of Ratcatchers, then running south(-west).
• From the Port Sarim docks, using a charter ship, or the Minigame Pest Control Minigame Teleport or scrolls, and running west then south.

From the dungeon entrance, climb down the trapdoor, first run north and then run east to find an open space with ice warriors and ice giants. The entrance to the wyverns' lair can be found on the southern wall of this room. Players with level 72 or 82 Agility may use a shortcut before the icy area or right from the dungeon entrance, respectively.

tactics.heading: Attack styles
tactics.text:
Skeletal wyverns attack with Melee, Ranged and their unique ice breath attack.
• The Melee attack is only used when the player is standing in Melee distance and can hit up to 13. Skeletal wyverns roll their slash accuracy against the player's stab defence when performing a bite or tail swipe attack.
• The Ranged attack has an attack range of 6 tiles and can hit up to 13.
• The ice-breath attack has an attack range of 5 tiles and can hit 50+, although this damage can be drastically reduced to a maximum hit of 10 by the following shields: elemental shield, mind shield, dragonfire shield, ancient wyvern shield, and dragonfire ward.
  • This attack may also freeze the player's character for a few seconds. During this period, the character is not able to move or attack.
  • There is a 1/7 chance to be frozen while wielding one of the shields listed above.
  • The ancient wyvern shield will grant an immunity against this freezing effect.
  • Without an appropriate shield, the chance to be frozen by a skeletal wyvern is determined by one's Magic defensive bonuses.
  • Antifire potions have no effect.

tactics.heading: Safespotting
tactics.text:
Skeletal wyverns can be safespotted because they have a shorter attack range than players using a crossbow or magic spells. They can be easily safespotted during a Slayer task by standing one tile north-west of Steve/Pieve.

• To safespot skeletal wyverns, first make sure to lose their aggressiveness. Aggressiveness is lost automatically after a player has spent 10 minutes in the same area (i.e. they don't move past a certain invisible border).
• After this time period, attack a wyvern and lure it behind an obstacle (e.g. a wall that is sticking out).
• While the wyvern is stuck behind the obstacle, move out of its attack range to make sure it can't attack the player anymore.
• Now start attacking the wyvern using Magic or Ranged.

Another common method for doing this is getting them stuck behind the main entrance. Players should always wait for the wyverns to become unaggressive, which takes 10 minutes, before attempting this; otherwise, they'll get hit by other wyverns when trying to safespot another. A good method to make them unaggressive is to wait in front of the main entrance for ten minutes; this will make the wyverns unaggressive near the entrance. Players who do this should be careful not to walk more than a few steps deeper into the cave, as if they do, the wyverns will get aggressive again. Alternatively, for safespotting, players can bring a few Prayer potions and attack the wyvern from seven steps away with Protect from Missiles on.

tactics.heading: Dwarf multicannon
tactics.text: Dwarf multicannon are allowed in the Asgarnian Ice Dungeon, however only in the lower part of the cave; the upper Slayer-exclusive part is a no cannon zone. Cannons will make killing skeletal wyverns faster and the profit from the extra drops often outweigh the cost of the steel cannonballs. Therefore it can be recommended to bring a dwarf multicannon when meleeing skeletal wyverns.

tactics.heading: Prayers
tactics.text: If in melee range then Protect from Melee; else if ranged/magic and not safespotting then Protect from Range.

gearNotes.text:

• Emergency food (not required if standing under overhanging rock)
• 2 antidote++
• Monkey greegree
• One-click teleport (ring of dueling is an alternative)
• 1 stamina potion

Using Ancient Magicks to kill skeleton monkeys is considered one of the best magic training methods. Due to the high cost of runes it is recommended to bring good equipment to minimize the amount of splashing. Note that in some cases prayer bonus should be prioritised over magic bonus.

The salve amulet (ei) will only work on the primary target when bursting/barraging, so the occult necklace is preferred for better experience per hour.

• 2 Antidote++ (4)

tactics.heading: Overview
tactics.text:
Skeletons are undead monsters that can be assigned as tasks at combat level 15 by various low-level Slayer masters. They are often found in cemeteries and dungeons. A good strategy to kill them is to use melee with a weapon with crush bonuses (such as a Viggora's chainmace) and a salve amulet or salve amulet (e), due to their low crush defence.

Another strategy to kill them would be with magic. Many skeletons have an elemental weakness to earth spells, making those a very effective option.

Players who seek a greater challenge can choose to kill Vet'ion or Calvar'ion. These bosses are significantly stronger than the typical skeleton, but provide plenty of rewards for players who seek to kill them. In order to access Calvar'ion, the player must have completed the Hard Wilderness Diary. Vet'ion only requires completing the Medium Wilderness Diary, but is deeper in the Wilderness and resides in a multicombat area. Accessing the bosses requires a one-time payment of coins, which must be repaid again if the player dies to another player in the Wilderness. Note that the skeletal hellhounds they summon also count towards the task, so every kill at the boss is equal to five skeletons per spawn.

If players are not seeking to kill either skeleton boss but are assigned them in the Wilderness, an ideal location would be the Edgeville Dungeon, as there is a good cluster of skeletons that can be easily cannoned and has a quick escape, provided that the player is paying attention.

tactics.heading: Skeleton monkeys
tactics.text:
Skeleton monkeys can be found in the Ape Atoll Dungeon. As the dungeon is a multicombat zone and the skeletons respawn rapidly due to their bone drops reanimating, they can be trained on with area of effect attacks like chinchompas or Ancient Magicks burst or barrage spells.

Skeleton monkeys provide excellent Ranged experience rates when attacked with chinchompas of any kind. High ranged bonus is advisable to reduce the amount of failed attacks. Upon death, chinchompas will not be removed from your inventory.

tactics.heading: Exceptions
tactics.text:
• Although it is insinuated in Tarn's diary that skeletal wyverns are undead, they are in fact re-animated remains, whereas actual undead creatures have come back to life. This causes the Salve amulet and its enchanted versions to not work against them.
• Although the Skeletal hellhound summoned by Vanstrom Klause during the In Search of the Myreque quest looks like a skeleton, crumble undead does not work against this monster, and the salve amulet seems to have no effect.

tactics.heading: Overview
tactics.text: Skotizo is a level 321 demon located underneath the Catacombs of Kourend. His arena requires sacrificing a Dark totem to the Altar in the centre of the catacombs to enter. He is commonly killed for his high valued drops, Ancient shards, Hard and Elite clues, and the Skotos pet.

tactics.heading: Requirements
tactics.text:
• Access to the Catacombs of Kourend
• A Dark totem, assembled from pieces acquired as drops from monsters within the catacombs.

tactics.heading: Suggested skills
tactics.text:
• 75+ Attack for Arclight
• 75+ Strength
• 75+ Defence
• 75+ Hitpoints
• 75+ Magic

tactics.heading: Transportation
tactics.text: The Altar is located in the centre of the Catacombs of Kourend. The quickest way to reach the entrance is to enter the Catacombs through the Statue of King Rada I located in the Kourend Castle courtyard. This can be reached by using a Xeric's talisman via the 'Xeric's heart' option. After completion of Client of Kourend, the Kourend Castle Teleport can be used.

tactics.heading: Strategy
tactics.text:
Like all demons, Skotizo is vulnerable to the powers of demonbane weapons. He counts as a black or greater demon for the purposes of a Slayer task.

Skotizo uses melee and magic attacks, and tends to prefer using melee while in melee distance. Players are advised to fight Skotizo with melee or ranged due to his high magic defences. Ranged typically provides better safety due to being able to pray Protect from Magic against all of Skotizo's attacks, but at the expense of a longer kill time for most players. A twisted bow with a dragon warhammer spec will beat out an Emberlight, while a bow of Faerdhinen with crystal armour is about equal to an Arclight. Players using melee should pray Protect from Melee in melee distance and use armour with high Magic Defence (e.g. black dragonhide armour) to mitigate the damage, although for players with endgame melee gear (e.g. oathplate or Torva) it is slightly more efficient to use those and pray Protect from Magic. Survivability is generally not an issue with the recommended stats and decent food as long as the player is praying and handling the mechanics correctly.

Arclight's special attack can lower Skotizo's Attack, Strength, and Defence levels by 10% per hit. It is thus strongly recommended to start the fight by using the special attack twice, even if using ranged for the rest of the kill. Players with access to better defence reduction special attacks (e.g. dragon warhammer) or highly damaging special attacks (e.g. burning claws) should use those instead.

At any time during the fight, Skotizo will randomly activate one of the four Awakened Altars on each side of the room. For each activated altar, the player will deal less damage to him: 15% less with Arclight/Emberlight and 25% less with other weapons (up to a maximum of 60% and 100% damage reduction, respectively). When travelling to disable the Awakened Altars, the player should temporarily switch to Protect from Magic, as Skotizo does not approach to use melee attacks. When an altar is deactivated, there is a cooldown of one minute before it can be reactivated.

Arclight and Emberlight (but not Silverlight or Darklight) will disable an altar in one hit regardless of the player's stats and gear; this effect does not extend to the demonbane spells in the Arceuus spellbook or the scorching bow. If using the amulet of blood fury, its passive effect can occur while disabling the altars, healing the player for 30 hitpoints if also using Arclight. Stamina potions are generally not required after the changes to run energy and reduction of room size. The toxic blowpipe is an effective weapon against the altars in case the player chooses not to use Arclight.

After two-thirds of Skotizo's health is depleted, he will summon three reanimated demon spawns to his aid, and may randomly summon a dark ankou at any point while an altar is active: neither of these will pose a threat if using Protect from Melee. Players ranging Skotizo with Protect from Magic should not switch prayers as Skotizo does more damage than the minions. Players may also take advantage of the fact that the minions cannot walk through each other (though they can walk through Skotizo) to stack them in such a way that only one can attack the player. If the minions are slain, Skotizo may summon them again. Fighting the minions provides no benefit, so the player should instead focus on Skotizo and the altars.

options.text: Ancient sceptre / Dragon hunter wand / Master wand

gearNotes.heading: Magic
gearNotes.text: This is the best-in-slot available equipment for maging smoke devils. Unlike dust devils, smoke devils have some magic defence, so gear that provides magic accuracy is beneficial. See the table below for an overview of equipment alternatives in case this setup is not accessible or too expensive.

gearNotes.heading: Notes
gearNotes.text:
• While the tormented bracelet does increase the maximum hit of the player's Magic spells, it is generally inefficient to use as the bracelet of slaughter will increase the task's length and maximise overall Slayer experience rates.
• It is recommended to use a staff or wand that can autocast Ancient Magicks. Kodai wand provides +15% magic damage bonus as well as infinite water runes and a chance to save runes, making it the most effective.

tactics.heading: Overview
tactics.text: Smoke devils are a slayer monster requiring level 93 Slayer in addition to an active slayer task to kill. When using Ice Barrage and a cannon, smoke devils can provide Slayer experience rates of up to 180,000 per hour, depending on the player's efficiency; however, a rate of 120,000 is more realistic. Valuable common drops like the rune chainbody as well as fire and air battlestaves generally compensate the rune and cannonball costs, and the rarer occult necklace drops can provide a net profit.

tactics.heading: Requirements
tactics.text:
• Level 93 Slayer
• Level 40 Prayer for Protect from Missiles

tactics.heading: Recommendations
tactics.text:
• Level 94 Magic for Ice Barrage. Ice Burst could be used at lower levels.
• High Defence to equip armour that boosts magic damage, such as Virtus or ancestral robes.
• Level 82+ Construction for an ornate pool and jewellery box for a teleport to Castle Wars. Alternatively, bring a ring of dueling for teleports to Ferox Enclave to restore stats and the Castle wars teleport.

tactics.heading: Transportation
tactics.text: Bank at Castle Wars then run south-west of the building, to the entrance to the Smoke Devil Dungeon. Alternatively, use a bank of your choice and use the fairy ring bkp to teleport south-west of the dungeon. Run to the centre of the room to the cannon spot.

tactics.heading: Attack styles
tactics.text: The smoke devils attack only with a ranged attack. Protect from Missiles will prevent all damage.

tactics.heading: Smoke
tactics.text: The smoke devils are located in a smoky environment. Players not wearing a facemask or slayer helmet will take 10 damage occasionally while in the dungeon, and attacks from the smoke devils will deal very rapid damage that also drain stats. When using the slayer helmet to check how many kills you have left on the task, take care not to misclick on unequipping the helmet; this can quickly lead to a death with smoke devils attacking you. This also applies on not misclicking rune full helms in the inventory that smoke devils drop as loot.

tactics.heading: Grouping
tactics.text:
Smoke devils should be grouped to maximise barrage hits. Place the cannon in the centre of the room to get them attacking, then run around each side of the skeleton to the west to group up the smoke devils.

It is also possible to lure smoke devils with a ranged weapon, such as a magic shortbow, although this results in lower experience rates and is typically only worth for some ironman accounts, particularly ultimate ironmen.

gearNotes.heading: Equipment
gearNotes.text:
Spindel's location in the Wilderness should warrant extra precautions. Bring defensive armour, especially against magic attacks from other players, as even with a scout and perfect reactions you can be caught inside the cave. Reduce risk accordingly.

Spindel has a lower defence level compared to her stronger counterpart, Venenatis.
The ursine chainmace is the strongest weapon against Spindel, costing coins. The four strongest items to bring are generally the chainmace, your strongest defender, the amulet of rancour, and your best strength ring (ultor ring or berserker ring (i)). A fourth valuable item should only be brought if you are confident in not getting Smited by player killers. Further upgrades are generally very expensive and add little additional damage for their risk and cost. Trouver parchments can be used on certain gear, such as an infernal cape or fighter torso, to gain additional strength bonus for additional risk of 500000+ coins each.

gearNotes.heading: Inventory
gearNotes.text:
Inventory setup will vary greatly depending on your gear and team. When deciding what supplies to bring, keep in mind that Spindel frequently drops large quantities of un-noted blighted food or potions that replace supplies used during the fight. Make sure to have the following:
• Grey chinchompas, blisterwood stakes, darts/throwing knives, or blighted ancient ice sacks for killing the spiderlings quickly, ordered from fastest to slowest
• Looting bag
• Stamina potion
• (Divine) super combat potion
• Anti-venom/Sanfew serum(s) — cures/prevents venom from player killers.
• Blighted super restores
• Blighted manta ray or blighted anglerfish (if the player is 93 or higher hitpoints) for the rest, and multiple blighted karambwan
Optional:
• Phoenix necklace — emergency healing whilst tanking
• Saradomin brews — more expensive outlast healing, combo eating with hard food is invaluable
• Royal seed pod — if not bringing a charged amulet of glory or ring of wealth
• Games necklace or revenant cave teleport to reach the Web Chasm faster.
• Runes for thralls and/or Death Charge
  • Death charge can be cast off cooldown with frequent spiderling spawns.
• Divine rune pouch locked with a trouver parchment — if using Arceeus spellbook, allows for more supplies.

Both the webweaver bow and Craw's bow offer very competitive damage against Spindel despite her higher ranged defences. Ranged also has the luxury of staying closer to the exit in case of player killers, although you will need to monitor and change your overhead prayers depending on the attack cycle. The twisted bow and bow of Faerdhinen are also both strong alternatives to some melee setups, but the former is generally not recommended due to the higher likelihood of being smited from PKers and Spindel's webs. Crossbows generally perform worse than most melee weapons, but offer some relative safety by being able to stay south of the entrance.

gearNotes.heading: Inventory
gearNotes.text:
• Royal seed pod acts as a one-click emergency teleport from up to level 30 Wilderness
• Super restore potions can be used in place of blighted super restores
• Blighted manta ray or blighted anglerfish (if the player is 93 or higher hitpoints) for the rest, and multiple blighted karambwan

tactics.heading: Overview
tactics.text:
Warning: Spindel resides in level 29 Wilderness. You may be attacked by other players at any time during the fight. Do not bring any items that you are not willing to lose. Items like the dragon defender will become broken if not protected and must be repaired at Perdu for a fee.

Spindel is a level 302 spider boss that is found in the Web Chasm. The fight with her is nearly identical to Venenatis, although with reduced stats and in a singles-plus combat area. Completion of the hard Wilderness diary is required to fight Spindel.

tactics.heading: Transportation
tactics.text:
Spindel is located in the Web Chasm, which is a lair located in the ruins north of the Graveyard of Shadows in level 29 Wilderness.

• Graveyard of Shadows teleport, then run north.
• Teleport to Ferox Enclave and run north past green dragons, or head north-east around the graveyard.
• Teleport to the level 26 Revenant Caves entrance with a revenant cave teleport and run east.
• With the Hunter cape, teleport to the black chinchompas and run south east.
• Take a canoe to the wilderness pond and run south east.
• A games necklace to teleport to the Corporeal Beast's lair, exit the cave then run north-west.

tactics.heading: Attacks
tactics.text:
Spindel has many attacks that she uses against her target.

• Melee attack: She simply lunges at the player. This is the only normal attack she will use if the player is within melee distance.
• Ranged attack: Launches green spit at players.
• Magic attack: Launches webs at players.
• Sticky Web: Spindel will occasionally deploy a sticky web at a player, sending a white-blue web at the target's location. It will then expand into a 7x5 AoE - while in this web, any player caught in it will take rapid hits of 3 damage, have their prayer drained by 3, and run energy by 10.
  • Note that aranea boots will only negate the first tick of damage taken from the web attack.
• Spiderlings: Spindel will occasionally call some spiderlings to assist her in battle. While fairly weak, they will drain prayer on every hit regardless if the attack does damage or if protection prayers are active. They will also increase her damage and allow her to hit through prayers if left alive. Player and thrall damage is slightly reduced while spiderlings are alive. Currently, spiderlings cannot spawn east of Spindel's location for reasons unknown.

tactics.heading: Suggested skills
tactics.text:
• 70+ Attack
• 70+ Strength
• 70+ Hitpoints
• 75+ Ranged (if ranging)
• 70+ Defence

tactics.heading: Overview
tactics.text:
Spindel can attack with all three forms of combat. While she will only use one combat style at a time, players in melee distance will instead only be attacked by melee. Like Calvar'ion, she is weakest to crush.

She will begin the fight using 8 ranged attacks, followed by 8 magic attacks, all while moving position every 4 attacks. She will spawn spiderlings on the 1st ranged attack in cycle, and deploy her web attack on the 3rd mage attack in the cycle. This pattern will repeat until Spindel is defeated.

Players who enter the arena will appear to the north, so always keep an eye out for PKers and teleport or run to the exit if needed.

Players should avoid the webs at all costs, as their ability to drain run energy will prevent them from escaping from player killers. The web can be positioned safely by standing on the outskirt of the arena on the 3rd magic attack to help prevent accidentally walking into the web.

The spiderlings should be killed as soon as they spawn to prevent them from empowering her too much; fortunately, they only have 5 health and can be killed in one hit by any combat style.

• Any tier of chinchompa can eliminate multiple spiderlings with a well-placed shot as well as damage Spindel's south-west tile, (Ensure PK Skull prevention is activated).
• Blisterwood stakes, darts, or throwing knives can quickly eliminate individual spiderlings. Blisterwood stakes have longer range than darts and knives, and can be reclaimed from a gravestone for free on PvP death due to being untradeable.
• Players with 70+ Magic and Ancient Magicks can use a burst spell with blighted ancient ice sacks to eliminate multiple spiderlings at once.

tactics.heading: Plugins
tactics.text: All of the following plugins are available on both officially approved third-party Game clients. On RuneLite they must be installed separately from the Plugin Hub, accessed from the Configuration button (wrench icon on sidebar), then clicking the Plugin Hub button (right-most plug icon). On HDOS these plugins come preinstalled.

tactics.heading: Custom Menu Swaps
tactics.text: • To have the Spinderling attack options appear on top of Spindel: Add Attack,Spindel's Spiderling* to "Custom Swaps"

gearNotes.heading: Equipment
gearNotes.text:
It is possible to cannon and safespot suqahs on the northern part of Lunar isle. They can be safespotted by standing next to the hill and hitting them with ranged (as pictured below).

Inventory

• Dwarf multicannon and steel cannonballs
• A Divine ranging potion or ranging potion
• 3-4 Prayer potions for Protect from Magic
• Some Food (Sharks / Karambwans / Monkfish)
• One-click teleport (optional)
• A Seal of Passage to use the bank if you have not completed the Fremennik Elite Diary or Dream Mentor
• A bonecrusher necklace or bonecrusher

Suqah are also located on the southern part of the island, albeit more sparsely.
These do not attack with magic, therefore making it a good spot for players assigned suqah as a Slayer task that do not wish to use the Protect from Magic prayer.
Their damage can be mitigated entirely with Guthan's equipment.

Inventory

• Dwarf multicannon and steel cannonballs
• 2 Divine super combat potions or Super combat potions
• A Seal of Passage to use the bank if you have not completed the Fremennik Elite Diary or Dream Mentor
• A Guthans set
• Some Food (Sharks / Karambwans / Monkfish)
• One-click teleport (optional)
• A bonecrusher necklace or bonecrusher

tactics.heading: Overview
tactics.text:
Suqah can be a good Slayer task, due to the relatively high amount of experience per hour that can be gained from killing them with the help of a dwarf multicannon. However, the use of a dwarf multicannon and toxic blowpipe will also result in a loss of coins due to their lack of valuable drops.

If using the northern area on Lunar Isle, players should pray Protect from Magic and wear armour with high Melee defence, as these Suqah attack with both a melee attack and a magic attack.

Players wishing to avoid the magic damage should fight the suqah on the southern part of the island, such as near the Astral Altar, as these attack with only melee. There are also three melee-only suqah on the south-west part of the island, over the bridge (abutting the city wall); specifically, a cannon can be placed directly north-west of the dead tree to target the melee-only suqah while avoiding the single mage-dealing suqah in the vicinity.

tactics.heading: Safespots
tactics.text:
Method 1: Bridge on Southern Lunar Isle

Notes:
• It's definitely worth considering adding this task to your slayer block list due to their poor drops and relatively slow kill time. Although it is an easy spot if you're just looking to AFK and don't mind using up runes/ammo.
• When standing on the safe tile if you move 1 step north it will cause the south-eastern Suqah to reset.
• When standing on the safe tile if you move 1 step south it will cause the northern Suqah to reset.
• It can actually be quite useful as if their positioning is bad and they come onto the bridge you only have to move 1 tile and they'll walk away enabling them to get stuck again.
• You can also get them stuck on the surrounding trees and other objects quite easily as they're 2x2 tiles in size and only attack with melee here.
• It might be worth grabbing 5 Suqah tooth while you're here for protecting Spirit Tree Patches.

Method 2: Northern Lunar Isle

Notes:
• Suqah's in the northern part of Lunar Isle can also attack using magic.
• Due to poor drops you will lose gp if cannoning.

gearNotes.heading: Equipment
gearNotes.text:
The Hueycoatl is vulnerable to the effects of dragonbane weapons and weakest to crush, so the dragon hunter lance outperforms all other crush weapons, barring a scythe of Vitur (if the player does not mind the upkeep cost). As the boss's auto-attacks barely deal any damage and the special attacks can be easily avoided, it is recommended to bring Inquisitor's armour for its accuracy and damage bonus. If not, bring the best strength-boosting equipment possible.

Due to the damage cap on Hueycoatl's tail, weapons that hit multiple times per attack, such as the dual macuahuitl or glacial temotli, are strongly recommended for the fight, as they will help speed up the phase significantly.

The Hueycoatl has a Defence level of 125, and Defence-draining effects will only drain up to 5 levels. Due to this, it is recommended to not bring them to the fight, and to prioritise damaging special attacks instead.

With best-in-slot gear, a solo kill should take around 8 minutes and 20 seconds on average, though this is primarily dependent on the duration of phase 3. In trio sizes, teams with sufficient gear can subdue the boss within 5 minutes.

gearNotes.heading: Inventory
gearNotes.text:
• Super combat potion, or super attack and super strength
• 1 prayer regeneration potion
• Prayer potions
• Food, such as sharks
• A special attack weapon, such as dragon claws or burning claws. For the tail phase, use an ursine chainmace
• A multi-hitting weapon for the tail, such as dual macuahuitl (which is further enhanced by Blood moon armour)
• Runes for resurrection spells and a Book of the Dead if on the Arceuus spellbook. Note: Death Charge only works if you get the last hit on the body or head; it does not work on the tail
• Imbued or saturated heart for Magic boost to increase thrall duration
• Holy wrench to make more effective use of prayer potions over long grinds

tactics.heading: Overview
tactics.text:
The Hueycoatl is a group boss located atop the Darkfrost in Varlamore, requiring only completion of Children of the Sun and having spoken to Taala at the base camp to fight. Players can enter the public area via the chain to fight the Hueycoatl with up to 20 players at once, or create a private instance at the meeting flag next to the bank buffalo. Creating a private group/solo instance costs 50,000 coins (25,000 if the player is eligible to claim the hard Combat Achievement rewards).

If the player dies while fighting the Hueycoatl, their grave will appear at the base camp.

The Chat-channel "Huey Host" can be used to find small teams.

"Varlamore PvM" worlds (340 and 517) are the designated worlds for the Hueycoatl masses. World 420, while not officially designated, is also often populated with a large amount of players killing the boss en masse.

tactics.heading: Recommendations
tactics.text:
• Moderate melee combat stats
  • Level 60 Attack or higher
  • Level 60 Strength or higher
  • Level 60 Defence or higher
  • Level 70 Hitpoints or higher
  • Level 43 Prayer for protection prayers
• Completion of The Heart of Darkness to acquire a Pendant of Ates

tactics.heading: Transportation
tactics.text:
The quickest methods of reaching the base camp are as follows:
• Using a Pendant of Ates to teleport to the Darkfrost, after activating the Statue of Ates just west of the base camp.
• Using the Quetzal Transport System to reach Quetzacalli Gorge, then running north-east through the gate and then north-west around the mountain.

tactics.heading: Starting the Fight
tactics.text:
Players can initiate the fight by climbing through the chains leading to the boss arena at any point they desire.

Entering the fight after phase 1 has been cleared will result in the player's contribution being significantly reduced.

The player can quick-peek the chain to see how many players are in the Hueycoatl's arena, along with the phase she is currently in:

• Fight not in progress: The Hueycoatl is preparing itself.
• Phase 1: The Hueycoatl's body can be seen on the mountainside.
• Phase 2: They have reached the summit.
• Phase 3: The Hueycoatl is defending itself with its tail.
• Phase 4: The Hueycoatl is making its final stand.

tactics.heading: Fight overview
tactics.text:
The Hueycoatl herself, her body, and her tail are all vulnerable to dragonbane weapons. Additionally, her stats do not scale with the quantity of players in the fight; thus, a fight consists of five body parts (with each having 250 health), the head itself (with 2,500 health), and the tail (with 300 health), requiring a total of 4,050 damage to clear the encounter.

The Hueycoatl will primarily use two attacks throughout the entire fight:
• Glowing symbols - these spawn around the ground near players. After 4 ticks, lightning will strike any player still standing on them for up to 16 damage.
• Rain Fire - the Hueycoatl will launch the feathers on her back on the team, and players must activate the corresponding protection prayer based on the colour of the incoming projectile. If correctly prayed against, the damage is reduced to 0-2; otherwise, the attacks deal up to 14 damage.
  • The red melee projectile's tail end is smoking.
  • The green ranged projectile moves toward the player without any noticeable animations.
  • The blue magic projectile spins as it moves toward the player.

tactics.heading: Phase one (body phase)
tactics.text:
Upon starting the fight, the path to the Hueycoatl herself is blocked, with a segment of her tail restricting access to the summit. There are five parts of the Hueycoatl's body that can be attacked, all of which must be defeated before the tail is forced to clear the way. Each body segment has 250 Hitpoints; they do not attack players.

Despite the body's appearance, it has a hitbox of 1x1, and it can be somewhat troublesome to click on it. On the Official Client, RuneLite and HDOS, players can hold the shift key and right-click "Tag-All" or "Mark object" in Runelite, to display the hitbox of the bodies.

tactics.heading: Phase two (head phase)
tactics.text:
Once the path to the summit opens, the Hueycoatl can be attacked directly. If the player has a thrall lingering from the previous phase, summon another one immediately regardless of its timer to position the thrall closer to the head, otherwise the original thrall will take some time to move up to the summit and engage the boss.

The seer will begin charging the three pillars located west of the head. Players can charge the blue, red, and green pillars by praying Protect from Magic, Protect from Melee, and Protect from Missiles respectively. The number of active prayers required to begin charging a pillar is based on the size of the team. To charge all 3 pillars, teams need to equally balance the number of players using each protection prayer. A team of 3 requires each player to use a unique protection prayer, while a team of 6 requires two players to use each prayer.

Each time the seer's yellow charge bar fills, he will check if the three pillars are full. At that time, if all three pillars are full (due to the active protection prayers being correctly balanced for the team's size), then the three braziers on top of the pillars will be lit. While the braziers are lit, players are given a 30% damage buff. When the seer's yellow charge bar fills again, if the three pillars are still full, the braziers will stay lit and the damage buff will remain active. If at least one pillar is draining (because the active protection prayers are no longer balanced) when the seer's yellow charge bar fills again, then the braziers will be extinguished and all players will lose the damage buff. This damage buff can be gained and lost multiple times per fight. The pillars can safely be temporarily drained while the seer's yellow charge bar is filling and players will retain the damage buff as long as the pillars are refilled before the yellow charge bar is full.

When running up to the mountain summit between the first phase and the second phase, it is common for players in teams to call out in the chat which prayer they will be responsible for during the fight. Teams can have the damage buff for the remainder of the fight by having each player camp their selected overhead prayer and tank the damage taken from the rain fire projectiles. Players can choose to quickly switch prayers to reduce damage taken from the rain fire projectiles, but should only do so when the seer's yellow charge bar is not close to being filled. If the seer's yellow charge bar is close to being filled, players should keep their balanced protection prayers active and tank the damage to prevent losing the damage buff, as the Hueycoatl's damage is inconsequential to the extra damage from the pillars.

Teams with only one or two players cannot meet the balanced active protection prayer requirement to charge all three pillars and therefore cannot earn the damage buff. In these circumstances, the seer, pillars, and braziers can be ignored. Instead, the player(s) should use their protection prayers to reduce damage from the rain fire projectiles.

The size of the team is based on all players within the arena, regardless their position or activity. Players who join or leave the arena mid-fight affect the team size instantly. This mechanic can be exploited by players who want the damage buff in a solo or duo by standing extra accounts near the entrance which can pray the other needed protection prayers. The accounts standing near the entrance will only be damaged by the rain fire attack, not the lightning and not the tail shockwave, in the last three phases and should be geared to tank the attack styles that they are not praying.

Upon reaching 50% or less health, the Hueycoatl will shield herself and become invulnerable to damage, and her tail will appear from the western cave entrance, starting the next phase.

tactics.heading: Phase three (tail phase)
tactics.text:
The Hueycoatl's tail has a shield that must be destroyed before she can be directly attacked again. The tail has only 300 hitpoints, but attacks made on the tail have a heavy damage cap which can significantly prolong the phase for small teams. Damage is usually capped at 4, but this can be increased to 9 if the player's crush attack bonus is their highest attack bonus, in addition to having all missed hits rounded up to 1 damage.

Once this phase begins, the player should try to keep their Hitpoints above 40 to avoid dying from being hit by the tail shockwave and an auto-attack or lightning strike at the same time.

Upon starting this phase, it is best to immediately swap to a weapon that is able to hit multiple times per attack; ideally the Blood moon armour set and dual macuahuitl will help speed up this phase significantly, given that its set effect will activate numerous times during the kill. If the player does not have the armour set, the macuahuitl will suffice; if the player does not have them, the glacial temotli are a reasonable alternative, as they possess the same attack speed as the macuahuitl of 4-ticks. If none of these are available, then Torag's hammers will do, though they attack a tick slower. Otherwise, simply continue using your normal weapons (provided the player's crush bonus is their highest attack bonus with that weapon equipped; see above). Thralls can also help in dealing extra damage, as do the special attacks of dragon/burning claws or the ursine chainmace, though these should not be used in trio and larger encounters as the phase is much shorter in groups, and the damage from special attacks would benefit more from increased pillar damage.

The tail will change sides approximately every 20 seconds. Attacks made during the transition will not damage it. Every time it reappears, it will slam the ground and send out a shockwave that deals 20-25 damage. Avoid it by running "through" the shockwave at the correct time; running diagonally through the wave is also an effective way to avoid it.

The standard method to avoid the shockwaves during this phase requires use of precise timing to skip over them, as seen below:

tactics.heading: Phase four (final phase)
tactics.text:
Once the tail is broken, the head of the Hueycoatl can be attacked once again.

The Hueycoatl's attack speed will significantly increase for the duration of this phase, so players should be mindful of the increased lightning strikes around the arena. In addition to the increased attack speed, the Hueycoatl's tail will continually send out shockwaves at a rate of one every ~15 or so seconds, requiring players to continually move to avoid getting struck by it. As with before, running diagonally towards the shockwave as shown above will avoid taking damage from it. If a player is not confident about their timing with the shockwaves, the two farthest tiles on both sides in the row in front of Hueycoatl provide safespots.

When the Hueycoatl is defeated, players can resupply at the bank buffalo if needed, by sliding down the slope to the east. Otherwise, she will "respawn" in 30 seconds. Any players at the summit when she fully recovers will be knocked back down to the starting point, so if staying for more kills, it is recommended to return to the start so players can immediately start attacking the Hueycoatl's body parts without delay.

gearNotes.heading: Equipment
gearNotes.text:
• With Masori armour and without access to ascension crossbows, the Zaryte crossbow is best in slot against the Leviathan until it reaches 450 HP (380 without a venator ring), at which point the toxic blowpipe with dragon darts surpasses it.
• The bow of Faerdhinen (with crystal armour) and the twisted bow don't have the damage falloff or chip damage of ruby bolts (e), and are better than the toxic blowpipe with amethyst darts.
• When inside the abyssal pathfinder, all ranged weapons cannot miss and deal a minimum hit of 20% of their maximum, making faster weapons such as the ascension crossbows and toxic blowpipe particularly effective for the enrage phase if the player can maintain their fast attack speed. Webweaver bow special attacks may also be used after the abyssal pathfinder activates to deal a large amount of damage quickly.
• The Zaryte crossbow with ruby bolts offers the strongest spec weapon at Leviathan, and using it at the beginning of the fight leads to faster kills overall.

Due to the Tumeken's shadow's passive effect boosting its accuracy, it can compete with and outperform lower-tier range weapons at the Leviathan. Additionally, with access to a volatile Nightmare staff, damage can be boosted through use of its special attack on the Leviathan's backside after stunning it.

Without access to several pieces of Ancestral equipment and/or a saturated heart, players should consider ranging the Leviathan instead.

gearNotes.heading: Inventory recommendations
gearNotes.text:
• Armadyl brew can provide ranged boost, slot-efficient healing and overhealing.
• Prayer potions or super restores (can replace food with more potions if experienced)
• Ring of shadows for teleporting back, or Amulet of the Eye if scarred tablet has not been acquired yet
• Anglerfish are for boosting health before starting a kill to lessen interruptions during the volley of attacks, as well as chip damage from the roar attack
• Shadow Rush is just as effective as Shadow Barrage in stunning the boss, whilst costing only a third per spell cast
• A magic staff with autocast can be used to auto-cast Shadow spells. Thammaron's sceptre is a lighter weight option. Manually casting a spell is the same number of clicks, with the bonuses of saving an inventory slot and having a bigger click box in the spellbook tab by filtering out spells you lack the runes to cast.
• Twisted bow can optionally be used for the backside attack, as it usually deals higher damage than crossbow attacks due to the vastly increased minimum hit, especially with a Dizana's quiver so as to not require two inventory slots

tactics.heading: Overview
tactics.text:
After the completion of Desert Treasure II - The Fallen Empire, players can fight a stronger variant of the Leviathan. An even stronger awakened variant can be fought by climbing the handholds with an awakener's orb in the player's inventory and selecting "Yes" when prompted.

If the player dies while fighting the Leviathan, their grave will appear in the Scar by the rowboat. Players will have their reclamation fee reduced by 75% until they have five kills, after which the standard death cost will apply.

tactics.heading: Requirements
tactics.text: • Completion of Quest Desert Treasure II - The Fallen Empire

tactics.heading: Suggested skills
tactics.text:
• 75+ Ranged
• 70+ Defence
• 80+ Hitpoints

tactics.heading: Transportation
tactics.text:
The quickest methods of reaching the Scar, where the Leviathan resides, are:
• Using the ring of shadows to teleport to the Scar, by the abyssal rift. This requires having used the scarred tablet on it, which is a 1/25 drop from the Leviathan.
• Teleporting to the Temple of the Eye via the Amulet of the Eye (or the Minigame Teleport for the Guardians of the Rift minigame), then reaching the Scar via the Catalytic Guardian.
• Reaching the Temple of the Eye via the portal in the Wizards' Tower basement (necklace of passage teleport or fairy ring code dis).

tactics.heading: Fight overview
tactics.text:
The Leviathan uses a volley of rapid-firing attacks which deal damage upon impact; protection prayers will fully block these attacks. The lure on its head will change colours accordingly as another indicator of the attack style it is using.

Alongside the orb attacks, the Leviathan can also utilise a biting attack when in melee range, which Protect from Melee will fully block. This is rarely used since it interrupts the volley sequence, but it has no warning animation. It will only be used if the player is directly next to the pool (including diagonal tiles), and it is recommended to mark these tiles to avoid running into them.

At the end of each volley, the boss will roar and cause debris to fall around the arena, with one falling down on the player's location as a permanent spawn for the remainder of the fight. Players will take up to 7 chip damage from the roar but can avoid the debris by moving at least 1 tile away. Every subsequent volley of attacks will increase in intensity, which can make it difficult to switch prayers at later volleys. The sequence of attacks are as follows:
• 3 tick attacks with magic and ranged
• 2 tick attacks with magic and ranged
• 2 tick attacks with all three styles
• 1 tick attacks with magic and ranged
• 1 tick attacks with all three styles
• All three styles with faster projectile time (2 ticks to react)
• All three styles with even faster projectile time (1 tick to react)

At any point during the volley of attacks, players can cast any type of shadow spell to stun the Leviathan, where it will stay still for 15 ticks (9 seconds). Damage against it is capped at 10 when stunned, but the player can run around to attack the gaping wound on its backside. When attacking the backside with ranged, it deals at least a minimum of ~65% of your maximum hit as damage, whereas attacking with magic is not guaranteed to hit and is subject to the usual accuracy rolls, but will deal double damage. Using Tumeken's shadow during this mechanic can be a highly effective way to reliably deal 100+ damage, especially if stunning right before triggering enrage. The Leviathan will break out of its stun when this occurs and use a special attack as retaliation.

Leviathan will progress down this list, of attack styles, throughout the fight whether you stun or not!

If you:

Stun and attack the gaping wound on The Leviathan's back

- OR -

Stun and have done 25% of The Leviathan's health in damage

The Leviathan will reset to the 2nd attack style on the list and then progress downwards again. This will then repeat resetting to the 3rd on your second stun, so on and so forth until The Leviathan reaches its fastest attack. This means you should use your shadow spells to stun sparingly.

tactics.heading: Special attacks
tactics.text:
• Lightning Barrage - The Leviathan unleashes a barrage of lightning towards the player while also launching orbs around it. The orbs will land across the arena, but never on the tiles surrounding the pool and have a 1x1 AoE. Run in a tight circle to stay ahead of the electric stroke (it can also be dodged with precise movement whilst also attacking it; see the demonstrations below). Once the attack ends, step away from melee range to prevent it from using its bite attack.
• Smoke Blast - The Leviathan begins to spit out debris that falls onto the player's location every tick. The debris take two ticks to land, so players can stand still for one tick on each tile if they want to attack. After throwing ten debris, it will discharge a blast of smoke that can be avoided by standing behind the debris left behind. Getting caught in the blast will deal up to 59 damage. Beginning the enrage phase during this special attack will NOT interrupt the smoke blast.

Damage dealt to the Leviathan is reduced by 33% for the duration of each special attack.

Players can determine which special attack will be used first in the fight after the first roar by observing where the debris remains, assuming that the Leviathan was not stunned before a volley ended. If the debris appears to the east and west, then the Lightning Barrage attack is used first. If the debris appears to the north and south, then the Smoke Blast attack is used instead. The boss will alternate between the two special attacks.

tactics.heading: Enrage phase
tactics.text:
Upon reaching 180 hitpoints (20% of its health), the Leviathan will begin to focus on the player intensely, beginning the enrage phase. It will roar, causing one set of debris to drop on the arena, while an abyssal pathfinder will spawn. The abyssal pathfinder will spawn in the north-west corner of the arena, unless the spawn tile is blocked by debris. If blocked, it will instead spawn in the next corner following a clockwise pattern, unless all four spawn tiles are blocked, which will cause it to spawn in the original north-west corner. The Leviathan will also change its attack speed to 2, (i.e. 1.2 seconds) between attacks regardless of the state it was in before the phase started. It will only use magic and ranged orbs in this state, though it can still bite players if they are next to it.

The abyssal pathfinder has a 5x5 Area-of-Effect that the player must stand in; if the player is not in its AoE, the Leviathan's attacks will pierce through protection prayers and the player's attacks will deal less damage. The player will glow when they are within the pathfinder's AoE, and will be granted perfect accuracy and an increased minimum hit, so switching to a toxic blowpipe can be beneficial for its increased attack speed. Attacking with magic instead of ranged while within the pathfinder's AoE will grant doubled damage instead of perfect accuracy.

Players who have a webweaver bow can instead use the special attack twice to immediately finish it off, however in most cases a lightbearer will not be able to restore back to full energy for the next kill. This approach is not recommended for players with a zaryte crossbow, and players using the crossbow should bring a toxic blowpipe switch in place of the webweaver bow.

Until the phase ends, debris will continually drop from above, including the permanent blocker debris, so it is important to defeat the boss before too many appear and restrict movement. Once the Leviathan is slain, all debris on the field will be removed.

tactics.heading: Awakened mode
tactics.text:
In Awakened mode, the Leviathan has the following changes:
• The boss's health increases from 900 to 2,700.
• The boss is immune to stat drains.
• Upon reaching 50% of its health, a tornado will spawn in the arena and move towards the player. This will deal 40+ damage if it makes contact with them.
• The permanent blocker debris is increased, from one to five dropped in a "+" style formation on the player.
• Stuns are 50% shorter in length.
• Its enraged attack speed is doubled to one tick (0.6s)
• The range of the abyssal pathfinder is increased to 7x7 tiles
• Damage from the smoke blast increases from 59 to 70+ damage.
• The black mask and Slayer helmet do not apply their usual on-task damage and accuracy bonuses while on a Leviathan boss slayer task.

Rather than letting the Leviathan finish an attack sequence, it is highly recommended to stun it before it ends. This is because the boulders will drop in a +- shaped formation on the player, which will severely impede movement if allowed to appear; likely resulting in death in the enrage phase. This also ensures minimal damage is taken until the enrage phase, as the player is expected to take no damage from the lightning current or shockwave attacks. As the boss's magic level is significantly increased from 160 to 280, a twisted bow is the preferred weapon of choice over a crossbow, since it will fully benefit from its passive effect.

Stunning the Leviathan resets the player's attack delay, meaning you can attack immediately after casting barrage to get a free ranged shot every stun before Levi's damage reduction kicks in.

Once the tornado appears at 50% health (1350 health), lightning runs are a bit different. Rather than running back and forth, as this would result in the player running into the tornado, the player needs to utilise two additional tiles to safely evade the tornado while maintaining attacks. This is not required, as the player can simply run clockwise or counterclockwise respectively to attack and avoid the tornado. During the debris attack, each quadrant can allow for two instances of each attack before being unusable; during the first instance for each quadrant, run two tiles to leave a gap between it and the next thrown debris, so that the player can simply walk between them for the second instance of the attack. When it is no longer possible to do this, simply fill a row or column accordingly at the edges of the arena. The majority of damage will be primarily dealt during the lightning current attack.

When rushing in to stun the Leviathan, make sure to swap to Protect from Melee to avoid any potential bite attacks. To avoid any unnecessary chip damage from incoming attacks as the enrage phase starts, leave the boss as close as possible to 20% of its health, then stun and hit from behind. Before starting the enrage phase, make sure to have max health and prayer. It is also encouraged to leave the north-west clear of debris to ensure the pathfinder spawns there and luring the tornado as south as possible to get a head-start once starting the phase, as it is important not to let it trail close to the player.

During the enrage phase (540 health), dump two webweaver specials upon being lit by the pathfinder, which should reduce the boss's health to ~360 and return to a twisted bow and continue attacking the boss while moving and reacting to incoming attacks. While a toxic blowpipe can be used for higher DPS with its attack speed, the boss's even faster attack speed and the tornado, along with having to flick the attacks, dodging the tornado and being in sync with the pathfinder makes this highly unfeasible. Make sure to stay away from the boss's melee distance to ensure that it will not bite, as there is a high chance of dying if a melee attack and an unprotected orb hit in a small time frame. The player should have enough time to defeat the boss before the pathfinder completes a full cycle, though this also depends on how much the boss will swap between combat styles.

With a Twisted bow and max ranged, Masori has ~9% higher DPS during the fight, while Void is ~9% stronger during Enrage. It's recommended to bring both and swap to void before enrage.
