gearNotes.heading: Equipment
gearNotes.text:
Using magic alongside the dragon claws will allow the player to kill the Mimic relatively quickly. High-levelled players should have little difficulty defeating the mimic with high-end gear.
The player should always use Protect from Melee and move around the room when the Mimic throws sweets, and the player should ignore the spawned Third Age minions. Protect from Melee should be activated before the player enters the instance. The player should use stat-boosting potions and the invigorate option of the imbued/saturated heart before entering the instance. The player should enter the fight in full melee gear and use both the dragon claws special attacks (can be substituted with burning claws or a dragon dagger if the player does not have dragon claws).
For lower-levelled players, it is helpful to freeze the Mimic in place with Entangle or ice spells, which renders the Mimic unable to use melee attacks or the stomp attack as long as you are standing away from it.

gearNotes.heading: Inventory
gearNotes.text:
As the fight is relatively short, a full inventory of food and potions is not necessary. For lower-levelled players, increase the number of prayer-restoring potions and food, and consider bringing freeze spells.
• Special attack weapon (optional)
• Melee switch (optional)
• Runes for Entangle or ice spells (optional)
• 1 divine super combat potion (if bringing a melee switch)
• 1 super restore or prayer potion
• 4–6 anglerfish
• Emergency teleport
• Saturated heart or Imbued heart or magic potion
• Watson teleport scroll
Though the Mimic is weak to magic, using ranged alongside the dragon claws will still allow the player to kill the Mimic relatively quickly. High-levelled players should have little difficulty defeating the mimic with high-end gear.

The player should always use Protect from Melee and move around the room when the Mimic throws sweets, and the player should ignore the spawned Third Age minions. Protect from Melee should be activated before the player enters the instance. The player should use stat-boosting potions before entering the instance. The player should enter the fight in full melee gear and use both the dragon claws special attacks (can be substituted with a dragon dagger if the player does not have dragon claws).

gearNotes.heading: Inventory
gearNotes.text:
As the fight is relatively short, a full inventory of food and potions is not necessary. For lower-levelled players, increase the number of prayer-restoring potions and food. Lower-levelled players should also consider bringing a stamina potion, as running around the room will drain run energy.
• Special attack weapon (optional)
• Melee switch (optional)
• 1 divine super combat potion
• 1 divine ranging potion
• 1 super restore or prayer potion
• 4–6 anglerfish
• Emergency teleport
• Watson teleport scroll
If you are an ironman or do not meet the minimum requirement for using Magic (Trident of the Seas or better powered staff), the fight is much easier using the Protect from Magic prayer against the Third Age Mage, utilizing melee gear to tank the Mimic, Third Age Warrior, and Third Age Ranger. Using Super strength and Super attack potions with Piety will typically do similar or more DPS than an average mage set using the Warped sceptre. This makes the fight much easier as you have more damage resistance and allows players to take more food for their first few kills, or until better magic switches or a more powerful powered staff is obtained.
The player should start with Protect from Melee until the Mimic throws a set of sweets which spawn the Third Age Mage, swapping then to Protect from Magic. Like the other strategies, ignore the Third Age minions. The player should enter the fight fully potted up and ready to use their best special attack weapon. Ensure Piety or your best melee boosting prayer is active for the duration of the fight.
Despite the Mimic's slight weakness to crush, a slash weapon will still typically outperform them.

gearNotes.heading: Inventory
gearNotes.text:
Two prayer potions should be enough for the entire kill duration, keeping Piety and Protect from Magic up the entire time. Fill your inventory with the best food you have access to, along with some Cooked karambwan so you can combo eat to maximize your healing while minimizing downtime. Keep auto retaliate off to avoid running to the spawned minions, and move around the room to keep from getting backed into a corner when the Mimic steps onto you, preventing unnecessary damage. You may wish to use the nearby Hosidius Kitchen to bank and pre-pot a Super defence.
• Special attack weapon
• 1 Super combat potion or 1 of each Super attack potion, Super strength potion
• 2 super restore, prayer potion, or Moonlight moth mix
• Best food available
• Cooked karambwan for combo eating
• Emergency teleport
• Travel method to Watson's house
• Mimic

tactics.heading: Overview
tactics.text: Upon completion of an elite or master clue scroll, the casket received has a chance of turning out to be a mimic chest. Mimic caskets can only be obtained from an elite or master reward casket after asking the strange casket to enable the chance to obtain a mimic casket (which is disabled by default). If players have not talked to the strange casket when they receive their first elite or master reward casket, they may choose whenever both casket types can roll for a mimic or not.

tactics.heading: Attacks
tactics.text:
The Mimic uses several attacks throughout the duration of the fight.

• Melee attack: The Mimic can hit you with a normal melee attack if you are standing beside it.
• Candy attack: The Mimic throws six candies at you. If you fail to step out of the way, you will receive about 10 damage. Three candies are purple, and there is one red, one blue and one green candy. The red, blue and green candies spawn the Third Age Warrior, Third Age Mage, and Third Age Ranger respectively. There is no benefit to killing them as they drop nothing and, when killed, they instantly respawn when another candy attack occurs.
• Stomp Attack: Sometimes, The Mimic will step one tile forward onto you. Alternatively, this attack is activated when you walk under The Mimic. For every tick (0.6 seconds) that you stand under The Mimic, you will receive damage. The damage scales as follows: 1-1-1-2-2-2-3-... and so on, capping out at 6 damage. Simply step away from The Mimic to stop and reset the damage counter.

tactics.heading: Suggested skills
tactics.text:
• 80+ Magic (Magic method)
• 90+ Ranged (Ranged method)
• 80+ Attack (Special attack)
• 80+ Strength (Special attack)
• 70+ Defence
• 45+ Prayer (74+ with Ranged)

options.text: Dual macuahuitl / Ursine chainmace (u) / Zamorakian hasta
Zombie axe / Sarachnis cudgel / Osmumten's fang
Elder maul / Saradomin godsword / Crimson kisten
Tumeken's shadow / Eye of Ayak / Harmonised Nightmare staff
Mage's book / Ancient wyvern shield / Malediction ward

gearNotes.heading: Equipment
gearNotes.text: Note that The Nightmare is not undead, therefore items such as Salve amulet will have no effect on her.

gearNotes.heading: Equipment
gearNotes.text:
• Upgrades to melee gear should be prioritised over magic gear upgrades.
• Using an alt account will allow for higher kill trips, as you can trade supplies or cast Energy Transfer between kills.
• If you are tanking, ensure that you have the highest defence bonus of all players in the group. Easy ways to ensure this are to wear Guardian boots over Avernic treads (max), wear Torva armour over Inquisitor's armour, wear Barrows gloves over Ferocious gloves.
Keep in mind to keep Piety activated at all times and only bring a magic armour switch if everyone else in the group is also doing so.
• All players not using a Dragon warhammer should use their Saradomin godsword special on the sleepwalkers that spawn between phases.
• In smaller group sizes, substitute some Anglerfish and Divine super combat potions for regular Super combat potions and Saradomin brews.
• Consider bringing an Amulet of blood fury when learning the boss for the passive healing effect, however this will increase supply costs per kill and slightly lower your DPS.
• If using thralls, the ghost (Magic) thrall is the best to use because it benefits from the double damage on totems.

As the Totems possess no stats, magic accuracy is not beneficial. Add magic damage switches when possible as all magic damage is increased significantly.
As the pillars have no defence, only armour with magic damage bonus has any effect. It's also strongly suggested to bring a Saturated heart if using a Powered staff.

gearNotes.heading: Equipment
gearNotes.text:
• Gear progression for solos is the same as that for 5 man
• As kills will be long, replacing Ancestral robes with extra Saradomin brews is advised to allow for more mistakes.
• Use a Crimson kisten special against the boss whenever your special attack regenerates, except for in Phase 2/the end of Phase 1 where they should be used against the Parasites.
• Switch to the Crimson kisten to kill any Husks that spawn or Parasites that you do not have enough special attack for. Alternatively, use the Inquisitor's mace or no switch at all, however the scythe has poor DPS against these spawns.
• During Phase 2, walk underneath The Nightmare just before the parasite bursts out. This happens roughly 5 bludgeon/mace attacks or 4 scythe attacks after the parasite attack lands. If the parasite spawns underneath the boss, it will be unable to heal the boss until it moves. Use this to kill any parasites that spawn and reduce their healing.
• Prayer flicking piety during the kill will save a significant number of prayer points, this can allow you to bring more brews.
• Using an Amulet of blood fury is recommended for learning solo kills and will reduce the need for brews substantially, since kills are long and The Nightmare does low overall DPS against you.
• The Sanguinesti staff is especially useful for healing the player since magic damage against the totems is doubled. As a result, it is recommended to use the Sanguinesti staff when learning solo kills.
• If using thralls, the ghost (Magic) thrall is the best to use because it benefits from the double damage on totems.

tactics.heading: Overview
tactics.text: The Nightmare is a group boss located in the Sisterhood Sanctuary, a dungeon beneath Slepe in Morytania.

tactics.heading: Requirements
tactics.text: • Completion of Quest Priest in Peril to access Morytania.

tactics.heading: Recommendations
tactics.text:
• High combat stats. Although not required, see the skill levels below for an indication of the advised stats:
  • Level 85 Attack or higher
  • Level 85 Strength or higher
  • Level 85 Defence or higher
  • Level 85 Magic or higher
  • Level 85 Hitpoints or higher
  • Level 70 Prayer or higher
• Completion of Quest A Taste of Hope for the Drakan's Medallion, which is the quickest teleportation method
  • Alternatively, completion of Quest Ghost Ahoy for the ectophial, which is the second quickest teleportation method.

tactics.heading: Transportation
tactics.text:
The five quickest methods of reaching Slepe, where Phosani's Nightmare resides, are (from fastest to slowest):
• Teleporting directly to Slepe via Drakan's medallion after unlocking this teleport via Slepey tablet, which is a drop from Phosani's Nightmare.
• Using the Spider cave teleport will put you north-west of Slepe.
• Teleporting to Hallowed Sepulchre using a Hallowed crystal shard, then running east to Slepe via an agility shortcut that requires 63 Agility and installing 2 Long ropes
• Teleporting to Ver Sinhaza via Drakan's medallion, then running north. Once players pass the small dock, run east to arrive at Slepe.
• Using the Ectophial to teleport to the Ectofuntus, then heading north to the small dock and paying Andras 10,000 coins to row to Slepe. The player will arrive at a dock just south-west of Slepe.

tactics.heading: Starting the fight
tactics.text:
Players can initiate the fight by disturbing The Nightmare while she is in her sleeping state.

If there is already a fight in progress, The Nightmare will be seen in a floating state with a glowing symbol on the ground beneath her. During this state, the symbol will indicate which of the 3 phases the current fight is in:

If The Nightmare is already in her floating state, players will need to wait for the current fight to finish as her instance is not joinable mid-fight. Alternatively, players can hop to look for potentially available worlds.

tactics.heading: Mechanics
tactics.text: The Nightmare's mechanics scale accordingly to the amount of players present when the fight starts. By default, she automatically scales her shield and totem charge to that of a 5-man encounter, and thus team sizes below that will use this value.

tactics.heading: Shields and Totems
tactics.text:
Players do not damage the Nightmare's physical health directly - instead, they must break her shield during each of her three phases, after which players can attack four totems in each corner of the boss room.

• The Nightmare has a minimum shield durability of 2,000 per phase, capping at 19,600. This value increases by 200 from the base amount for every player in a six man or greater encounter.
• The totems have a minimum charge requirement of 300, capping at 2,640. This value increases by 30 from the base amount for every player in a six man or greater encounter.
• The amount of sleepwalkers present during phase transitions will gradually increase with more players present in the arena.

Once the shield is shattered, players must stop attacking the Nightmare (as their attacks will have no effect on her) and must instead charge the totems around the corners of the arena. When all four totems are fully charged, they will unleash a magical blast of energy onto the Nightmare, dealing 800 damage to her. The Nightmare has 2,400 physical health, and does not regenerate it, so three blasts will end the encounter. After the first 800 damage, the Nightmare will be in phase 2, and after the second blast of 800 damage, the Nightmare will be in phase 3, also known as the final phase.

The totems cannot be leeched off of with blood spells. However, the Sanguinesti Staff's and amulet of blood fury effects do work. Players do not receive any experience for dealing damage to the totems, and they will take two times as much damage if struck with magic.

tactics.heading: Standard attacks
tactics.text:
Players can use protection prayers to mitigate damage from some of The Nightmare's attacks, in a manner similar to the Great Olm - attacks that are successfully prayed against will deal less damage, while an attack that is incorrectly prayed against will result in more damage; 120% of her maximum hit for her melee attack. This may also be the case with her Magic and Ranged attacks but has yet to be confirmed.

The Nightmare has a unique aggression mechanic in which she determines the highest Defence roll out of all five types for each player in her dream world, and will immediately focus on the player with the highest overall value. This in turn makes her melee attack only hit in the direction she is facing.

• Ranged attack: The Nightmare will contort herself and shoot out projectiles toward players; having game sounds enabled will help as this attack performs a loud clicking sound per contortion. Players have 3 ticks (1.8s) to react with Protect from Missiles.
• Magic attack: The Nightmare will flail to the side surrounding herself with pink flower petals, then spin back shooting the petals toward players. Players have 3 ticks (1.8s) to react with Protect from Magic.
• Melee attack: The Nightmare will charge her claws and quickly slashes forward. Players have 2 ticks (1.2s) to react with Protect from Melee.
  • Melee damage is dealt to everyone in front (including diagonally across) as well as under her. This attack will always hit regardless of the player's defensive bonuses, but it can be avoided by simply being in a direction the Nightmare is not facing or walking one tile away if facing her.

tactics.heading: Special attacks
tactics.text:
• Grasping Claws: The Nightmare will spawn a black portal underneath her, and numerous smaller "end" portals before sticking her claws inside. If the player stands on any portal, they will take up to 50 damage. Simply move into a tile free of a black portal to avoid damage. The Nightmare uses this attack during all three phases.
• Sleepwalkers: At the start of the second and final phases, the Nightmare will summon sleepwalkers that walk toward her, the number of which is dependent upon the number of players in the instance, ranging from 1-24. They possess 10 health, but instantly die upon taking any damage. At the end of this attack, she will charge up a power blast that hits all players in the room for a minimum of 5 damage. The more sleepwalkers she absorbs, the more damaging the power blast becomes, capable of dealing over 70 damage to each player in masses. This damage is unavoidable, so kill as many sleepwalkers as possible before they reach the Nightmare. In a solo encounter, if the player doesn't kill the sleepwalker, the power blast will always result in death.
• Husks: The Nightmare spawns two husks around random players in her arena. The targeted players will be frozen in place until the husks are killed. The blue, skinny husk uses magic attacks, while the green, bulky husk uses ranged attacks. The Nightmare will not spawn Grasping Claws portals under players that are frozen by the husks, however if the player is under the Nightmare while frozen by husks they will still take damage. The Nightmare only uses this attack during phase 1.
• Corpse Flowers: The Nightmare will divide the room into four equal quadrants with lines of flowers. One quadrant will be safe as indicated with white nightmare flowers, while the remaining quadrants are unsafe as indicated with red nightmare berries. The safe quadrant is the one with both sides having nightmare flowers. If the player is standing on a quadrant with nightmare berries, they will rapidly attack the player for up to 20 damage every tick. The Nightmare will heal for double the amount they deal, and any attacks made from an incorrect quadrant will also heal her. This attack is only used during phase 1.
  • Standing on a quadrant with only nightmare berries will cause players to take twice as much damage as the berries on both sides will attack them.
• Curse: A pink glow fills the player's screen and protection prayers are shuffled. Clicking on Protect from Magic activates Protect from Missiles, Protect from Missiles activates Protect from Melee and Protect from Melee activates Protect from Magic. After 5 attacks, the curse is lifted. The Nightmare only uses this attack during phase 2.
• Parasites: The Nightmare throws a parasite onto random players. After ~18 ticks (10.8s), it will grow and burst out of the player, dealing massive damage, and will then begin healing the Nightmare until killed. Drinking a dose of Sanfew serum or Relicym's balm before it emerges will weaken the parasite and greatly reduce the damage taken when the parasite bursts out. The Nightmare only uses this attack during phase 2. Players may click the Hitpoints Orb to weaken the Parasite instead of clicking the potion within their inventory as well.
• Surge: The Nightmare will teleport to one of the four edges of the room, then immediately surge across to the opposite side dealing up to 60 damage to anyone caught in her path. Move out of the way to avoid taking damage. The Nightmare only uses this attack during phase 3.
• Spores: Puffshroom like objects spawn around the arena. Standing within 1 tile of one will cause it to explode, causing the player to become weary; their run is disabled and their attack speed is increased by 1 tick for a short duration. The Nightmare only uses this attack during phase 3.

tactics.heading: Fight overview
tactics.text:
Players should pre-pot with an Anglerfish and a sip of a stamina potion before running over to the Nightmare from a bank. Players should also be familiar with the Nightmare's mechanics, especially which special attacks are used during each phase, and how to take down all of the Sleepwalkers that spawn between phases. When bringing a team, it's not uncommon to designate players to specific sections of the arena, to more consistently deal with all of the Sleepwalkers. In larger teams, consider bringing Blood Barrage on one or more players, to dispatch multiple Sleepwalkers at once. If in a smaller team, such as a duo, if one player dies, the remaining player must deal sufficient damage, or they will be automatically teleported out of the instance, with a message saying, "The nightmare grows tired of your poor efforts."

The Nightmare is susceptible to defence-reducing special attacks, such as dragon warhammer's, but her Defence level cannot be reduced below 120, and she will restore her defence stat back at the rate of 20 defence per minute.

As the Nightmare has extremely high shield charge, players soloing the boss generally do so for the sake of Combat Achievements or practising for Phosani's Nightmare, as each solo kill generally takes well over 16 minutes. If the boss is being fought solo, an amulet of blood fury and/or Sanguinesti staff is required to counter all chip damage incurred during the fight.

Unlike most bosses, the Nightmare prioritises her targets based on their Defence level and defence bonuses from worn equipment. She will select the highest values of both of these. For example, a player wearing full justiciar will be targeted over a player using oathplate armour. Therefore, a "designated" tank can be assigned by simply having the tank use high defence equipment to ensure she only focuses on them. All players who are not designated as the tank should stay away from the direction the boss is facing so they do not get hit with melee.

tactics.heading: Phase 1
tactics.text:
During this phase, the Nightmare will use the special attacks Grasping Claws, Husks, and Corpse Flowers. Deal with these special attacks while continuing to have the correct prayer active.

Players immobilised by Husks will usually not have a portal spawn under them during the Grasping Claws attack, and the Nightmare does not seem to use the Corpse Flowers attack while players are immobilised. During the Corpse Flowers attack, be aware of where your tank is - players who end up on the same side of the Nightmare as the tank will need to be aware that they can be hit by the Nightmare's melee attack afterward, and should move or pray accordingly.

After depleting the Nightmare's shield, the totems will become vulnerable. The Nightmare will continue using its phase 1 attacks while you attack the totems. Fully charge all four and they will damage the Nightmare for 1/3rd of its health, and begin phase 2.

In this phase, be cautious of fully charging all of the totems if the Nightmare has not recently used her Husks attack. If she spawns Husks as the Totems fully charge, it can result in one or more players being immobilised while the Sleepwalkers spawn at the start of the next phase, possibly leading to the party taking massive damage from her power blast. It is recommended for immobilised players to use their magic weapon to kill the Sleepwalkers to prevent the party from taking massive damage.

If players bring a Saradomin godsword they can use a special attack on the Sleepwalkers to restore health and prayer.

tactics.heading: Phase 2
tactics.text:
The Nightmare will use her Sleepwalker attack at the start of this phase, and will deal considerable damage to your party if not all of the Sleepwalkers she spawns are killed. This is a good time to restore some HP and Prayer with a saradomin godsword special attack, if you brought one.

During this phase, the Nightmare will use the special attacks Grasping Claws, Curse, and Parasites.

The Nightmare will spit out parasites from her mouth, which will then fly towards random player(s) in the arena based on the group size. When this occurs, the player's Hitpoints icon will turn pink. If the player does not drink a dose of Relicym's balm or Sanfew serum before the parasite bursts from the player, they will take massive damage, and the parasite will be stronger, spawning with 80 hitpoints and slightly more defensive values compared to a weakened parasite. If the player does drink one of these two in time, the damage dealt is much less, and the parasite will have 40 hitpoints instead.

Parasites will attempt to support the Nightmare, periodically launching blasts of energy that restores her shield by 31-50 units. They will also do the same for totems if the totem phase is initiated. If none of these are available, the parasite will attack the player instead, starting with ranged and alternating between it and magic until something is damaged.

Parasites are extremely annoying in this phase, especially in solo encounters since the player will likely have to deal with multiple parasite specials in a row.

tactics.heading: Phase 3
tactics.text:
This phase begins with a Sleepwalker attack, just like the last one. Deal with it normally, optionally healing on the Sleepwalkers using your Saradomin godsword or Blood Barrage.

During this phase, the Nightmare will use the special attacks Grasping Claws, Spores, and Surge. Spores will be scattered in set patterns around the arena, and while they have a 1x1 appearance, they actually have a 3x3 AoE. Getting in a spore's AoE will cause it to burst, making whoever triggered it lethargic, disabling their run and decreasing their attack speed by 1 tick for a short duration. This can spread to other players, so avoid infecting them with spores.

It's common that the Nightmare will use her Grasping Claws attack while some spores are still active. Whenever spores are active, figure out beforehand which square(s) you can walk to so that you'll dodge a Grasping Claws portal without triggering any spores.

After the Nightmare's shields are depleted, simply charge all four totems for one final time while continuing to avoid her phase 3 special attacks, and the Nightmare will be defeated.

options.text: Ahrim's hood / Blue Moon helm > Bloodbark helm
Rada's blessing 4 / Any arrow (if using Venator bow)
Harmonised Nightmare staff > Eye of Ayak
Ahrim's robetop / Blue Moon chestplate > Bloodbark body
Ancient wyvern shield / Malediction ward / Mage's book
Ahrim's robeskirt / Blue Moon tassets > Bloodbark legs

gearNotes.heading: Equipment
gearNotes.text:
Magic is the most effective way to defeat the Whisperer, due to her high ranged defense and her very powerful melee attack.

The Whisperer has a relevant weakness to earth; Earth spells (with the tome of earth) often perform better than powered staves, especially at lower levels and with less gear available, though being on the standard spellbook loses a significant amount of damage from Thralls.

Special weapon options are limited. The best (and expensive) option is the eldritch Nightmare staff, which restores prayer upon a successful hit. The accursed sceptre or eye of Ayak can be used to lower the boss' stats, though this reduction is reset when enrage phase begins.

Bring a fast ranged weapon for souls phase. Darts or blowpipes are sufficient to clear the high priority souls, while the (far more expensive) venator bow can clear every soul.

gearNotes.heading: Inventory recommendations
gearNotes.text:
• Blackstone fragment
• Saturated heart or forgotten brews
• Special attack weapon
  • An accursed sceptre helps reduce the boss's Magic level if it hits, making kills a bit faster, though this is completely optional. Otherwise, an eldritch Nightmare staff will help sustain trips far longer.
    • The boss also drops a single 3-dose prayer potion and 2-dose ancient brew, which helps sustain trips even longer.
• Venator bow (with cheap arrows) or another fast ranged weapon for Lost Souls
• Rune pouch and Book of the Dead for thralls, or runes for ice spells (up to player preference)
  • If using the standard spellbook, bring runes for your strongest earth spell; the Book of the Dead and Explorer's ring can be replaced with another super restore and runes for High Level Alchemy
• Ring of shadows for teleporting if sirenic tablet has been acquired
  • Mind altar teleports are the next best alternative for those without a sirenic tablet.
• Fill rest of inventory with prayer potions or super restores (can replace with more food and/or combo eats, i.e. cooked karambwan, if inexperienced)
  • Bluefin may be brought in place of other regular food to hold even more prayer, if desired.
  • An Explorer's ring 4 can be helpful to alchemise the dragon plateskirts that are dropped at a rate of 1/100.
• The boss drops plenty of manta rays to help sustain food, assuming the player does not make too many mistakes. Even then, a single small mistake is often recovered with the Soul Siphon mechanic.

tactics.heading: Overview
tactics.text:
After the completion of Desert Treasure II - The Fallen Empire, players can fight a stronger variant of the Whisperer than the one fought during the quest. An even stronger, awakened variant can be fought by disturbing the Odd Figure with an awakener's orb in the player's inventory and selecting "Yes" when prompted in a fresh instance - having obtained an orb in the instance will not cause the prompt to appear.

If the player dies while fighting the Whisperer, their grave will appear in the Ruins of Camdozaal, by the rope leading to the Lassar Undercity. Players will have their reclamation fee reduced by 75% until they have five kills, after which the standard death cost will apply.

tactics.heading: Requirements
tactics.text: • Completion of Quest Desert Treasure II - The Fallen Empire

tactics.heading: Suggested skills
tactics.text:
• 75+ Magic
• 80+ Hitpoints

tactics.heading: Transportation
tactics.text:
The quickest methods of reaching the Lassar Undercity, where the Whisperer resides, are:
• Using the ring of shadows to teleport to the Lassar Undercity exit. This requires having used the sirenic tablet on it, which is a 1/25 drop from the Whisperer.
• Using the Mind Altar Teleport spell (or tablet/portal), then running south-east to Camdozaal.
• Using the Lassar Teleport spell or tablet, then using the shortcut to the north-west (requires 68 Agility Agility), or running around the mountain.

Once in the Ruins of Camdozaal, climb down the rope in the north-west end to enter the Lassar Undercity. Then, use the teleporter to reach the cathedral.

tactics.heading: Fight overview
tactics.text:
The player must bring the blackstone fragment to initiate the fight, as parts of the fight will require the player to enter the Shadow Realm. The player will refuse to fight the Whisperer without it.

The sanity mechanic is present throughout the fight. When outside the Shadow Realm, the player will slowly restore 1% sanity every 4 ticks; inside, the player will lose 3% sanity along with 3 prayer points. Sanity can be further decreased (regardless of realm) by tentacle hits or by unavoided special attacks. If the sanity bar fully depletes, the player will go insane and will quickly die within 10 ticks; teleport out if this occurs.

The fight begins by disturbing the Odd Figure, who will then knock the player back and begin attacking as the Whisperer.

The Whisperer's regular attack involves shooting three projectiles per attack in either Ranged or Magic. The ranged attacks consist of grey barbs, while the magic attacks consist of a cluster of three blue orbs; the Whisperer's chest will additionally emit a blue aura. Protection prayers fully block the projectiles' damage if activated before the projectile hits the player; if not blocked, they can deal up to 40 and 36 damage respectively. The pattern of these projectiles changes depending on how far into the fight the player is.
• Upon beginning the fight, she will only use Magic (M) or Ranged (R) for all three projectiles.
• After one or two special attacks have been used, she will use M-M-R or R-R-M.
• After all three special attacks have been used, she will use M-R-M or R-M-R.
• During her enrage phase, she will start with ranged, and switch styles every two attacks.

After each regular attack, four shadow tentacles will surface four tiles from the player, converging on the tile they were on when they first appeared. If the player is struck by a tentacle, they will deal 20 damage and drain sanity by 20% (only one tentacle can hit the player at a time). These initially converge in an "X" formation, and a "+" formation can be used after two special attacks. Both formations can be dodged by performing an L movement (two tiles forward/backward, then one tile left/right - analogous to a knight move in chess).

The tentacles will only spawn on a valid empty tile; if they would spawn on the arena edge, or if the Whisperer herself is on top of the tile, they will not spawn on that tile. This can be manipulated into creating safe tiles.

The Whisperer will melee the player if they stand next to her, dealing two heavy hits in two ticks. This melee attack hits through prayer, always hits and has the second hit mirror the first (e.g if the first hit deals 40 damage, the second also deals 40). The Whisperer actively checks if the player is in melee distance; if the player runs into melee distance in the middle of a volley, she will immediately cancel it for a melee attack, which is extremely dangerous. Players should stay at least five tiles away from the Whisperer to avoid misclicks and accidentally wandering into melee range.

Perfect kills are disqualified on a tentacle hit or on damage from a projectile (the player is still eligible if the projectile misses off prayer).

tactics.heading: Special attacks
tactics.text:
When the Whisperer reaches or falls below 720 (80%), 495 (55%), and 270 (30%) hitpoints, she will perform a special attack. The possible special attack rotations are:

• Corrupted Seeds -> Screech -> Soul Siphon
• Screech -> Soul Siphon -> Corrupted Seeds

During the special attack animation, the Whisperer will take 70% less damage outside of the Shadow Realm and 60% within. Thralls are unaffected by this damage reduction.

• Corrupted Seeds: The Whisperer will appear in the centre and scatter corrupted seeds around her. The player must step on all the light green seeds to stop the attack, which can only be seen in the Shadow Realm; if the timer runs out before the attack is stopped, the player will take 75 damage and lose 75% sanity. Stopping the attack without stepping on any dark green seeds will restore sanity by 15%. Stepping on a dark green seed will deal 15-25 damage.
  • There are two layouts in which the seeds can spawn, and each layout has two patterns for the light green seeds. Each pattern has two lines of symmetry. To preserve sanity and prayer, players can memorise the seeds' locations, then activate the blackstone fragment again and step on them in the real world.
  • An easy way to memorize the current layout is to assign nicknames to them and spending minimal time in the shadow realm to check which one is active. For example, route 1 can be thought of as "Diagonals" due to only needing diagonal movement. Route 2 can be thought of as "T shapes". Route 3 can be thought of as "Buildings and fences" due to the large square alignment on opposite sides and small lines adjacent. Route 4 can be thought of as "Triangles and boxes" due to the triangle shapes opposite of each other and the small squares adjacent.
  • With a N-tick weapon, players can destroy N-1 seeds between attacks (e.g. with a five-tick weapon players can destroy four seeds between attacks).
  • An alternate view of all possible correct seed spawns/locations to step outside of the realm is also shown in addition to the route images. Do not stand on singular number seeds unless attempting to determine the pattern without entering the realm. For example: 1/2 (both patterns 1 and 2 use this), but number 2 is only used by pattern 2.

• Screech: The Whisperer will teleport to the southern end of the cathedral and gather energy for three screeches. At the same time, floating columns will emerge from the water to block the incoming attacks. The pillars have 20, 40, or 60 health; their health bars can only be seen when in the Shadow Realm. Players must stand within the 2x2 square directly behind a pillar (clipping inside a pillar does not count) to avoid getting hit by the screech; other tiles do not work even if they'd appear safe. Each screech will deal 20 damage to every pillar and destroy the pillar the player is hiding behind, so you must save the 60-health pillar for the final screech. A screech deals 45 damage and drains sanity by 45%.
  • To avoid the attack: enter the Shadow Realm, look for the 60-health pillar, and then look for a 40-health pillar nearby the 60-health pillar. Hide behind pillars in the following order: any 20-health pillar, the 40-health pillar, and finally the 60-health pillar.
  • To preserve sanity and prayer, players can enter the Shadow Realm and quickly check which pillars to stand behind, then exit and move in the real world. This needs to be done quickly, as the blackstone fragment deactivates within a few seconds and prevents a swap back for the remaining special duration.

• Soul Siphon: The Whisperer will appear in the centre and summon twelve lost souls, beginning a powerful chant that completes in 20 ticks (12 seconds). Players must activate their blackstone fragment to enter the Shadow Realm, then kill at least one set of souls chanting the same phrase. If the player fails to kill a full set of souls within the time limit, the chant deals 50 damage to the player and heals her for 100 health. Souls can only be damaged in the Shadow Realm.
  • This special is signalled by the Whisperer disappearing and reappearing in the centre of the room. Immediately switch to your ranged weapon once she disappears, and be ready to click the blackstone fragment.
  • Depending which set(s) of souls are killed, they will cause the following effects:
    • (2 yellow souls): Restores ~20% of the player's Hitpoints level.
    • (3 blue souls): Restores ~20% of the player's Prayer level.
    • (3 cyan souls): Restores 15% sanity.
    • (4 green souls): Deals 50 damage to the Whisperer (increased to 75 if all twelve souls are killed).
  • A venator bow can kill all of the spirits within the time frame. Attack the top or bottom spirit in the "\" or "/" formations to ensure all three are hit (any spirit can be shot in the "L" formation).
  • Without a venator bow, the next best weapons are 2t ranged weapons: blisterwood stakes, any blowpipe, or knives (in order of their range). These can kill up to 7 souls if the player promptly enters the Shadow Realm. Players who are unable to clear all souls should simply clear the yellow spirits and leave to avoid prayer drain.

tactics.heading: Post Special Attack Bind
tactics.text:
After each special attack, the Whisperer will usually launch a binding projectile at the player that lasts for ~8 seconds. She will then move towards the player in an attempt to melee them. After the bind hits the player, any ice spell or standard spellbook binding spell will successfully freeze her and end the player's bind. On the Arceuus spellbook, the only guaranteed bind is Undead Grasp while under the effects of Mark of Darkness; other grasp spells are not guaranteed a bind. Alternatively: if the player stands at least 10 tiles away from where she launches the projectile, they will unbind and can run away (one tile is sufficient) before she reaches the player.

Less experienced players can use the standard or ancient spellbook to simply freeze the Whisperer. More experienced players should instead use the 10 tile distance trick to avoid her melee attack, as this allows the use of other spellbooks (particually the Arceuus spellbook for its thralls).

At higher health, the Whisperer can sometimes forgo the post-special binding projectile and use auto-attacks instead, so be prepared to flick. This seems to occur the most often after the first special attack. If the Whisperer is damaged below the next special attack health threshold, she will begin that special rather than launch the bind.

With a weapon that has a distance of 10, players can "lure" the Whisperer by dragging her to the extreme end of the arena after each special attack, allowing the player to get several free hits in before she resumes combat. Stand at least two or three tiles from the marked tiles; run after the first attack, switch to long ranged as she closes in, then back to accurate. The player can also stand one tile from the marked tiles but they will need to move just as she closes in on them. RuneLite's radius markers (with a range of 10 centered around the Whisperer) can also be used.

After the third special attack, the Whisperer will cancel the melee attempt if she falls below 100 health.

tactics.heading: Enrage phase
tactics.text:
Upon reaching 0 health, the Whisperer will heal 140 hitpoints, restore any drained stats, and pull the player into the Shadow Realm. She will alternate between ranged and magic every two attacks and increase her attack speed to 2 ticks (1.2 seconds). A single tentacle is launched alongside every attack, rather than a cluster of four.

Players should restore their health and prayer before triggering her enrage phase, as it's difficult to heal during the phase itself.

The tentacles still drain sanity and are a serious threat, so the focus should always be on movement. There are two general movement strategies:

• Basic movement (recommended for beginners). Players can dodge most of the tentacles just by running in a straight line; even running directly into a tentacle usually won't cause damage as long as the player is moving. To take advantage of this, run in a large square around the Whisperer (stay out of melee range) or back-and-forth in a line in front of her, taking care not to stop for more than a few ticks. When the second auto-attack of the same style (ranged or magic) is just about to hit the player, click to move and then switch prayers. Fit in your own attacks where possible, then immediately keep moving. Do not panic if you're hit, simply click a a good distance away and ensure your prayers are correct.
• Advanced movement. Utilises L-movement to dodge all tentacle attacks. See the video to the right for an example.

Once the Whisperer dies, the player's sanity is instantly restored to 100% and any attacks launched in transition will not cause damage. She will respawn as the Odd Figure in roughly 18 seconds.

Tips for mobile:
The sanity interface, chat menu, and world map all take up extremely valuable space on the screen, and this can especially be a problem during the enrage phase. Long tap the world map icon to collapse the world map before the fight begins, and collapse the chat menu after the Whisperer’s specials to help you focus more on the direction of the tentacles during enrage.

tactics.heading: Awakened mode
tactics.text:
In Awakened mode, the Whisperer has the following changes:

• The black mask and Slayer helmet do not apply their usual on-task damage and accuracy bonuses while on a Whisperer boss slayer task.
• The Whisperer's health increases from 900 to 2,700.
• The Whisperer is immune to stat drains.
• Sanity does not restore outside of the Shadow Realm. While in the Shadow Realm, the sanity and prayer drain is increased to 4.
• The Whisperer's regular attacks now consists of five projectiles rather than three.
  • Upon beginning the fight, she will use two of one style and three of the other (e.g R-R-R-M-M)
  • After two special attacks, she will use one of one style, two of the other, and then two of the first style (e.g. R-M-M-R-R)
  • After the seventh special attack, she will alternate between both styles per hit (R-M-R-M-R)
• Damage from the Whisperer's regular attacks is significantly increased.
  • Her regular magical attack can deal upwards of 45 damage, while her regular ranged attack can deal upwards of 53 damage. Praying correctly fully negates the damage.
  • Her regular melee attacks deals between 50-72 damage if not prayed against. If prayed against, it deals between 37-52 damage. This still respects normal mode modifiers (e.g first hit deals 50, second hit also deals 50).
• The Whisperer's tentacle formations are changed - the "X" now becomes an attack with seven tentacles (without any formation change) while the "+" becomes an attack with six tentacles all next to each other (which starts to appear after four special attacks are used), making the player run at least two tiles to the sides to avoid the attack. The damage and sanity drain is also increased from 20 to 30.
• Unlike other bosses who retain their normal mode mechanics at set health percentages, the Whisperer does not and will instead perform her special attacks at roughly 10% hitpoint thresholds:
  • ~2400 health, ~2120 health, ~1820 health, ~1600 health, ~1310 health, ~1050 health, ~800 health and ~500 health for a special attack.
  • The possible special attack rotations are:
    • Screech -> Soul Siphon -> Corrupted Seeds -> Screech -> Soul Siphon -> Corrupted Seeds -> Screech -> Soul Siphon
    • Corrupted Seeds -> Screech -> Soul Siphon -> Corrupted Seeds -> Screech -> Soul Siphon -> Corrupted Seeds
• The Whisperer's Screech attack hits five times rather than three, and damage/sanity drain is increased from 45 to 70.
• An additional four lost souls are added for the Soul Siphon attack, increasing the total from 12 to 16, with these new souls being added to all cardinal directions. The timer is increased to 21 seconds (35 ticks) to compensate.
  • However, all souls must be killed in time, as the Whisperer will manipulate the remaining souls to perform the full attack. If sets of souls are left, then they will restore her as normal, while the sets the player killed will have their effects applied to them.
• The timer for the Corrupted Seeds mechanic is reduced to 15.6 seconds (26 ticks), damage/sanity drain is increased from 15 to 20 if not stopped, while stepping on a dark green seed deals between 60-75 damage.
• After a bind attack, the boss runs for 1.2 seconds (2 ticks) prior to walking 3.6 seconds (6 ticks) towards the player, instead of walking for the entire duration.
• During the enrage phase, she now heals from 140 to 250, sends two or three tentacles every two attacks instead of one, starts with magic instead of ranged and also swaps styles after every attack.

Due to the player not regaining sanity outside the Shadow Realm, the player must essentially perfect every mechanic or they will go insane at some point during the fight. Utilising L-movements will dodge every tentacle attack other than the changed "+" formation, which the player will have to dodge reactively.

During the Screech mechanic, the player must quickly identify the pillars' health, as staying in the Shadow Realm for the entire mechanic will drain 40% of the player's sanity; doing it even once will likely result in failure. Likewise, getting hit by a screech will result in failure due to the 70% sanity drain incurred.

During the Soul Siphon mechanic, the player must bring a blowpipe to deal with the souls that spawn in the cardinal directions alongside a venator bow. Kill a cluster of souls with a bow, then switch to the blowpipe to kill the lone soul and repeat. Immediately exit the realm once the last soul is killed. This will deal additional damage to the boss.

During the Corrupted Seeds mechanic, quickly enter the Shadow Realm, then leave once the pattern is discovered to minimise time spent inside. Avoid stepping on a dark green seed, as the damage is significantly increased that stepping on two seeds without healing will result in death.

After every special attack, do not attack the Whisperer until she launches the binding projectile and stay at least 8 or more tiles away from her. Once this projectile is launched, immediately freeze the Whisperer, as she will run towards the player, and trying to get an auto-attack in will likely result in her reaching the player and using melee, causing severe damage or death.

Before starting the enrage phase, it is highly encouraged to begin with over max health and as much prayer as possible, as focusing on the Whisperer's attacks is much more important than trying to eat or restore prayer. Likewise, the player should enter the enrage phase with ~60% or more sanity; the higher is better in case mistakes are made. Players using a shadow may opt to bring a 4-tick weapon such as a sanguinesti staff to match the Whisperer's attack speed and tentacles on enrage, though this is completely optional.

tactics.heading: Overview
tactics.text: The thermonuclear smoke devil is a boss variant of the regular smoke devils, requiring 93 Slayer to kill. Similarly to Kraken, despite its high requirements, the boss fight is mechanically simple and kills are quite quick, reaching 60–100 kills per hour depending on gear and strategies used.

tactics.heading: Requirements
tactics.text: • Level 93 Slayer to deal damage against the thermonuclear smoke devil.

tactics.heading: Recommendations
tactics.text:
• High combat stats. Although not required, see the skill levels below for an indication of the advised stats:
  • If using Melee:
    • Level 90 Attack or higher
    • Level 90 Strength or higher
    • Level 90 Defence or higher
    • Level 90 Hitpoints or higher, required to utilise the Redemption prayer method
    • Level 70 Prayer or higher for the Piety prayer
  • If using Magic:
    • Level 75 Magic or higher to equip the correct staves
    • Level 90 Hitpoints or higher, required to utilise the Redemption prayer method
    • Level 49 Prayer or higher for the Redemption prayer

tactics.heading: Transportation
tactics.text:
The thermonuclear smoke devil is located in a separated section of the Smoke Devil Dungeon, as seen on the image. The quickest way to get to this dungeon is via fairy rings:
• Use the code BKP, then run north-east to the dungeon entrance.

If fairy rings are not unlocked, teleport to Castle Wars and run south-west of the building, where the entrance to the Smoke Devil Dungeon is.

Run north-west after entering the Smoke Devil Dungeon to find a crevice leading to the section with the thermonuclear smoke devil.

tactics.heading: Attack styles
tactics.text:
The thermonuclear smoke devil only attacks with a typeless magical ranged attack:
• 'Typeless' means that protection prayers will not have any effect.
• 'Magical ranged' means that the attack accuracy is decided by the ranged attack bonuses of the thermonuclear smoke devil and the magic defence bonuses of the player.
• The max hit of this attack is 8.
• The attack is very accurate and has an attack speed of 2 ticks (1.2 seconds).
• The attack range is eight tiles.

tactics.heading: Smoke
tactics.text: The thermonuclear smoke devil is located in a smoky environment. Therefore players must equip either a gas mask, facemask, or slayer helmet, or they will take damage from the smoke. As with all other smoke and dust devils, these are also mandatory when fighting the boss, or it will deal even more damage and drain stats.

tactics.heading: Blood Barrage Healing
tactics.text:
A simple method that allows extended kill count and trip length is to utilise Blood Barrage; though it is only profitable if lucky on unique drops.
Players with high enough magic attack and strength bonus gear can outheal the thermonuclear smoke devil's damage. The passive bonuses of the Ancient Sceptre and select gear such as Bloodbark Armour can be worn for this method with little loss to magic bonuses. Forgotten Brew/imbued heart and Augury also go a long way to increase effectiveness. Bring plenty prayer/super restore potions and a few emergency high healing food for those several unlucky splashes in a row.

Utilising the smaller smoke devils in the arena for group blood barrages is also a way to get back to full health quickly, though this is detrimental for pet hunters.

Players should note this method takes roughly 2-3x longer than utilising the Tumeken's Shadow.

tactics.heading: Safespotting
tactics.text:
The player's magic spells have a longer attack range (9 tiles) than the thermonuclear smoke devil (8 tiles). This difference may be utilised by freezing the thermonuclear smoke devil and then moving out of its attack range, so that the player can still attack the thermonuclear smoke devil, while the thermonuclear is not able to reach the player. Powered staves require the use of the longrange attack style for this method, except the Eye of Ayak, which cannot be used to safespot at all. Use the best ice spell available.

An Ice ancient sceptre is recommended with this method, as it provides a 10% accuracy bonus against unfrozen targets and increases 1-3 extra ticks of freeze time (depending on the ice spell used).

tactics.heading: Redemption method
tactics.text:
Players with a Prayer level of 49 or higher are able to make use of the Redemption prayer. The Redemption prayer can be used at the thermonuclear smoke devil as a way of restoring hitpoints. When the player's hitpoints are reduced below 10% of their maximum hitpoints while the Redemption prayer is active, the Redemption prayer will use the player's remaining prayer points to heal the player. The number of hitpoints healed is equal to 25% of their Prayer level (rounded down).

After the Redemption effect is triggered, the player will have to quickly restore their prayer points by drinking a dose of a prayer potion, super restore, ancient brew, zamorak brew, or forgotten brew and reactivate the Redemption prayer. This can be supplemented with the use of a Prayer regeneration potion, as while its effects are active the player will regenerate 1 prayer point every 12 ticks, or every 6th attack from the boss. See Calculator:Prayer/Prayer point cost to determine cost efficient methods of restoring prayer sorting by the gp/dose column. Jangerberies are not recommended due to only restoring 1 prayer point and not having multiple uses.

Players with a Prayer level of 96 or higher are able to restore 24 hitpoints with the Redemption prayer. Since a prayer restore potion has four doses, each potion could potentially heal 96 hitpoints, which is significantly higher than the best healing regular food (which restores 26 hitpoints), albeit at a significantly higher cost compared to food. If the player has high enough defensive bonuses, they can primarily rely on the Prayer regeneration potion, as one only needs to not drop below 9 hitpoints between each 12 tick regeneration cycle.

A more cost-effective method involves using zamorak brew, ancient brews or forgotten brews, which cost significantly less than prayer potions or super restores in addition to boosting Magic. However, these reduce Defence, which will make the thermonuclear smoke devil's attacks slightly more accurate - you will need to be quick on drinking a dose and reactivating redemption, and you will do this more often, but the cost offset is still significant. This downside can be offset by either bringing regular restore potions (1:1 with Ancient Brews) and taking a sip of each when Redemption activates (Shorter trips, slightly more expensive than ancient brews alone, slightly more forgiving), or super restores (again, 1:1 with Ancient Brews), and alternating which potion you use every redemption (Longer trips, more expensive, but just over half the cost of Prayer Potions/Super Restores alone, and almost as forgiving). Alternatively, two Menaphite remedies are enough to offset the defence reduction of a full inventory of forgotten brews and only need to be drunk once every five minutes. At high levels, a full inventory of only zamorak brews is sufficient to sustain a long trip.

Since the maximum hit of the thermonuclear smoke devil is 8, the player should always stay at least 9 hitpoints while utilising the Redemption prayer method, to reliably survive all of the thermonuclear smoke devil's attacks. Therefore it is highly recommended to have a Hitpoints level of 90 or higher, to make sure the Redemption prayer always gets activated when the player gets damaged below 9 hitpoints.

tactics.heading: Walk-under method
tactics.text:
This method is preferred for those not wanting to mage the boss or don't have the gear to do so. When walking under the thermonuclear smoke devil immediately after performing an attack, the player is able to hide from the thermonuclear smoke devil's attacks until they step out to perform another attack. When utilising this method correctly, the thermonuclear smoke devil will only perform 1 attack for every attack the player performs; therefore reducing the damage taken by 50 to 60 percent.

A more advanced version of the walk-under method utilises the fact that NPCs do not move when the player they are targeting is underneath them if the player clicks on an item on the ground or an interactive object (producing a red 'X' when clicked). If an item or object, such as the ashes that the boss drops every kill or the entrance to the room, is under it or on the opposite side of the boss from the player, it is relatively easy to walk under the boss and attack on a constant rhythm. This works even with the left-click attack option on. This is easy to do if the item is under the boss's hitbox and not under its clickbox, or if the item is on the opposite side from where you are attacking; simply kill the first one as normal with the walk-under method, then drop the ashes in the south-west corner of the boss's hitbox where it normally spawns. If done correctly, after the next kill, more ashes will be dropped in the exact same tile and you do not have to drop more.

Another easy way to set up the walk-under method is by positioning oneself to the west side of Thermy, and then clicking on the door. With a 4-tick weapon you can exchange 1:1 hit by attacking the boss, clicking the door, and then clicking Thermy again after walking two tiles under it. Once the player sees an XP drop from the attack, they may click the door again and continue in this 1:1 cycle.

tactics.heading: POH/Nardah method
tactics.text:
Similarly to the Abyssal Sire, the thermonuclear smoke devil is close to a fairy ring. As such, players can also utilise a similar method for killing the boss. A weapon that can deal very high special attack damage is recommended for this method; dragon claws are useful for this purpose. As the fight is expected to end very quickly, the player brings the best strength-boosting gear they can afford and dumps all specials on the boss, before killing it as normal.

After killing the boss, the player teleports to their house and uses the rejuvenation pool to restore lost health, prayer, and special attack.

Alternatively, if the elite desert diary has been completed, the player can use a Desert amulet 4 to restore health, prayer, and special attack and a Quest point cape to teleport close to a fairy ring. This yields more profit with low input cost, with the only costs coming from house tabs if not using the Construction cape and super combat potions. However, kill rates are slower than killing it normally due to the simplicity of the boss fight and its 9 second respawn timer.

gearNotes.heading: Equipment
gearNotes.text:
Like demonic gorillas, players will have to use multiple combat styles to be able to attack the demons off-prayer. Unlike demonic gorillas, tormented demons remain on one style for 150 hitpoints instead of 70, meaning players will have to switch less often and can bring more gear switches if they prefer. However, the player will continue attacking when the demon changes prayers. Switches can be reduced when not much damage is gained to save inventory space.

The demons' unique accuracy mechanic encourages bringing different ranged weapons for the high and low accuracy phases, such as the toxic blowpipe and bow of Faerdhinen respectively. There is usually little benefit in switching into armour that only provides accuracy bonuses during the high accuracy phase, for example this can make the toxic blowpipe viable in full melee strength boosting gear reducing switches. The shield mechanic promotes bringing a strong, slow Crush (melee) or Heavy (ranged) weapon for when the shield is down. Ranged weapons brought for this purpose should be set to Accurate to increase their maximum hit and damage scaling, as the decrease in weapon speed is ignored.

Note: All weapons that are not classified as abyssal or demonbane deal 20% reduced damage against tormented demons.

With no additional gear switches, the heavy ballista (on accurate) and Dharok's greataxe (on crush) are the strongest weapons for hits when the shield is down. Dharok's greataxe becomes even more powerful when used with the full Dharok's armour set, which multiplies damage after it is rolled (and after the 33 bonus damage is added) based on the number of hitpoints the player is missing. Similarly, using a tzhaar-ket-om with a berserker necklace multiplies damage by 1.2 after the bonus damage has been added, making it more effective than a Dharok's greataxe on its own.

The Saradomin godsword and the eldritch Nightmare staff are solid options to extend trips with their special attacks if no other weapon is being used. These are best used during the shieldless state, where the accuracy is guaranteed. The godsword's special should not be used as a melee punish, as the flat damage does not restore the player's health or prayer.

These weapons pair well with Death Charge at the cost of not being able to alch drops unless an explorer's ring 4 is brought. If using thralls, use the thrall on the combat style the player is not using, as this allows the thrall to have full uptime on attacking for its duration unless it causes a prayer swap. A Lightbearer can be brought in addition should the player still struggle with supplies, though this is not recommended if the player is using Arclight or Emberlight as they benefit greatly from strength bonus.
Melee is the strongest style against the demons, especially considering the accessibility of Arclight for most accounts. Due to non-reduced damage and 100% accuracy for a large portion of the fight, abyssal weaponry outperforms weapons like the Inquisitor's mace and Osmumten's fang.

The scorching bow and the twisted bow are the best ranged options. Ranged typically performs worse than melee or magic setups, but requires less switches and is cheaper to use than magic. Twisted bow and toxic blowpipe do considerable damage during the 100% accuracy phase. Elite Void ranged will outperform Masori armour when off-task in most setups. Notably, the toxic blowpipe benefits more from the accuracy and damage from Masori compared to Void, and the twisted bow performs marginally worse in Void.

Demonbane spells with a purging staff are the 2nd most powerful setup behind the Emberlight. Without a scorching or twisted bow, demonbane spells can outperform similar range setups but have additional rune cost and require occasionally applying Mark of Darkness.

tactics.heading: Overview
tactics.text:
Tormented demons can be fought within the Ancient Guthixian Temple after completing the While Guthix Sleeps quest. As with their original version from RuneScape 2, multiple combat styles and protection prayers are needed to successfully fight these demons. They count as greater demons for the purposes of a Slayer task.

They drop the tormented synapse, which is used to create powerful demonbane weaponry, and the burning claw, which can be combined in a pair to make burning claws.

tactics.heading: Requirements
tactics.text: • Completion of Quest While Guthix Sleeps for access to the Ancient Guthixian Temple.

tactics.heading: Recommendations
tactics.text:
• High combat stats in at least 2 combat styles.
  • Level 75 Attack or higher
  • Level 75 Strength or higher
  • Level 70 Defence or higher
  • Level 70 Ranged or higher
  • Level 75 Hitpoints or higher
  • Level 70 Prayer or higher (for Piety, 74 for Rigour, 77 for Augury)
  • Level 82 Magic or higher (Dark Demonbane and magic defence)
• Completion of Quest Shadow of the Storm for access to Arclight.
• Completion of Quest A Kingdom Divided for access to Dark Demonbane.

tactics.heading: Transportation
tactics.text: The quickest way to reach the temple is by using a Guthixian temple teleport scroll, which are dropped by tormented demons at a rate of 1/12. Alternatively, players can use a games necklace to teleport to Tears of Guthix via either jewellery on the player or in a Jewellery box in the player's POH. From here, a lit sapphire lantern must be used to attract a light creature in order to descend into the chasm. Follow the chasm and climb the walls next to the centre skull, and enter the skull above to enter the central chamber of the temple.

tactics.heading: Fight overview
tactics.text:
Tormented demons can use protection prayers, attack using every combat style along with ground-targeted fire bombs, and possess routefinding capabilities, allowing them to move around objects and stack on top of each other. They are capable of attacking with melee if players stand underneath them, and will switch randomly to a magic or ranged attack if they cannot reach the player and were previously using melee, which makes them difficult to safe-spot.

Their first attack upon initiating combat deals ~75% less damage if the demon is attacking with magic or ranged, the player is praying Protect from Magic or Protect from Missiles, and its shield is down (i.e. the demon has not taken damage from the player's 5+ tick attack).

Every 150 health lost since its last prayer swap (roughly 25% of its max health), the demon will change its protection prayer to the last combat style it was damaged with, as well as stop attacking for 6 ticks (3.6s). Summoning a thrall with a third attack style can be used to occasionally exploit this.

tactics.heading: Multicombat
tactics.text:
Tormented demons are spread out in groups throughout the temple, and players can fight up to three of them should they choose to do so, which results in varying attack behaviour.

With two demons attacking, one will always use melee, and the other using magic or ranged; they will not attack simultaneously as to allow players to prayer flick their attacks. If the player moves, it may change the cadence of the attacks and make it harder to prayer flick. If a third demon attacks, it will only use fire bombs, requiring the player to move frequently.

tactics.heading: Fire bombs
tactics.text:
Roughly every 60 ticks (36s), the demon(s) will briefly bind the player in place, disable their run, then release two fire bombs: one targeting the tile the player stood on, and one in a 3x3 area centered on the player's location in a valid tile. Players have 2 ticks (1.2s) to move to a safe tile before they land and explode, or they will take 40+ damage. Players can Ctrl click to run if this is enabled in the in-game settings.

It is recommended to stand out in the open and not by a wall or obstacle, especially when fighting multiple demons at once, as the fireballs will only land on valid tiles. Some areas may only allow for up to three safe tiles, meaning that without use of control clicking, the player is guaranteed to be hit by one of them.

Fire bombs will still cause damage even if the demon is killed while they are airborne.

The demon will always change its combat style after this attack, and the player's run will be re-enabled. Players can determine the next attack style through the following observations:
• If it approaches the player, it will use melee.
• If it does not approach the player, it will use magic or ranged - whichever wasn't used before.
• If the demon previously used melee, you will have to guess and/or correct your protection prayer as it can be magic or ranged.

tactics.heading: Shield
tactics.text:
Tormented demons usually have a fire shield that reduces damage done by non-demonbane weapons/spells and non-abyssal weapons by 20%. They will drop this shield after first being attacked and after each fire bomb attack; this is indicated by an animation as if flames descend from above and then blow away. The shield remains down until they are attacked once, allowing time to switch gear. This allows you to use weapons they are weak to as early as the second hit of combat, reliably increasing DPS.

For the player's one attack while their shield is down, all damage dealt by specific weapons is increased by , where is the weapon's attack speed. The attack speed for this one attack is also set to 4 ticks (2.4s); if multiple demons are attacking, the attack speed decreases by one tick per additional demon that is fighting the player, allowing back-to-back powerful hits if timed correctly. These benefits only apply to:
• Melee weapons set to the crush attack style (this works even if the attack rolls against Slash or Stab defence, for example while using a godsword's special attack)
• Heavy ranged weapons (crossbows and ballistae)
• Spells (not from a powered staff).

As such, heavy ranged weapons with a Rapid style should be set to Accurate instead.

It is also possible to benefit from a weapon's slow attack speed by manually casting a spell with it equipped. This is particularly effective with the Dark bow or the Ogre bow set to Accurate.

If the player mistakenly uses a weapon matching the protection prayer of the monster while the shield is down, the attack speed and damage bonus will still apply, but be divided by 3 and rounded down. For example, a 7 tick weapon (+33) will always hit 11 on prayer.

tactics.heading: Defencelessness
tactics.text:
Roughly 30 ticks (18s) after the start of the fight, the demon will become defenceless, giving the player 100% accuracy when attacking it; this is indicated by the flames on the demon's back being extinguished. This increased accuracy will last until the player's first hit after the fire bomb attack. After the fire bomb attack, the player's accuracy will return to normal until 30 ticks pass again and the demon becomes defenceless once again. The 100% accuracy bonus makes it a good time to use a spec weapon as soon as the demon becomes defenceless.

These frequent periods of defenselessness can also make it worthwhile to bring extra damage boosting gear to increase max hit. Alternatively a fast weapon can be used, such as a toxic blowpipe, though it is still inferior to demonbane weaponry.

gearNotes.heading: Equipment
gearNotes.text:
Mountain trolls are slightly resistant to crush attacks, but equally weak to stab and slash, making a wide range of weapons suitable for melee.

Ice trolls in the Trollweiss dungeon can comfortably be fought without a Neitiznot shield and have a 100% elemental weakness to fire spells, making maging them particularly effective, although more expensive.

Mountain trolls only have a 50% elemental weakness to fire spells, with worse value drops, but due to their lower health, can be a better option to finish a task quickly.

Ice trolls are slightly resistant to slash attacks, making stab and crush weapons typically favoured here. When combined with a Dwarf multicannon, killing ice trolls can be a reasonably fast task with reasonable drops, although care needs to be taken due to the unavoidable damage.

Inventory

• Dwarf multicannon and steel cannonballs
• 2 Divine super combat potions or Super combat potions
• Prayer potions
• Bonecrusher necklace to save on prayer potions
• A Seed box to pick up seeds
• Soul bearer to bank ensouled heads
• One-click teleport (optional)
• Enchanted lyre(i)
• Herb sack to pick up valuable herbs
• Divine rune pouch / Rune pouch with Fire and Nature runes to cast High Alchemy (set warning value to 50,000)
• Food (Sharks / Karambwans / Monkfish)

Meleeing mountain trolls is an easy and accessible option for a Troll task with no quest requirements to complete, and with all damage able to be completely negated through Protect from Melee.

Protect from melee and Piety are strongly recommended, although forgoing one or both and using Bones to peaches is viable, albeit significantly slower. Thralls and Death charge on the Arceuus spellbook can be used to speed up the task significantly, in addition to a Dwarf multicannon. This also allows players to use Adept reanimation on any ensouled troll heads received on the task.

Players may also wish to use equipment such as Sunfire fanatic armour, Proselyte, or Initiate armour to maximise prayer bonus, especially if combined with a Bonecrusher necklace to minimise prayer potion usage.

Inventory

• Dwarf multicannon and steel cannonballs
• 2 Divine super combat potions or Super combat potions
• 6 Prayer potions
• A Seed box to pick up seeds
• Soul bearer to bank ensouled heads (optional, if not using Adept reanimation)
• One-click teleport (optional)
• Teleport to get to Mount Quidamortem if not using a mounted Xeric's talisman
• Herb sack to pick up valuable herbs
• Divine rune pouch / Rune pouch with runes for High Alchemy or Thralls
• Food (optional, not needed with Protect from Melee)

Ice trolls in the Trollweiss dungeon can comfortably be fought without a Neitiznot shield and have a 100% elemental weakness to fire spells, making maging them particularly effective, although more expensive.

Mountain trolls only have a 50% elemental weakness to fire spells, with worse value drops, but due to their lower health, can be a better option to finish a task quickly.

tactics.heading: Overview
tactics.text:
Trolls can be assigned as a Slayer task at 60 combat level by various Slayer masters. Trolls are, for the most part, found in the Fremennik Province and north of Burthorpe.

Trolls fought in quests all count towards the Slayer task, with the exception of sea trolls. The bosses can be fought again in the Nightmare Zone.

Players who have completed the hard Morytania Diary might want to bring the bonecrusher to gain passive Prayer experience from the big bones drops. Players with 92 Magic and the Arceuus spellbook may opt to use the Sinister Offering spell instead.

There are two types of trolls that players can fight for a troll task: mountain trolls and ice trolls.

Mountain trolls are found in many locations, primarily around the Fremennik Province, though a group of fourteen trolls are also found in Mount Quidamortem. The Mount Quidamortem trolls can be easily accessed with the Xeric's talisman if players have received an ancient tablet from the Chambers of Xeric unlocking the Xeric's Honour teleport, although using the Lovakengj Minecart Network teleport or nearby fairy ring are also suitable.

Other variants include thrower trolls and troll generals, however these are scarce, far, and have nonexistent drops.

The other trolls, ice trolls, can be found in the Ice Path, Trollweiss Dungeon, and the isles north of Neitiznot and Jatizso.

The trolls in the Ice Path are not worth killing, as these are far stronger than other trolls and have incredibly poor drops for their level. Instead, players are advised to kill the trolls on the isles, as they are weaker, have a slightly better drop table, and are found in larger quantities in an open multicombat area. If killing trolls here, prayer and a Neitiznot shield are required in order to reduce damage taken from the ice troll females, who are much more accurate and damaging if not using a Neitiznot shield. Out of the two isles, it may be preferable to kill the trolls north of Jatizso, as the trolls there will often focus on the guards fighting them, which will lower the damage the player receives. Additionally, the bank on Jatizso is slightly closer to the troll area than it is on Neitiznot.

Regardless of the troll being killed, a dwarf multicannon is highly recommended as trolls have low aggression range.

One quick way to complete a trolls task for players not using a dwarf multicannon is to kill the ice troll runts in the first island north of Neitiznot. This method requires completion of The Fremennik Trials to access Neitiznot. There are several guards nearby constantly fighting the trolls, who deal considerable damage and will help speed up kills. They also keep the trolls distracted so that players are able to range or mage without utilising safespots. Note that if guards deal the finishing blow, the Slayer experience received is halved, but drops are still received as long as the player dealt any damage. Fire spells are recommended, as ice trolls have a fire weakness of 100%.

tactics.heading: Recommendations
tactics.text:
• Medium combat stats. See the skill levels below for an indication of the advised stats:
• Level 40 Attack or higher.
• Level 40 Strength or higher.
• Level 43 Prayer or higher for Protect from Melee strongly recommended
• Completion of Quest The Fremennik Trials to be able to speak to Mord Gunnars for access to Jatizso for ice trolls.
  • Quest The Fremennik Isles does not need to be completed to access Jatizso as Mord takes the player at the start of the quest.
• Completion of Quest Dwarf Cannon to be able to use a dwarf multicannon.
