gearNotes.heading: Equipment
gearNotes.text:
Vardorvis is weakest to slash attacks, followed by crush. The difference between the two is significant enough that crush is not recommended, however. Despite being an undead vampyre, Vardorvis is not susceptible to the effects of silver weaponry, Crumble Undead, or the Salve amulet.

The soulreaper axe is the best weapon to use against Vardorvis, as his 2x2 size and high defence inhibits the scythe of Vitur. Alternatively, the noxious halberd or blade of Saeldor work well, and lower tier slash weapons are also viable. However, due to Vardorvis healing on damage dealt to the player and having high defence, several equipment downgrades can compound and make the fight significantly longer.

Oathplate armour is extremely effective against Vardorvis due to its high slash defence and additional slash accuracy. Alternatively, a full set of justiciar armour can be used, which prevents Vardorvis from healing as often at the cost of lower melee strength. Echo boots can be used to provide defence and reflect damage; a ring of suffering serves the same purpose, but the DPS loss from not using an offensive ring is much greater. An amulet of blood fury can also provide longer trips, but the high upkeep cost and lower damage compared to the amulet of rancour can make it less desirable. The ancient godsword can instead be used to provide additional sustain if desired due to its guaranteed heal.

Players should be on the Arceuus spellbook to utilise thralls and Death Charge. Burning claws, dragon claws, and Voidwaker are all also effective options against Vardorvis in particular, with lower tier special attack weapons providing much less utility. If a player is confident in their ability to defeat the enrage phase, it is better to use these special attacks early in the fight due to their high accuracy. Otherwise, they are very useful at quickly ending the chaotic enrage phase towards the end of the kill.

In Awakened mode, an amulet of rancour is strongly recommended, as the player will generally be overhealing constantly to avoid dying to mistakes and as such rarely be capable of receiving the blood fury's healing effect.

When learning the Vardorvis fight, players are recommended to maximize slash defence. This can include opting to use a weaker 1-handed weapon (such as an abyssal tentacle) and a defender over stronger 2-handed weapons which provide little to no defence bonuses.

All weapons that have a Slashing combat style should be set to it, including Burning Claws if they are the special attack weapon used.

gearNotes.heading: Normal
gearNotes.text:
• Special attack weapon (e.g. dragon claws, burning claws, Arkan blade)
• 1 divine super combat potion

• House tablets (or Construct. cape/Max cape) or Desert amulet 4

tactics.heading: Overview
tactics.text:
After the completion of Desert Treasure II - The Fallen Empire, players can fight a stronger variant of Vardorvis. An even stronger awakened variant can be fought by climbing the rocks with an awakener's orb in the player's inventory and selecting "Yes" when prompted.

If the player dies while fighting Vardorvis, their grave will appear by the rocks leading to the Stranglewood Ritual Site. Players will have their reclamation fee reduced by 75% until they have five kills, after which the standard death cost will apply. Note: If you have an active gravestone prior to dying at Vardorvis, the full death cost applies without reduction.

tactics.heading: Requirements
tactics.text: • Completion of Quest Desert Treasure II - The Fallen Empire

tactics.heading: Suggested skills
tactics.text:
• 80+ Attack
• 85+ Strength
• 80+ Defence
• 85+ Hitpoints
• 76+ Magic for Resurrection spells

tactics.heading: Transportation
tactics.text:
The quickest methods of reaching the Stranglewood Ritual Site, where Vardorvis resides, are:
• Using the ring of shadows to teleport to the Stranglewood Temple entrance. This requires having used the strangled tablet on it, which is a 1/25 drop from Vardorvis.
• Using fairy ring code bls and run west to the rowboat. From there, run all the way west to the entryway leading to the Ritual Site.
• Using Xeric's talisman to teleport to Xeric's Honour, running east to the Mountain Guide and travelling to the base of Mount Quidamortem, then running west to the rowboat.
• Using Rada's blessing to teleport to the Kourend Woodland. From there, run north-east to Buneir and ride the Lovakengj Minecart Network to Mount Quidamortem. Run north-east to the Mountain Guide and travel to the base of Mount Quidamortem, then run west to the rowboat.

During the quest, the player should have unlocked the shortcut from the temple grounds to the ritual site; this will save a significant amount of time. If the shortcut is not accessible after the quest, the player must unlock it by running the long way to the ritual site and unlocking by using the shortcut at the other end.

Note: All routes will require player to traverse the Stranglewood, and players will be running past several Strangled and a Strangled Boar while reaching the boss, even with the shortcut unlocked. The strangled will deal 1-3 damage, while the boar can deal 2-4 damage if they attack the player. Make sure to click on the shortcut as soon as it renders, in the event of a disconnect. The shortcut is not indicated on the map but can be selected from North West of the Temple players teleport to with the ring of shadows.

tactics.heading: Fight overview
tactics.text:
Vardorvis has 700 hitpoints. He has an Attack level of 280 and attack bonus of +190, meaning he is very accurate regardless of the armour players use. He starts off with a Strength level of 270 and Defence level of 215. He is weakest to slashing attacks, with +65 slash, +85 crush and +215 stab defence bonus. Vardorvis is highly resistant to ranged and magic, with a Magic level of 215, +580 magic and ranged defence. Vardorvis only attacks with melee, but he is able to chase after players with routefinding. If Vardorvis is somehow unable to reach his target, he may either dart to them to catch up (without creating cracks in the ground) or may instead launch a crack under the player which can be avoided.

The melee attack has a max hit of 32, but will increase to 43 when his health is critically low. Both his normal and special attacks will also heal him for 50% of the damage inflicted, rounded down. Using Protect from Melee will reduce the potency of his auto-attacks by 75%, turning his max hit to 8-10.

Vardorvis, much like Duke Sucellus and The Whisperer, is not aggressive if fighting him after the quest, and the fight only begins when he is attacked. Once attacked, tendrils will burst from the ground and surround the arena. If the player did not bring a teleport, the tendrils can be used to quickly escape the arena, as the rock will have its options disabled. These tendrils will disappear after Vardorvis is killed, and the rock can be used once again to leave. Unlike the other bosses who use their special attacks at predictable intervals, Vardorvis uses them at random. This can be problematic during the enrage phase; learners are likely to be killed due to the large number of overlapping threats to manage.

Vardorvis has a unique mechanic in which his Strength and Defence levels scale linearly with his remaining hitpoints; as his health falls, his Defence level will lower, making him easier to hit, but his Strength level will increase, increasing his max hit. Due to this, defence-draining weapons are useless (zero Defence reduction), and players should opt for damage or sustain-type special weapons.

Upon reaching 33% of his health (~231 health), Vardorvis will enter an enrage phase after his next non-enraged attack. Similarly to Duke Sucellus, there is no visual indicator when enrage starts. During the enrage phase, Vardorvis' axes will appear more frequently, with a new set of axes appearing after the previous set have been thrown off the arena. The head will also appear at a more frequent rate, which when combined with spikes can deal a lot of damage or even kill the player if they are not prepared for it. If there is a lull in the axes, then the strangle mechanic is coming up, which can give players a brief moment of respite.

tactics.heading: Special attacks
tactics.text:
Unlike the other Desert Treasure II bosses, Vardorvis does not follow a set attack rotation; his special attacks are used at random.

Vardorvis will perform three auto-attacks before axes begin to appear in the arena.

• Swinging Axes: The Strangler's tendrils will bring up Vardorvis' axes into the arena before releasing them across the arena. Getting hit with this attack will deal up to 35 damage (reduced by ~50% with Protect from Melee) and additionally incurs a bleeding effect over the course of 14 ticks (8.4 seconds), which deals 15+ damage (3 bleed damage every 3 ticks, or every tick if the player runs while bleeding).
  • The amount of axes thrown is dependent on Vardorvis' health; one if he has more than 690 hitpoints, two between 231-690 hitpoints with a possibility of a third axe, and three after falling below 231 hitpoints.
  • The arena is divided into nine 3x3 quadrants, and the axes will follow either a straight or diagonal path, depending on where they emerge.
  • To dodge the axes, players must run two tiles diagonally away from where the axe is headed. Of these spots, twelve spots allow for safe axe dodging; one each in the cardinal four directions, and the two tiles in front of each pillar, towards the centre. The demonstration shown uses three of these twelve spots.
  • If axes are being swung from three quadrants horizontal to the player (either the near or far three quadrants), the player should run four tiles diagonally from the starting central square. Alternatively, the player may perform the Axe Skip manoeuvre, which involves tick-precise movement to "skip" over the Swinging Axes. The required movement depends on where they are swung from:

• Darting Spikes: Vardorvis will dart around the player, causing cracks in the ground which will release tendrils after a few seconds, dealing up to 25 damage and healing him for half the damage dealt. Under most circumstances, a crack will always appear under the player.
  • Standing by the edges of the arena (next to the tendrils) will cause Vardorvis to dart around in place, minimising the amount of cracks to one and also preventing one from appearing underneath the player.
  • Each dart will delay Vardorvis' next auto-attack by one tick.
  • The amount of darts Vardorvis makes is dependent on health; one above ~500 hitpoints, two from 231-500 hitpoints and three below ~130 hitpoints. The single crack that appears under the player, if allowed, will only appear for the first dart if the player does not move.
  • The layout of the cracks are always consistent; one dart leaves a half X in a 3x5 AoE, the second dart fills the other half, and the third fills random spots in a 5x5 AoE centered on the player, assuming the player is not standing near the edges of the arena and is not running diagonally from the boss.
• Head Gaze: Once below 570 health, the Strangler's tendrils will begin to use Vardorvis' Head to launch a single green projectile, indicated by the game message . The head will fire a green, cone-shaped projectile at the player, which must be blocked with Protect from Missiles.
  • Failing to block the attack will drain 10 prayer points and prevent use of overhead protection prayers for 3 ticks if Vardorvis is not killed before the projectile lands.
  • The projectile will always hit off-sync with the body's attacks. He will not melee while the projectile is in the air and will take 2 ticks to begin attacking again after the projectile has hit the player. As stated above however, failing to block the attack will likely result in the body attacking and dealing damage. The only instance this would not occur is if Vardorvis' Darting Spikes mechanic causes him to dash three times in a row.
  • The head's appearance is completely random, but will usually appear alongside an axe cycle.
• Strangle: Once below 570 health, Vardorvis will begin using this attack in which he strikes his arm into the ground and entangle the player in tendrils. Several spores will appear at the centre of the game screen, and the player must destroy them all within 5 game ticks, otherwise the tendrils will tighten and deal high damage.
  • The mechanic will prevent the player from attacking, but Vardorvis is still able to attack through the animation.
    • However, it is possible to resume normal attack speed by right clicking on Vardorvis, then selecting the attack option after the tendril overlay appears. This helps get a free hit in without losing ticks.
  • A minimum of four spores can appear in the overlay, with the number increasing the more times Vardorvis uses this attack, up to a maximum of six.

tactics.heading: Awakened mode
tactics.text:
In Awakened mode, Vardorvis has the following changes:
• The boss's health increases from 700 to 1,400.
• The boss is immune to stat drains.
• An additional Swinging Axe appears for each set of axe thrown.
  • While unlikely, two axes will spawn if Vardorvis has taken less than 20 damage.
  • Three axes are guaranteed from 462-1,380 health, with the possibility of a fourth axe appearing.
  • Below 462 health, four axes are guaranteed to appear.
• Swinging Axes damage increased from 35 to 96.
• Swinging Axes will deal damage upon appearing. This will not cause a bleed however.
• Swinging Axes spawn on par with normal mode enrage speed for the entire fight.
• Bleed damage is increased from 3 to 5.
• The spores from his Strangle attack have to be destroyed before the tendrils tighten. Damage is increased from ~25 to ~40.
• Damage from Darting Spikes increases from 25 to 40.
• Vardorvis' Head may use a magic attack (resembling a blue crescent wave) to disable protection prayers.
  • Once below 50% health, Vardorvis' Head will attack in pairs of both magic and ranged projectiles, launching 1 tick apart in a random order.
• The black mask and Slayer helmet do not apply their usual on-task damage and accuracy bonuses while on a Vardorvis boss slayer task.

Due to the increased frequency and number of axes swung, performing axe skipping is just about mandatory to successfully complete the fight. It is possible to complete a kill without axe skipping, but this will require a lot of precise movement and the ability to stay calm during enrage. Players are recommended to stand in the corner quadrants of the arena and should avoid the cardinal directions whenever possible. Under most circumstances, the player should utilise one of the four corner quadrants and continually run back and forth whenever an axe appears at and across from that quadrant.

Unlike normal mode, where the player would normally stand by the edges by the tendrils and are safe from axes when they first appear, players must instead stand by the pillars, due to the axes damaging upon appearing and the anti-edge mechanics. It is extremely important to prioritise movement over attacking, as getting caught by an axe off-prayer will deal up to 96 damage (half with prayer) and is almost guaranteed to instantly kill the player when combined with Vardorvis' own attacks. As with normal mode, praying against melee will significantly reduce his overall damage. The spikes and strangle attack can also deal up to 40 damage if not dealt with properly. Unless the player is able to consistently clear spores with the reduced time, it is not recommended to use the strangle trick to deal extra damage.

While the first half of the fight is basically the same as normal mode enrage, the difficulty increases once Vardorvis reaches under 50% health, as the head will now begin attacking in pairs, with one using magic and the other using ranged one tick apart from each other, necessitating the need to frequently perform two actions in the span of one tick (ex. flicking projectiles and axe skipping simultaneously); one tip is to only pay attention to the first head's projectile, and pray against it immediately, then using the opposing prayer once the attack lands and then returning to protecting from melee, as the second projectile will always be the other combat style.

A second difficulty spike begins once enrage begins, with the player having to handle four axes at a time while the heads' spawn rate is increased, often resulting in the player having to flick six times in the span of one axe cycle. If a prayer is missed, prioritise dodging and eating immediately, praying against the next head attack after the body does so. Trying to react to the body's attack after a missed prayer will likely result in the next two projectiles hitting, significantly increasing the chance of death. If there is a lull in the heads, it means Vardorvis is about to use his Strangle attack.

gearNotes.heading: Equipment
gearNotes.text:
• Note that Venators are not undead, therefore items such as Salve amulet will have no effect on them.
• Efaritay's aid provides a 15% accuracy bonus that stacks with slayer helmet.

tactics.text: Venators can only be found in Vampyrium.

tactics.heading: Recommendations
tactics.text:
• High combat stats. Although not required, see the skill levels below for an indication of the advised stats:
  • Level 50 Attack or higher
  • Level 70 Strength or higher
  • Level 70 Prayer and 70 Defence or higher for Piety, or at least 43 Prayer/41 Prayer for Protect from Melee/Protect from Missiles
• 73 Agility to access the shortcut to the Hunting Grounds, a pickaxe is required to clear rubble south of the shortcut.
• 70 Construction to build a bank chest in Sangvesti.
• If not burying the bones with a Bonecrusher or Bonecrusher necklace, and if you have unlocked Bones to Peaches at the Mage Training Arena, then converting bone drops into peaches can help recover the chip damage that Venators deal through protection prayers.

gearNotes.heading: Equipment
gearNotes.text:
For Venenatis, her location in deep wild in multicombat should warrant extra precautions. Bring defensive armour, especially against magic attacks from other players, as even with a scout and perfect reactions you can be caught inside the cave. Reduce risk accordingly.

For Spindel, her location below 30 wilderness means escaping other players is much easier. However, players may bring more powerful equipment that can deal more damage. Spindel also has a lower defence level compared to Venenatis, so your equipment and setup can focus more on strength bonus and longevity.
The Ursine chainmace is the strongest weapon against Venenatis while costing coins. The strongest 4 items to bring are generally the Chainmace, your strongest defender, the Amulet of rancour, and your best strength ring (Ultor ring or Berserker ring(i)). A 4th item can be brought if you are confident in not getting Smited by Pkers. Further upgrades are generally very expensive and add little additional damage for their risk and cost. Trouver parchments can be used on certain gear, such as an Infernal cape or Fighter torso, to gain additional strength bonus for additional risk of 500000+ coins each, however this is not generally recommended due to the risk of multi-wilderness.

The Webweaver and Craw's bow offer competitive damage against Venenatis and Spindel despite their higher ranged defences. Ranged also has the luxury of staying closer to the exit in case of pkers, however you need to monitor and change your overhead prayers depending on the attack cycle. The Twisted bow and Bow of Faerdhinen are also both strong alternatives to some melee setups, although are generally not advised due the significant risk of being smited in multi-combat and from Venenatis' webs. Crossbows generally perform worse than most melee weapons, but offer the relative safety of being able to stay south of the entrance.

gearNotes.heading: Inventory
gearNotes.text:
You should aim to take 4 valuable items you wish to keep if killed by another player, usually Craw's bow, Necklace of rupture, Slayer helmet (i) (on-task), and Dinh's bulwark provide the best balance of damage against Venenatis and survivability against other players.

• Dinh's Bulwark, Grey chinchompas, Darts/Throwing knives, or Blighted ancient ice sacks — kill spiderlings quickly, ordered from fastest to slowest
  • Note that setting your Combat Options to defensive provides an invisble +5 level boost to your defence and also reduces non-pvp damage by 20% (with the Bulwark equipped) [Prevents attacking]
  • The shield's animation will play when the wielder fails to block an incoming attack. This can alert the wielder to heal as it occurs prior to the hit landing.
• Looting bag
• Stamina potion
• Ranging potion
• Anti-venom/Sanfew serum(s) — cures/prevents venom from player killers and poisonous spiders in the Escape Caves
• Blighted super restores
• Blighted anglerfish/Blighted manta ray for the rest, at least one Blighted karambwan(s)
Optional:
• Phoenix necklace — emergency healing whilst tanking
• Saradomin brews — more expensive outlast healing, combo eating with hard food is invaluable
• Royal seed pod — if not bringing a charged amulet of glory or ring of wealth
• Wilderness crabs teleport, Annakarl teleport (tablet), or Wilderness sword 4's fountain of rune — reach the Silk Chasm faster

gearNotes.heading: Example melee setup
gearNotes.text:
The aim is to maximise damage output while minimising risk. The protected items should be items that either grant very high melee strength bonus increases or a large percentage damage increase like the Slayer helmet (i). The ultor ring and the avernic defender both give major buffs to the player's offensive stats, and can be used along with cheaper items to deal high damage with limited risk. Items that can be easily replaced such as barrows gloves, amulet of strength, and dragonhide armour are wise choices as the chance of dying is fairly high.

If on a boss task, the player can use bracelet of slaughter to extend the task. This will affect damage output, but lower the player's risk slightly.

gearNotes.heading: Items protected:
gearNotes.text:
• Ultor ring
• Ursine chainmace / Viggora's chainmace — This adds between and to the value risked, as it uses revenant ether for charges. The DPS difference from Inquisitor's mace is significant.
• Avernic defender (Can be switched out to Book of War in order to use Dinh's bulwark, as this can be used to AoE minions and survive attacks from PKers)
• Slayer helmet (i) if on a slayer task

gearNotes.heading: Example ranged setup
gearNotes.text:
The Masori body (f) can be traded out for a Black d'hide body and Dinh's bulwark for survivability and AoE damage against the spiderlings. Ranged allows the player to more easily damage the enemy for the duration of the entire fight, and stand closer to the door where it may be more safe. In lower risk gear, the damage output of the bow doesn't match up to melee; the difference is significant.

Additionally, due to the bows faster attack speed, the player consumes more revenant ether than if they were using melee. This is compounded by the longer fights with more hits. Because of this, extra ether is risked and used for slower fights, reducing potential profits.

As with melee, the player can use bracelet of slaughter to extend the task, if on a boss task for Venenatis. This will affect the player's accuracy and magic defence slightly.

gearNotes.text:
Inventory setup will vary greatly depending on your gear and team. When deciding what supplies to bring, keep in mind that Venenatis frequently drops large quantities of un-noted blighted food or potions that replace supplies used during the fight. Make sure to have the following:
• Dinh's Bulwark, grey chinchompas, blisterwood stakes, darts/throwing knives, or Blighted ancient ice sacks — kill spiderlings quickly, ordered from fastest to slowest
• Looting bag
• Stamina potion
• Divine/Super combat potion

Optional:

• Divine rune pouch locked with a trouver parchment — if using Arceeus spellbook, allows for more supplies

tactics.heading: Overview
tactics.text:
Warning: Venenatis resides in a multi-way area in moderately high-level Wilderness. You may be attacked at any time during the fight, and this is always a possibility in any deep wilderness multicombat area. Do not bring any items that you are not willing to lose. Items like the Dragon defender become broken if not protected on death.

Venenatis is a level 464 spider boss that is found in the Silk Chasm. Completion of the medium Wilderness Diary is required to fight Venenatis. Spindel is the level 302 lesser variant of Venenatis found in the Web Chasm, requiring the hard Wilderness Diary to access, but otherwise her mechanics are identical. Being on a Venenatis slayer task bypasses the diary requirement for both bosses.

tactics.heading: Transportation
tactics.text:
Venenatis is located in the Silk Chasm, which is a lair in the far east of the Wilderness at level 35.

• A Wilderness crabs teleport is the fastest way to reach Venenatis, and will teleport you to the dark crab fishing spot just south-east of the lair.
• With 90 Magic, players on the Ancient spellbook can use Annakarl Teleport, which will teleport them into the Demonic Ruins. Simply go south-east of your location after arriving. Be wary of PK'ers upon arrival.
  • Alternatives to this also include the Annakarl teleport tablet and a portal attuned to Annakarl. Be wary of PK'ers on arrival; if using the house portal, you should have a scrying pool to check the area first.
• With 57 Woodcutting, players can make a Waka canoe and use it to go to the Wilderness. Go east of your location past Vet'ion's rest and the poisonous spiders.
• A games necklace to teleport to the Corporeal Beast's lair, exit the cave then run north-east.
• Players who have completed the Hard Wilderness Diary can utilise the Wilderness obelisks to teleport to levels 19, 35, or 55 to get closer to the Silk Chasm.
• Players who have completed the Hard or Elite Wilderness Diary can use the Wilderness Sword to teleport to the Fountain of Rune and run south-west to Venenatis.

tactics.heading: Attacks
tactics.text:
Venenatis has many attacks that she uses against her target.

• Melee attack: She simply lunges at the player
• Ranged attack: Launches green spit at players
• Magic attack: Launches webs at players
• Sticky Web: Venenatis will occasionally deploy a sticky web at a player, sending a white-blue web at the target's location. It will then expand into a 7x5 AoE - while in this web, any player caught in it will take rapid hits of 3 damage, have their prayer drained by 3, and run energy by 10.
  • Note that aranea boots will only negate the first tick of damage taken from the web attack. Because of this, it is not recommended to use them at Venenatis due to the extremely small benefit they will provide, while adding unnecessary risk.
• Spiderlings: Venenatis will occasionally call some spiderlings to assist her in battle. While fairly weak, they will drain prayer on every hit regardless if prayed against or hits. They will also increase her damage and allow her to hit through prayers if left alive. Thrall damage is reduced while spiderlings are alive.

tactics.heading: Suggested skills
tactics.text:
• 75 Attack (85+ Recommended)
• 80 Strength (90+ Recommended)
• 70 Hitpoints (85+ Recommended)
• 75 Ranged (85+ Recommended if ranging)
• 70 Defence (75+ Recommended)
• 94+ Magic

tactics.heading: Overview
tactics.text:
Venenatis can attack with all three forms of combat. While she will only use one combat style at a time, players in melee distance will instead only be attacked by melee. Like Vet'ion, she is weakest to crush.

She will begin the fight using 8 range attacks, followed by 8 magic attacks, all while moving position every 4 attacks. She will spawn spiderlings on the 1st range attack in cycle, and deploy her web attack on the 3rd mage attack in the cycle. This pattern will repeat until Venenatis is defeated.

All players who enter the arena will appear to the north, so it is recommended to hang south as much as possible to escape player killers, as she is no longer under level 30 Wilderness following the Wilderness boss rework. This does not apply to the weaker variant of the boss, Spindel, as her lair is still below level 30 Wilderness and can be teleported out of directly.

Players should avoid the webs at all costs, as their ability to drain run energy will prevent them from escaping from player killers.

The web can be positioned safely by standing on the outskirt of the arena on the 3rd magic attack to help prevent accidentally walking into the web.

The spiderlings should be killed as soon as they spawn to prevent them from empowering her too much; fortunately, they only have 5 health and can be killed in one hit by any combat style.

• Darts or Throwing knives can quickly eliminate individual spiderlings.
• Any tier of Chinchompa can eliminate multiple spiderlings with a well-placed shot (Ensure PK Skull prevention is activated).
• Players with 70+ Magic and Ancient Magicks can use a burst spell with Blighted ancient ice sacks to eliminate multiple spiderlings at once.

gearNotes.heading: Equipment
gearNotes.text:
Always keep risk to a minimum in the Wilderness! - Whenever gearing, check your Items Kept on Death and enable "Wilderness beyond level 20" to make sure important items will not be lost.

The most effective equipment to fight Vet'ion involves a large amount of risk by using items that can be protected with Trouver parchments, but most players should opt for cheaper setups until they are confident in their ability to handle PKers. The Ursine chainmace is by far the most effective weapon against Vet'ion, but comes with additional risk as it must be charged with Revenant ether. Players should choose three (or four, with Protect item if you are confident you can mitigate the risk of being Smited) valuable with the most strength bonus possible compared to cheaper alternatives.

Note: The benefit from Salve amulet (e) does not stack with a Slayer helmet. As Salve amulets are free and kept on death below Level 20 Wilderness they should always be prioritised.

gearNotes.heading: Example setup
gearNotes.text:
The aim is to maximise damage output while minimising risk. Choosing three items with a large amount of melee strength bonus is recommended, such as
the ultor ring or the avernic defender, and using cheap items otherwise which can be easily replaced such as barrows gloves, Salve amulet (e), and the helm of Neitiznot.

If on a skeleton or boss task, the player can use bracelet of slaughter to extend the task. This will affect damage output, but lower the player's risk slightly.

gearNotes.heading: Inventory
gearNotes.text:
As Vet'ion is possible to defeat without taking any damage, supplies are mostly tailored to surviving PKers. Vet'ion frequently drops un-noted blighted food or potions that replace supplies used during the fight.

• Royal seed pod or any other level 30 Wilderness teleport. Ring of wealth (5) can be configured to be a one-click teleport to the Grand Exchange using menu entry swapper.
• Divine super combat potion
• 4+ Blighted super restores or Prayer potions and 1+ Sanfew serum
• Saradomin brews with blighted super restores for emergency food
• Looting bag (strongly recommended, can also be obtained from Vet'ion or his summons)
• Some form of antipoison e.g. Sanfew serums (optional, recommended, if poisoned/venomed by a PKer or inside the escape caves)
• Rest food — Blighted manta ray or blighted anglerfish at 93+ Hitpoints (optional: 2+ Blighted karambwan for combo-eating)
• Stamina potion, Guthix rest (+5% energy per dose), summer pies (+10% energy per half) for escaping PKers —

For more advanced setups, if players are confident in their ability to tank PKers to safety and are comfortable risking more and/or staying longer, an inventory could look more like the second example. None of these are required for the boss fight and may add some risk, but can be worthwhile additions for players barely failing to escape.

• Dinh's bulwark switch — greatly increase survivability against multiple attackers
  • Note that setting your Combat Options to defensive provides an invisble +5 level boost to your defence and also reduces non-pvp damage by 20% (with the Bulwark equipped)
  • The shield's animation will play when the wielder fails to block an incoming attack. This can alert the wielder to heal as it occurs prior to the hit landing
• Phoenix necklace — emergency healing whilst tanking
• Anti-venom or Sanfew serums — cures/prevents venom from the commonly used weapons such as the toxic staff of the dead or noxious halberd. The player can bring one or two doses of each to reduce total cost.
• Consider bringing low-risk hand slot switches with high magical defence bonuses such as a staff of earth and red d'hide shield (can be brought with Dinh's bulwark for the duration of being unfrozen)
• Alternatively bring a rune crossbow with cheap bolts instead of a staff to fight back while being frozen/entangled to force PKers to eat instead of attacking you (less effective against multiple attackers)

tactics.heading: Overview
tactics.text:
Warning: Vet'ion resides in a multi-way area in moderately high-level Wilderness. Completion of the medium Wilderness Diary is required to fight Vet'ion.

You may be attacked at any time during the fight, and death is all but guaranteed in any deep wilderness multicombat area. Do not bring any items that you are not willing to lose. Some untradeable items like the Dragon defender will become broken or mangled, requiring you to pay to repair them if they are not protected on death or protected with a trouver parchment.

tactics.heading: Transportation
tactics.text:
Vet'ion resides in Vet'ion's Rest, the entrance of which is located just north of the Bone Yard. There is a small building where he originally roamed before his rework where the player may drop into his chambers, requiring a fee of 50,000 coins to enter which can be taken from the bank. This fee decreases by 10,000 for every kill for the player who deals the most damage. The fee is not required again on subsequent trips unless killed by another player.

To get there quickly, you can:

• Teleport to the level 40 Revenant Caves entrance with a Revenant cave teleport, then run south-east.
• Teleport to Carralanger with a tablet or your PoH portal, then run north-east.
• Teleport to Annakarl with a tablet or your PoH portal, then run south-west.
• Teleport to the Wilderness Obelisk at level 35 wildy from outside Ferox Enclave or your PoH, then run east.
• Teleport to the Corporeal Beast's Lair with a Games necklace or your PoH, then exit the cave and run north.
• Teleport to the black chinchompa hunting ground with level 99 Hunter and a hunter cape, then run east. NOTE: as Vet'ion's Rest lies beyond level 20 Wilderness, you will LOSE your cape on death.
• Ride a waka canoe up to the Wilderness pond from any canoe station with 57 Woodcutting and any type of axe, then run east.

tactics.heading: Suggested skills
tactics.text:
• 70+ Attack
• 70+ Strength
• 70+ Defence
• 75+ Hitpoints
• 70+ Prayer (for Piety, highly recommended)

tactics.heading: Attacks and abilities
tactics.text:
Vet'ion has several attacks and abilities:
• Magic attack: Five bolts of lightning strike various tiles across the arena, much like the Grotesque Guardians' lightning attack. Each lightning bolt deals damage in a 3x3 area, but any tile that is about to be struck glows, giving players the chance to dodge the attack. When soloing, one bolt will always target the player's tile or an adjacent tile, while four more will target random tiles around the arena. In groups, one bolt will appear for every player in the chamber, capped at seven. Being caught in its AoE will deal light damage, while being directly on a strike will deal higher damage.
• Hellhounds: Upon reaching half health, Vet'ion will summon two skeletal hellhounds to attack players. They attack with melee, so activate Protect from Melee when they spawn or keep it active during the fight. They will provide him with complete damage immunity while present. He will do the same again in his enraged form.
• Shield Bash: Vet'ion will raise his shield to bash an area in front or around and underneath him; shadows will appear forewarning the AoE of the attack. If the player doesn't move out of range, they'll take up to 35 damage and be unable to attack for the next 4.8 seconds. This attack is only used when in melee distance.
• Enraged Form: Upon losing all health in his first form, Vet'ion will summon orange lightning bolts (which share his standard lightning bolts' 3x3 area damage) in a circle around him and restore his health to full. In his second form, the hellhound mechanic is repeated, but he will die after losing all of his health in this form.

tactics.heading: Strategies
tactics.text:
While Vet'ion's stats were not changed following the 25 January 2023 rework, Vet'ion has the highest defensive capabilities of the three bosses. However, his negative crush defence of -10 makes him fairly easy to hit.

Since all of Vet'ion's attacks are AoE it is possible to avoid all damage from his attacks - meaning it is possible to logout or hop worlds during the fight to avoid player killers if you haven't taken any damage 10 seconds prior. This will eject the player outside his arena into the Escape Caves. The shield bash is the only major concern due to its larger AoE, but is still otherwise easy to dodge as the attack is signalled by a slight delay from his regular attacks.

When Vet'ion reaches 50% of his health in either form he will summon Skeletal Hellhounds during his first and Greater Skeletal Hellhounds in his second phase to assist him in battle. The hellhounds will channel immunity to Vet'ion until they are killed. While they deal powerful melee hits, they are not durable, with both the normal and greater versions only having 30 health. Vet'ion will gain 90% damage resistance after falling below half health, so it is not possible to skip the hellhounds.

Upon reaching 0 health in his standard form, he will charge up lightning around him as he yells that the player has to defeat him a second time. This can be avoided by being far enough from him or standing under him in his middle tiles. Vet'ion will restore his health to full, restore any drained stats, increase his max hit and attack speed from a 6 tick cycle to 5 ticks.

As Vet'ion will move towards a player between his attacks, the player can draw him towards the exit to his arena and keep him there for the majority of the time. This is fairly easy to set up in small teams and for solo players and enables a faster escape, as getting frozen in the middle of the room will likely result in death from both player killers and Vet'ion's attacks.

Unlike his lesser counterpart Calvar'ion, Vet'ion resides in a Multicombat area and in level 35 Wilderness, so teleports cannot be used to directly escape player killers. The only chance a player has to escape is by running out the exit, which will take them into the Escape Caves where they must navigate their way to an exit. The Escape Caves are full of aggressive monsters, such as Grizzly bears and poison spiders, so antipoison is recommended. It is recommended to leave a "scout" outside, giving the player an early warning and can sometimes cause other players to ignore whoever is inside.

In the event you are targeted by player killers and are leaving via the escape caves, the fastest exit to level 30 Wilderness for a teleport is the southern exit from the caves. However, the north-eastern exit is preferrable for players confident in their ability to tank a single PKer to level 30 wilderness or for the duration of a Tele Block, as teams may wait at the southern entrance to attack players.

gearNotes.heading: Equipment
gearNotes.text:
The dragon hunter crossbow, (with ruby and diamond dragon bolts (e)), is the most effective ranged weapon to use against Vorkath. The crossbow's passive effect damage and accuracy boosts stack with the Salve amulet (i) / Salve amulet(ei) and Void Knight equipment. When using diamond dragon bolts for the last third of the kill instead of a blowpipe, Elite Void generally has better damage output than Masori armour. However, Masori provides additional magic defence over Elite Void, which can extend trips by reducing the amount of food eaten – especially relevant if using a reagent pouch to store crushed superior dragon bones.
The Toxic blowpipe (especially with defence reductions), with Masori armour can provide higher damage output than the dragon hunter crossbow as the ruby bolts' damage begins to fall off. However, the blowpipe is much more expensive to use over time (especially with dragon darts), and requires praying magic without a shield which significantly increases overall damage received from ranged and dragonfire attacks.
Players should note that the Salve amulet and Salve amulet (e) provide no bonuses to Ranged whatsoever; the amulet must be imbued (i) or (ei) to provide Ranged bonuses. Rings of recoil do not inflict damage on Vorkath.
In order to take the least amount of damage possible, players should use a dragonfire ward or anti-dragon shield with a crossbow, while praying Protect from Missiles. The dragonfire shield is an inferior option to the anti-dragon shield despite its defences, as it provides a negative Ranged bonus. Other offhand items such as the twisted buckler or book of law force players to pray Protect from Magic, causing them to take more damage each kill, and shortening their trips.
With 99 Ranged and a high Defence level, players should expect anywhere from 3-6 kills with this setup.

The dragon hunter lance is the most effective melee weapon to use against Vorkath. The lance's passive effect damage and accuracy boosts stack with the salve amulet(ei), so it scales incredibly well with high-tier armour and jewellery. With worse equipment, the Osmumten's fang is sometimes a superior option.

Players use Protect from Magic and wear the best melee armour possible to maximise their ranged defence. Players should stay in melee range when not dealing with specials, as despite taking the occasional melee, being out of melee range increases the rate of ranged attacks and results in more damage taken overall. If using defence-draining specials, the Bandos godsword is superior over the dragon warhammer due to the increased accuracy even when factoring in a defender for the warhammer. If your gear has -64 magic attack bonus or lower, your Crumble Undead will not hit.
Below Bandos equipment, prioritise defensive bonuses over strength bonus if you find your trips cut short by Vorkath's normal melee and ranged attacks. With regard to profit, consistently higher kills per trip are more valuable than marginal damage gains. Additionally, if sacrificing defensive bonuses for melee strength in a given slot, ensure that you are actually gaining a max hit (check with the DPS Calculator) and that you are not reducing your kills per trip. For example, depending on your other equips and Strength level, it is possible that the +2 melee strength bonus of Bandos tassets does not improve your max hit and instead increases the likelihood that your trips are cut short compared to using Justiciar legguards, which has higher melee and ranged defences.

gearNotes.heading: Inventory setups
gearNotes.text:
In all setups, chaos runes must be brought in order to cast Crumble Undead, along with dust runes (or air and earth runes). A rune pouch (or its divine variant) can be used to significantly reduce the number of inventory slots needed. As air and earth runes will already be brought, law runes can be brought to cast Teleport to House as a cheap teleport option.

Fire and nature runes can also be brought to cast High Level Alchemy on Vorkath's valuable drops, but will take up additional inventory space. With a divine rune pouch, nature runes can be brought without taking up an extra inventory space, and a low quantity of fire runes (20-30) can be brought outside of it, with leftovers being dropped at the site to free up the space for more loot.

Much of the value of Vorkath's drops is in its guaranteed drop of superior dragon bones. To save space in inventory without a significant loss in profit, if not all bones can be picked up at once, a pestle and mortar and reagent pouch can be brought to convert the bones to crushed superior dragon bones, which can be stored in the pouch. Be aware that crushed bones will not sell as quickly as the original version.

A Huntsman's kit with multiple Imp-in-a-box stored inside can also be used to effectively increase the number of drops that can be picked up.

• An ammo switch (if using crossbow)
• Zaryte crossbow preferably. Toxic blowpipe alternatively (for special, if using crossbow)
• 1 extended anti-venom+ (skip if using Serpentine helm)
• 3-4 super restores or prayer potions (crossbow only; 1-2 with blowpipe)
• Rune pouch with dust runes, law runes, and chaos runes to cast Crumble Undead spells and Teleport to House
• Divine ranging potion or a Divine bastion potion
• Extended super antifire (regular extended antifire works, but is less effective)
• An emergency teleport (optional)
• A teleport to Rellekka (see the section above for teleports of choice)
• Food (sharks or better, preferably manta rays for longer trips; with very high stats and optimal gear, an inventory of karambwans is likely to be more than enough while they have a lower attack delay when eaten during combat)
• Guthix rest allow you to heal small amounts of health without losing ticks, otherwise cooked karambwan are useful for combo eating at low HP. It can also be used as a replacement to extended anti-venom+, as it reduces venom to poison.

Tip: Players may use their antifire and stat boost potions at a bank to create more room for food.

Tip: Bringing a Slayer's staff while setting Crumble Undead as the auto-cast spell is an easy transition and safer alternative to using the spell from the spellbook.

Note: This setup is only recommended if you do not have a dragon hunter crossbow or dragon hunter lance.

• Melee gear for 2 special attacks. If using dragon warhammer, mythical cape is better for the higher crush accuracy compared to the fire cape.
• 1 super antifire potion
• 1 extended anti-venom+ (skip if using Serpentine helm)
• 1 divine bastion or ranging potion
• 1 super combat potion
• 1-2 prayer potions
• 13 sharks or better

• Law runes (in rune pouch) or house tablets to Teleport to House to refill special attack after the fight

• An emergency teleport (optional)

• A Slayer staff can be used to autocast Crumble Undead while also ensuring your magic bonus is more than -64 so you will almost never splash (Alternatives are slayer's staff (e), staff of the dead, toxic staff of the dead, staff of light, staff of balance, void knight mace, Skull sceptre.)
• Voidwaker or Burning claws for special attacks
• 1 extended anti-venom+ (skip if using Serpentine helm)
• 3-4 super restore or prayer potion
• Rune pouch with dust runes, law runes, and chaos runes to cast Crumble Undead spells and Teleport to House

• Anglerfish for overhealing at the start of a trip (Players may find it worthwhile to bring more to overheal before each kill)
• Food (sharks or better, preferably manta rays or dark crabs to ensure longer trips)

Tip: Players may use their antifire and stat boost potions at a bank to create more room for food.

Tip: If choosing not to use a staff to autocast Crumble Undead, make sure that your magic bonus is higher than -64, otherwise you will occasionally splash on the spawn.

tactics.heading: Overview
tactics.text:
After completion of Dragon Slayer II, Vorkath can be fought again. This time, it is stronger.

To get to Vorkath, talk to Torfinn, located in Rellekka on the 3rd dock to the right. This brings you to Ungael, at the entrance of Vorkath.

Warning: Beware of Vorkath's acid pool quickfire barrage, insta-kill vertical dragonfire, and suicide spawn as each of these attacks can kill players almost immediately.

tactics.heading: Requirements
tactics.text: • Completion of QuestDragon Slayer II for access to Ungael.

tactics.heading: Suggested skills
tactics.text:
• 85+ Ranged (Ranged method)
• 80+ Attack (Melee method)
• 85+ Strength (Melee method)
• 75+ Defence
• 70+ Prayer for Piety (74+ for Rigour)
• 82+ Construction (for Ornate rejuvenation pool (with boost) - (optional for faster resupply and resetting))

tactics.heading: Fight overview
tactics.text:
Vorkath is similar to most dragons in that it is weak against stab melee and heavy ranged. Upon awakening, Vorkath's attack pattern consists of six random standard attacks, one special attack, another six standard attacks, then the other special attack, and so on until defeated. During the fight, it is recommended to always maintain at least a super antifire potion and Protect from Magic, or a regular antifire potion and a dragonfire protection shield.

Whether to have run on during the fight is a matter of preference. Keeping run on, except for during the acid special attack, increases the margin for error when dodging the fireball attack, but requires the player to manually toggle run when the acid attack occurs. Leaving run off eliminates the need to toggle and players can rely on quick reactions to dodge the fireball while walking, and use Ctrl-click to override the run setting if needed.

The optimal protection prayers to use will depend on the gear being used:
• Protect from Magic if using melee, a toxic blowpipe, or if holding a book of law (along with a super antifire potion)
• Protect from Missiles if using a crossbow with a dragonfire ward, dragonfire shield or anti-dragon shield

Vorkath is capable of envenoming players with its venom dragonfire; as such, bring appropriate venom protection. The prayer dragonfire turns all active prayers off, including Preserve; for this reason, divine potions are recommended over normal potions. Additionally, recoil damage such as Vengeance and rings of recoil do not work on Vorkath.

tactics.heading: Standard attacks
tactics.text:
Vorkath uses the following standard attacks:

• Vorkath's standard attacks are unreactable, and therefore the player should constantly pray against the attack style they are weakest to

• Dragonfire: Aside from standard dragonfire, Vorkath has multiple variants that it can use, similar to the King Black Dragon

tactics.heading: Advanced dragonfire
tactics.text: Vorkath's advanced dragonfire attacks that are not all affected by dragonfire protection.

tactics.heading: Rapid Fire
tactics.text:
Rapid Fire is the deadliest of Vorkath's attacks, and is one of the two special attacks it'll use after six standard attacks. When used, Vorkath will launch acid pools around the arena (with one landing on where the player stood), then fire dragonbreath every tick at the tile the player is standing on.

Standing on or running over an acid pool will deal up to 10 damage, which Vorkath will leech as health. Getting hit by the rapid-fire dragonfire will deal 25-41 damage regardless of the player's dragonfire protection. As such, the basic principle to surviving this special attack is to always be on the move whilst walking on clean tiles. Players can find a line (at least five tiles free of acid) and walk back and forth said line. This is relatively safe but no damage will be dealt to Vorkath in the process.

If you find that you are still taking damage despite walking consistently, especially when changing direction, note that your character's true tile is roughly two tiles ahead of where your character's animation is shown to be. You should change direction on a safe line well before you reach the end of your current path to avoid stopping and taking damage.

Players new to fighting Vorkath may use the fact that there is always an acid-free line directly next to the exit, when walking side to side ('hugging' the wall). Be wary that running to this back line while the acid is being thrown has a chance of spawning an acid pool in this line, because theres a chance Vorkath throws acid right behind you, regardless of proximity to the entrance.

tactics.heading: The Woox Walk
tactics.text:
Experienced players may utilise a technique known as the "Woox Walk", named after the player who devised it, to continue attacking Vorkath whilst avoiding his dragonfire attacks. Mastering the Woox Walk is highly recommended for players seeking to kill Vorkath many times over, as this significantly decreases kill time and results in more kills per hour, despite the halved damage he takes during this special attack. It is generally easier to learn with sounds enabled, as you should click every time you hear Vorkath shoot its fireball. Practicing the moves throughout the fight is also useful for learning with no punishment upon mistakes.

The basic principle of the Woox Walk involves tick-perfect movements to move towards Vorkath to attack, then immediately moving to another tile out of the player's attack range, then moving to attack again once they are able. It is recommended to enable tile highlighting in the settings, then enabling "Highlight current tile", as this helps visualise which tile you are on rather than using your character to do so.

The way in which the Woox Walk is performed is dependent on the type of weapon chosen:

tactics.heading: Zombified Spawn
tactics.text:
Vorkath's other special attack involves launching an icy breath toward the player. While this deals no damage, it will freeze the player in place, and Vorkath will spit out a Zombified Spawn that always lands ten tiles away from the player. Vorkath is immune to damage as soon as the breath is launched, and remains as such until the spawn is killed or explodes.

The spawn has 38 Hitpoints and will walk towards the player. If it reaches the player, it will explode, dealing damage based on its current Hitpoints prior to explosion; this can deal up to 60 damage. Casting Crumble Undead will instantly kill the spawn, and it will always hit, provided that the player's Magic attack bonus is above -64. If the spell is cast and lands on the spawn just as it reaches the player, it will explode, but no damage will be incurred. Once the spawn is killed or explodes, the freeze will wear off and Vorkath can be damaged again.

It is best to bring a magic staff swap, ideally a slayer's staff or dust battlestaff for the spawn; the former allows for auto-casting, while the latter eliminates the need for dust runes. It is important to avoid attacking after Vorkath's sixth auto-attack, since Vorkath becomes immune to damage before the breath is launched and also prevents delay from setting in. While there is more than enough time to kill the spawn if this occurs, Vorkath is immune to damage, rendering the extra attacks null. One way to avoid continuing to attack Vorkath is to keep auto-retaliate off and eat food or drink a potion when hit with the icy breath. This will stop the player from attacking Vorkath and give more time to cast Crumble Undead on the spawn.

tactics.heading: Divine potions
tactics.text: It is recommended to use divine potions over normal potions at Vorkath, as the prayer-disabling dragonfire's timing often causes Preserve's +30 second timer duration to be nulled, especially if it hits when the stat drain tick falls below 15.

tactics.heading: Defence reduction
tactics.text:
If using crossbows, dragonbane weaponry, Osmumten's fang, or a Bow of Faerdhinen, defence reduction is typically less beneficial than higher damage special attacks like burning claws, the Voidwaker, or the Zaryte crossbow.

However, players with lower level stats and gear or the toxic blowpipe may benefit from lowering Vorkath's defence with the Bandos godsword or dragon warhammer special attacks at the start of each kill. At lower ranged levels or if struggling with the fight, failing to hit at least one dragon warhammer special attack or not dealing enough damage with the Bandos godsword special may cause the fight to last much longer. If this is the case, resetting and replenishing your special attack energy at the player-owned house may be better for getting more consistent killcount.

tactics.heading: Banking and transportation
tactics.text:
It is recommended to use Fremennik sea boots 4; have your house in Rellekka (or have the Construction cape); use an Enchanted lyre (or Enchanted lyre(i)); use a Rellekka teleport; or have a portal attuned to Lunar Isle or Waterbirth Island. After each successful Vorkath attempt using the toxic blowpipe, or once out of supplies with the dragon hunter crossbow, players should re-gear with one of the following methods:

• POH without pool: On world 330 (or 465/512), set your POH to Rimmington or Yanille, teleport to outside your player-owned house with a house tablet, runes in your rune pouch or max cape/construction cape, enter a host's house at that location and use their ornate rejuvenation pool. This method requires a way of returning to Vorkath that doesn't depend on a Rellekka POH teleport. You can also use the Miscellania teleport from an Ornate Jewellery Box, run to the port, then use the Sailor to travel to Rellekka, or a Waterbirth Island teleport to quickly return to the Rellekka docks with the nearby sailor.

• POH with pool: Teleport to your player-owned house with a house tablet, runes in your rune pouch, or max cape/construction cape, and use an ornate rejuvenation pool.
  • Players may teleport to Lunar Isle through a portal and bank with 'Birds-Eye' Jack, then talk to any other person to get kicked off back to Rellekka, or by using the Return orb next to the bank booth
  • Players may also attune a POH Portal or Teleport Nexus to Waterbirth Island, and quickly take the boat back to Rellekka, which leaves you at the west dock, only a few steps away from the Vorkath dock.
• POH & Camelot teleport: After completing the Hard Kandarin Diary, you may switch Camelot teleport to the location of the Seers' Village bank. While having dust runes, chaos runes, and law runes in a rune pouch, Teleport to Seers' Village to bank and teleport back to POH while having your house in Rellekka.
• Ferox Enclave: Teleport to Ferox Enclave with a ring of dueling, use the Pool of Refreshment to reset your stats and use the bank chest to re-gear. Then, return to Vorkath using Fremennik sea boots 4, or teleporting to POH located in Rellekka. Note: this does not restore special attack, and resets any stats (boosted or drained) upon exiting.
  • Ferox Enclave also allows you to consume blighted anglerfish within to boost health above maximum (particularly after consuming a divine potion) for considerably cheaper than using anglerfish for the same purpose, and not risking entering the wilderness.
• Nardah: Teleport to Nardah with your Desert Amulet 4 and pray at the Elidinis Statuette there, which provides the same benefits as an Ornate rejuvenation pool (excluding stat restoration), as well as a temporary boost to hit points above the player's maximum based on level. A bank is located nearby to the south. This method requires completion of the elite Desert Diary.

gearNotes.heading: Equipment
gearNotes.text:
• After completing The Blood Moon Rises, you need a garlic cocktail in your inventory for Vyrewatch Sentinels to be aggressive. However, you don't need the vyre noble outfit to bank after the quest.
• Note that Vyrewatch Sentinels are not undead, therefore items such as Salve amulet will have no effect on them.
• Efaritay's aid provides a 15% accuracy bonus that stacks with slayer helmet.
• You may opt for higher prayer bonus in exchange for lower DPS.
• Note that vyrewatch can only be damaged by the Ivandis flail, blisterwood flail, hallowed flail, Sunspear, or blisterwood stakes.
• The Saradomin godsword's special attack still heals health and prayer normally based on the calculated roll even though it will result in doing 0 damage, similar to kurask.
• Burning claws' special attack doesn't deal any damage directly, but the burn effect can still be applied if rolled successfully.

tactics.heading: Overview
tactics.text: Vyrewatch Sentinels can be found in Darkmeyer, the capital city of Morytania located in the Sanguinesti region, north of Meiyerditch.

tactics.heading: Requirements
tactics.text:
• Completion of Quest Sins of the Father for access to Darkmeyer.
• Level 43 Prayer for Protect from Melee.

tactics.heading: Recommendations
tactics.text:
• High combat stats. Although not required, see the skill levels below for an indication of the advised stats:
  • Level 50 Attack or higher
  • Level 70 Strength or higher
  • Level 70 Prayer and 70 Defence or higher for Piety
• Completion of Quest Sins of the Father to unlock the Drakan's Medallion teleport to Darkmeyer.

tactics.heading: Transportation
tactics.text:
The two quickest methods of reaching Darkmeyer, where Vyrewatch Sentinels reside, are:
• Teleporting to Darkmeyer via Drakan's medallion, then running north.
• Teleporting to Ver Sinhaza via Drakan's medallion, then talking to a Vyrewatch to be teleported to the Meiyerditch mine. By talking to a vampyre juvinate with either completion of The Blood Moon Rises, having vyre noble clothing equipped, or after mining 15 daeyalt ore, you will be taken to the north of Meiyerditch. Just north of this is a crack in the wall to enter Darkmeyer.

tactics.heading: Prayer AFK Area
tactics.text:
• When you reach Darkmeyer using Drakan's medallion, run north to the bank area. Using the the nearby altar to restore prayer points, you can avoid using prayer potions and save money. Activate Protect from Melee and fight the vyrewatch. When you reach low prayer points, pray at the altar.
• To use the bank you have to bring your vyre noble costume, put them on when you want to deposit any item, or withdraw super combat sets.
• After completing the quest The Blood Moon Rises, the Vyre noble costume is no longer required to use the bank. Make sure to bring a garlic cocktail to keep the vyrewatch sentinels aggressive.
• You may want to collect the vampyre dust for use at the Hallowed Sepulchre.
• You may also opt for a ring of wealth since these monsters regularly drop up to 1,000 coins.
• Stand at least 1 tile away from the lamps on either side. This is to prevent the vyres from getting stuck and it makes it more efficient for everyone on every world.

gearNotes.heading: Equipment
gearNotes.text:
Using magic can be beneficial since it allows safespotting waterfiends in some locations. If using any of the one-handed weapons, it is highely recommended to primarily use Confliction gauntlets to benefit from its passive effect, and only switch to Expeditious bracelet just before a waterfiend is about to die. Bringing Saturated heart is also beneficial for both higher damage output, and for higher magic defence if not safespotting.
Use Earth Surge if using Harmonised Nightmare staff, and Earth Wave if using Twinflame staff.

tactics.heading: Overview
tactics.text:
Waterfiends can be assigned as a slayer task at 75 combat level by two Slayer masters, Konar quo Maten and Duradel. Waterfiends can only be assigned as a slayer task after being granted access to the Ancient Cavern. They are found in the Ancient Cavern, Kraken Cove, and Iorwerth Dungeon. Iorwerth Dungeon is only accessible after completing Song of the Elves.

Waterfiends attack with Magic and magical Ranged so protection Prayers cannot be used to negate all of their damage. However, both types of attacks roll against the player's Magic Defence, so armour with Magic Defence bonuses, such as fortified Masori armour, Eclipse Moon armour, or dragonhide armour is most helpful when fighting them. A saturated or imbued heart can also help slightly increase magic defence. Protect from Missiles will be the most helpful if they are dealing too much damage.

Waterfiends have low crush Defence, so crush weapons are recommended, such as a soulreaper axe (on crush), Inquisitor's mace, or abyssal bludgeon. Ranged can also be used in the case of Ranged armour being used to defend against their attacks.

Waterfiends also have a 100% elemental weakness to earth spells, which makes maging them generally faster than meleeing them, but at a greater cost. Using non-earth magic is only recommended if player has either the Eye of Ayak or Tumeken's shadow.

Bringing runes for High Level Alchemy is recommended due to their somewhat common armour and staves drops.

Because waterfiends have moderately high stats and are fairly accurate, it is advisable to skip their tasks. They do not provide as many valuable drops as other preferable Slayer monsters, aside from the mist battlestaff for Ironmen. It is not advised to block waterfiends, as they have an incredibly low weight value of 2, thus making them very unlikely to be assigned.

gearNotes.heading: Equipment
gearNotes.text: Due to wyrms' 50% earth weakness and lava strykewyrms' 50% water weakness, elemental spells can be very effective against them. By standing outside of melee range, you can cast protect from magic for standard wyrms or protect from range for lava strykewyrms to avoid all damage.

tactics.heading: Overview
tactics.text: Wyrms are draconic creatures requiring 62 Slayer to harm. Players can choose to kill any of three different variants for a wyrms task: Wyrms (sometimes referred to as adult wyrms), wyrmlings, and Lava Strykewyrms.

tactics.heading: Monster variants
tactics.text:
Adult wyrms have a flat armour value of 1 and use both melee and magic attacks, using magic only when attacking from a distance. They have a superior variant, the Shadow Wyrm, which cannot be safespotted and has 2 flat armour, but otherwise shares the same attacks and mechanics. Adult wyrms notably drop dragon swords, dragon harpoons, dragon knives, and dragon thrownaxes.

Wyrmlings attack only with melee and do not have flat armour. Unlike adult wyrms, they do not have a superior variant and have no drops aside from their bones.

Lava Strykewyrms are aggressive, use ranged and melee attacks, and do not have flat armour. Their superior variant, the magma strykewyrm, has a unique burrowing mechanic that requires the player to move at least two tiles from their position when the attack was initiated or they will take moderate damage. They drop dragon metal sheets, with an increased drop rate while on a wyrms task.

tactics.heading: Wyrmscraig
tactics.text:
All three variants of wyrms can be found on Wyrmscraig, making it the most versatile location for completing a wyrms task. The island requires level 62 Sailing to access. Before partially completing Fallen From Grace, only the wyrmlings on the island's surface are accessible; completing the required portions of the quest unlocks access to the Wyrmscraig Cavern, where adult wyrms and Lava Strykewyrms can be found. Full completion of the quest also unlocks a buildable bank, as well as teleportation to the island via the slayer ring and necklace of passage, making completion of Fallen From Grace necessary to take full advantage of the location.

Wyrmlings can be found in the wyrmling nest on the island's surface. This is the recommended location for quickly completing a wyrms task as the wyrmlings have lower health, reside in a multicombat area where a dwarf multicannon can be used, and are close to a bank and the necklace of passage teleport.

Adult wyrms and Lava Strykewyrms can both be found in the Wyrmscraig Cavern which can be easily reached using the slayer ring teleport. The cavern is a single-way combat area, but a multicannon can be used to draw aggression from the adult wyrms, providing a faster and lower-effort method of killing them than at other locations. Although a multicannon can be set up near the Lava Strykewyrms, they are immune to cannon damage.

tactics.heading: Karuulm Slayer Dungeon
tactics.text: Adult wyrms are also found in the Karuulm Slayer Dungeon. Unless the elite tier of the Kourend & Kebos Diary has been completed, players must wear boots of stone, boots of brimstone, or granite boots to prevent taking rapid damage from the overheated floor.

tactics.heading: Earthbound Cavern
tactics.text: Wyrmlings are also found in the Earthbound Cavern in Neypotzli. This location requires partial completion of Perilous Moons to access and is generally not recommended due to its distance from a bank and lack of convenient transportation methods. However, Neypotzl is a convenient location for players who don't wish to use their own supplies as they can use resources within the cavern to sustain their trip.

tactics.heading: Charred Dungeon
tactics.text: Lava Strykewyrms are also found in the Charred Dungeon on Charred Island. This location requires level 60 Sailing to access.

tactics.heading: Safespotting
tactics.text:
If the player is on a Slayer task in the Karuulm Slayer Dungeon, any idle wyrms on the eastern alcove of the second island can be attacked and then lured to the corner to trap them, allowing players to range them at a specific spot while staying out of their magic attack range of 6 squares. Wyrms will return to their idle state after being unable to retaliate for several hits, and may walk out of the safespot area in the process. This can cause the player to run after the wyrm and start taking damage. For this reason, it is recommended to pay some attention even while using this method. A player can ensure more idle time by attacking with a weapon that has an attack speed of 5 ticks (e.g., magic longbow or rune crossbow in with their attack style set to rapid). If timed correctly, the attack will hit the wyrm as soon as its "re-idling" animation ends, preventing it from moving away and undoing the safespot.

Furthermore, if the wyrm manages to move away and enter the platform's northern "corridor", the player can avoid having to reposition it by setting up a safespot along the second island's north-western edge, 6 squares from the corner.

To set up this safespot, attack a wyrm when it is in the eastern alcove and run to the shown tile. The more north and east the wyrm is, the higher the chance of instant success. You may have to run to the back of the northern alcove to lure the wyrm's character box past the western wall of the northern alcove if the wyrm doesn't automatically get stuck on said western wall. Note that the shadow wyrm cannot be safespotted.

Wyrms can be safespotted at Wyrmscraig Cavern, see the screenshot with marked tiles. From the marked southwest tile, you can safe spot the wyrms spawning north-east of the tile.

gearNotes.heading: Equipment
gearNotes.text:
Yama is weak to slash and can also be fought effectively with magic if using the purging staff or Tumeken's shadow due to their higher accuracy compared to other magic weapons and Yama's lower magic defence bonuses. Yama has a Defence level of 225 and Magic level of 250, with +80 slash defence and -30 magic defence, making magic hit well on him despite his higher Magic level. If the player currently targeted by Yama is using magic during phase 1 and 2, his magic defence raises to 60. It is not recommended to use any other combat style, as he has +100 stab, +333 crush/light/heavy ranged defence, and +220 standard ranged defence.

During the final phase, his defence bonuses increase to +135 stab, +108 slash, +449 crush/light/heavy ranged, +297 standard ranged, and +81 magic defence.

Melee= Meleeing Yama provides the highest damage output while being cheaper than magic. In solo encounters, melee-only setups can be a bit more difficult to damage Yama while avoiding waves and preventing flares from spawning as rapidly in the final phase of the fight.

Defence reduction is especially helpful against Yama. In duos, an elder maul (or dragon warhammer) with a partner using the soulflame horn is recommended, while solo players should use an emberlight.

If soloing Yama with melee, purging Staff + 10% additional magic damage is needed to 2-shot the Void Flares.

Mage=Magic gives players more leeway in fighting Yama, as his ranged and magic attacks are fully blocked with prayer until the last phase and it is easier to manage positioning compared to melee. It is not recommended to mage without Tumeken's shadow and/or a purging staff, as the player's damage output will be significantly lower otherwise and void flares cannot be managed effectively.

gearNotes.heading: Inventory setups
gearNotes.text: Melee=This setup is ideal for duo encounters as Yama's defence can be reduced for higher damage output.

gearNotes.heading: Inventory
gearNotes.text:
• Purging staff and equipment with high magic damage for Void flares
• Soulflame horn and Elder maul for consistent defence reduction (Optional in duo. Each player brings only 1).
• Saradomin godsword for consistent heals when used against the Judge of Yama
• Divine rune pouch with cosmic, soul, death, and blood runes, with fire runes in inventory, for Thralls, Death charge, Mark of Darkness, and Dark Demonbane
  • Nature runes for Ward of Arceuus (optional)
  • Aether runes instead of cosmic and soul runes to save an inventory slot (optional)
• One click teleport to bank and restore stats such as a Construct. cape and Crafting cape, or Teleport to house (tablet)
• Dramen or lunar staff if the Elite Lumbridge & Draynor Diary has not been completed
