tactics.heading: Overview
tactics.text:
After the completion of A Kingdom Divided, players can fight Yama once they speak to him in person. In order to challenge Yama, players must first speak to the Voice of Yama at the bottom of the Chasm of Fire to reach Yama's Domain, then agree to sign a contract to face him in an inhibited form.

Yama can be fought solo or with another player. His stats are not affected by group size, but some mechanics can be made easier and the fight will progress much faster with another player.

Unlike other bosses, players who die fighting Yama are sent back to the Voice of Yama instead of their respawn point, where their graves are also located. Players will have their reclamation fee reduced by 75% until they have ten kills, after which the standard death cost will apply.

tactics.heading: Requirements
tactics.text: • Completion of Quest A Kingdom Divided

tactics.heading: Recommendations
tactics.text:
• 82+ Magic for Dark Demonbane
• 80+ Attack
• 80+ Strength
• 75+ Defence
• 70+ Prayer for Piety (if using melee), 77+ Prayer for Augury (if using magic); if not, 63+ Prayer for Mystic Vigor is fine as the kill times are extremely similar (second/s of difference)
• Completion of Quest While Guthix Sleeps for access to the Emberlight and purging staff
• At least one player with a purging staff to quickly destroy void flares
• 73+, 83+ agility for shortcuts in the Chasm of Fire

tactics.heading: Transportation
tactics.text:
There are several ways to access the Chasm of Fire:
• The chasm teleport scroll brings players in front of the Voice of Yama.
• The fairy ring code DJR is south-east of the Chasm.
• Casting Battlefront Teleport will take players north-west of the Chasm.

Players with level 73 Agility can run north to the platform edge (marked by a icon) and hang-down to instantly reach the middle level, jumping over the two gaps directly east, and finally using the north-eastern gibbet to reach the bottom level. Alternatively, with level 83 Agility, players can slide down the chain next to them after entering the Chasm to instantly reach the bottom level near the Voice of Yama. Protect from Melee is highly advised regardless of the route taken, as players will pass by several aggressive demons. Though this is less of a case with the level 83 shortcut, it is still recommended to avoid unnecessary damage from a black demon if it is idling by the shortcut.

The Voice of Yama will take you to Yama's Domain via the right-click "Travel" option; for players joining their duo partner, they must use the "Join" option and enter their partner's username.

tactics.heading: Fight overview
tactics.text:
The fight with Yama begins when a player uses the "Challenge" option. Yama will then disappear from his throne and reappear in the arena in a much larger form. He will randomly target a player and begin attacking; in duo encounters, he can also periodically change targets. He will usually accompany the aggression change with a quote. Unlike other demons, he has 120% demonbane vulnerability instead of the normal 100%, meaning that Emberlight has 84% increased damage and accuracy against him rather than 70%.

Yama has a unique combat behaviour in which he will adjust his combat stance depending on what he was recently attacked with. If his primary target last attacked him with melee, Yama will act like most normal NPCs would, chasing after them until he gets in melee distance. If he cannot attack with melee due to his target being away from him, he will attack with ranged and magic until he closes the distance. If his primary target last attacked him with magic, Yama will stay still and attack with ranged or magic (depending on the special attack in line) and will only use melee if the target is next to him. If his primary target attacks him with magic, his magic defence will significantly increase from -30 to +60.

Yama's basic attacks cover all three combat styles, all of which can hit up to 46 without prayer:
• Melee - Yama swings his axe at his target. This is only used if the target is adjacent to him, and will hit everyone within three tiles of his main target. Activating Protect from Melee before the attack is used will block a majority of the damage, reducing its max hit to 6.
• Magic - Flames begin to envelop the player, after which Yama will snap his fingers to deal damage. Activating Protect from Magic before his fingers snap will fully protect the player.
• Ranged - Shadowy swirls begin to engulf the player, after which Yama will snap his fingers to deal damage. Activating Protect from Missiles before his fingers snap will fully protect the player.

Yama can also poison the player starting at 20 poison damage, and this will deal significant damage if not cured. Curing poison at Yama is primarily done through sanfew serums, as these also restore prayer. If resupplying with alt accounts, araxyte venom sacs are preferred as these are stackable at the cost of taking 4 damage per sac when used.

Additionally, Yama's Defence level can only be reduced by 80 (from 225 down to 145). The closest option to reach this cap is one elder maul special, which reduces his Defence to 147. Using the maul will require a partner with the soulflame horn, as Yama's higher crush defence makes the maul unlikely to land. If soloing or neither player has a soulflame horn, emberlight is recommended, with three specials reducing his Defence to 145. A bandos godsword is the last option as this requires both hits to average at least a 40, while emberlight simply requires damage to be dealt and additionally drains both his Attack and Strength.

If using magic, an accursed sceptre's special attack will drain Yama's Defence level by 34 (from 225 to 191) and Magic level by 38 (from 250 to 212). This will slightly improve accuracy with magic, and is the only way to consistently drain his Magic level, since any damage from a special attack will drain the maximum amount, something which a seercull is unable to match. An Eye of Ayak can also be used to drain Yama's magic defence and should be used in conjunction with the sceptre to make him easier to hit, since Yama has +60 magic defence if maging, or +81 in phase 3. When applying the sceptre's debuff, make sure to have Yama in his melee stance so his magic defence is significantly reduced.

Yama restores 1 stat point per minute like most other NPCs, so drained levels will maintain fairly well for the entire fight.

tactics.heading: Phase 1
tactics.text:
Yama's first attack is determined by the colour of the Glyphs nearest the throne (being the opposite of his regular attack colours), with red Glyphs of Fire indicating Yama will use one ranged attack first, and purple Glyphs of Shadow indicating Yama will use one magic attack first. After the first magic/ranged attack, Yama will use his first special attack, swap combat styles, and continue attacking. After three regular attacks (either magic, ranged, or melee), Yama uses another special attack, and repeats this pattern for the rest of the phase.

Yama's special attacks in the first two phases require the player to stand on the centre of the matching glyph to negate the attack's damage and effects. The player will take 2, 6, 9 or 12 damage upon stepping on a Glyph of Fire depending on how close Yama was to it when stepped on; 2 damage if Yama was four or more tiles away, 6 if three tiles, 9 if two tiles and 12 if one or adjacent to it. The Glyph of Shadow will drain 2-12 prayer points, and like the Glyph of Fire, drains more if Yama is closer to it.

Standing on a glyph will provide the player with 10 ticks (6.0 seconds) of immunity against the corresponding attack; e.g being under the effect of a Glyph of Fire negates all of Yama's magic attacks and fire-based special attacks. Additionally, the glyph will provide a unique buff; fire will boost the special attack of Zorya's tome and a volatile Nightmare staff, while shadow will boost the prayer restoration of the Saradomin godsword, eldritch Nightmare staff and ancient mace. Enhancing a special attack this way will consume the glyph immediately, potentially leaving the player open to an incoming special attack. These are mostly useful in duos, but even then, other special attacks are much more beneficial.

In duo encounters, only one player needs to stand on the glyphs for both to be protected. These glyphs can also be used to block damage from the corresponding attack, but this is not recommended unless a special attack is incoming.

After a special attack, Yama will switch combat styles and special attacks, unless void flares are used, in which case he will remain with the same combat style. The flares can only be used on the second or third shadow attack (if the phase started with a shadow special attack first) or the first or second shadow attack (if a fire special attack is first). Their appearance is consistent across both phase 1 and 2, so players should take note of this to make sure their Mark of Darkness is active when they spawn.

Lastly, Yama uses several arena hazards to keep players on their toes and will spawn these right before doing a special attack:
• Shadow Waves - Waves of shadowy flames will spawn from the south-east or south-west and move across the entire arena, which the player must "skip" over to avoid taking up to 20 damage and having their protection prayers disabled briefly, leaving them open to Yama's attacks.
• Fire Streaks - Fires are ignited at the east and west edges of the arena before moving across the entire arena at running speed. If not avoided, the player will take damage and be seared to the ground, temporarily binding them in place and potentially unable to move towards a Glyph to negate Yama's special attacks. So long as the player does not pause or stop moving, they may path directly through the flames without taking damage.
• Void Flares - Yama will snap his fingers, summoning a fire and shadow void flare in the arena. These orbs must be destroyed before the yellow bar fills up (in roughly ~15 seconds) or they will explode. The amount of damage dealt, along with health restored to Yama, scales on their remaining health at the time of explosion. At full health, they will hit between 42-44 damage.
  • They have 200% demonbane vulnerability and using magic attacks or the scorching bow will always deal their max hit. The purging staff is most useful for this, as it can take down flares in two hits especially when using Dark Demonbane under the effects of Mark of Darkness. Death Charge works against the flares, even if the player doesn't destroy it as Yama initiates the phase transition.
  • Afflicting a flare with poison or venom will result in the flare healing Yama and damaging the player for around 75% less than normal when it detonates.
  • Players can choose to destroy only one void flare and stand on the matching Glyph before it fully charges to block the explosion damage and healing to Yama, however this not recommended due to losing out on Death Charge bonuses.

tactics.heading: Judge of Yama
tactics.text:
Upon reaching 66.6% and 33.3% of his health (not a hard cap), the first and second phases of the fight ends and an intermission phase will occur where Yama becomes bored and slams his axe's pommel to the ground, teleporting the player(s) away from the main arena. The player is fully immune to any incoming attacks during the teleport, and any void flares that were present when this occurs are immediately destroyed without penalty, which additionally triggers Death Charge, provided the player damaged them at least once before this occurs. The first player (instance creator) will always be placed west, while the second player will always be placed east.

As players hop across the stones to reach the Judge, it will launch fire spells in one or two of five potential spots en route every five ticks. Getting hit by these will deal up to 30 damage, meaning the player must dodge them or attack it with water spells, which deal the player's max hit.

Upon reaching the last stone, the Judge will start launching fireballs on the last tile the player stood on. This deals around 20 damage if hit by it; if the projectile lands under the demon, it will deal 13-18 damage to it. Periodically, the cavern will shake, dealing 5-7 damage; the first instance of damage occurs on the demon's fifth attack, and the second occurs around the demon's thirteenth attack.

The Judge has 400 health, and uses two protection prayers at once. Initially, it will always pray against melee and ranged attacks, then switching based on the player's last attack style, so magic is essentially mandatory to defeat it. It does not react to attacks made by thralls, but the short duration of the fight makes summoning one infeasible. The player will always land a maximum hit on the Judge, though multi-hitting weapons will only hit once. Additionally, the Judge's health pool is shared between both players in a duo encounter.

When using melee, prioritise strength bonuses and prayer, as these give more damage compared to magic bonuses and prayer. When using magic (with melee being primary), only prioritise swaps that give +5% magic damage bonus, as anything else gives minimal return. For example, a player using an Inquisitor's mace without any melee boosts would have a max hit of 26, whereas adding Piety increases the max hit from 26 to 32. On the other hand, players using Dark Demonbane with best-in-slot magic and augury would inflict 63 damage; disabling Augury would reduce the damage to 61. With minimal swaps while taking advantage of damage and the step-under method, the player should easily subdue the judge before the cavern shakes a second time.

At the start of the phase, if the player spam-clicks the first stone and has no tick loss while jumping across the lava, the player will always be able to reach the platform before the judge makes its third attack. If the player is one tick late at any point during the crossing, they must wait after the third attack if it is launched at the middle.

When the Judge is killed, players are teleported back to Yama to begin the next phase of the fight. They will always be teleported back in front of Yama's throne, while Yama himself will reposition in the centre of the arena once the judge is killed, though he may displace himself shortly afterwards.

For duo teams, if one player is using magic while the other attacks with melee, it is recommended for the mage to repeatedly hop between the stones once the judge is defeated. This will ensure that Yama always targets the melee attacking player and will have a lower magic defence of -30 rather than +60.

tactics.heading: Phase 2
tactics.text:
The second phase of the fight is similar to the first, except that two Shadow Waves spawn instead of one, and more Fire Streaks spawn when they appear. Yama will reset to his melee combat behaviour at the start of this phase, so maging players should attack him immediately to set him in place.

Additionally, Yama's attacks are enhanced:

• Meteor Strike - Yama's fire-based special attack now drops a large meteor on his target, which has a 5x5 area-of-effect. The target's actions are cancelled for one tick, and their run is disabled (including Ctrl-clicking). Failing to move at least two tiles away from the centre of the meteor will instantly kill the player.
  • Being at the edge of the blast radius (two tiles away from centre) will deal 80 damage. If the player is one tile away (three tiles from centre) they will take 40 damage. Getting hit by this attack without protection will additionally inflict a burn value of 8.
    • If the player somehow manages to get two tiles away from the looming shadow (four tiles from centre), they will take no damage. This can be achieved by using melee and being at least six spaces away from Yama, rapidly clicking him when the fireball is launched. It is possible to do it in five or four tiles, but this requires more precise clicking.
• Shadow Stomp - Yama stomps the ground and sends a shadow-based attack towards players, dealing up to 60 damage, rooting the player in place for 2 ticks and draining prayer.

As with phase 1, Yama will make use of void flares, which follow the same spawning mechanics.

Upon reaching 33.3% of his health, the second phase of the fight ends and players will once again be teleported away to defeat the Judge of Yama.

tactics.heading: Phase 3
tactics.text:
Upon returning, Yama will position himself in the centre of the arena and increase his defence bonuses, though drained stats still remain. His attack speed will also increase from 8 ticks (4.8 seconds) to 7 (4.2 seconds). Unlike the previous phases in which he chases melee players, he will remain in place in the centre of the arena. All glyphs in the arena are now disabled.

Yama will alternate between ranged and magic each standard attack, and he will start with the style of the more abundant glyph in the previous phase; e.g if the glyphs closest to the throne were shadow, he will open with a ranged (shadow) attack. Note that this is the opposite of what he started with in phases 1 and 2. In this phase, Yama's prayer piercing effects are stronger; the melee attack deals up to 22 damage (from 6), while the normally blocked magic and ranged attacks will now have a max hit of 3.

Players may continue to use melee or mage, depending on their primary style. If players are meleeing, they may either flinch Yama or use the one of the methods below. Due to the slightly increased magic defence, maging players may opt to bring a Tumeken's shadow switch, as it is slightly more accurate compared to a purging staff, although splashes will not benefit from confliction gauntlets. If the player has to mage, it may be beneficial to throw an accursed sceptre and Eye of Ayak special before the phase to lower Yama's magic defences.

Yama's only special attack is Shadow Crash, which he only uses when the player is outside melee distance. Shadow Crash is a set of three fireballs in a line which fall upon the player. The side fireballs will spawn shadows after impact that converge toward where the centre fireball landed (forming a bowtie shape). Yama will perform this attack three times, each one centred on the player at a cardinal, diagonal, and cardinal angle respectively. Getting caught in this attack will deal up to 20 damage per explosion. Players can dodge this by moving at least one tile from the centre fireball perpendicular to the line (ex. one tile horizontal from the centre fireball if they fall vertically).

The Shadow Crash fireballs will always require the player to step north/south or east/west, diagonally across and then east/west or north/south (depending on which one was used first, if the player is required to step north/south for the first, the third one will require the player to step east/west instead). Additionally, if the player only moves one tile away from the crash and has Mark of Darkness active, their next attack will be used one tick faster than usual. Performing a perfect dodge will also provide 2 ticks of immunity from the shadow waves. Each crash is individual to the player themselves and they will not take damage from another player's crash.

Note that Yama will still use his standard attack while the fireballs drop, so pray accordingly.

As with the previous phases, Yama will summon void flares into the arena. Two are summoned intermittently during the fight, but one will always spawn if Yama attacks with melee. Up to four flares may be present at any given time. Unlike the previous phases, the flares spawn with half (71) health and deal reduced damage (23-25) if allowed to charge. In order to one-shot void flares during this phase, the player must use the purging staff to cast Dark Demonbane while under the effects of the Mark of Darkness, with a 20% magic damage bonus (including the staff's 10%). If more than eight are allowed to spawn, Yama will summon three flares at a time, though this should be highly unlikely in any scenario with decent gear.

A set of two shadow waves will first appear shortly after the final set of fireballs drop. Another set of two will appear shortly after void flares, and a final set of four will appear right after this set of two waves, which is combined with Shadow Crash and an auto-attack. This will continually repeat until the encounter ends.

In duo encounters, using the donofly method is highly recommended. If this is not feasible, one player should stand east of Yama and the other west to handle shadow flares that appear, if they do.

tactics.heading: Melee Yama P3 Methods
tactics.text:
Melee with the Arclight or Emberlight is the highest DPS against Yama, but can be challenging to use during phase 3. The player must dodge Yama's shadow waves and shadow crashes, and if they are in melee range when Yama attacks, Yama will attack with melee and spawn a void flare, slowing down the kill. Several methods have been developed that allow the player to maintain high DPS with melee, while dodging all special attacks and preventing Yama from using melee attacks.

The Donofly is a cycle-based, tick perfect method where the player must run to specific tiles after attacking Yama and immediately run back to attack Yama after reaching each tile. The tile pattern provided will automatically dodge all shadow waves and shadow crashes without any extra effort from the player, meaning that all your attention should be focused on moving and attacking correctly, and praying against Yama's standard attacks.

There are multiple ways to perform the Donofly; one example of a cycle is as follows:
• Upon returning to the arena, move towards tile 1.
  • If the player is within five spaces of Yama, there is enough time to attack him once before running to tile 1.
• Wait for Yama's attack animation to have his hand above his head, then click on him to attack.
• After clicking, immediately move to tile 2. Once your true tile is there, attack Yama.
• Immediately move to tile 3. Once your true tile is on tile 3, attack Yama.
• Immediately Ctrl click-walk to tile 4. Once your true tile is there, attack Yama.
• Immediately move to tile 5. Once your true tile is on tile 5, attack Yama.
• Immediately move to tile 1 and repeat the cycle.
  • Note that on the third cycle, you should attack Yama as soon as he begins his attack animation rather than waiting for his hand to move above his head.

In solo encounters, donofly is not likely to defeat Yama before he spawns two void flares, but will deal a significant amount of damage. More advanced variants of donofly can have the player kill both void flares before resuming the cycle. Alternatively, stay in mage gear after killing the void flares and finish off the kill using magic.

In duo encounters, donofly will defeat Yama without usage of special attacks, though dumping a few will not hurt to speed up kill times. However, the maul-using player should keep 50% special and the horn-using player 25% so they can immediately debuff Yama on the next kill.

Because Donofly is heavily dependent on staying in the correct cycle, it can be very difficult (though not impossible) to recover from mistakes. Learners are recommended to get off and kill the boss with magic, since further mistakes will significantly hamper the kill, especially if Yama is able to attack with melee and spawn more void flares.

The Godfly is a reaction-based method where the player stands in front of Yama and steps out of melee range every time Yama attacks. Dodging the shadow crashes is the most important part of this method, and the player dodges them in two different ways, reacting to whether the first set of fireballs are vertical (north-south) or horizontal (east-west). Because the Godfly is not dependent on following an exact cycle, it is much simpler to recover from mistakes by standing outside of Yama's melee range and waiting for the next opportunity to attack safely. A simple way to learn the timing for avoiding Yama's melee attacks is to click to step back when the hitsplat from Yama's standard attack disappears from the player.

Unlike the Donofly, the Godfly takes advantage of the speedup mechanic in phase 3 where the player's next attack comes out one tick faster if they move one tick away from a shadow crash's centre while Mark of Darkness is active. This makes the Godfly higher DPS overall, though more difficult to execute, as the player must react to the shadow crash patterns and dodge correctly while maintaining DPS.

A good resource for learning Godfly is this video from redeyejedi.

The Robospear is an advanced cycle-based, tick perfect method that involves unfreezing Yama with the special attack of the Blue Moon spear and using specific tile markers as he chases you around. Because Yama begins chasing the player, certain movement can be used that allows the player to gain the one-tick speedup from every shadow crash during the fight, making this the highest DPS Yama method overall. However, if a mistake is made, the method is extremely difficult to salvage, and the player usually will need to finish the rest of the kill with magic.

This method was found by jeremiah855 and Muffyn using a computer-optimized algorithmic search for the highest DPS Yama method. More info can be found in jeremiah's video here.

tactics.heading: Contracts
tactics.text:
By using a specific contract on Yama, players can tackle a more challenging fight with him in exchange for guaranteed rewards. The contract is burned up once the fight starts, but will be returned to the player as a drop should they complete the challenge; acquisition contracts are not returned to the player, however (except for familiar acquisition).

All contract fights have a base set of changes compared to the regular fight:
• Yama has increased stats, and all specials do more damage.
• Phase transition thresholds during contracted fights trigger at 75% and 50% health, rather than 66% and 33%.
• Yama's attack cycle in phase 1 and 2 is 1 tick faster, matching phase 3 (8->7 ticks).
• Yama does two standard attacks before a special attack; glyphs respawn faster.
• Shadow Waves and Fire Streaks appear more frequently.
• Special attacks in phase 1 land 1 tick faster (6->5 ticks).
• The Judge of Yama throws fire bombs 2 ticks faster (5->3 ticks), and throws two per attack.
• Shadow Waves and Shadow Crashes are more frequent in phase 3, and have some variation in their positioning.

tactics.heading: Strategy
tactics.text:
• Hitpoints and prayer restoration is halved and then rounded down.
• A partner is allowed and may be required due to the number of Void flare spawns.
• The hourglass fireball attack drops in 3 fireballs in 5 total waves (up from 3 waves).

tactics.heading: Items
tactics.text: • Combo eating Anglerfish and Cooked karambwan is a reliable way to burst heal through the health restoration debuff.

tactics.heading: Strategy
tactics.text:
• Recommend players use the the 'gridlock' method; a solve that eliminates the mechanical complexity of shadow tiles by restraining all movement and positioning into the 3x3 square area of a shadow or fire glyph.
  • The shadow tiles cannot spawn in this area and will instead be randomly spawned outside of the 3x3 area.
  • This effectively 'solves' the tile ragging mechanic, allowing for more consistent clears.

tactics.heading: Items
tactics.text:
• Snowy knight (item) or Snowy knight mix (2) can both be valuable instant healing in this encounter.
  • Take note that because of the halving and rounding mechanic, a Snowy knight mix (2) restores 8 total Hp across two uses, and a Snowy knight (item) restores 7 in one.
• Phoenix necklaces can restore up to 14 Hp each and are the highest potential healing item for this fight.
• Cooked moonlight antelope can effectively replace Phoenix necklaces if players would rather use a less complex healing method.

tactics.heading: Healing
tactics.text:
• 6x Phoenix necklace → 84 hp
  • No attack or eating delay, can save player from some types of mistakes.
• 3x Anglerfish → 33 hp
• 8x Snowy knight mix (2) → 64 hp
  • Uses potion delay, no attack delay.
• Total: 181 hp

tactics.heading: Prayer restoration
tactics.text: • 5x Sanfew serum → 320 pp

tactics.heading: Healing
tactics.text:
• 5x Cooked moonlight antelope → 65 hp
  • 7 hitpoints are restored immediately, 6 more after a delay of 7 ticks (4.2s)
• 3x Anglerfish → 33 hp
• 9x Snowy knight → 63 hp
  • restores 7 hitpoints each, uses potion delay, no attack delay.
• Total: 161 hp

tactics.heading: Prayer restoration
tactics.text: • 4x Sanfew serum → 256 pp

tactics.heading: Strategy
tactics.text:
• Forfeit Breath's conditions make it the easiest among the five sigil contracts to get to grips with the fundamental changes present throughout all sigil contracts.
• Because of the run energy penalties, players must keep an eye on their run energy so that errant damage does not instantly kill them.

tactics.heading: Items
tactics.text:
• With a charged ring of endurance, each dose of stamina potion will restore 40% run energy, allowing for multiple mistakes. The player may opt to bring less as they become more consistent at the fight.
• An Explorer's ring 4 can be extremely helpful, as it can be used to restore 100% run energy up to 3 times per day. If using the Runelite client, the ring can be shift-right-clicked with the Menu Entry Swapper plugin enabled to change the left-click option from Wear to Energy, making it a single click to fully restore run energy.

tactics.heading: Strategy
tactics.text:
• Players should always be in position to move toward the next glyph, but far enough away to minimise the tripled penalty from stepping on them.
• Knowing how to melee during phase 3 with methods such as "No Fly" will help immensely.

tactics.heading: Items
tactics.text: • The listed setup will always allow players to two-shot void flares at full health.

tactics.heading: Strategy
tactics.text: • Use a stepback method to prevent Yama from using melee; a good indicator to step back is when the player's hitsplat disappears after Yama's magic or ranged attack.

tactics.heading: Items
tactics.text:
• The forgotten brew and Saradomin brews are used to recover health and boost Magic during phases 1 and 2.
• The scorching bow is used during phase 3 to bind Yama via its special attack. With an upgraded Death Charge and lightbearer, the player should never run out of special attack energy to bind Yama with when destroying void flares.
• A dose of surge potion is used in case the player forgets to cast Death Charge during a phase 3 cycle.

tactics.heading: Strategy
tactics.text:
• Players do not need to flick their protection prayers, only activate them, as Yama will turn it off for them.
• Always pay attention to spawning void flares as an unprotected explosion will kill the player.
• During phases 1 and 2, when Yama would spawn two void flares, players should kill the void flares with the opposing element of the glyph they are next stepping on to focus on Yama instead.
• Step on the glyph shortly after he performs his special attack rather than immediately or before, which will protect the player from Yama's first standard attack and save the player from needing to activate their prayer for one attack.

tactics.heading: Strategy
tactics.text:
• The player and Yama both gain Wretched Strength. Unlike the Dharok's set effect of the same name, this increases the minimum hit of the player and not the maximum hit. As such, the player must camp low health in order to achieve a massive damage output.
• The contract effectively requires players to perform a perfect kill, as any damage will kill the player at low health. With current best-in-slot Magic damage gear (+46% with Augury, shown on the left) the player must stay at or below 16 hitpoints in order to two-shot void flares; any gear downgrades will require the player to stay slightly lower (down to 11 if downgrading to Virtus robes, eternal boots, tormented bracelet, unfortified Elidinis' ward, and no magus ring).

tactics.heading: Items
tactics.text:
• The locator orb is used to reduce the player's health to 1 for the first two phases.
• Use the Eye of Ayak special attack twice at the beginning to considerably reduce Yama's magic defence.
• The two cooked moonlight antelope are used to restore the player's health during the Judge of Yama intermissions.
• The Saradomin godsword is used to melee the Judge and heal off them using its special attack in case the player is hit by a fire bomb.
• The dwarven rock cake, snowy knight mixes, and Guthix rests are used to fine-tune the player's health during phase 3.

tactics.heading: Contract of Forfeit Breath
tactics.text:
It is strongly recommended for players aiming to complete any of Yama's contracts to begin by completing the Contract of Forfeit Breath, as it allows the player to learn the baseline set of changes that apply to all contracts. Furthermore, the stamina-related restrictions added to the fight are relatively easy to manage through extreme energy potions and extended stamina potions.

The player's run energy is continously depleted throughout the fight, both passively and for every point of damage received. Keep run energy high throughout the kill, and be prepared to restore run energy after making a mistake that causes a lot of damage. Players on the RuneLite client may choose to enable the 'Status Bars' plugin to display their current run energy more prominently.

tactics.heading: Phase 1 and 2
tactics.text:
Begin the kill by using two Eye of Ayak special attacks, optionally first attacking the boss with regular attacks until missing once for the passive accuracy increase from the confliction gauntlets. It is important throughout the phase to be aware of which special Yama will use next: as specials happen much more frequently than the base fight, it is easy to lose track. It can be useful to look at in-game messages beginning with , as the colour of these messages indicate the previous special used by Yama ( for shadow, and for fire).

It is often useful to kill both void flares that Yama spawns, as although they can be skipped using the glyphs, the extra special attack can be used for more Eye of Ayak or Saradomin godsword special attacks. The surge potion is useful in Phase 1, as the player will not have regenerated 25% special attack for the purging staff in time. A common mistake is forgetting about the first fire special after Yama summons void flares, which is sometimes caused by the player using both fire and shadow glyphs to skip the void flares and losing track of the next special.

Avoid waiting until the Judge of Yama to heal, and remain high HP throughout the fight.

In Phase 2, there is a significant threat posed by Meteor Strike specials that occur after Yama has spawned void flares: these overlap with Shadow Waves, which can be difficult to skip over as the player is forced to walk. It can be helpful to proactively activate a fire glyph, and then skip over a nearby shadow wave before the player's run is disabled. It is not recommended to skip the Meteor Strike special over using a glyph of fire: this is often more dangerous as the player is forced to walk in a straight line, and may be unable to dodge nearby Shadow Waves.

tactics.heading: Phase 3
tactics.text:
One key change in Phase 3 of the fight is the increased frequency and somewhat random nature of the Shadow Waves that spawn. In the base version of Yama, the vertical column where Shadow Waves intersect is the same for the entirety of Phase 3. However, in all contract fights the column where the waves intersect is random for the 2nd and 3rd waves in each set, as it can be shifted either one tile to the east, west, or not at all. Furthermore the hitbox of the wave changes if it is shifted east or west: it is moved 1 tile south, which can be disorienting as this causes the correct timing to skip over waves to change.

The following procedure using the provided tile markers is effective for dealing with the Shadow Waves in this phase:

• Move to the northernmost green tile when Shadow Waves appear in the south of the arena.
• When the three fireballs appear from the Shadow Crash special that Yama uses, click to the southernmost green tile. This will skip the 1st waves (which are always consistent), and also the 1st and 2nd parts of the Shadow Crash AOE.
• After the Shadow Crash special ends, move to the northernmost grey tile. The column where the 2nd and 3rd waves intersect will align with one of the three white 2x1 rectangles marked.
• When the intersection point of the shadow waves enters the white 2x1 rectangle, click to move to the grey tile in the same vertical column as the 2x1 rectangle. Then return north and repeat to dodge the 3rd wave.
It is important to be very consistent at this wave cycle, as it is fundamental to all of Yama's contracts and being hit by a Shadow Wave can cause significant damage to the player, due to the increased damage of the special and the prayer disabling effect potentially causing the player to tank a mage or ranged attack off-prayer.

After the set of shadow waves, Yama will spawn orbs, and then another set of Shadow Waves will enter the room. This cycle of waves -> orbs -> waves repeats for the entire phase.

gearNotes.heading: Setup
gearNotes.text:
The best setup uses both Ranged and Magic to exploit Zulrah's weaknesses.

Due to Zulrah's weaknesses, lower-levelled players (or higher ones with the Harmonised Nightmare staff) are encouraged to use fire spells, as they are 50% more accurate and deal 50% more damage to Zulrah. Powered staves don't have this benefit, and Zulrah's low defences in its green form make the spells fairly accurate.

Beginners may find it easier to bring fewer Magic/Ranged switches until they are comfortable with Zulrah's mechanics and phases.

A Serpentine helm is very useful for its immunity to venom, despite it having negative Magic and Ranged bonuses. It prevents the need for anti-venom+ potions, therefore freeing up an inventory slot, but over time it's less cost efficient than the potions, considering it needs to be charged with Zulrah's scales. It's recommended for beginners to wear the Serpentine helm until they are able to kill Zulrah consistently. Players who can kill Zulrah consistently and efficiently can forgo the helm, as they will be using the house and fairy ring method to return to the boss.

gearNotes.heading: Equipment
gearNotes.text:
Magic can be used on all phases, but performs much worse than even simple ranged switches for the tanzanite phase. Zulrah possesses a 50% elemental weakness to fire spells, but the Standard spellbook loses out on additional damage and utility of thralls or Vengeance, so it usually is less effective at higher levels.

The Twisted bow and Bow of Faerdhinen are both powerful enough to be used on all 3 phases to reduce switches, if desired. Otherwise, ranged is primarily used on the Tanzanite phase in addition to magic. If hybriding, ranged helmet and boot switches provide fairly minimal dps increases while also having negative magic accuracy. Consider swapping them for supplies instead.

The Noxious halberd is powerful enough to be used on all 3 phases to great effect. The Crystal halberd special attack is very effective during the last hit of each phase, as the double hitsplats get around the 50 damage cap on Zulrah. Attacking primarily with the crystal halberd is possible, but significantly less effective than simply using other styles, due to its slow attack speed. A small Ranged switch is recommended to bring as some phases cannot be attacked with melee due to poison clouds obstructing the area, and to fit in extra hits with a faster weapon. The Eclipse atlatl is best suited to this, as it scales very well from the already worn melee gear, although other options from the ranged gear tab can work in its place with one or two additional switches. Note: No other halberd besides the Noxious halberd (and the Crystal halberd for the special attack) is worth using to melee Zulrah due to the slow 7 tick attack speed of other halberds. If other styles are particularly poor for your available gear, the crystal halberd can still be worth using however.

Due to Zulrah's elemental weakness to fire spells, they perform particularly well against Zulrah, especially at a lower magic level when powered staves are less effective.

With slower kill times, it may be beneficial to hide behind a pillar for Zulrah's tanzanite phase to maximise damage output and minimise damage taken.

tactics.heading: Overview
tactics.text: Zulrah is a level 725 solo-only snake boss found at a shrine east of Zul-Andra, accessible by boat. Zulrah's shrine can be exited through victory, death, logout/hopping worlds, or teleportation.

tactics.heading: Requirements
tactics.text: • Completion of Quest Regicide to access Zul-Andra

tactics.heading: Recommended skills
tactics.text:
• 75+ Magic(if using Magic)
• 80+ Ranged(if using Ranged)
• 70+ Defence
• 80+ Hitpoints
• 45+ Prayer for Eagle Eye, Mystic Might, and Protection prayers
• 82+ Construction (In order to boost for Ornate rejuvenation pool)

tactics.heading: Transportation
tactics.text:
• A Zul-andra teleport scroll will take you directly next to the dock, which is about 20 seconds faster than using the Fairy ring. Despite their high cost, they are worth using once you are able to kill Zulrah consistently without as many deaths, because the price is offset by the extra kills per hour.
• The fairy ring (code BJS) to the Zul-Andra stepping stone, requiring level 76 Agility (can be boosted). Quick fairy ring access:
  • Inside the Player-owned house with a built Fairy ring
  • Outside the Legends' Guild (via Quest point cape)
  • Outside the Fremennik Slayer Dungeon (via Slayer ring)
  • Next to the Salve Graveyard Teleport
• A Charter ship to Tyras Camp, requiring 3,200 coins (1,600 with Cabin Fever/Ring of Charos or 800 with both).
Due to the high damage the boss can deal and shorter trip lengths, having access to a continuous source of healing is helpful to continue fighting the boss quickly.

• An Ornate rejuvenation pool in a Player-owned house can quickly cure venom and restore prayer and hitpoints.
• The Pool of Refreshment in the Ferox Enclave can be quickly accessed with a Ring of dueling.

tactics.heading: Forms
tactics.text:
Throughout the fight, Zulrah will continually dive into the swamp, sending out a plethora of attacks before doing so. It will then re-emerge in its next phase and continue its attacks, usually as a different form.

If struck with a hit just as it dives, the hit will register on Zulrah shortly after it resurfaces. Unlike the Alchemical Hydra, Zulrah's existing attacks will cause damage even after it is killed, so it is important to keep health and the appropriate prayer up to avoid an accidental death.

Zulrah has a Defence, Magic, and Ranged level of 300, along with +50 ranged and magical accuracy and strength bonus on all forms. Although Zulrah has no melee defence in any form, Zulrah can only be reached with a halberd-type weapon. The ranged and magic attacks will envenom the player unless they miss, even if blocked by a protection prayer. Damage dealt to Zulrah is capped at 50, with hits dealing more than that randomly hitting it for 45-50 damage.

• Zulrah's green form, in which it will attack with Ranged, with a few exceptions such as its "Jad" phase (see rotations). While in this form, Zulrah is weak to magical attacks - possessing -45 magic defence and +50 ranged defence.

• Zulrah's crimson form, in which it will attack with Melee. Zulrah will stare at the player's position for several seconds before whipping its tail at that area. If the player does not move away from the targeted area in time, they will be dealt 20-30 damage and be stunned for several seconds. While in this form, Zulrah is weak to magical attacks - possessing +0 magic defence and +300 ranged defence.

• Zulrah's tanzanite form, in which it will randomly attack with both Magic and Ranged attacks, although it uses magic much more frequently compared to ranged. While in this form, Zulrah is weak to ranged attacks - possessing +300 magic defence and +0 ranged defence.

tactics.heading: Special attacks
tactics.text: During the fight, Zulrah can summon snakelings and/or venom clouds in any form, however the phase at which it does so, as well as when during the phase, is predetermined by the rotation.

tactics.heading: Snakelings
tactics.text:
Snakelings are monsters that Zulrah will summon during the fight via shooting white orbs. Each snakeling attacks with either magic or melee, but never both. Despite their combat level of 90, they have extremely low defence and only 1 Hitpoint; this is made up for by their incredibly accurate attacks, which can hit up to 15.

Protection prayers block their attacks; however, it is better to tank the snakelings' attacks if Zulrah is also attacking, since Zulrah can deal more damage, and it is nearly impossible to flick multiple snakelings and Zulrah attacking together. It is highly recommended to bring a ring of recoil or ring of suffering(r/ri) to kill the snakelings.

While most snakelings spawn immediately, in some of Zulrah's attack rotations it will occasionally throw a white orb and then dive into the swamp. The summoned snakeling will only appear after Zulrah reemerges from the swamp.

If you are hiding from Zulrah, it is best to use this time to kill the snakelings to lessen the need to eat and/or use recoil charges during the fight.

Snakelings will also die off if they have been lingering around for more than 40 seconds, whether they are in combat with the player or not, although this generally occurs when the snakeling is stuck and cannot reach the player. They will automatically die off with Zulrah when it is killed.

tactics.heading: Venom clouds
tactics.text:
Zulrah will spawn venomous clouds during the fight via a barrage of dark-green orbs. If a player stands within a cloud's 3x3 area, they will be dealt varying damage per tick which can add up quickly. Players will want to position themselves accordingly for each phase as to minimise the potential damage from these clouds.

Certain phases may force the player to run through venom clouds in order to re-position themselves. Doing so will deal some damage to the player, however, this is a much better outcome than the potential damage inflicted by an unprepared Zulrah attack.

Similarly to the snakeling orbs, if Zulrah launches a dark-green orb just as it dives, the venomous cloud will not appear until Zulrah resurfaces.

While these clouds inflict venom damage, they do not envenom the player.

tactics.heading: Fight overview
tactics.text:
All damage towards Zulrah is capped at 50; if players would have dealt over 50 damage to Zulrah, it is reduced to 45-50 damage. Despite this, using the twisted bow with seeking dragon arrows is still recommended, as dealing above 50 damage more often will result in more hits dealing 45-50 damage, and still increase the average damage output.

At the start of the fight, Zulrah will be in one of four possible rotations (see chart), with each rotation consisting of predefined phases. It takes Zulrah about three minutes to complete each full rotation. After it finishes a rotation, Zulrah will then begin a new one; it is possible to be the same rotation as the previous one. All rotations after the first one have a chance for Zulrah to randomly be in a phase different from the expected phase. There is also a chance for Zulrah to enter a form where it will randomly switch between mage and ranged attacks in a way that cannot be predicted and prayed against (unlike the "Jad" phase, which alternates between Magic and Ranged each attack). Because of this, it is best to try to kill Zulrah within the first rotation.

Each column in the chart corresponds to one of Zulrah's rotations, with each row corresponding to that rotation's phase. The green, red, and blue circles indicate Zulrah's form and position in each phase. The "x" represents where to run, and the tile markers above correspond to these locations. Ensure the camera's orientation is pointed south to better align with the images.

It is recommended to always use Protect from Missiles (green form) or Protect from Magic (tanzanite form) when learning Zulrah, as its attacks are very accurate and often hit hard. The only exception is its green "Jad" phase, which requires alternating between Protect from Missiles and Protect from Magic after every attack it performs. Not every phase has Zulrah attacking the player, however, it is only recommended to disable these prayers once the player is comfortable with the fight's rotations. Zulrah's attacks are capable of hitting up to 41, and with the high damage of the snakelings, can easily combo a player in seconds.

Beginners may want to stop attacking or healing during the "Jad" phase and simply focus on praying correctly. As with most attacks in the game, a protection prayer only needs to be active starting on the same tick that Zulrah begins its attack animation. This means that as soon as a green ranged projectile is fired, overhead prayer should switch back to Protect from Magic. As soon as a red magic projectile is fired, overhead prayer should switch back to Protect from Missiles. The projectile may hit the character while the opposite prayer is active, but 0 damage will occur as long as the correct prayer was active at the start of Zulrah's attack animation.

If Zulrah dies just as it launches an attack, the attack can still deal damage, and can potentially kill the player.

tactics.heading: All rotations
tactics.text:
At the start of the fight, Zulrah will always be in its green form in the middle of the shrine. It will never attack directly at the start; rather, Zulrah will fill the area with venom clouds, leaving the tips on the east and west sides clear. After filling up the area with venom clouds, Zulrah will dive into the swamp and continue on to one of the four rotations.

At the end of every rotation, Zulrah will once again appear in the middle of the shrine in its green form. It will attack the player with ranged attacks several times before filling the area with venom clouds. This phase counts as the first phase of the new rotation.

tactics.heading: Rotations 1 & 2 ("Crimson A & B")
tactics.text:
After filling the shrine with venom clouds, Zulrah dives back into the swamp and reappears in the same spot in its crimson form. It will use two melee attacks before diving back down, appearing at the same spot in its tanzanite form.

When it performs enough attacks in its tanzanite form, Zulrah dives back into the swamp, and the rotations separate until the second-to-last phase in the rotation.

In this second-to-last phase, informally known as the "Jad" phase, Zulrah appears to the west in a green form. It will alternate between ranged and mage attacks, starting with ranged. Players are advised to switch between Protect from Missiles and Protect from Magic on each attack accordingly, otherwise they can be dealt high amounts of damage in a short amount of time. At the end of this phase, Zulrah fills the shrine with venom clouds, leaving the tips on both sides clear of them.

For the final phase, Zulrah appears in the middle in its crimson form and uses two melee attacks. It will then continue on to the starting phase of the next rotation, in which it appears in the middle in its green form and attacks the player with ranged attacks.

tactics.heading: Rotations 3 & 4 ("Serp & Tanz")
tactics.text:
In these rotations, Zulrah's initial phases are different, though the last three phases are similar to each other.

In Rotation 3, right before the second-to-last phase, Zulrah will send out snakelings; this does not occur in Rotation 4. Regardless, the mechanics are still the same in that phase.

In the second-to-last phase, informally known as the "Jad" phase, Zulrah appears to the east in its green form. It will alternate between magic and ranged attacks, starting with magic. Players are advised to switch between Protect from Magic and Protect from Missiles on each attack accordingly, otherwise they can be dealt high amounts of damage in a short amount of time. Zulrah does not send out venom clouds at the end of this phase and simply dives back into the swamp when it's done attacking.

For the final phase of these rotations, Zulrah appears in the middle in its tanzanite form, summoning four snakelings (two on each side). It will then continue on to the starting phase of the next rotation, in which it appears in the middle in its green form and attacks the player with ranged attacks.

tactics.heading: Rotation overview
tactics.text:
Zulrah will start the fight in one of the four rotations below, chosen at random.

You can tell which rotation Zulrah is in by either the second or fourth phase:
• If the second phase is Zulrah in its crimson form, then its third phase will be in its tanzanite form. Afterwards, Zulrah will be in its green form in the south (Rotation 1) or in the west (Rotation 2).
• If the second phase is Zulrah in its green form, then it's in Rotation 3.
• If the second phase is Zulrah in its tanzanite form, then it's in Rotation 4.

The phases below specify Zulrah's position in bold and form by colour, while the "Jad" phase has been underlined.

Beginners may wish to focus on one specific rotation to learn, immediately hopping worlds to try again if not in that rotation at the start of the second phase. Hopping worlds is possible because the player will not be in combat until the second phase. Rotation 3 is often best for learning since rotations 1 and 2 are ambiguous for longer at the start, and rotation 4 tends to cause more damage.

tactics.heading: Rotation 1 ("Crimson A")
tactics.text:
• Phase 1: Zulrah appears in the middle in its green form, spewing out 4 venom cloud barrages.
• Phase 2: Zulrah appears in the middle in its crimson form, attacking twice with Melee.
• Phase 3: Zulrah appears in the middle in its tanzanite form, attacking with Magic and/or Ranged 4 times.
• Phase 4: Zulrah appears in the south in its green form, attacking with Ranged 5 times, followed by 2 snakeling orbs, 2 venom cloud barrages, and 2 snakeling orbs.
• Phase 5: Zulrah appears in the middle in its crimson form, attacking twice with Melee.
• Phase 6: Zulrah appears in the west in its tanzanite form, attacking with both Magic and/or Ranged 5 times.
• Phase 7: Zulrah appears in the south in its green form, spewing out 3 venom cloud barrages, followed by 4 snakeling orbs.
